author: chimera-defi
body:
## Summary

Nightly maintenance pass. The known session-alias store-poisoning issue (doubled `ah-ah-...-MMDD-MMDD` names) was audited and found already comprehensively fixed and regression-tested in this repo (fixed-point desessionify, read/write guards, `--audit-store`, 45 passing tests) — no changes needed there. Everything below is new findings from auditing the rest of the scripts/docs.

- **`session-doctor.sh` `reap-local` orphan gate never actually fired.** The orphan-unit loop required `systemctl --user is-active` to report false before reaping, but the generated units are `Type=oneshot`/`RemainAfterExit=yes` (see `new-session.sh`), which stay `active (exited)` **indefinitely** once `ExecStart` completes — independent of whether the tmux session they spawned later dies. That silently defeated the loop's entire purpose (the common "tmux died, unit is still enabled" case). Verified against the pre-fix code with a `systemctl` stub (reaped 0 items) vs. the fix (orphan correctly flagged). Dropped the gate to match `report` mode's liveness definition (no live tmux), and added a regression test.
- **`new-session.sh` telemetry measured the wrong `CLAUDE.md`.** It always passed the canonical `$WORKDIR` to `record-spawn-telemetry.sh`, even when `session-git-prep` redirected the actual session into a fresh worktree (dirty/busy canonical tree) — so `claude_md_bytes` missed the bootstrap fragment that's only appended in the worktree. `systemctl --user enable --now` blocks until the generated script finishes and already logs the real `rundir=`, so read that back and prefer it, falling back to `$WORKDIR`.
- **Docs drift:** the fallback-recipe's disclaimer undersold what it drops vs. the installed script (also missing: the same-minute collision lock and the kickoff-verification retry) — documented both in `references/fallback-recipe.md` and `.claude/commands/create-session.md`. README/SKILL.md's script-usage sections were missing `--dry-run`/`--alias`, present in `new-session.sh --help`.
- **Test coverage gap:** `session-git-prep.sh` (the most git-state-mutating script — checkout, ff-merge, worktree add, owner-lock) had zero test coverage. Added `tests/test-session-git-prep.sh` covering non-git passthrough, clean+free canonical-branch checkout, dirty→worktree isolation, and housekeeping-dirt exclusion (busy/owner-lock path intentionally left uncovered — needs a live tmux session).

## Test plan

- [x] `for t in tests/test-*.sh; do bash "$t"; done` — all 6 suites pass (`new-session names`, `session-alias` 45/45, `session-doctor` 8/8 incl. new regression test, `session-git-prep` 10/10 new, `session-handoff`, `spawn telemetry`)
- [x] Reproduced the `session-doctor.sh` bug against the pre-fix script with a `systemctl` stub to confirm the new test actually catches it
- [x] No changes to `session-alias.sh` — confirmed via manual review + existing 45-test suite that the known poisoning class is already fully handled

author: machine-blac9216
body:
Closes #442

## Summary

Adds `compliance-runner` and `download-runner` as first-class Compose services (ADR-0013/0014/0015), each with its own least-privilege Postgres role and only the mounts its domain needs, and trims `backend` down to control-plane-only mounts. Also closes the .NET-host build gap #459/#460 deferred: both runner Dockerfiles now compile their own `Waypoint.ComplianceRunner`/`Waypoint.DownloadRunner` executable in a repo-root `dotnet-build` stage and copy it into the runtime stage alongside the existing PowerCLI/InSpec/SAF/pwsh toolchain.

- **Database roles** (`backend/Waypoint.Infrastructure/Data/Migrations/0025_runner_db_roles.sql`, `deploy/postgres/initdb/01-runner-roles.sh`): `waypoint_compliance_runner` and `waypoint_download_runner` get table-scoped SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE on exactly what their job handlers touch (queue/lease/event tables, credential read for local decrypt, their own domain tables), never DDL, never `appliance_state`, never each other's domain-exclusive tables, never `credentials`/`credential_secrets` writes (API-only per ADR-0005). Role creation (needs the actual password) is split from grants (versioned with schema) so an operator with a pre-#442 `pgdata` volume only needs to create the roles once by hand.
- **Runner images**: two-stage builds (`dotnet-build` + toolchain runtime), a root-then-drop-privilege `docker-entrypoint.sh` in each that chowns the service's own read-write mounts before exec'ing as its non-root user (uid 1654, matching backend's), and image-owned file-sentinel health checks wired as Compose `HEALTHCHECK`s.
- **Compose topology**: one replica of each runner by default, internal-network only (no `ports:`, never reachable from nginx or the host), `depends_on: postgres` with `condition: service_healthy`, each connecting with its own DB role/password. `backend` loses every `PowerShell__*`/`WAYPOINT_VCF_*`/`WAYPOINT_VMWARE_STIG_DOCKER_*` env var and every execution-script bind mount; it keeps only a read-only `artifacts` mount to serve results.
- **deploy/README.md**: new "Database roles", "Runner health checks", and "Replica-safe scaling" sections; the obsolete backend PowerShell-mount sections are replaced with a short pointer to where that content now lives (baked into each runner image).

Also fixes a couple of things found only by actually bringing the stack up (see Verification below): `WaypointDownload`'s PowerShell module was missing from any `ModulePreloadPaths` list on `main` even before this issue (a `download` job would fail at `Invoke-WaypointDownload` — pre-existing gap, added here since it's in the exact config block this PR rewrites), and both runner Dockerfiles needed a privilege-drop entrypoint because Compose named volumes always mount root-owned regardless of what the Dockerfile chowns at build time.

## Risk

- **Largest risk: DB grants are too narrow and a job silently fails at runtime.** I verified every grant against the actual repository classes each runner's composition root uses (`JobQueueRepository`, `CredentialRepository`, `CredentialSecretStore`, `RunSecretStore`, `DepotArtifactRepository`, `DownloadRepository`, `InventoryRepository`, `SiteRepository`/`TargetRepository`, `StigManagerRepository`, `AttestationSnapshotRepository`) and probed every grant/denial with `psql` against a live container (see below) — but I have not run an actual `discover`/`scan`/`download` job end-to-end against these roles (no lab target in this sandbox), so a code path I didn't trace could still hit a permission error that only a real job exercises.
- **Backend can no longer execute compliance/download jobs at all** (no PowerShell mounts left). Its in-process job dispatcher is still registered (removing it is #443, explicitly out of scope here) — if it ever claims a job before a runner does, that job will fail. In practice the runners exist now and claim first, but this is a real behavior change from `main`, disclosed per the issue's scope guard.
- **Devcontainer bind-mount trap**: the shipped compose file's relative bind sources (nginx conf.d/certs, frontend/dist, postgres/initdb) only resolve correctly on a real appliance host — verifying from inside this sandbox's devcontainer required a scratch-only path-translation override (not committed) per `docs/testing.md`. This is a pre-existing, documented property of the repo, not something this PR changes.
- **Postgres role passwords are dev-only defaults** (`waypoint_compliance_runner_dev_only` / `waypoint_download_runner_dev_only`) unless overridden in `deploy/.env`, same convention as the existing `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` default.

## Rollback

`git revert a1e6dd7 0c3e1e5 0209af2` (revert all three commits, in that order, to unwind cleanly — each depends on the one before it). No destructive data migration: the 0025 migration only adds `GRANT`s (no schema/data change), and a revert leaves the two runner roles in place but ungranted, which is harmless. If a stack was already brought up with this PR's Compose file, the runner-role passwords and the `compliance-profiles`/`depot`/`managed-tool` named volumes it introduced would need `docker compose down -v` to fully clear, same as any other volume-adding change.

## Verification

**Backend test suite** (`export PATH="$HOME/.dotnet:$PATH"; export WAYPOINT_TEST_PG_NETWORK=git_devcontainer_default`, from `backend/`):
- `dotnet build -warnaserror` — clean, 0 warnings/errors.
- `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` — clean.
- `dotnet test Waypoint.sln` — **959/959 passed** (includes the updated `SchemaMigrationTests.ExpectedMigrationCount` = 25 and the new `PostgresFixture.CreateRunnerRolesAsync` role fixture).

**Live stack** (isolated project `wp-442verify`, unique port, torn down fully afterward — containers, networks, volumes):
- `docker compose build` for all five services succeeded (found and fixed two real build-time bugs in the process: a `COPY` path that assumed the old per-service build context instead of the new repo-root one, and a `useradd --uid 1654` collision on the `dotnet/sdk:8.0` base image, which already ships that uid as `app`).
- Fresh `docker compose up -d`: all five containers (nginx, backend, postgres, compliance-runner, download-runner) reported **healthy** simultaneously once the master key and compliance-profiles content were mounted.
- **Missing runner dependency test**: with the master key and compliance-content volume left unmounted, `compliance-runner` reported `unhealthy` with the exact reasons in its own readiness report (`Scans:ProfilePath ... does not exist or is not mounted`, `Master key is unavailable ...`) while nginx/backend/postgres/download-runner stayed healthy throughout — confirms AC3.
- **DB role probing** (`psql` as each role against the live container): `waypoint_compliance_runner` and `waypoint_download_runner` can SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE their own tables; `DELETE FROM jobs`, `CREATE TABLE`, cross-domain table access (compliance role reading `downloads`; download role reading `sites`/`run_secrets`), `appliance_state` access, `credentials.name` UPDATE (column-level grant excludes it), and `credential_secrets` INSERT (API-only) all correctly denied with `permission denied`. Both roles confirmed `rolsuper=f rolcreatedb=f rolcreaterole=f`.
- **Backend mount check**: `docker exec` into the live backend container showed zero `PowerShell__*`/`WAYPOINT_VCF_*`/`WAYPOINT_VMWARE_STIG_DOCKER_*` env vars and exactly two mounts (`artifacts` read-only, master key read-only) — confirms AC5.
- **Replica-safe scaling**: `docker compose up -d --scale download-runner=2` started a second independent, healthy replica with no name/network collision; scaled back to 1 cleanly.
- Stack torn down with `docker compose down -v`; confirmed zero leftover containers/networks/volumes/images under the `wp-442verify` project name afterward.

### Verification limits

- No real lab target was available to run an actual `discover`/`scan`/`catalog-index`/`download` job end-to-end through a runne

author: blakebauman
body:
The audit's advice on this one was "do it early to avoid a backfill" — it's the only item left whose cost grows while you wait, so it goes in ahead of larger work.

## What it buys

Nothing recorded which SDK emitted telemetry, so three questions had no answer: *is anyone still on a version too old for this feature?*, *which build produced the trace in this bug report?*, and *how far has the upgrade rolled out?*

## Design

`POST /v1/ingest` accepts an optional `sdk: { name, version }`. Two decisions worth stating:

- **Body, not a header.** The identity has to survive the blob → replay path, where headers are long gone. A header would have needed threading through the job payload to reach the worker; a body field just travels with the batch.
- **A daily rollup (`SdkUsageDaily`), not a column on every trace.** The questions above are about a *project over time*, not about one trace, so this needs no telemetry-schema migration, no mutable-state plumbing, and no mirror change. What it deliberately doesn't buy is per-trace attribution — that's when you'd pay for the trace column, and it can be added later without invalidating this.

All three official SDKs send it, each from the same constant its release bumps. The **doc-drift checker now covers all five version declarations** (js package.json + `version.ts`, python pyproject + `_version.py`, go `SDKVersion`) — a stale constant wouldn't just mislabel a release, it would misreport which build a customer is running. Python's version moved to a leaf `_version.py` because the client importing it from the package root would have been circular.

`GET /v1/usage/sdks` returns the inventory, surfaced as a card on the ops page.

## Honest about what it doesn't know

A sender that doesn't identify itself — an SDK older than 0.5.0, a hand-rolled client, the OTel endpoint — records nothing. Absent means *unknown*, not zero, and the console says exactly that rather than implying no traffic. A malformed `sdk` is dropped rather than rejecting the batch: a client mislabelling its own identity must not cost the customer their telemetry.

## Verification

Exercised end to end against a running API + worker by flushing through the **real JS SDK**, which is what caught the API rebuilding the payload as `{ batch }` and dropping the field before it ever reached blob — invisible to every unit test. Also checked: a batch with no `sdk` still 207s, a malformed `sdk` still 207s, and `/openapi.json` still renders (an earlier `.catch()` in the envelope schema broke it — the tolerance now lives outside the schema).

Unit tests in all three SDKs assert the field is on the wire; server tests cover the rollup upsert, clamping, and the per-build collapse.

author: cpacker
body:
Closes #270.

## What

`send()` takes an optional second argument so a caller can supply the correlation id for the user message it is about to render optimistically:

```ts
const otid = crypto.randomUUID();
await session.send("Summarize today's changes.", { otid });
```

```ts
export interface SendOptions {
  /** Caller-supplied OTID for this user message. Generated when omitted. */
  otid?: string;
}

send(message: SendMessage, options?: SendOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Semantics:

- The caller value is sent as the wire `otid` on the `create_message` payload, so it lands on the persisted user message (visible as `otid` on the raw rows from `listMessages()` / `bootstrapState()`).
- It also becomes the turn's `client_message_id`, so the same id shows up on `SDKQueueItem.clientMessageId` in `queue_update` events while the message is queued. One id correlates the optimistic row, the queue entry, and the persisted row.
- Omitting it preserves today's behavior exactly: the SDK mints `sdk-message-<ts>-<n>` as the `client_message_id` and sends no `otid`.
- An empty/whitespace-only `otid` throws (`send() otid must be a non-empty string`) instead of silently defeating correlation. It throws before anything reaches the wire.
- Reusing the same `otid` on a retry is the documented idempotency path — the runtime deduplicates on it.

`SendOptions` is exported from the package root and, via `export type *`, from the portable `/client` entry, which shares `LettaCodeSession` with the root. Both entries pick the change up from the single `types.ts` declaration.

## Full otid support was possible — no protocol limitation

I checked the wire before assuming, since the issue left it open:

- `InputCreateMessagePayload.messages` is `Array<MessageCreate & { client_message_id?: string }>` (`@letta-ai/letta-code` `types/protocol_v2.d.ts`), and `MessageCreate` already carries `otid?: string | null` — the offline threading id used for dedupe/idempotency.
- The listener only *defaults* the otid when the caller omits it: `stampInboundUserMessageOtids()` and `ensureTurnInputMessageOtids()` both return the payload untouched when `payload.otid` is set, and otherwise fall back to `client_message_id` (then `crypto.randomUUID()`).
- Local transcript writes read `message.otid ?? message.client_message_id`.

So a caller-supplied otid is honored end to end; nothing had to be invented. Sending it explicitly (rather than relying on the `client_message_id` fallback) keeps the caller's value canonical on transports that do not apply that fallback.

## Scope

Deliberately limited to the `send()` / `SendMessage` path: `types.ts` (the `SendOptions` type and the `LettaCodeSession.send` signature), the turn coordinator's id minting, the `RuntimeSendTurnOptions` plumbing, and the `create_message` payload. `sendAndWaitForResult()` and `prompt()` are untouched — they are one-shot helpers with no optimistic row to reconcile; say the word and I will thread the option through them too.

`remote-client-session-core.ts` sits exactly at its 900-line source-size ceiling, so the send-site change is net-zero on line count: the inline wire-options literal moved into a `turnSendOptions(turn)` helper next to `TurnTracker` in `remote-session-protocol.ts`.

## Tests

Four tests added to `src/tests/client.test.ts`, using the existing `FakeAppServerSocket` harness:

- a caller-supplied otid is forwarded as both `otid` and `client_message_id` on the wire;
- omitting it still generates an `sdk-message-*` `client_message_id` and sends no `otid`;
- a caller-supplied otid is the `clientMessageId` on the resulting `queue_update` item;
- an empty otid rejects and sends no input command.

## Checks

- `bun run check` (tsc + source-size budget): pass
- `bun test`: 220 pass, 11 skip, 0 fail (231 across 22 files)
- `bun run build`: pass

The repo has no separate lint script; `check` is tsc plus the source-size budget. Note: the source-size budget passes on this branch and on unmodified `main` — `remote-client-session-core.ts` is at 900/900, i.e. one line from failing, which is why the send-site edit was kept net-zero rather than growing the file.

author: leojung0823
body:
Closes #55

## Legacy MVP audit
The existing MVP keeps a single token per session. This PR preserves its RPCs and UI as the `checkin_qr_v2` OFF/evaluation-failure rollback path.

## V2 architecture
A durable parent check-in session owns short-lived child credentials. Credentials are 256-bit opaque values, SHA-256 hashed at rest, never logged or persisted by the client, expire after 60 seconds, automatically refresh every 20 seconds, and have a maximum 30-second automatic overlap. Emergency rotation revokes prior credentials immediately.

## Policy and authority
All V2 RPCs are `SECURITY DEFINER` with a fixed search path, derive the caller from `auth.uid()`, revalidate active account, membership, club, event and session server-side, and retain advisory-lock/unique-index duplicate protection. Manual check-in and revoke retain `attendance.manage`, required reasons, and append-only attendance history.

## UX, rollback, and compatibility
The V2 member surface uses camera scanning with `BarcodeDetector` plus an in-browser `jsQR` fallback. Camera frames remain in-browser and tracks stop on success, error, backgrounding, explicit stop and unmount. V2 has no manual raw-token field; flag OFF retains legacy MVP recovery. Member Home remains an unchanged projection and receives no secret/session detail.

## Verification
- New forward-only migration and deterministic V2 SQL security fixture (23 manifest fixtures total)
- Unit/server suite: 61 files, 389 tests
- Local reset, DB lint (three pre-existing warnings), full security verification, migration/manifest guards
- Browser Smoke adds local V2 manager/responsive/rollback coverage; real-device checklist is included and is NOT RUN

## Limits
No GPS, attendance statistics UI, Club Profile Editing, hosted migration, feature-flag mutation, staging/production mutation, real member data, or provider call. Real iPhone Safari and Android Chrome verification remains manual.

author: coghex
body:
Closes #1189

## Approach

Both live helpers now delegate their boundaries to `scripts/ui/utf8_safe.lua`.

- **`crafting_panel.lua`'s `truncate`** is a character CAP, so it counts and slices **code points** (`utf8Safe.codepointLength` / `utf8Safe.prefix`). Per the issue review's correction, merely snapping the existing `maxChars - 2` byte offset would have avoided malformed output but kept `maxChars` a lie for multi-byte text — 22 CJK characters capped at 20 came back as **8**. It now returns the input unchanged when its code-point length is at most `maxChars`, else the first `maxChars - 2` complete code points plus the existing `..`.
- **`unit_info_v2_panel_engine.lua`'s `abbreviateToWidth`** walks its pixel-width search down by code point instead of by byte. The byte walk handed `engine.getTextWidth` candidates cut inside a multi-byte sequence, and re-measured the same visible prefix once per byte of every multi-byte character (30 measurements where 12 were needed).
- Both are attached to their module tables so the regression test exercises the **real** helpers rather than a copy.

On pure ASCII, code points and bytes coincide, so both are byte-for-byte unchanged — single U+2026 ellipsis and two ASCII periods included. Verified old-vs-new directly: every ASCII fixture matched across both helpers.

The two dead `truncateTabName` twins are deleted along with their `baseSizes.tabNameMax` caps and `combat_log.lua`'s stale "12-char display cap" comment. Per the review's correction, **both** caps were removed unconditionally — a repo-wide search confirmed each was referenced only by its own dead function.

## Spec note (comment-derived requirements)

Implemented from the issue review's amendments: unconditional `tabNameMax` removal; code-point-count semantics (not byte-offset snapping) for `truncate`; a focused `Lua.TextTruncation` describe instead of the broad `--match "Lua"`; tests executing the production helpers rather than a copied algorithm; a width stub rejecting **every** invalid UTF-8 argument so intermediate candidates are verified; ASCII fixtures pinning exact outputs and suffix forms plus each helper's already-fits branch; and a dead-code audit asserting both names and the stale comments are gone.

## Tests

New `test-headless/Test/Headless/Lua/TextTruncation.hs` (9 examples) loads the real panel modules on the headless Lua backend. `engine.getTextWidth` is stubbed to measure 10 px per code point, **raise** on any argument that is not valid UTF-8, and record every call — so "no fragment was ever measured" and "measured once per character" are observed facts, not source greps. One example proves the stub itself rejects a byte fragment, so the guard is load-bearing.

**Mutation-checked:** reverting both helpers to their pre-#1189 bodies fails 5 of the 9 examples (the four multi-byte behaviour ones plus the delegation audit), while the two ASCII byte-identity examples pass against both implementations — exactly their purpose.

### Checks run

```
cabal build synarchy-test-headless                                   # warning-clean
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "Lua.TextTruncation"'    # 9 examples, 0 failures
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "Lua.TextWrapping"'      # 7 examples, 0 failures
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "UI.ElementInputPolicy"' # 36 examples, 0 failures
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "UI.ResponsiveGameplay"' # 91 examples, 0 failures
python3 tools/lua_module_budget.py          # pass
python3 tools/haskell_module_budget.py      # pass
python3 tools/unicode_operator_audit.py     # pass
python3 tools/cabal_module_audit.py         # pass
```

The last three UI/wrapping suites are the existing specs that read or load the four Lua files touched here.

Issue acceptance greps all return no matches:

```
rg -n 'n = #text' scripts/unit_info_v2_panel_engine.lua
rg -n '#text <= maxChars' scripts/crafting_panel.lua
rg -n 'truncateTabName' scripts/combat_log.lua scripts/injury_log_panel.lua
```

body:
## Summary

`standard:indent` now matches JVM ktlint 1.8.0 line-for-line across the whole
consumer corpus — **7366/7366 rows (0 FP / 0 missed)** on ktor, okhttp and
nowinandroid, closing out issue #202 (over-indent detection + indent parity).

## Changes

### Annotation rows (31e300b)
- Standalone annotations (`@Test`, `@get: Rule(...)`) are checked against their
  declaration's expected indent (JVM oracle); mixed rows (`@JvmField val x`) stay
  ordinary rows
- `accessor_row` replaces the `contains("get(")` skip that killed `@Target(...)`
- Error files (tree-sitter parse errors) fall back to the line-scan model —
  garbage AST expectations no longer leak into reports

### .kts / strings / raw strings / accessors (fc1bc56)
- `.kts` scripts skipped by extension (`check_with_path`) instead of the content
  heuristic that misfired on top-level-val-only `.kt` files (Type.kt, ~311 rows)
- `"`-starting continuation rows are checked; raw-string opener rows
  (`value = """`) checked, content/delimiter rows skipped
- Top-level property accessors lift via property ancestor + line-scan fix

### Code-style-dependent `=`-value lift (8033fbf)
- Key discovery: ktor's `ktlint_code_style = intellij_idea` accepts aligned
  named-arg values (no lift); the default (KtlintOfficial) lifts +1 — the
  earlier "TestEngineMultipart mystery" was a style difference, not a shape
- Binary continuations (`a() &&`, `+ second`) = expression first row + 1,
  gated to statement-direct expressions (excludes if/while conditions, chains,
  call args); line-scan operator detection with import/KDoc/postfix exclusions
- `//` comments checked (under-indent only) against the next code row, with
  exemptions for comment blocks, same-indent rows, closers, commented-out code

## Related Issues

Closes #202

## Verification

- Three corpora (LC_ALL=C): ktor 4/4, okhttp 2/2, nowinandroid 7360/7360
  (0 FP / 0 missed); non-probe (shipped) mode also 0 FP
- cargo test 768 green; oracle-diff 108 ALL MATCH; mutation 40 files pass;
  spotless oracle match; fmt clean
- Perf gates: per-file lint gate is timing-sensitive and fails on this machine
  under load for the baseline too (not a regression)

author: val-grasley
body:
Four self-draining must-fail pins for four typecheck defects found while adversarially
reviewing PR #1573. **All four are live on `main` and none is introduced by that PR** —
each was measured byte-identical on a binary built from its merge-base (`8379bcd7`) and on
one built from its head (`573e08db`), so none of them drains when it lands.

This PR adds **fixtures only**: no compiler source, no gate script, no golden. The member
set of the must-fail suite is derived from `ls test/must_fail_fixtures/`, so there is
nothing to register.

## What is pinned

| fixture | issue | severity | pinned observation | verb |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `1575-self-naming-requires-aborts-compiler` | issue 1575 | S1 | exit **134** + the `E-STACK-OVERFLOW` line | `build` |
| `1576-ground-requires-chain-silent-past-33` | issue 1576 | S0 | binary exit **139**, stdout exactly the pre-fault marker | `build-run` |
| `1578-mixed-vector-no-matching-impl-silent` | issue 1578 | S0 | exit **0**, stdout `int-bool` — a wrong value | `run` |
| `1579-residual-commits-general-impl-requires` | issue 1579 | S1 | exit **1** + `T-NO-IMPL 27:16-27:20` — a false reject | `check-json` |

Each ships a control isolating **one** distinguishing feature — the `requires` clause that
names its own head; one fewer `Wrap`; an impl that actually matches; the general impl's
`requires` with the overlap left intact — so a broken environment reports CONTROL-BROKE
rather than reading as the pinned bug.

## Evidence

Every claim was **run, not reasoned**. Exit codes read from direct invocations, never from a
pipeline; the real output pasted into `claim.txt`.

```
$ sh test/diff_compiler_must_fail.sh
checked 95 fixtures: 95 still reproduce, 0 DRAINED, 0 control-broke, 0 malformed
```

**Both assertion kinds were proved fail-capable rather than assumed.** Corrupting 1579's
`diag-code` range to `99:99-99:99`, and separately 1576's `stdout` marker to `NOTALIVE`,
each flipped exactly that row to `DRAINED` and reddened the gate (`94 still reproduce,
1 DRAINED`). Both were restored and the suite re-run green. A pin that cannot fail is a
skip-list with extra steps.

**The pins survive PR #1573 landing.** The suite was also run against a binary built from
that PR's head: all four rows `REPRO`.

## ⚠️ One pin was changed because of something measured, not predicted

1575 pins with `stdout-line`, not `stdout`. The `build` verb is the only one whose graded
stream is stdout **and stderr combined** (`run_verb`: `>"$_out" 2>&1`), and the staleness
guard (`checkSourceStaleness`) writes its `may be stale; rebuild` warning to **stderr**. An
exact whole-stream pin therefore **falsely drains** for anyone whose `./medaka` lags their
tree: the bug still reproduces, the `E-STACK-OVERFLOW` line is still right there, and the row
nonetheless reports *"issue 1575 APPEARS FIXED"* — someone then closes a live bug.

I hit this on a run with a deliberately mismatched binary and nearly dismissed it as
apparatus contamination. It is not: it is a property of the pin. `exit: 134` is still pinned
exactly alongside the line, so this is two independent observations, not one loose one. The
reasoning is recorded in the fixture's own `why-stdout`, including the note that the other
three verbs grade stdout alone and are not exposed.

## Not pinned, deliberately

**Issue 1580** (S2 — at a multi-parameter interface the displayed context names variables
absent from the displayed type, `f : Tag c => a -> b -> String`) is filed but **not** pinned.
On `main` today none of those shapes renders a context at all, so a fixture added now would
report `DRAINED` immediately — a false drain. The pin is owed the moment PR #1573 lands, at
which point `stdout-line` on `check --types` is a clean assertion. Recorded on the issue.

## Review notes

- No closing keyword anywhere: these issues stay **open**; the fixtures are what will close
  them, by going red.
- One fixture per issue, and each directory name matches its own `claim.txt` `issue:` field
  (the harness checks both).
- `1579/main.mdk`'s **line count is load-bearing** — its `diag-code` range is pinned, so a
  comment-only edit moves the pin. Its own header says so.

Refs issue 1575, issue 1576, issue 1578, issue 1579, issue 1580.

author: kelenhappy
body:
### Motivation

- Add a safe, isolated Phase‑1 macOS native adapter that exercises CoreFoundation, Disk Arbitration, and IOKit without changing the production backend yet.
- Replace platform-specific formatting/PowerShell glue with a shared, in‑process FAT32 formatter and move Windows to native Win32 APIs for robust device handling.
- Surface the new work in docs, translations, third‑party notices, and CI so the macOS native proof‑of‑concept is validated on both Intel and Apple Silicon runners.

### Description

- Implement an in‑process, platform‑neutral FAT32 formatter in `internal/fat32` and switch Linux/macOS/Windows callers to use it instead of shelling out or duplicated formatters.
- Add macOS native bindings under `internal/disk/darwin/native` using `github.com/ebitengine/purego` and expose a Go adapter in `internal/disk/darwin/adapter.go`, plus Phase‑1 tests that exercise CF/DA/IOKit callbacks and conversions.  Add CI job `macos-native-phase1` to validate on Intel and arm macOS runners.
- Implement a native Windows backend that uses Win32, SetupAPI, cfgmgr32 and IOCTLs in `internal/windows/native_windows.go` and refactor `internal/windows/backend_windows.go` and tests to use the native API (removing PowerShell invocation).
- Wire the shared formatter into the privileged helper and macOS backend (use `fat32.Format`), add helper and backend changes for label validation and progress updates, and add/adjust tests accordingly.
- Update `go.mod` to include `github.com/ebitengine/purego`, update README/BUILDING/TESTING/SECURITY/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES and add Traditional Chinese translations and macOS Phase‑1 documentation.

### Testing

- Ran the headless unit test suite: `go test ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `gofmt` checks; all updated tests passed.
- Exercised focused tests: XZ streaming test `go test ./internal/image -run XZ`, FAT32 formatter tests in `internal/fat32` and Phase‑1 macOS native tests in `internal/disk/darwin/native`; these tests passed in CI.
- CI matrix updated to run `internal/disk` and platform tests on Linux, Windows, macOS and added `macos-native-phase1` jobs that run the Phase‑1 native tests on both Intel and arm runners; those CI validations completed successfully.

body:
## The live find
5090 rig, real `StableDiffusionXLPipeline` on a w8a8 tree, nerijs/pixel-art-xl r32 kohya adapter. `normalize_adapter_state_dict` → `StableDiffusionXLPipeline.lora_state_dict` emitted **half-converted** keys — `unet.down_blocks.4.1.proj_in.lora.down.weight`, an SGM block index renamed but never *remapped*, and SDXL has `down_blocks` 0-2 — so `map_adapter` failed loud with **2166 unresolved keys** and the w8a8-lane request died typed. The raw dict through `map_adapter`'s own kohya/SGM grammar maps **722/722** modules on the same model.

Every kohya SDXL adapter — most of civitai's SDXL catalog — has hit this on branch-capable lanes since 0.33.0.

## Both fix directions, because only the second closes the class

**1. `unet_config` now reaches `**kwargs`-accepting converters.** The old check required a NAMED `unet_config` parameter; diffusers' real SDXL converter has VAR_KEYWORD instead, so on the exact class that needs the SGM remap the kwarg was silently dropped. `_accepts_unet_config` is the rule, tested on all three signature shapes (named / VAR_KEYWORD / neither — do not invent a kwarg).

**2. The converted dict must PROVE it resolves before it is preferred.** The only previous guard was gw#627's `.processor.` NAME test, which catches the family whose breakage it was written from; the SGM failure contains no `.processor.` at all. The general question is *"does this dict resolve against THIS model"*, and it is now asked with **`map_adapter`'s own oracle** — `_group_keys` over `branch_modules` — not a second copy of its grammar, so guard and mapper cannot drift the way the name test did.

The rule is **strictly worse**, not "not perfect": an equally-unresolvable conversion still goes to `map_adapter`, which raises its own typed error — swapping to raw keys there would only move where the failure appears. An unanswerable probe never decides (no resident denoiser, no denoiser keys, torch absent ⇒ conversion stands, old behaviour unchanged).

## Tests
`tests/convert/test_p8_convert_publish_contract.py`'s pgw#566 row was an `xfail(strict=True)` placeholder — it is now a passing test. New suite `tests/test_kohya_sgm_normalize_pgw566.py`: the half-converted repro (RED before this commit), good-conversion-still-preferred, equally-bad, the signature rule, the unanswerable probe, and a class-closer that the guard uses the mapper's own oracle.

Gates: mypy 270 files clean, ruff clean, all five hard-gate lints green. Targeted: pgw566 + w8a8_moe + lora_cells + adapter_fidelity_pgw794 + p8_convert_publish_contract = 59 passed.

Rides the next wheel; no release cut here.

author: dhajdu
body:
Follow-up to #574, from testing it live.

## What was broken
A member with no manager on file could not save a goal at all: `coaching_profiles.coach_id` was NOT NULL, so there was nowhere to hang the profile and the page showed "You have no manager on file yet, so your goals have nowhere to go."

## What changed
- **`coach_id` is now nullable.** Everyone gets a coaching profile on first save, coached by their manager when there is one and by nobody when there isn't. Getting them a manager is the company's problem, not a blocker on their goals.
- **Delete is the author's alone.** `coaching_goals` records `created_by`. A member can delete only goals they wrote; a goal their coach or manager set for them shows "Set for you, so only they can delete it" instead of a Delete button. They can still edit it or mark it dropped. The 7 pre-existing goals have a null author, so they are coach-owned.
- **Fallout handled.** The daily coaching cycle skips coachless profiles (no 1-1 rhythm to run), and `/team/my-coaching` reads "No coach assigned yet. Your goals and commitments are still yours to run." instead of interpolating a missing name.

## Done when
A member with no manager can add, edit, and delete their own goal, and cannot delete one set for them.

Migration `scripts/coaching/coach-optional.mjs` (idempotent, already applied to the live DB). Typecheck and build clean. The profile + goal insert path was dry-run against the real no-manager record and rolled back: both succeed.

Auto-bootstraps the default chart of accounts once if empty, otherwise fails closed on a missing account.
- `fee_ledger.py` / `expense_ledger.py`: account-mapping + posting rules for assessment, discount deltas, receipts, expenses, and their void.
- `JournalEntry` gains `source_type`/`source_id`/`idempotency_key` (unique), `reverses` (self-FK), and void metadata. `Payment`/`Expense` gain `status`/`journal_entry`/void metadata; `Expense` gains `payment_method`.
- `StudentFeeViewSet`, `PaymentViewSet`, `ExpenseViewSet`, `FeeDiscountViewSet.apply`, and the eSewa/Khalti/ConnectIPS gateway callback path all post through the shared service in the same DB transaction as the source write.
- Completed Payments/Expenses can no longer be edited or deleted (403); a new `void` action reverses the journal entry and restores the `StudentFee` subledger — reason-required, audited.
- Manual `JournalEntryViewSet` create/post/reverse refactored onto the same primitives, fixing two latent bugs on that path: `record_audit_event()` was called positionally against a keyword-only signature (500s after the DB write committed) on 7 call sites, and `JournalEntry.save()` broke on a string `date_ad` (always true for JSON request bodies).
- TDS deposit and ConnectIPS gateway-MSF now post to the ledger using the `journal_entry` FKs that already existed on those models.
- New `reconcile_ledger` management command: dry-run discrepancy report by default; `--apply` (gated behind an explicit confirmation flag) backfills pre-migration Payment/Expense/StudentFee postings idempotently.
- Frontend: `Expense` gets a `payment_method` field and a reason-gated Void action replacing Edit/Delete once posted.

## Migrations

Additive-only — new nullable/defaulted columns, one new conditional-unique constraint (`idempotency_key`, blank on all existing rows). No drops, no data rewrites. **Not applied to any dev/shared database.**

- `backend/billing_school/migrations/0005_ledger_source_linkage_and_void.py`
- `backend/billing/migrations/0011_payment_expense_void_workflow.py`

## Test plan

- `python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` — clean

Payroll posting, full vendor/AP + TDS-on-bill lifecycle, depreciation-run posting, period close/reopen, partial refunds, effective-dated regulatory-rule engine.

- Refund semantics: `void` always reopens the student's receivable. A genuine cash-back-to-payer refund that should stay recognized as income (bypassing receivable) is not implemented.

author: lsnepomuceno
body:
This package exists for Brazilian signing and could not answer the first question anyone asks of a signed document: **who signed it.**

In Brazil that answer is a CPF or a CNPJ. The package handed back this:

```php
$signer->commonName;   // "JOAO DA SILVA:11144477735"
```

So every consumer wrote `explode(':', $commonName)`. That breaks on a name containing a colon, and it is **simply wrong for an e-CNPJ**: its common name carries the company, while the CPF in the extension belongs to whoever answers for it.

## Now

```php
$signer = A1PdfSign::validate($path)->signers()[0];

$signer->icpBrasil?->cpf;                 // '11144477735'
$signer->icpBrasil?->cnpj;                // the company, for an e-CNPJ
$signer->icpBrasil?->formattedRegistry(); // '11.222.333/0001-81'
$signer->name();                          // 'JOAO DA SILVA', without the number
```

## Why it was not read before

`openssl_x509_parse()` cannot do it. Every ICP-Brasil field is an `otherName` under 2.16.76.1.3, and PHP renders each one as `othername:<unsupported>`. The `Asn1Reader` that [0019](https://github.com/lsnepomuceno/laravel-a1-pdf-sign/blob/main/docs/decisions/0019-validation-reads-what-it-writes.md) built for the CMS goes where it cannot.

## Three ways to read the layout wrong, from the specification itself

Verified against the Receita Federal's certificate layout, §2.2.5 for e-CPF and §3.2.5 for e-CNPJ, not from memory:

- **There are no separators.** A field read one character short reads the *next* one wrong rather than failing.
- **The last field of a layout may run short.** The six positions for the RG's issuing authority "refer to the maximum size, and only the positions needed are used". It is read as the remainder, and the width check allows exactly that one field to be short.
- **"Unavailable" is written as zeros.** Eleven zeros and an absent field are the same fact, so callers get null rather than a string they would have to know to test for.

## The structural check

`A1PdfSign::icpBrasil($pfxPath, $password)` says which field is wrong, from the file, before anything is signed.

| | |
|---|---|
| Required fields | three `otherName` entries for e-CPF, four for e-CNPJ |
| Widths | the layout's, with the last allowed short |
| Alphabet | "only A to Z and 0 to 9" |
| Check digits | modulus eleven, both numbers |
| Birth date | a real date in `ddmmyyyy` |
| RG | an issuer named for a number that is absent, which the specification calls out |
| The CPF twice | common name against extension, which nothing in the format makes agree |

### ⚠️ `conforms()` is not `isTrusted()`

**A self-signed certificate can be built to satisfy every rule above, and this PR builds one**: `DebugCertificate::icpBrasil()` is what the tests run against. It chains to nothing and no trust store will accept it.

The value is upstream of trust rather than instead of it. A certificate that fails here will be read wrong by everything downstream, and finding that out from the bytes beats finding it out from a rejected filing. Stated in the class docblock, the report docblock, the contract and [0029](https://github.com/lsnepomuceno/laravel-a1-pdf-sign/blob/main/docs/decisions/0029-the-identity-a-brazilian-signer-is-known-by.md), because it is the one thing about this feature that is dangerous to get wrong.

## Surface

- `Contracts\A1PdfSign` gained `icpBrasil()`: a break for implementers, which Roave reports.
- `Data\Signer` gained `$icpBrasil` and `name()`, appended with defaults.
- `Pkcs7Reader::signers()` goes through the PEM rather than through a parse, because the identity is only in the bytes.
- `Support\NationalRegistry` is bespoke by necessity: neither Laravel nor any dependency here validates a CPF.

**It says a number is well formed, never that it exists.** Whether the Receita Federal issued it is a question only they answer, and asking would mean a network call from validation, which nothing here does.

`composer check` green: **473 passing**, 30 of them new, PHPStan level max, Pint clean.

author: kristenmartino
body:
Bing URL Inspection on `https://gridpulse.kristenmartino.ai` reported three issues and one non-issue. I checked each against the served HTML rather than taking the report at face value.

| Bing said | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Title too short | **True** — `<title>GridPulse</title>`, 9 chars |
| H1 tag missing | **True** — zero `<h1>` in the initial bytes |
| Meta Language tag missing | **Technically true, practically obsolete** |
| No Markup found | **False** — the page serves JSON-LD and has since [#498](https://github.com/kristenmartino/gridpulse/pull/498) |

Only the Dash shell at `/` was affected. All four static pages already had an `h1`, JSON-LD, and a descriptive title — which fits, since `/` is the only JS-rendered one.

### Title

`GridPulse` says nothing to a searcher who has not heard of it. Now **"GridPulse — live US electricity demand forecasts"**.

Deliberately **not** `/about`'s title: that page is *about* the platform and this one *is* it, and two near-identical titles compete for the same query. A test asserts they differ.

### H1

The shell renders its heading client-side via `cards.build_page_title`, so a crawler that does not execute JavaScript saw a page with no heading at all. The `<h1>` goes in the `<noscript>` block — **the same content a no-JS reader already gets**, which is why this is a fix rather than a trick. The visible page is unchanged.

### Meta language

`<html lang="en">` has been there since #498 and is what Google actually uses; `content-language` is superseded by it. Added anyway, with a comment saying so — one obsolete line is cheaper than a permanent warning nobody reads.

### "No Markup found" — nothing to fix

`curl` shows one `application/ld+json` block on `/`. Either the report predates that deploy or the inspector does not surface it. Flagging it rather than silently ignoring it, since it is the one item where the tool is wrong.

### Drive-by

That noscript block said *"the two pages above"* while listing four — stale copy of mine from when there were two.

### Verified non-vacuous

Restoring the 9-character title and removing the `<h1>` fails `test_shell_title_is_descriptive_and_distinct_from_about` and `test_has_an_h1_in_the_initial_html[/]` respectively.

Full suite: 3,720 passed, 3 skipped.

author: 0xmhha
body:
## Summary

Three legacy-stack packages leave the legacy tree (worklist T7.11). None of
them was broken code — each was sound code in the wrong place — so this
moves each to the package whose concern it actually is, and routes the
surfaces through the app layer.

## Moves

**pipeline/verify -> core/health.** It answers "is this network producing,
and what state is each node in": an inspection read over every node. That is
distinct from engine's `NewBlockAdvanceGate`, which polls one node to a
target height as a bring-up precondition — one produces a report about every
node, the other blocks a launch on one node, and merging them would bend
both. The package doc now records that. `cmd verify` and the MCP verify tool
both call `app.VerifyNetwork`, so the two surfaces share one verdict.

**pipeline/attach -> core/node.AttachedSet.** Building a NodeSet from RPC
endpoints is a pure constructor over node's own types with no launch concern
in it. The input struct is named `RPCEndpoint`, not `Endpoint`, to stay
clearly distinct from `node.Endpoints` (the per-node port map).

**core/state's network registry -> core/netreg.** core/state held three
concerns under one name: the legacy setup command's data-dir files, and —
unrelated — the registry of named attached networks. The registry is not
legacy: it backs the live network attach/list/info/detach surface plus
remote_rpc and topology, so it must not die with the code it happened to sit
beside. Its package doc states the lifetime that distinguishes it from a
session (one run) and a composition (one workspace): a machine-wide
inventory keyed by name.

## Measured effect

Legacy pipeline packages: 5 -> 3 (verify and attach gone; Plan already
relocated in #237). core/state: 238 -> 88 lines, now purely the legacy
remnant.

Remaining stack A, unchanged in scope but now unobstructed:
- `pipeline/setup` — cmd setup/node/clean/stop + mcp
- `pipeline/testrun` + `testkit` — gated on the 103 unmigrated test cases
- `core/state` (88 lines) — goes with the setup migration

## Verification

```
gofmt -l cmd internal scripts tests   # empty
go build ./... && go vet ./...
go test -race ./...                   # all packages pass
golangci-lint run ./...               # 0 issues
```

No behavior change: every moved function keeps its signature and semantics.

author: aarirealty
body:
## Summary

`closed_payment_reminder_daily` (pg_cron, 14:00 UTC daily) has been active since Dec 2026 but sent **zero** emails — the reason Samantha's 3815 NW 22nd Ter TC fee sat 5 days past close with `payment_reminder_count=0`. Two schema-alignment bugs in the query plus the raw-untagged-link issue (same class as #263).

## Fixes

1. **`closed_at` → `coalesce(actual_closing_date, closing_date)`**
   The `closed_at` column doesn't exist on `public.files`. Query filtered `.not("closed_at","is",null)` and the loop read `new Date(f.closed_at)` — both were no-ops or `NaN`, silently killing the run.

2. **`.eq("payment_confirmed", false)` → `.eq("payment_status", "pending")`**
   Migration `20260607_payment_gate.sql` seeds TC files with `payment_confirmed=true` because TC services bill at closing (CDA), not upfront. The real pending signal is `payment_status='pending'` — what the manual "mark paid" flow flips.

3. **Append `?client_reference_id=<file.id>` to the Stripe link**
   Same fix pattern as `payment-reminder` (line 94) and the drawer Copy button in #263. Otherwise a payment made through this email would land in Stripe untagged.

## Dry-run against production (Aug 11)

Exactly what the fixed function would do on next fire — run before any deploy:

| Property | Agent | Hours past close | Rung status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1130 NW 14th Ter | Samantha | 25 | **Day 1 · would send** |
| 816 Frederick Reid St E | Marlenyi (own file) | 169 | **Day 7 · would send** |
| 3815 NW 22nd Ter | Samantha | 145 | Between Day 1 and Day 7 (skipped) — enters Day 7 window ~Aug 13 |
| 313 NE 5th Ter | Samantha | 529 | Past Day 7 (skipped, morning briefing owns Day 14+) |
| 4518 SW 22nd Pl | Samantha | 505 | Past Day 7 (skipped) |
| 1607 Roosevelt Ave | (no agent) | 625 | Past Day 7 + agent email null (skipped) |

So **on the next 14:00 UTC fire**, 2 emails go out: Marlenyi to herself for 816 Frederick Reid, Samantha for 1130 NW 14th Ter. **Samantha's 3815 NW 22nd Ter will land the day after** (Aug 13 fire, Day 7 window at ~168h).

## Deployment plan

Merging this PR alone doesn't change any behavior — the cron calls the **deployed** edge function, which is still the old buggy version until I redeploy it via Supabase MCP. That redeploy is the "fire" moment. Waiting on your go-ahead before I redeploy.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

Window gap in the Day 1 rung: files closing between certain UTC hours can miss the 20–28h window entirely (a file closing at 22:00 UTC is 16h past at the next cron, 40h at the one after — never fits). Worth widening to "≥20h AND no reminder yet in period" in a later change.

author: krulldna
body:
The settings page linked to /wp-admin/kdna-tables-styles — no admin.php, no query string. WordPress does not recognise that as an admin URL, so the request fell through to the front end and rendered the theme's 404.

The cause was registration order, not the URL. add_submenu_page() derives the load hook it registers the page callback against from the global $admin_page_hooks, and the parent slug only lands there when add_menu_page() runs. KDNA_Tables_Style_Admin boots before KDNA_Tables_Admin — deliberately, so its REST routes register outside the admin — and both hooked admin_menu at priority 10, so the submenu was registered before its parent existed. The hook came out as 'admin_page_kdna-tables-styles' instead of
'kdna-tables_page_kdna-tables-styles'; WordPress recomputes that name when it prints the menu, found nothing listening, and fell back to linking the bare slug. The same mismatch also stopped the page's own CSS and JS loading, since the hook suffix it compares against was wrong.

Fixed by registering the menu at priority 11, with the reasoning written down next to it — this is the kind of ordering dependency that gets re-broken by a later tidy-up.

Also fixed the per-table panel's link to the settings page, which used admin.php?page=…. That does not reliably resolve for a page parented to a post-type menu: admin.php looks it up against admin.php as the parent, which is not where it was registered. Both now go through a page_url() helper that builds the same URL WordPress links.

── Why no test caught it ────────────────────────────────────────────

The stub's add_submenu_page() returned 'kdna-tables_page_<slug>' unconditionally — the right answer, hardcoded, which is exactly the answer the bug made wrong. So the stub now models the real thing: $admin_page_hooks, add_menu_page() populating it,
get_plugin_page_hookname()'s derivation, and the URL branch from _wp_menu_output(). add_action() grew priority ordering too, since the whole defect is an ordering one and a stub that ignores priority cannot express it.

The new suite runs both classes through the real bootstrap sequence rather than calling register_menu() directly, and ends by re-registering at the old priority to show it reproduces the reported symptom exactly: the orphaned hook name, and a menu href of 'kdna-tables-styles'.

23 assertions. All prior suites re-run green.

author: ossabellator
body:
## Finding

`isolated_workspace_snapshot_supported()` is meant to report whether the host can safely capture the isolated workspace snapshot used by the remote replay groundwork, but it had drifted from the actual capture implementation:

- it checked `os.listdir` fd support while capture uses descriptor-backed `os.scandir`;
- it omitted Linux, memfd, and required file-seal capabilities;
- `sealed_workspace_archive_supported()` already owns the complete authoritative predicate.

This could advertise snapshot support on a host where sealed capture would still fail closed.

## Fix

Delegate `isolated_workspace_snapshot_supported()` directly to `sealed_workspace_archive_supported()` and remove the duplicate/stale primitive list.

Remote container replay remains unconditionally fail-closed; this changes capability reporting only.

## Regression coverage

The focused capability test now verifies the wrapper exactly mirrors the authoritative sealed-archive predicate for both supported and unsupported cases.

## Validation without GitHub Actions

No GitHub Actions were used.

- source-level dependency review confirms `workspace_archive` does not import `isolated_runner`, so the delegation introduces no cycle;
- GitHub compare shows only `isolated_runner.py` and its focused capability test changed;
- branch is 0 behind current `main`;
- production behavior of `isolated_container_replay_supported()` and the fail-closed public runner is unchanged.

author: phatbanana
body:
Second hygiene round, looking for bugs rather than tidiness. It found a bad one.

## The app could silently destroy every saved recipe

`load()` wrapped everything in `try{}` and silently returned `null`. So **any** throw while reading saved data — corrupt storage, a schema slip, the missing-import bug this very refactor produced two commits ago — showed an empty library. The recipes were still on disk at that moment, entirely recoverable. Then the first thing you added called `save()`, and `writeStore()` wrote the empty state straight over them.

Reproduced end to end with one injected error:

| step | what's on disk |
|---|---|
| baseline | `Lavender Bar \| Gift Soap \| Shampoo Bar` |
| after the failed load | *still all three* — recoverable |
| **after adding one oil** | **`My recipe`** |

Three recipes and a batch history, gone. Silently, permanently.

**Two rules now.** *Never overwrite data you failed to read* — a failed load parks all writes and says so, offering to reload, to download the unreadable file before anything touches it, or to start fresh as a deliberate confirmed choice. *Never fail silently* — `writeStore()` no longer swallows its own errors, because quota exhaustion and Safari's private mode both throw there, and the old behaviour was to carry on looking like the batch was logged.

## Fixing it produced a fourth bug

`var loadBlocked=null` sat **below** `var state = initState()`, and `load()` runs inside that call. Module evaluation reset the flag to `null` immediately after `load()` had set it, so the guard did nothing at all. First test run after "fixing" it still destroyed the data. The declaration is now above its first use, with a comment saying why it has to be.

## Dead weight → coverage

Five imports in `main.js` and six exports in `core/` were unused after the split. Rather than delete the chemistry ones, `chem.js` being independently testable was the *point* of extracting it — so there are now **23 assertions running the lye maths directly, with no browser**:

- the classic bar worked by hand (145.53 × 0.95 = 138.2535)
- superfat as a discount on saponification only
- KOH's molar ratio, and purity **dividing** (more flake for weaker lye)
- dual-lye splits, citric acid outside the discount
- all three water modes, unknown oils contributing no lye
- injected SAP overrides, water-replacer arithmetic

Every one passed first time, which is the best evidence the v54 extraction was faithful.

## Verification

**1654 → 1686 assertions.** Mutation-checked — each of these fails:

| mutation | caught by |
|---|---|
| remove the write guard | the data-loss assertion |
| re-swallow the save error | the quota assertion |
| reintroduce the hoisting bug | the data-loss assertion |
| let superfat discount the acid | 3 assertions |
| invert the KOH purity division | 3 assertions |

Screenshots differ from v54 by **70 pixels** — the version glyph in the footer. (An initial 6444-pixel reading turned out to be date drift in a baseline captured on an earlier day; re-capturing v54 the same day isolated it.) Offline reload still clean.

v54 → v55.

author: silasfelinus
body:
Follow-up human gate for #1769 after Silas approved batch 001's voice direction and explicitly deferred Resources.

## What this is

`config/comment-calibration-batch-002.json` is a **publication-free GPT-5.6 Sol stress test**, not a hand-polished showcase. The prose was authored in the approval session with `humanPolish: NONE_BEFORE_REVIEW`.

This batch deliberately tests the two holes from the first calibration:

- **repeatability:** Maestro Clank (RICH), Marrow (THIN), and The Time-Office Agent (SPARSE) each appear twice on unrelated targets;
- **range:** comment lengths run from **9 to 75 words**, including genuine micro-reactions rather than making every character deliver a polished 30-50 word miniature essay.

It also keeps weak/noisy casting visible with explicit contrast directives instead of pretending lexical affinity solved those cases.

## Samples worth judging hardest

**Maestro Clank, Melodic Note, 9 words**
> Pianissimo. One note is enough. Do not improve it.

**Maestro Clank, Public Notary, 75 words**
> The stamp descends on the page in perfect common time: one blow, one witness, no encore. They ask you to say nothing, which is sensible; testimony ruins the acoustics. I would place the document on the second stand, not the first. The first is for scores that want to be heard. This one wants only the downbeat acknowledged. Mm. Raise the seal. Again. No, softer. The room is listening even if the record is not.

**The Time-Office Agent, Common, 9 words**
> The backward watch stayed quiet. I checked twice. Good.

That last one is the hardest SPARSE test: second appearance, unrelated low-signal Facet, and deliberately **no numbered-attempt tic**.

**Marrow, Always Online**
> Eleven tabs is too many pots on one stove. You stop tasting any of them. Close three. The world will still be there after the water boils.

## Contract added

`verifyCommentCalibrationBatch002.ts` is separate from the approved batch-001 verifier. It enforces:

- model/session provenance and no human polish before review;
- Reward + Facet only, with Resources still deferred;
- score recomputation through the existing ranker;
- archive draft ownership/tiering after the 706-row dedupe;
- the same banned review vocabulary and 8-word no-paraphrase check as batch 001;
- repeated speakers spanning RICH / THIN / SPARSE;
- novelty decay from actual prior appearances;
- at least one <=12-word micro-reaction and one >=60-word turn;
- multiple explicit contrast directives.

The Comment Migration workflow now runs both calibration contracts.

## Human gate

Please judge specifically:

1. Do Clank, Marrow, and the Time-Office Agent stay recognizably themselves across unrelated objects without merely repeating a tic?
2. Does the 9-to-75-word range feel healthier than batch 001's polished middle band?
3. Does the Time-Office Agent's second 9-word line still read as the same SPARSE-evidence character without the numbered-attempt construction?
4. Is the invisible house author less audible, or are too many lines still performing the same clever landing?
5. Which individual lines, if any, should be rejected or regenerated?

**Do not merge this PR on green checks alone.** This remains the subjective calibration gate before scale. No database write, persistence migration, or publication path is included.

## Change contract

Productize the proven Rust LOB Shadow soak as one installed command. Each run uses a candidate/run/market-scoped spool, bootstraps before observation, re-enters bounded bootstrap after transport resets, drains and independently verifies OSS triplets, synchronously cleans the units and transient environment overrides, and writes one receipt.

## Issue relationship

Refs #846

## Out of scope

No Collector parsing change, runtime execution, formal Gate, cutover, Live, or cleanup of historical shared Shadow spools.

## Dependencies and merge order

Depends on #848. Merge #848 first, then retarget this PR to main without changing its exact head diff.

## Focused validation

- `deployment/aliyun/test-rust-lob-shadow-soak.sh`
- `deployment/aliyun/test-rust-lob-control-plane.sh`
- Bash syntax and ShellCheck for the four owning shell files
- `git diff --check`

Counterexamples covered: stale post-reset health cannot clear recovery; a failure keeps its run-scoped spool; transient overrides are removed only after both Shadow primaries are inactive; hardcoded candidate or production identities are rejected by the contract test.

## Rollout and rollback

No runtime impact until a later exact release is installed. Rollback is the prior release bundle; the optional EnvironmentFile is absent outside the command and does not affect normal Shadow operation.

## Scope exception

The 1,149-line command is the already exercised fail-closed soak body moved from a temporary runtime script into one reviewable installed tool. Splitting health, cleanup, upload-only, and verifier stages would create partial tools that cannot safely run or roll back independently. Named reviewer approval is required before this draft becomes ready.

body:
Os títulos que ficam acima das molduras de upload e dos cards passam a 16px, e
voltam aos 24px do Figma a partir de 1600px — a mesma fronteira que devolve ao
grid o recuo de duas colunas. Vem de um token só, `--texto-subsecao`, no mesmo
formato da escada de margens: 16px por padrão, 24px num `min-width: 1600px`.

## O que muda

| Título | Onde |
|---|---|
| "Logo principal", "Logo cor única (preta)" / "(branca)" | `UploadArquivo` |
| "Ícone principal", "Ícone cor única (preta)" / "(branca)" | mesmo componente |
| "Outras variações" | Logo |
| "Adicionar tipografia secundária" | Tipografia |
| "Adicionados" | Elementos |
| Nomes de categoria ("Produto", "Retratos"…) | resumo da Fotografia |

## O que fica em 24px

O título principal de cada passo: "Paleta da Marca", "Tipografia da Marca",
"Tom de Voz", "Estilo de Fotografia", "Personalidade da Marca" e "Elementos
adicionais".

Em três arquivos o título principal e o subtítulo dividiam a mesma regra de CSS
(Tipografia, Elementos e Fotografia), então foram separados. Na Tipografia isso
pediu uma classe nova no JSX.

O campo de nome do `ModalCor` também usa `--texto-secao`, mas é um input, não um
título de seção — ficou como estava.

## Verificação

Percorrendo o fluxo inteiro e medindo o `font-size` computado de cada título
visível. A **1440px** os subtítulos saem em 16px e os principais em 24px; a
**1920px** tudo em 24px. A fronteira foi conferida nos dois lados: **1599px →
16px, 1600px → 24px**. O "Adicionados" só aparece com algum elemento na lista,
então entrou um upload de verdade no teste — 16px a 1440, 24px a 1920.
Screenshots nas duas larguras confirmam a hierarquia.

Uma nota sobre o próprio teste: a primeira versão rotulava os títulos por um
índice de passo presumido e saiu de sincronia depois do resumo da Fotografia,
pulando Personalidade e Elementos sem avisar. O rótulo passou a vir do topo da
própria tela, e aí os oito passos foram de fato lidos.

author: tmorrowdev
body:
## Description

Implements the token-system restructure from the "A token system you can white-label" proposal, for the `cre8-a2ui` brand.

`packages/cre8-wc/design-tokens/brands/cre8-a2ui/css/tokens_brand.css` shipped **491 flat declarations, 367 of them raw colour literals with zero `var()` references**. Rebranding meant a find-and-replace across the file, 152 tokens existed only to restate components on a dark surface, and dark mode had no path in at all.

The file is now tiered — **seed → primitive → semantic → component** — with each tier referencing only the one above it.

- **Rebranding is the seed block**: 11 declarations (`--cre8-seed-primary`, `-neutral`, `-success`, `-error`, `-warning`, `-accent`, `-font`, `-radius`, `-space`, `-font-size`, `-border-width`). Nothing else in the file is a literal.
- **Primitive ramps derive** from the seed with `oklch(from var(--cre8-seed-*) …)`.
- **Dark mode arrives**: `[data-mode="inverse"]` remaps 20 mode variables; `[data-mode="auto"]` follows `prefers-color-scheme`.
- **Theming can be scoped** to a subtree with `[data-cre8-theme]`.

**No visual change and no token removed.** All 491 legacy `--cre8-color-*` names are still declared as aliases, each resolving to the exact value it had before. None of the 161 component files that read them needed changes.

## Scope

- [ ] __Bug fix__ - non-breaking change which fixes an issue
- [x] __New feature__ - non-breaking change which adds functionality
- [ ] __Breaking change__ - fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change

Non-breaking for token consumers. It **does** raise the browser floor — see Additional Information.

## Quality Checks

- [ ] Resolves an issue - Github Issue and/or Jira story created; No duplicates
- [ ] Follows branch name convention
- [ ] Version updated per [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org) standard, if needed
- [x] Documentation - CSS comments, JS comments, Doc blocks
- [ ] Did you use CSS Logical Properties for your CSS? — n/a, custom properties only
- [ ] Create React wrapper — n/a, no new components
- [ ] Storybook WC, React — n/a, no new stories; Storybook picks the tokens up via `tokens_cre8-a2ui.module.ts`
- [x] Performed a self-guided visual regression test for each respective brand
- [x] Updated CHANGELOG
- [x] I've performed a self-review of my code
- [x] My code passes linting and code quality checks
- [x] New and existing tests pass with my code changes
- [x] My code builds without generating new errors/warnings

## Additional Information

### Verification

Every check ran against real computed values in headless Chrome, not hand-derived colour math.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| All 491 legacy tokens resolve identically (canvas-painted pixel compare, so `rgb()` vs `oklch()` formatting can't mask a difference) | **491/491 identical, 0 missing** |
| `tokens_cre8-a2ui.module.ts` defines the same token set as the CSS | **737/737 present** |
| `pnpm test` (cre8-wc) | **413/413 passing** |
| `pnpm run test:a2ui` (incl. the prepack parity gate) | **13/13 checks passing** |
| `tsc --noEmit` (cre8-studio) | **clean** |
| Whole-document mode, scoped mode, scoped rebrand | **all resolve correctly** |

### Two deviations from the proposal, both because testing showed it doesn't work as written

**1. The published `oklch` coefficients drift.** They give a worst ΔE of 0.042 against the shipped ramp — `#1D4ED8` renders as `#0C54BF`, visibly more saturated. Adding a per-step hue delta brings ΔE to exactly **0** across all six ramps, which is what makes this a zero-visual-change migration rather than a repaint.

**2. Component tokens did not follow the mode.** This is the significant one. A CSS custom property is substituted **where it is declared, not where it is read**. With the tiers on `:root`, a `[data-mode="inverse"]` block on a descendant changed the semantic tier while every button stayed pinned to its `:root` value — so the proposal's "no component token changes, so every component follows automatically" silently did nothing. Same root cause made a subtree reseed a no-op. Fixed by routing mode-dependent semantics through a `--cre8-mode-*` indirection and declaring the stack for `:root, [data-cre8-theme]`.

### Reviewer notes

- **Browser floor.** `oklch(from …)` requires **Chrome 119+ / Safari 16.4+ / Firefox 128+**. Below that the primitive ramps are invalid at parse time and colours fall back to unset. `cre8-studio`'s generated themes carry an `@supports`-gated static ramp; **the shipped brand file does not.** If the CDN build must support older engines, this needs a build-time-resolved fallback layer before merge.
- **Two consumers were updated because they would otherwise have broken silently.** `brand-theme.ts` parsed the token CSS and rewrote blue hexes — against a `var()`-based file that returns an empty `:root {}` with no error. It now emits the seed. `ramp.ts` previews the ramp as swatches while `brand-theme` applies it, so it now uses the same coefficients (verified to reproduce the shipped blue ramp exactly).
- **`tokens_cre8-a2ui.module.ts` is a second copy** of the brand block that Storybook imports rather than the CSS; regenerated to match. Worth confirming there is no generator upstream of it that would overwrite this.
- **The seed is 11 values, not the proposal's 8** — plus `accent` (used by `link:visited`) and two scale seeds the proposal didn't account for.
- **Anchor step tradeoff.** `--cre8-primary-500` is the seed verbatim so an integrator's brand colour appears in its own ramp. For an extreme seed the ramp is non-monotonic around that step.
- **Deliberately out of scope:** the other 9 brands still ship flat token files (unaffected — tier 3 exposes the same names), and the `--cre8-color-*` → `--cre8-*` rename still needs a codemod across component styles. The typography layer still reads `--cre8-font-families-inter`, which now aliases `--cre8-font-family-base`.
- One test changed: `checkbox-field-item.test.ts` asserted the literal string `--cre8-border-radius-checkbox: 4px;`. The value is now derived; the test asserts the derivation *and* that it resolves to 4px at the shipped seed.

body:
## Outcome

This draft publishes a representative, backend-free CON website for human
review. It expands the accepted full-content migration with repeatable Zotero
API ingestion, a GitHub Pages project preview, and a credential-free SHACL Vue
editing handoff that downloads an RDF review bundle.

This is not a production cutover. It does not change DNS, add a custom domain,
run a persistent metadata service, write to Zotero, or put a GitHub credential
in the browser.

## Review the preview

- [Homepage](https://con.github.io/orinoco-lite-dev/)
- [People](https://con.github.io/orinoco-lite-dev/whoweare/)
- [Projects](https://con.github.io/orinoco-lite-dev/projects/)
- [Publications](https://con.github.io/orinoco-lite-dev/publications/)
- [Engage](https://con.github.io/orinoco-lite-dev/engage/)
- [Yaroslav Halchenko](https://con.github.io/orinoco-lite-dev/persons/yaroslav-halchenko/)
- [DataLad](https://con.github.io/orinoco-lite-dev/projects/datalad/)
- [DataLad JOSS publication](https://con.github.io/orinoco-lite-dev/publications/datalad-joss-2021/)
- [Static editor](https://con.github.io/orinoco-lite-dev/edit/)

The editor loads static, digest-bound records and shapes. Saving changes only
updates its in-memory review queue; downloading creates a review bundle for the
checked-in local validation helper. No browser write request or authentication
flow is involved.

## What is included

- 186 canonical records and 13 reference records;
- 126 publications from public Zotero group `6197458`, library version 451;
- 186 graph nodes, 467 native relationship edges, and 185 record pages;
- restored CON people, projects, editorial content, branding, and reviewed
  assets;
- deterministic root and project-path static builds;
- a production dependency audit with zero findings; and
- exactly one parent PR, with no component-repository PRs.

The site is pinned at
`26907c487efaa2c31bba9d02398aa201ab6f774b`. Zotero ingestion, the pool UI
wrapper, and nested SHACL Vue are pinned respectively at `062da59c`,
`93961ace`, and `3be33196`.

## Acceptance evidence

- [Milestone 3 acceptance report](https://github.com/con/orinoco-lite-dev/blob/codex/milestone-3/docs/milestone-3-acceptance.md)
- [Decision register](https://github.com/con/orinoco-lite-dev/blob/codex/milestone-3/docs/milestone-3-decisions.md)
- [Static editor contract](https://github.com/con/orinoco-lite-dev/blob/codex/milestone-3/docs/milestone-3-editor.md)
- [Dependency review](https://github.com/con/orinoco-lite-dev/blob/codex/milestone-3/docs/milestone-3-dependencies.md)
- [Exact-head branch build and Pages deployment](https://github.com/con/orinoco-lite-dev/actions/runs/31558932625)
- [Exact-head pull-request build](https://github.com/con/orinoco-lite-dev/actions/runs/31558935096)

The release gate runs 106 parent tests, builds the 144-file editor twice,
builds the 444-file Pages artifact twice, and exercises the project-path editor
in Chromium. The static artifact contains no Quicklink prefetcher and no
platform-dependent Hugo image derivatives. Engage loads preview images and
keeps the preserved print-resolution artwork behind explicit links.

## Human review requested

Please review the content and the open questions in the decision register,
especially creator identity, duplicate publications, venue and topic modeling,
supporting-person visibility, asset custody, the patch contribution repository,
the two-repository content/gitlink boundary, Pages reviewers, the external
Roboto font, and the four development-only VitePress advisories.

Known bounded debt is listed in the acceptance report. The safe defaults remain
fail-closed; the preview does not silently promote unresolved source evidence.

## After review or merge

- remove the temporary `codex/milestone-3` Pages push trigger and environment
  branch policy once `main` is the publication branch;
- retain the named clean-migration checkpoints used by reproducibility checks;
- keep hosted authentication and automatic pull-request creation deferred until
  a separate authorization and trust-boundary design; and
- treat production-domain cutover as a separate human decision.

author: sebailla
body:
Closes #5

## Summary

Wires the cascade endpoints from `openspec/specs/taxonomy-hierarchy`
so the frontend can walk Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family →
Genus → Species by appending one path segment per rank. The leaf
`/species` endpoint ships in this slice so the cascade UI's sixth
scrolling panel has real data to render.

## Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `taxon/api/router.py` | Replace `/api/_meta` placeholder with 7 cascade endpoints + smoke probe |
| `taxon/api/hierarchy.py` | New: path-name resolver with case-insensitive, parent-anchored lookup |
| `taxon/api/db.py` | New: FastAPI `Depends` factory for request-scoped sessions |
| `taxon/api/errors.py` | New: extract HTTP error classes to break the router → api circular import |
| `taxon/api/__init__.py` | Re-export errors + AppState so existing callers keep working |
| `taxon/tests/test_api_hierarchy.py` | New: 18 RED-first contract tests covering all 7 endpoints |

## Endpoint matrix

```
GET /api/kingdoms
GET /api/{kingdom}/phyla
GET /api/{kingdom}/{phylum}/classes
GET /api/{kingdom}/{phylum}/{class}/orders
GET /api/{kingdom}/{phylum}/{class}/{order}/families
GET /api/{kingdom}/{phylum}/{class}/{order}/{family}/genera
GET /api/{kingdom}/{phylum}/{class}/{order}/{family}/{genus}/species
```

## Design notes

- The first segment matches by `rank == 'kingdom'` (not `parent_id IS
  NULL`) because WoRMS attaches a Biota superdomain above every
  kingdom and the cascade UI starts at Kingdom, not at the
  superdomain. Subsequent segments anchor on the previous match's id.
- A 404 is returned when any segment fails to resolve; the error body
  identifies the failing segment so the cascade UI can highlight the
  dropdown that produced the bad path.
- Empty children produce an empty list with status 200, never 404 —
  the cascade UI treats "no results" and "rank does not exist" the
  same way.
- `display_name` is preserved verbatim including author citations and
  the rank suffix the parser appends.

## Out of scope (Sub-PR 2C)

- 409 ambiguity candidate responses (`candidates[]` with breadcrumbs).
- Inclusion filters on the species list (`include=extinct`, etc.).
- Per-species search-links endpoint.
- Pagination cursors on long species lists.

## Test plan

- [x] 18 new RED-first contract tests cover the spec
- [x] All 43 tests pass (25 pre-existing + 18 new)
- [x] `mypy --strict` clean on 18 source files
- [x] `ruff check` clean
- [x] `ruff format --check` clean

## Contributor checklist

- [x] Linked an approved issue (#5)
- [x] PR opened against `develop` (never `main`)
- [x] Conventional commit format (3 commits: refactor + test + feat)
- [x] No `Co-Authored-By` trailers
- [x] No regression on Sub-PR 2A endpoints

author: ossabellator
body:
## Finding

Container checks explicitly bound `/tmp`, memory, pids, CPU, workspace access, and the root filesystem, but did not pass Docker `--shm-size`. Docker's daemon has a configurable `--default-shm-size`, so `/dev/shm` could silently vary with operator daemon configuration.

Closes #322.

## Fix

Pass `--shm-size 64m` for every container check. This preserves Docker's common default for compatibility while making the writable shared-memory mount part of E2H's explicit runtime contract instead of a daemon default.

The existing cgroup memory limit remains the aggregate memory ceiling; `/tmp` remains separately bounded by the capsule's `tmpfs_mb` policy.

## Regression coverage

A focused argv regression verifies exactly one `--shm-size 64m` flag while preserving the default `--memory 512m` and `/tmp:...size=64m` controls.

## Validation without GitHub Actions

No GitHub Actions are required. The branch is 0 behind `main` and changes only `src/e2h/sandbox.py` (3 additions) plus one focused test file.
