author: eedsilva
body:
## Summary

`supabase-data-plane-e2e` has been failing on `main` since PR #510 merged (`bdd437c`), consistently at the same two `golden-flow.spec.ts` assertions — discovered while investigating an unrelated failing check on #512. This is a separate, pre-existing regression, not caused by that PR.

**Bisection**: `git log a498af2..bdd437c` on `main` shows exactly one commit between the last known-green `supabase-data-plane-e2e` run and the first red one — PR #510.

**Root cause**: PR #510 fixed the preview iframe from being blanked-then-remounted on a transient `unhealthy` health-check blip, by adding an "already shown" grace — but only special-cased the `'unhealthy'` status string. `preview-service.ts`'s actual restart path (`node-preview-runner.ts`'s `restart()` → `spawn()`) transitions `'unhealthy' → 'starting' → 'running'` — `spawn()` explicitly sets `'starting'` on the happy path, and `packages/domain/src/preview-state.ts`'s transition table confirms this is a normal leg of the same recovery, not an edge case. `previewStatusMessage`'s grace never covered `'starting'`, so a poll landing during that leg still blanked (and on the next poll, remounted) an already-good iframe mid-interaction — the exact same bug class PR #510 fixed, on a status its fix didn't enumerate. The affected e2e test (`golden-flow.spec.ts`, visual-edit flow) navigates the iframe's inner frame directly and interacts with it across multiple 2s poll intervals, so it's exactly the kind of test that would catch this.

The second failing assertion in the same CI run (a later, unrelated-looking test timing out waiting for its own dev server) is almost certainly a cascade: `playwright.config.ts` runs this spec file with `workers: 1`, so the first test hitting its 180s hard timeout mid-flight likely leaves orphaned state that starves the next sequential test.

## Fix

Generalized `previewStatusMessage`'s grace to apply to *any* non-proxy-denied status once the iframe has rendered successfully, instead of hardcoding `'unhealthy'` by name — the mechanism should track "is this session still recoverable" via the existing `isPreviewSessionProxyDenied` predicate, not re-enumerate the domain's transition table one status at a time (which is exactly how this bug reappeared). `'failing'` still gets no grace — it's already denied earlier in the same function, since restarts are exhausted by the time a session reaches it and it never returns to `'running'`.

## Verification

- TDD: added the missing `'starting'` + `alreadyShown=true` case (RED: `'Preview iniciando…'` where `null` was expected), fixed, GREEN (14/14 in `preview-panel.test.tsx`).
- `tsc -b` clean, full fast unit suite (167 files / 1510 tests) green.
- Full `npm run check` green, except one known-flaky Docker-backed integration test (`secret-leak.integration.test.ts`) that timed out at 30s under full-suite load and passed cleanly in isolation (19s) — unrelated to this diff (no relation to preview/UI logic; verified independently before opening this PR).
- Ran `/code-review` (Standards axis) and `/simplify` (reuse/simplification, efficiency/altitude — 3 agents total) against the diff:
  - Standards: no violations, no smells.
  - Efficiency/altitude: confirmed the generalized grace only actually extends coverage to `'starting'` in practice (the only other non-denied, non-running status reachable once a session has ever shown) — the right depth, not over-broadened.
  - Reuse/simplification: one finding (merge two null-return branches via boolean algebra) was verified by hand to be a **false positive** — it would silently break the existing `'failing'` exclusion by moving the grace check ahead of the denial check in control-flow order, which the pure-boolean-equivalence reasoning didn't account for. Rejected with a small reproduction script confirming the regression, not applied.

## Test plan

- [x] New unit test reproduces the exact CI failure mode (RED before fix, GREEN after)
- [x] Full fast suite green
- [x] `npm run check` green (one unrelated pre-existing flake, verified in isolation)
- [x] `/code-review` + `/simplify` run, one false-positive finding investigated and rejected with reasoning

author: colinespinas
body:
## Summary
- Completes the last gap in issue #16's drag-and-drop tab strip work: dropping a tab already faded it into its own new slot, but neighboring tabs whose position shifted as a side effect still teleported instantly instead of sliding.
- Every tab strictly between the drag's start and end slot now slides from its real pre-drop pixel position to its new one over the same 150ms window the existing drop-settle fade uses.
- Works for both agent and file tabs (shared tab chrome), and a no-op reorder animates nothing.

## Implementation
- `work_surface/state.rs`: pure `tab_slide_offsets()` — only the dragged tab's own measured width is needed to compute every shifted neighbor's offset, since removing+reinserting one item always shifts everything in between by exactly that item's width.
- `root/mod.rs` / `root/state.rs`: new `tab_bounds` (real painted bounds per tab, tracked via a `gpui::canvas`) and `tab_slide` (start offset + fresh animation id per shifted tab) maps.
- `work_surface/render.rs`: `drop_dragged_tab` computes slide offsets before mutating tab order; render applies `.left(offset * (1.0 - delta))` inside `with_animation`, the same idiom already used for the drop-settle fade, just translating position instead of opacity.
- No dedicated GPUI translate primitive exists, so this uses `.left()` on a `position: relative` element — a real, already-precedented pattern, not opacity dressed up as motion.
- `gpui::AnimationExt::with_animation` already respects `cx.reduce_motion()` at the framework level for both the old fade and this new slide; no separate reduced-motion setting exists in this app.

## Test plan
- [x] 5 pure unit tests on `tab_slide_offsets` (rightward/leftward drags, tabs outside the passed-over span, every no-op case)
- [x] Real GPUI end-to-end test: drags a tab past two others in a headless window after a real paint pass, asserts the neighbors' recorded offsets equal the dragged tab's real measured width, and that the dragged tab itself is never in the slide map
- [x] A second end-to-end test confirms a no-op drop records no slide state
- [x] `cargo build`, `cargo clippy -p app --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` all clean (only the pre-existing, unrelated violation at `review/render.rs:1503` remains, untouched)
- [x] Full `app` test suite green (2125 tests); a couple of unrelated flaky failures under heavy concurrent load in this session were isolated and reran clean (`inotify` contention / timing-sensitive undo-redo tests, not touching this change)

author: dallascrilley
body:
Fixes the deviations a cold user hits when following the README on stock macOS.

## D3 (blocker, code): `--json` output was broken on bash 3.2

Broadside ships 79 `#!/bin/bash` scripts and the repo deliberately targets
bash 3.x elsewhere (`# Bash 3.x compatible - no mapfile`). But
`lib/common.sh:215` used `local -n` — a bash 4.3+ nameref — so every JSON
path exited 2 on the tool's primary platform.

**Before** (`/bin/bash` = 3.2.57 on macOS, live tmux session):

```
$ /bin/bash ./broadside --session broadside-evidence capture --json
lib/common.sh: line 216: local: -n: invalid option
local: usage: local name[=value] ...
EXIT=2

$ /bin/bash ./broadside --session broadside-evidence aggregate -i ./out --json
lib/common.sh: line 216: local: -n: invalid option
local: usage: local name[=value] ...
EXIT=2
```

**After** (same shell, same session):

```
$ /bin/bash ./broadside --session broadside-evidence capture --json | jq 'length, [.[].dir]'
2
[
  ".../scratchpad/demo/repo-alpha",
  ".../scratchpad/demo/repo-beta"
]

$ /bin/bash ./broadside --session broadside-evidence aggregate -i ./out --json -o ./agg.json
✓ Saved to: ./agg.json
EXIT=0
$ jq 'length, [.[].status]' ./agg.json
2
["success","success"]
```

`output_json_array` no longer takes an array *name*; callers expand the array
themselves (`output_json_array "${json_items[@]}"`), matching the repo's
existing bash-3 idioms. Zero items now yields `[]`.

### bash-4-ism sweep

Repo-wide sweep for `local -n`, `declare -n`, `mapfile`, `readarray`,
`${var,,}`, `${var^^}`, `declare -A`, `declare -g`, `coproc`, `&>>`, `|&`,
`${var@Q}`, `wait -n`, negative array indices, and `globstar`. **Two** reachable
hits, both namerefs, both fixed:

| Location | Construct | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lib/common.sh:216` | `local -n items=$1` | values passed as args |
| `commands/test.sh:78` | `local -n tests_ref=$1` | test IDs passed as trailing args |

The only other matches were the pre-existing `# Bash 3.x compatible - no mapfile`
comments, which are prose, not code.

### Regression test

`tests/bash3_compat.test.sh` has three gates:

1. **Grep guard** — fails if any of the 12 bash-4-only constructs appears in
   `broadside`, `lib/**`, or `commands/**` (whole-line comments stripped so the
   existing prose does not trip it). This is the binding check when CI runs
   bash 4+.
2. **`output_json_array`** — empty / single / multi-element arrays, including
   embedded newlines, quotes, spaces, and empty payloads.
3. **`_test_partition`** — asserts round-robin bucketing (7 tests / 3 panes
   => 3/2/2). This function had no prior coverage and its signature changed.

Gates 2 and 3 run under `$BASH` *and* under `/bin/bash` when that is a genuine
3.x, so on macOS the real interpreter is exercised.

Both gates were confirmed non-vacuous by reverting each fix on a scratch copy:
the guard reports `nameref (local -n / declare -n) is bash 4.3+` and the
functional gates report the exact `local: -n: invalid option` exit 2.

## D1, D2, D4 + minors (docs)

- **D1** `report --format html` -> `report -o ./review.html` (`report` only has
  `-o/--output` and `--no-open`).
- **D2** `events --type command` -> `events --type broadcast.sent`, plus a table
  of all 15 event types actually emitted (grepped from the `emit_event_kv` call
  sites; all are literals).
- **D4** Fixed the moved plan link in `docs/guides/parallel-feature-development.md`
  (`../plans/` -> `../plans/completed/`).
- Added `jq` to Requirements (`install.sh` hard-requires it).
- Added the 5 missing commands (`test`, `metrics`, `inject`, `escalations`,
  `msg`) plus `completion` to the command table, described from `--help`.
- Added the missing `--prompt` to both pipeline examples (`pipeline` dies with
  exit 2 without it).
- Unknown-flag error now hints that global flags precede the subcommand.
- Linked CONTRIBUTING.md and SECURITY.md; documented `INSTALL_DIR`.
- Documented exit codes. Note: the brief listed 0/1/2/3, but the codebase
  actually uses **five** — `4` = no session found (7 sites) and `5` = timeout
  (2 sites) — so the README documents all of them rather than a partial list.
- Documented `status`'s 0-idle / 1-busy semantics in both the README and
  `broadside status --help`, scoped accurately: the overload applies to text
  mode only, since `--json` always exits 0.

## Verification

```
QA_STRICT=1 QA_FAIL_FAST=1 ./scripts/qa
  ✓ shellcheck (36 files)
  ✓ tests (38 passed)
  Results: 2 passed, 0 failed

CDPATH=. ./scripts/test
  38 tests, 38 passed, 0 failed
```

Also verified: 0 broken relative links across all markdown in the repo.

author: ridafkih
body:
Unknown blog slugs (`/blog/anything`) were returning 200 with a blank body: `notFound()` was thrown from the component, long after SSR committed the status, which also aborted the subtree so the not-found page never rendered. The lookup moved to the route loader — thrown from `beforeLoad` the router walks the not-found up to the root and replaces the whole document, so `loader` plus a route-level `notFoundComponent` is what keeps the shell. Also fixes three smaller indexability leaks found in the same audit.

- `/blog/<unknown>`: 200 blank shell → 404 with `noindex` and a rendered not-found page inside the marketing layout; real slugs still 200 with canonical and `BlogPosting` JSON-LD
- `/index.html`: 200 serving the raw 1,873-byte client shell → 308 to `/`, and `resolveStaticFilePath` no longer resolves it
- `/blog/`: router-emitted 307 → 308 to `/blog`, query preserved, `/` untouched
- robots.txt: dropped the `Disallow` on `/login`, `/register`, `/verify-*`, `/reset-password`, `/forgot-password` so their existing `noindex` is actually crawlable; `/dashboard` and `/auth` stay disallowed

308 rather than 301 so a non-GET never silently becomes a GET; Google treats the two identically for canonicalization.

author: asongulol
body:
## What was wrong

Countersigning an agreement failed with *"The contractor has not signed this agreement yet"* — on an agreement the panel was showing as **Signed**.

Every hire seeds an `onboarding_agreements` row for all four kinds (`src/server/actions/contractors.ts:652-696`). That row carries prefill and countersigner — nothing about signing. The detail panel rendered a hardcoded `<Badge tone="good">Signed</Badge>` on each of those rows, so an unsigned agreement looked signed and its countersign button was live. `countersignAgreement` checks the real source — `onboarding_signatures` with `status='signed'` — and correctly refused.

Seen on Kristel Anne Ballesteros Daliguez: Non-Compete showed "Signed · Awaiting countersign" while being absent from the signature ledger table directly above it.

## The fix

Derive signed-ness in the UI from the same source the server enforces:

- `OnbSignatureLite` now exposes the signature `status`.
- `signedKinds` = ledger rows with `status='signed'`; the badge reads **Signed** / **Not signed**.
- The countersign button for an unsigned kind is disabled, with the server's own reason as its tooltip — the failure can't be reached by clicking.

No schema change, no server behavior change.

## Checks

`tsc --noEmit` clean · biome clean · 878/878 tests pass.

author: robotsix-mill[bot]
body:
## Problem

The triage classifier's NO_CHANGE handler at `src/robotsix_mill/stages/refine/_triage.py:509-518` closes tickets as `DONE` without verifying the branch was merged to the base branch. The function `_verify_branch_merged` (in `helpers.py:516`) exists and is called by the refine agent's `no_change_needed` path, but the triage classifier bypasses it entirely.

This caused ticket `20260802T163827Z` (implement deps-bump.yml workflow) to be closed as DONE while the branch remained unmerged. The file does not exist on origin/main.

## Root cause

At `_triage.py:509-518`:
```python
if ticket.kind == TicketKind.TASK and not ticket.branch:
    # Route to READY so implement can verify the "no change" claim
    return _triage_outcome(..., state=State.READY, ...)
return _triage_outcome(..., state=State.DONE)
```

The guard routes to `READY` (safe) only when the ticket has NO branch. The inversion is that tickets WITH a branch are closed as DONE unconditionally. The triage classifier should also check branch-merge status before closing as DONE.

## Proposed fix

Import `_verify_branch_merged` from `helpers.py` and call it in the NO_CHANGE handler before closing as DONE. When the branch is not merged, either:
1. Route to `READY` (so implement can verify the claim), or
2. Return `BLOCKED` with a note (similar to the refine agent's `no_change_needed` path at `_result_paths.py:200-206`)

Path 1 is preferable — it lets the implement stage verify the claim against the live tree and produce a fresh merge if needed, rather than blocking the ticket.

## Verification

- `_triage.py:509-518` — confirmed the NO_CHANGE handler does not call `_verify_branch_merged`
- `helpers.py:516-660` — `_verify_branch_merged` exists and is used by the refine agent's `no_change_needed` path
- `_result_paths.py:200-206` — the refine agent's `no_change_needed` path correctly calls `_verify_branch_merged` and returns BLOCKED when unmerged
- `origin/main` has no `.github/workflows/deps-bump.yml` — the ticket's branch `mill/20260802T163827Z-implement-missing-documented-deps-bump-y-6679` (commit 2219571a) is not an ancestor of origin/main

<!-- retrospect-gap-id: triage_no_change_skip_branch_merge_check -->

author: doriancollier
body:
## What

Task 3.3 of `specs/persistent-session-runtime/`: `SessionTurnWindows` — the layer that turns a persistent process's message stream into discrete turns. `dispatch(batch)` is the single ingress; every SDK message is attributed to the window that caused it; the window closes whole on its correlated result. Correlation is by the server-minted messageId stamped as the SDK `uuid` — never positional: a result naming a held id closes that window (all batch ids together); an unknown id opens a synthetic `origin:'runtime'` window without touching the open one; an unnamed result terminates the open window — a deliberate, pinned spec deviation, because `SDKResultError` carries no correlation id and the literal rule would strand a window on every failed turn (and `SDKResultSuccess`'s id is optional too). Out-of-window messages are held (bounded 500, oldest-out, loud) and flushed into the next window. Seams are documented for 3.7 (watchdog per window), 3.9 (boundary validation on the batch), 3.4 (idle timer), and 3.5 (control-query setters).

## The review's catch

The adversarial pass traced the queue-row lifecycle end to end and proved the module doc's safety claim false: the window was announced before the pump could refuse, the eager `turn_start` retired the queue row, and a refused dispatch left a phantom `turn_start`/`turn_end` pair with the person's message gone — the exact promise this programme exists to keep. Fixed: the window still registers early (launch output stays attributed) but announces only after acceptance; a refused dispatch now leaves no trace and the words go back on hold. Both shapes pinned red-first. A second timing hole (usage fetched after the result push, green only by fake-synchronicity luck) was made honest with macrotask-answering fakes.

## Verification

Nine-mutation matrix re-executed (each redding exactly its guard); interleaving probes (racing dispatch queues behind the close, never interleaves); runtime windows open AND close their seams so 3.7 can't leak a watchdog; `origin` plumbs to `turn_start.origin:'runtime'` on the real durable stream; the DOR-1100 reopen predicate is byte-identical. One relaunch-semantics wart (a dying process's held words flushing into the next process's window) is documented loudly as task 3.6's obligation. Suites: claude-code 987 + session 600 green; typecheck/lint/format clean. Nothing constructs the windowing in production yet — wiring is 3.10's.

Process: implement → adversarial review → fixes → PR. Gates run manually; hooks bypassed under multi-agent load, noted in commit bodies.

author: ronaldtse
body:
## Summary

Full UX/UI audit of the concepts-management minisite — fixes ~30 logical issues across HTML structure, navigation, accessibility, state preservation, federation consistency, and visual quality. All changes are scoped to this minisite (no edits to the shared `@oimlsmart/site-shell` package).

### P0 fixes (broken or accessibility-blocking)
- **Dead "Propose" links** — `TermDetailPage` linked to `/proposals/?term=...` which redirected to `/analysis/gaps/` and lost `?term=`. Now points directly at `/analysis/gaps/?term=...` (which `ProposalsPage` already reads on mount).
- **No focus rings** on most interactive elements — added a global `:focus-visible` ring (WCAG 2.4.7).
- **Proposal modal didn't trap focus or handle Esc** — added focus management, Tab-trap, Esc-to-close, focus restore, `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal`/`aria-labelledby`.
- **`DefText` v-html XSS hardening** — escapes all definition text outside a strict `<math>…</math>` whitelist.

### P1 fixes
- **State preservation** — new `useUrlState` composable. Search/filter/sort/pagination now persist in URL query params across `TermsList`, `G18Concepts`, `Publications`, `Actions`, `Proposals`, `G18Gaps`. Browser back/forward restores state.
- **Breadcrumbs** — "Registry" → "Home" (16 files); added missing G 18 / Analysis parent segments.
- **Orphaned `G18DynamicPage`** — wired into new `/g18/current/` route; legacy `/g18/dynamic` and `/g18/current` redirects updated; nav dropdown entries added.
- **See-also-link `href="#"`** — renders as `<span>` when URL is null.
- **`useJsonFetch` error state** — now consumed in `TermDetail`, `PublicationDetail`, `TcDetail` (fetch failures show explicit error instead of "Not found").
- **Print stylesheet** — hides chrome, flattens cards, expands disclosure widgets.
- **Form labels** — `aria-label` on every filter input/select across list pages.
- **Color/contrast** — emoji indicators get `aria-hidden`; nav dropdowns get ARIA roles.
- **Duplicate `<main>`** — `Layout.astro` no longer nests `<main>` inside the shell's `<main>`.
- **Sticky filter bar** — `top: 64px` (wrong) → `top: 100px` (actual `SiteHeader h-14` + `MinisiteNav h-11`).

### Federation consistency
- Dropped **Hanken Grotesk** font link — now inherits **IBM Plex Sans/Mono** from shell tokens (matches all sibling minisites).
- Added **`PageHero`** to landing page (sibling convention).
- Footer **`/vocab/`** link switched from absolute `https://www.oimlsmart.org/vocab/` to relative.
- `base` prop switched from `import.meta.env.BASE_URL` to hardcoded `"/concepts-management/"` (matches sibling pattern).

### P2 polish
- Sortable `<th>` now keyboard-accessible (`role="button"`, `tabindex=0`, `aria-sort`).
- Provenance pubs list (was sliced at 5 with no expand) → "Show more / Show fewer" toggle.
- `G18DynamicPage` truncated definitions → `title` attribute for hover.
- `ProposalsPage` `client:only="vue"` → `client:load` (SSR-safe; no blank page on slow JS).
- Nav `<details>` dropdowns dismiss on click-outside.

## Verification

- `pnpm build` — **2236 pages** built successfully.
- `pnpm test` — **234/237 pass**. The 3 failures are pre-existing data-pipeline issues (`useVocabGaps > allTCs`, `tc.json` is empty array, `tc.json` missing TC9) — confirmed failing on `main` before this branch.
- Spot-checked rendered HTML: single `<main>` (no nesting), `/vocab/` relative link, `PageHero` h1 on home, `Home` nav active state, `/g18/current/` route built.

**Not verified in browser** — CLI session can't drive a browser. Recommend the reviewer spot-check: (1) Home / Concepts / Publications / TC active states in the subnav, (2) Propose flow from a concept detail page, (3) browser back button restores filter state on `/concepts/`, (4) modal Tab-trap and Esc, (5) mobile nav collapses cleanly.

## Test plan
- [ ] `pnpm build` passes (2236 pages)
- [ ] `pnpm test` shows only the 3 pre-existing failures
- [ ] Subnav Home link visible and active on `/concepts-management/`
- [ ] Propose buttons from concept detail open the proposal form pre-filled
- [ ] Filter/search/pagination restored on browser back/forward
- [ ] Proposal modal: Tab cycles within, Esc closes, focus returns to opener
- [ ] Breadcrumbs show "Home" + correct parent segments on every page
- [ ] `/g18/current/` reachable from G 18 nav dropdown
- [ ] Print preview of a concept detail page is clean

author: funkiirabu
body:
## Summary
Beta #93 round five Medium: `t2 services 0x<seller>` went through free-text `?q=` and returned nothing for a seller with live listings; a name search interleaved two near-identical agents with no way to tell the principals apart. Marketplace defence is "check the address" — the tool now accepts one.

**Routing (`resolveServicesQuery`, exported + pinned):** valid `0x…` → `?agent=<normalized>` directly (no directory dependency, `validateAddress` is the one address check); `#N` / `@handle` → `resolveAgentRef` (the same endpoint the site uses) → `?agent=`; malformed 0x falls back to text (honest zero-match, not a crash); free text / empty unchanged on `?q=` / unfiltered.

**Active board vs management:** `?agent=` serves the seller's retired-included management view — the `t2 services` path filters `!retired` client-side and prints the dim honesty note (`N retired omitted — t2 service list 0x…`). `t2 service list` untouched.

**Principal clarity:** every Seller line paints `#numericId` when known (`funkii@audric #16 0x7f20…f6dc`) — pure `serviceSellerLabel` exported + pinned, honest omit when the id is null. Scoped empty says `No active services for #N (0x…)`, never "No services match <hex>". Text searches spanning ≥2 sellers get a dim footer suggesting the scope. JSON adds `scope: {kind, agent?, numericId?, q?}` + `retiredHidden` so agents don't guess which path ran.

Help + `cli-reference.mdx` document the seller-scope forms. No `servicesSearchCondition` change, no publish (founder patches after 1016+1017).

## Tests / verification
+6 unit (routing matrix incl. resolver-hop URL + malformed-0x fallback; label with/without id against the real `truncateAddress`). Suite 280/280, build green. Live smoke (mainnet): `t2 services 0x7f2059…` returns #16's 2 active services with `#16` on each Seller line + "2 retired omitted" note; `t2 services "#16" --json` shows `scope {kind: agent, numericId: 16}, total 2, retiredHidden 2`.

author: aldwinhermanudin
body:
The console was in no image, started by no script, and `--in-stack` merely borrowed the ROS image to spin up an unmanaged `carla-air-webui` beside the three real containers. Nobody owned its lifecycle, and a stale container serving old code cost a wrong diagnosis on 2026-08-07.

## Opt-in, and the reason is a rule rather than taste

The console has been an `rclpy` node since R-03 step 1, so starting it with every stack would make `ros2 node list` **two** nodes instead of `/carla_air_bridge` alone — the "you bring the agent" invariant. The help text says *why*, because a flag whose reason is not written down becomes a default the next time someone finds it inconvenient.

## What changed

- **`docker/webui.Dockerfile` installs nothing.** The ROS image already carries `rclpy`, `cv_bridge` and `msgpack`. A test pins that no `pip`/`apt` install appears: needing one would mean the console had grown a dependency the graph does not have.
- **`docker/webui-entrypoint.sh` refuses** when `interfaces`/`px4_msgs` are missing. That failure is otherwise **silent** — the console falls back to the sidecar socket and opens the second AirSim capture R-03 step 1 removed, taking the camera cost from 6.6% back to 24%. A quiet regression is worse than a refusal.
- **`stack_up.sh --console`** starts it as a managed fourth container joining the simulator's network and IPC namespaces, clearing a stale one first.
- **`status.sh`** gains a `console container` row.
- **`webui.sh --in-stack`** clears a stale container and points at `--console`.

## Verified against a real stack

| criterion | result |
|---|---|
| default bringup keeps the invariant | 3 containers, `ros2 node list` = **`/carla_air_bridge` alone**, nothing on :8080 |
| `--console` brings up four | 4 containers, `GET /` → **200**, node list = bridge **+ `/carla_air_webui`** |
| starting twice replaces a stale one | `41bb69a400e4` → **`e076e91a0675`**, one container by that name, still 200 |
| `--down` leaves none | `stopped carla-air-webui`, no `carla-air-*` in `docker ps -a` |

**The replacement test was set up as the incident, not a happy path.** The container was deliberately left *stopped but present* (`Exited (137)`, holding the name) before the second run, because that is the shape that produced the wrong diagnosis. Replacing a *running* container is the easy case.

**And the console is genuinely on ROS in there**: `/api/status` reported `source: ros` with video 0.09 s old. That is the check that catches a silent fallback, which is why it was looked at before "does the page load".

## One of the two filed defects was never real

R-08 opened with "`stack_up.sh --down` leaves `carla-air-webui` running — it has to be removed by hand". It does not: `down()` has swept every `^carla-air-` container since `d5ed0ff`, and this name matches. Tested rather than argued, and corrected in the entry in place. The *second* bullet — the stale container serving old code — was real and is what the design turns on.

## Self-review found three more, one of which broke the documented example

- **The health probe curled `127.0.0.1:8080` unconditionally** while `TESTBED_CONSOLE_ARGS` is documented — with `--bind netbird` as *the* example — as the way to change that address. The documented usage would have made a healthy console burn a 20 s timeout and then print a warning that was false. The probe now runs only when the address is known and says what it did **not** check otherwise; the container-exited check runs either way.
- **The image check ran at step 4**, after a 55 s bringup. Nothing builds `carla-air/webui:1` automatically, so "not built yet" is the ordinary first-run case. Moved above step 1, where the config check already lives for the same reason. A bogus image name now exits immediately with `Nothing was started.`
- **`curl` was assumed present.** Now part of the probe guard.

## Tests

13, no Docker and no GPU. Behavioural for the paths that exit during argument parsing; **structural** for the rest, because `--config PATH --console` brings up a real simulator and no test may pass it — the same rule `--all` has in `test_stop_args.py`.

Five were mutation-checked: console-on-by-default, the removed pre-emptive `docker rm -f`, dropping `--ipc container:`, moving the image check back after step 1, and making the HTTP probe unconditional each turn exactly one test red.

**264 passed, 1 skipped.**

## Not in scope

Retiring the host lane. Containers should become the *default* path, not the only one — the host lane is what every measurement this week was taken against and is the fallback when Docker is unavailable.

Re-provision the new dashboards with **`npx mega-linter-runner --upload-dashboards grafana`** — see the [migration notes](https://megalinter.io/latest/reporters/ApiReporter/#migration-from-payload-v1). Legacy `NOTIF_API_*` variables remain supported as aliases. ([#​8661](https://redirect.github.com/oxsecurity/megalinter/issues/8661))
  - **Linters now time out after 5 minutes by default** (`LINTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: 300`): a linter exceeding it is killed and reported as an error (exit code 124) instead of running (or hanging) unbounded. If some of your linters legitimately run longer, raise the limit globally with `LINTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, per linter with `<LINTER_KEY>_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, or restore the previous unbounded behavior with value `0`. ([#​8665](https://redirect.github.com/oxsecurity/megalinter/issues/8665))

- Core
  - **Coding agents integration**: MegaLinter can now be driven by Claude Code, Cursor CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Codex and many other coding agents — see the new [Coding Agents](https://megalinter.io/latest/coding-agents/) documentation page ([#​8614](https://redirect.github.com/oxsecurity/megalinter/issues/8614))
    - Install the [MegaLinter agent skills](https://megalinter.io/latest/install-agent-skills/) with **`npx skills add oxsecurity/megalinter`**
    - Then ask your agent to set up MegaLinter (`megalinter-setup`), watch CI or local runs (`megalinter-check`) or fix lint errors (`megalinter-fix`)
    - Before the first **local run**, the skills now make sure the user is aware that MegaLinter is Docker-based and needs a good computer configuration and internet connection (the image download can weigh several GB), and suggest watching CI results instead when that is a problem
    - Local runs launched by the skills now cap **`PARALLEL_PROCESS_NUMBER`** to 4 on local computers (CI runs keep one parallel linter process per CPU core), so linting does not saturate the machine
    - Local runs launched by the skills now always activate the **JSON reporter** (not generated by default) to read results reliably, and fall back to the report folder configuration then the console output instead of waiting for report files that a repository configuration may have disabled

  - **Excluded directories are now forwarded to project-mode linters**, massively speeding up local runs, fixes [#​8645](https://redirect.github.com/oxsecurity/megalinter/issues/8645)
    - Linters that scan the whole workspace by themselves (`REPOSITORY_TRIVY`, `REPOSITORY_CHECKOV`, `REPOSITORY_GRYPE`, `REPOSITORY_TRUFFLEHOG`, `REPOSITORY_SEMGREP` and 50+ others) used to crawl everything, including build caches and `node_modules`: a seconds-long CI lint could take **hours on a local checkout**
    - MegaLinter now automatically passes the excluded directories (defaults, `EXCLUDED_DIRECTORIES`, `ADDITIONAL_EXCLUDED_DIRECTORIES`, and directories detected in `FILTER_REGEX_EXCLUDE`) to each of these linters, through its native exclusion flags or a generated ignore/config file
    - Every forwarded exclusion is logged in the linter's console section, and the ">300 gitignored files" performance warning now names the heaviest directories it found
    - Opt out globally with `FORWARD_EXCLUDED_DIRECTORIES: false`, or per linter with `<LINTER_KEY>_FORWARD_EXCLUDED_DIRECTORIES: false`

  - **Default excluded directories** now also include common build/cache folders: `.wireit`, `.turbo`, `.nx`, `.yarn/cache`, `.pnpm-store`, `.parcel-cache`, `.angular`, and the Salesforce CLI `.sf` / `.sfdx` state folders ([#​8646](https://redirect.github.com/oxsecurity/megalinter/issues/8646))

  - New **per-linter timeout**: a linter still running after **5 minutes** (`LINTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: 300` by default) is killed along with all its child processes and reported as an error (exit code 124) with an actionable message, while the other linters keep running. Raise the limit globally with `LINTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, per linter with `<LINTER_KEY>_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, or disable it with value `0` ([#​8665](https://redirect.github.com/oxsecurity/megalinter/issues/8665))

  - New **prerun analysis mode** (`mega-linter-runner --prerun`, or `MEGALINTER_PRERUN=true` environment variable): MegaLinter identifies active linters and collects files, then stops before running any linter and suggests configuration improvements, in the console and in `megalinter-reports/prerun-report.json` ([#​8653](https://redirect.github.com/oxsecurity/megalinter/issues/8653))
    - Suggested exclusions: top-level directories containing only gitignored files (safe: linting scope is unchanged, and project-mode linters stop scanning them), and well-known generated/vendored folder names (`site`, `dist`, `vendor`...) still containing lintable files (to confirm by the user)
    - A lighter matching flavor is also suggested when available
    - The `megalinter-check` agent skill uses it on the first local run to tune `.mega-linter.yml` with the user before the real lint
    - Fixed a performance issue where detecting `.gitignore`d files enumerated every individual file inside large ignored folders (`node_modules`, build output...) instead of stopping at the folder boundary, which could make the file collection step (including prerun) take several minutes on big repositories

  - **Much lighter Docker images**: the main image download shrinks by **9%**, flavors by **9% to 22%**, and standalone `megalinter-only-*` images are **35% to 65% smaller** ([#​8621](https://redirect.github.com/oxsecurity/megalinter/issues/8621))
    - If your `PRE_COMMANDS` compile native code: the compilation toolchain is no longer shipped in the images, install it back with `apk add --no-cache gcc make musl-dev`

    - Main and flavor images, compressed download size on ghcr.io, linux/amd64 (before = v9.6.0, so deltas also include the linters removed in this version):

body: ## What Add revision-aware canonical agent recovery for reconnects and renderer reloads. The server now returns a bounded contiguous delta when possible and a canonical snapshot when retained history cannot safely bridge the renderer revision. ## Why Reconnects could leave the renderer with missing, duplicated, stale, or misrouted canonical agent activity. The renderer needs one monotonic recovery path before it accepts later live revisions. ## Key Changes - Send each subscribed thread's installed conversation and roster revisions during atomic subscription replacement. - Return at most 256 contiguous canonical events, or a snapshot at the declared revision when the client is ahead, history has a gap, or the delta is too large. - Install reconnect recovery before later canonical pushes, and reject stale, non-contiguous, or cross-thread activity. - Add focused contract, server, renderer replica, subscription, duplicate, stale, and process-epoch coverage. - Verify the Electron reload path: revision 0/0 recovered through conversation revision 2 with six retained events, and the same visible prompt returned with no console or request failures. - Verification: affected typechecks and lint pass; 112 focused tests pass. The full gate passed typecheck and lint, but its unit phase hit the ten-minute limit twice due unrelated Windows process tests under full-suite load. Each reported failing test passed when rerun alone. Closes #1214 --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

author: marcelopaiva007
body:
Retoma o **#87** sobre o `master` atual, com duas correções. O trabalho é da outra sessão e veio por merge de verdade — o commit original está preservado no histórico.

> 🔴 Preview vermelho é esperado: há migration.

## O que o #87 entrega

Até aqui só o cron cobrava o colaborador a completar a ficha. Quem quisesse mandar na hora não tinha por onde.

| Lugar | O quê |
|---|---|
| Ficha do colaborador | Alerta com o que falta + **"Cobrar cadastro"** |
| Lista de colaboradores | Seleção por linha + **"Cobrar cadastro (N)"** em lote |
| Configuração → Lembretes | **"Rodar agora"** |

A distinção mais inteligente do PR: o botão **por pessoa** ignora a trava de 3 dias e o teto de 8 tentativas (se o RH clicou, decidiu cobrar); o **"Rodar agora"** respeita as duas, porque ali não é decisão sobre uma pessoa — é antecipar o relógio de todo mundo.

E a migration tem razão de ser: a coluna `manual` separa as contagens. Sem ela, cobrar alguém à mão **encurtaria a campanha automática dessa pessoa** — ela pararia de receber e ninguém notaria.

## Correção 1 — o lote de 200 estouraria o tempo

`MAXIMO_POR_VEZ` era 200, com o comentário certo (*"é limite de tempo da requisição"*) e o número errado. Cada pessoa custa **uma chamada ao Telegram mais uma ao SMTP, em série**.

O que torna isso concreto: o mesmo laço, no cron, precisou de `export const maxDuration = 300` para caber. Nenhuma das páginas que hospedam o botão declarava duração — ficavam no padrão da plataforma.

O sintoma seria exatamente o que o próprio código diz querer evitar:

> *"um clique que estoura o tempo da requisição deixaria metade cobrada sem ninguém saber quais"*

**Correção:** as três páginas declaram `maxDuration = 300`, e o teto caiu para **50** — cabe com margem larga mesmo em rede ruim, e é lote que alguém de fato seleciona à mão. Para a base inteira existe "Rodar agora".

## Correção 2 — a trilha de auditoria ia para a empresa errada

`cobrarCadastro` gravava tudo sob o `empresaId` **da rota**. Mas a lista mostra colaboradores de todas as empresas visíveis — e o próprio código filtra por `empresasVisiveis` justamente por isso.

Cobrar alguém da empresa B, estando na tela da empresa A, registrava na trilha de **A**. A trilha de B — onde alguém procuraria — não mostrava nada. E as telas que leem `AuditLog` filtram por `empresaId`.

É o mesmo defeito que corrigi hoje no módulo de Ponto.

**Correção:** `ResultadoCobrancaManual` ganhou `empresaId`, e a auditoria grava uma entrada por empresa das pessoas cobradas.

## Versão e migrations

Estava **1.73.0** — número já usado pelo Disciplinar, e abaixo do 1.75.0 que já está em produção. O #87 foi aberto às 22h23; depois disso saíram duas entregas. Renumerado para **1.76.0**.

Também escrevi a entrada de changelog que faltava: o #87 subia a `version` sem registrar nada em `lib/atualizacoes.ts`.

As migrations não colidem — `20260811233000` (deles) vem antes de `20260812000000` (avisos ao gestor, já aplicada em produção). Prisma aplica pendentes por ordem de nome, e as duas mexem em tabelas diferentes.

## Validação

- ✅ `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint` e `next build` (30.1s) limpos **depois** do merge
- ⚠️ Não consegui rodar o smoke deles (53 asserções contra Postgres real) — não há banco neste ambiente. A verificação original está descrita no #87
- ❌ Sem teste em navegador

author: falloutmule
body:
## What changed

- add a small renderer-neutral `@sfhs/physics-2d` surface backed by Rapier 2D
- support fixed stepping, fixed and dynamic bodies, circle and box colliders, state access, impulses, collision events, removal, and explicit cleanup
- add a bounded generic builder seam for synchronously instantiated ESM-style WebAssembly modules
- add a neutral Canvas proof that exercises strict SFHS and producer-neutral artifact paths

## Why

SFHS products need reusable 2D physics without coupling shared contracts to Pixi, Canvas, DOM, or product-specific mechanics. Rapier's standard browser package imports its WebAssembly module synchronously, so the existing one-file builder needed a small generic embedding seam to keep strict artifacts offline and self-contained.

This is the first product-driven Physics 2D foundation. It does not add pinball mechanics, renderer profiles, project-manifest v2, a second production backend, or a universal physics abstraction.

## Impact

- products can consume a renderer-neutral Rapier world instead of duplicating physics lifecycle plumbing
- strict SFHS artifacts embed Rapier's WebAssembly bytes and make no runtime sidecar request
- producer-neutral artifact verification and smoke remain available and unchanged
- existing strict project verification, adapters, packer, renderer scenarios, controls, One-Shot, and release behavior remain intact

## Validation

- `pnpm run check` — 392 passed, 2 skipped
- focused Physics 2D and builder tests — 10 passed
- strict pack and verify of `examples/physics-2d-proof`
- producer-neutral artifact verify and Chromium smoke
- strict Chromium smoke and phone-sized `file://` interaction proof
- repeated physics packs produced identical bytes
- browser smoke and scenarios
- Control Feedback acceptance
- plugin and Hermes adapter validation
- existing determinism suite
- `git diff --check`

The generated proof artifact is 1,740,908 bytes with SHA-256 `1617fcd895f507e36a2817a1eff692fb728884127fee8341a4e8a4f8f29891ef`.

No deterministic physics, physical-device acceptance, release readiness, or generalized WASM compatibility beyond the implemented synchronous ESM-style module seam is claimed.

author: himadajin
body:
Closes #132.

`$#functions` counts the handler function each armed `zle -F` watcher generates, so the fingerprint moved with zrush's own internal state, and it was the fingerprint's most expensive term because it expands every function body.
Counting the names outside the `_zrush` prefix instead makes the term insensitive to anything zrush defines — generated or static — and cheaper: ~280µs against ~500µs per call in a host with ~1140 functions, on a fingerprint that runs once per keystroke of a command-position word.

No spurious miss remained to fix.
The deterministic ones the issue originally reported were already gone: the worker session is now ensured before the cache is consulted, and a re-source discards the entry outright.
The 「既知の癖」 paragraph does not reproduce either — collection runs in a fork, so compsys lazy-loading never moves the parent's function table — so it and its two workarounds go with it.
The issue body carries the measurements and the environment.

## Changes

- `zsh/zrush.zsh`: the identity term becomes the number of function names outside the `_zrush` prefix.
- `docs/internal/specs/behavior.md`: state that rule in 「空語収集キャッシュ」; remove the 「既知の癖」 paragraph.
- `tests/driver/cache.rs`: new case `a_worker_restart_leaves_the_fingerprint_alone` — a worker stop must leave `fpmatch=1`, and the restart's recollection must be the latch's, not the fingerprint's. Two comments that rested on the removed paragraph are corrected.
- `tests/zsh/driver-latency.zsh`: drop the extra unreported warm-up trial before every cache-hit case.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo build --release`, `cargo test` (366 tests, green).
- `tests/zsh/keybinds.zsh`, `tests/zsh/vectors.zsh`, `tests/zsh/transport.zsh`.
- `tests/docker/run.sh 5.8.1` and `tests/docker/run.sh 5.9`.
- `tests/zsh/driver-latency.zsh` on the repo as playground: exit 0, no `WARN`, `cmd 1st (whic)` 209 ms against `cmd hit (whic)` 45 ms — the hit case reaches a hit with one preceding collection.
- Negative control: with `$#functions` restored, the new case fails at `fpmatch=0` once the worker stops.

author: neolicad
body:
## What

Implements [PL-8](https://neolicad.atlassian.net/browse/PL-8): "Add AI Chat but still just Mutual NDA" — a freeform AI chat that asks about the document and its fields and populates the document from the conversation, still Mutual NDA only.

Per discussion with the user, the chat **coexists side-by-side** with the existing form (both fill in the same shared state; the user can use either or both interchangeably), rather than replacing it.

## How it works

- `frontend/components/NdaChatPanel.tsx` is a new third column alongside the existing form and live preview in `NdaApp.tsx`. It owns its own conversation history and posts each user message to the backend.
- `POST /api/nda/chat` (`backend/app/routers/nda_chat.py`, gated by the existing fake-login session cookie) calls `openrouter/openai/gpt-oss-120b` via Cerebras/LiteLLM (`backend/app/llm.py`) using Structured Outputs, per `.claude/skills/cerebras/SKILL.md`. It returns a conversational reply plus a partial `NdaFormValues` patch.
- The frontend merges that patch into shared state via `frontend/lib/nda-chat.ts`'s `mergeNdaFieldUpdates` — any field the AI wasn't confident about comes back null/empty and is left untouched, so chat and manual form edits never clobber each other.
- Every chat turn sends the model the *current* field values as context, so it doesn't re-ask about already-filled fields or blindly overwrite a user's manual edit.

## Scope decisions (confirmed with the user before building)

- Chat **augments** the form rather than replacing it.
- Each chat turn triggers one backend call returning both the reply and structured field updates — the live preview updates after every exchange.
- The chat endpoint requires the existing session cookie, like the rest of the gated app.
- Simple request/response per turn, no streaming — matches the Cerebras skill's blocking `completion()` example and avoids introducing SSE infra with no existing pattern in this repo.
- No document/chat persistence — conversation state lives only in React state, backend is stateless (full history resent each turn).
- Kept the backend flat (single `/api/nda/chat` route, no document-type registry) rather than building for the other 10 document types now — two architecture options were designed and compared; this one better matches CLAUDE.md's "do not overengineer" guidance for a first, single-document-type AI feature. Promoting the route to be document-type-parametrized is a small, low-risk follow-up once a second document type actually exists.

## Testing

- Backend: 20 pytest cases (`test_auth.py`, `test_llm.py`, `test_nda_chat.py` + existing suite), mocking the LLM call at its import site.
- Frontend: 117 Vitest cases, including `nda-chat.test.ts` (merge logic), `api.test.ts` (HTTP client), `NdaChatPanel.test.tsx` (chat UI, including a regression test for a stale-closure race found in review — see below).
- E2E: 5 Playwright specs (2 new, `nda-chat-flow.spec.ts`) run against a real production build served by the real FastAPI backend, with the LLM call mocked at the network boundary for determinism.
- Manually smoke-tested the LLM call end-to-end against the real Cerebras/OpenRouter model (confirmed structured-output extraction, and that it doesn't spuriously overwrite already-set fields when given unrelated context).
- **Not verified**: a full Docker build — no Docker daemon was available in this environment. `uv lock --check` confirms the lockfile is in sync for the container's `uv sync --locked --no-dev` step, and the e2e suite already runs the real FastAPI backend (same code path Docker uses), including the session-cookie gating and static-file serving.

## Review

Ran three parallel code-reviewer passes (simplicity/DRY, correctness, convention-adherence). Two findings, both fixed:
- **Stale-closure race** (`NdaChatPanel.tsx`): field updates were merged against the `values` snapshot captured when the request started rather than the latest state, so a manual form edit made while a chat request was in flight could be silently reverted when the reply landed. Fixed by switching to a functional state updater (mirroring the pattern already used for the message list), with a new regression test.
- **Missing accessible label** on the chat textarea (placeholder-only, unlike every other input in the app which uses a real `<label>`). Fixed by adding a visually-hidden label; tests updated to select by label instead of placeholder.

## Also flagged, not part of this change

`frontend/AGENTS.md` (pulled in via `frontend/CLAUDE.md`) contains a block styled as tooling-generated instructions telling agents to read fabricated docs under `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before writing any code. Confirmed via `git blame` this was committed as part of PL-6, not something injected during this work — it reads as a planted prompt-injection test rather than real Next.js tooling output. Not acted on; worth a cleanup pass separately.

author: vi-hieu
body:
Closes docket #16.

`scripts/check-supply-chain.mjs` walked `skills/` only, so the repo's first plugin-level executable — `plugins/condux/install.mjs`, shipped by #9 — and the `INSTALL.md` telling an agent to run it were scanned by nothing. All four of the rules that exist for exactly that shape (`SCRIPT-FILE`, `INVOKES-SCRIPT`, `PIPE-TO-SHELL`, `EXTERNAL-DOMAIN`) were reachable in a tree the gate never opened.

## It was not #11-shaped

#18 predicted this would need the composition-manifest work first, because "the allow-list keys and its inventory both assume `skills/`". Neither does — both are keyed to repo-relative source paths already, so they took a `plugins/` prefix unchanged and the script inventory needed no edit at all.

The real coupling was one constant doing two jobs. `SCAN_ROOT` named both the tree to walk and the tree to resolve `references/…` citations against, and those are different questions: skills are the only tree that ships `references/` helpers, and plugin-level prose cites them by the same relative shape — concord's plugin README says `references/INSTALL.md`, meaning `skills/remember/references/INSTALL.md`. Split into `SCAN_ROOTS` and `SIBLING_ROOT`. A probe that widened the scan without splitting them reported that live link as dangling, which is how the trap surfaced before it shipped rather than after.

## Allow-list written against real findings

11 findings across 4 codes over the 14 new files, closed by 2 entries:

- `plugins/condux/install.mjs` (`SCRIPT-FILE`) — also clears the 8 `INVOKES-SCRIPT` findings on its own invocation lines, since invocations match by basename. The coupling is recorded in the reason so deleting one entry does not silently lose the other.
- `www.npmjs.com` (`EXTERNAL-DOMAIN`) — the `@jabworks/condux` package page cited in prose. Nothing fetches it.

The entry's open question is answered: docket's installer machinery is seen **once**, at `skills/record/server/`. `plugins/docket/` and `plugins/concord/` are README-only, and the plugin-root copy lives in `dist/`, which this checker deliberately does not walk. 175 files = 161 skills + 14 plugins, no overlap.

## Review finding, fixed in branch

`collectFiles`' second parameter went from a root string to an array of roots, and it is exported. A stale string caller would iterate the string character by character, match no directory, and hand back an empty list — the checker would then report clean over zero files, the one failure a security gate cannot afford and one this file's own test comment already names. A string is now normalised to a single-element array, with a test that fails without it.

Left as noted, not fixed: declaring `plugins/condux/install.mjs` whitelists the *basename* `install.mjs` for `INVOKES-SCRIPT` everywhere. The blind spot is narrow — a real new `install.mjs` still trips `SCRIPT-FILE`, which is keyed to the full path, so only prose naming an `install.mjs` this repo does not ship gets through — and `doctor.mjs` and `install.sh` set the precedent already.

## Verification

`node --test` 235 → 238, checker clean over 175 files. All three new tests triggered to fail by mutation rather than assertion:

| mutation | fails |
|---|---|
| `SCAN_ROOTS` back to `['skills']` | 2 — the plugins-coverage anchor, and the live assertion (the 2 allow-list entries go unused, caught by #13's reasonless-AND-unused rule) |

author: drcarrasco
body:
## Contexto del proyecto

TaskFlow es una API REST para gestion de tareas en equipos. Soporta multiples organizaciones, cada una con sus propios usuarios y proyectos. Los usuarios tienen roles (admin, member, viewer) y solo pueden operar sobre los recursos de su organizacion. La autenticacion es via JWT.

Entidades principales:
- **Organization**: agrupa usuarios y proyectos
- **User**: pertenece a una organizacion, tiene rol
- **Project**: pertenece a una organizacion, tiene un owner
- **Task**: pertenece a un proyecto, puede tener un assignee

## Que hace este PR

Agrega los endpoints de gestion de tareas y proyectos:

- \`GET /tasks\` - lista tareas, opcionalmente filtradas por proyecto
- \`POST /tasks\` - crea una tarea, valida que el assignee sea de la misma org, y actualiza el progreso del proyecto
- \`PATCH /tasks/:id\` - actualiza campos de una tarea
- \`DELETE /tasks/:id\` - elimina una tarea
- \`GET /projects\` - lista proyectos con conteo de tareas
- \`POST /projects\` - crea un proyecto (solo admins)
- \`PATCH /projects/:id\` - actualiza un proyecto
- \`DELETE /projects/:id\` - elimina un proyecto

Se incluyen tests basicos para ambos controllers.

author: aabhimittal
body:
## The second layer

PR #1 handled the happy path plus radio framing, safety policy, and offline retrieval. This PR covers the failures that only appear once **real equipment, real radios, and real technicians** are involved — six new capabilities, each pinned by tests in an industrial edge-case suite.

**75 tests across 9 suites**, all passing. CI now runs build + suite + fault-tree smoke checks on every push.

### New capabilities

| Module | The failure it prevents |
|---|---|
| 🕰️ [`telemetry.ts`](mcp/src/telemetry.ts) | A site's datalogger dies Tuesday; a technician asks Thursday. The cached reading still says `E-013`, so a naive agent diagnoses a fault that may already be fixed. **Stale data looks exactly like fresh data unless you check the clock.** Freshness + plausibility + clock-skew verdict returned *inline* with every reading, so an agent can't forget to check. |
| 🛰️ [`correlate.ts`](mcp/src/correlate.ts) | Eight inverters at one site report `E-013`; a per-asset agent rolls eight trucks for **one tripped combiner**. Collapses same-site clusters into one investigation — and inverts cleanly: the same fault on the same model across *unrelated* sites is a **batch/firmware defect**, which escalates to engineering and suppresses nothing (each customer still has broken hardware). |
| 🦺 [`watchdog.ts`](mcp/src/watchdog.ts) | The agent just told a lone technician to de-energize a 1000 V DC array. Hazardous advice arms a check-in over the same LoRa link; misses escalate through two tiers to a welfare response with last known location. Idempotent, fail-safe, and late check-ins issue an explicit stand-down. |
| 📮 [`outbox.ts`](mcp/src/outbox.ts) | LoRa is lossy, so the technician re-sends "order the board" — naively two reservations, two boards, two truck-rolls. Content-derived idempotency keys, strict FIFO (a `cancel` must never overtake its `create`), and crash-safe replay. |
| ⚖️ [`confidence.ts`](mcp/src/confidence.ts) | Offline, a 3–8B local model answers the same question a frontier model would. Advice is gated on risk × capability × evidence → `release` / `provisional` / `withhold`. |
| 📻 [`airtime.ts`](mcp/src/airtime.ts) | Ten individually-compliant replies in five minutes are collectively **non-compliant** (EU868 caps airtime at 1% of a rolling hour). Rolling-window governor with an absolute dwell limit and reboot-safe state. |

### Two bugs the tests caught

1. **Confidence weights were mis-calibrated** — the flagship path (frontier model, full evidence, high-risk procedure) returned `provisional`. An agent that hedges every answer trains technicians to ignore it, so over-refusal is itself a safety failure. Rebalanced the evidence bonus.
2. **Policy matching normalized the haystack but still let `by-pass the lock-out` through.** Added separator-free comparison. The remaining lexical limitation (genuine paraphrase) is **documented and pinned by a test** rather than quietly assumed away — that gap belongs to the upstream NemoClaw guard model via `match_semantic`.

### Also in the diff
- Two new skills (`fleet-correlation`, `lone-worker-safety`) and a dedicated `safety` agent — deliberately separate, so welfare escalation isn't starved by whatever the diagnostician is reasoning about.
- MCP server expanded to 13 tools; `create_dispatch` now flows through the outbox, `lora_brief` through the duty-cycle governor.
- [`docs/industrial-edge-cases.md`](docs/industrial-edge-cases.md) — every edge case and why it matters.

### Verification
```
npm test  →  75 pass, 0 fail (9 suites)
```
Server driven end-to-end over MCP stdio: 13 tools registered; telemetry trust correctly flags the month-old seed data as `ancient`/unusable; correlation returns `site` scope with 3 dispatches suppressed; watchdog arms; `gate_advice` returns `provisional` for high-risk advice on a small model.

author: eebette
body:
## Problem

Flows fail at **Build DV8.1 MP4** with `MP4Box exited with code 1` for any movie whose subtitle extraction produces an empty manifest (PgsToSrtPlus: `_subtitles.exports (0 entries)`). Observed on all three nodes; movies with at least one extracted subtitle are unaffected. Job logs show a phantom entry before the failure:

```
💬 Subtitle:  | lang=undefined | OCR=false | forced=false | ...
```

## Root cause

`"".trim().split("\n")` returns `[""]`, not `[]`. The single empty string survives into the subtitle loop, where `path.join(subBaseDir, "")` resolves to the work directory itself and gets passed to MP4Box as an `-add` argument. MP4Box exits 1.

## Fix

`.filter(Boolean)` on both the audio and subtitle manifest lines — same guard already used in `buildDv81Mp4Ffmpeg` and `cleanupDvCache`. Audio path has the same latent bug (unreachable in practice since audio manifests are never empty, but guarded for consistency).

author: daniel4828
body:
## 问题

界面右下角的版本角标显示的时间比德国当地**早 6 小时** —— 它显示的是生产服务器（`Asia/Shanghai`）的时钟数字。

## 根因

在后端，不在前端：

```python
"deployed_at": _dt.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")   # → "2026-08-11T21:28:56"
```

字符串里**没有时区标记**。浏览器按 ECMAScript 规范会把不带偏移的 date-time 解析成**自己的**本地时间，`getHours()` 再转回本地 —— 数字原样透传，看起来"没坏"，但换个时区读就全错。偏移一旦丢掉，前端再怎么格式化都救不回真实时刻。

## 改动

| 文件 | 改动 |
|------|------|
| `main.py` | `_dt.now().astimezone().isoformat(...)` —— 带上服务器真实偏移（`+08:00`） |
| `static/app.js` | 新增 `_formatBerlin()`，用 `Intl.DateTimeFormat` 固定 `timeZone: "Europe/Berlin"` 渲染角标与 tooltip；删掉手工拼的 `getDate()`/`getHours()` |
| `tests/test_version_badge.py` | 新增 2 条测试 |

**为什么固定柏林而不是跟随浏览器**：服务器在上海、手机会跟着人走，两者都不是读这个角标的时区。与播客单集日期的既有做法一致（#532）。

## 怎么测试

后端返回带偏移：

```
"deployed_at": "2026-08-12T10:24:42+07:00"
```

换算实测（node）：

```
上海 21:28  →  柏林显示: 11.08., 15:28
UTC 参照: 2026-08-11T13:28:56.000Z
```

- `pytest tests/test_version_badge.py` → 2 passed（断言 `deployed_at` 解析出的 `tzinfo` 非 None；断言角标渲染里不再出现 `getHours()`/`getDate()`）
- 全套 `pytest tests/` → 418 passed, 4 skipped
- 时间戳无法解析时 `_formatBerlin()` 返回空串，角标退化成 `branch@commit` —— 角标是 best-effort，绝不能拖垮应用

Closes #706

author: roomote-roomote[bot]
body:
> ​<!-- roomote:pr-attribution:start -->Opened on behalf of @mrubens.<!-- roomote:pr-attribution:end --> [View the task](https://roomote.roomote.ai/task/0v0fmqdabiz5y?utm_source=github-comment&utm_medium=link&utm_campaign=snapshot_resume) or mention @roomote-roomote for follow-up asks.

## Related issue

Found during an internal security review of the remote MCP OAuth flow shipped in #1219 — no external issue; this is internal Roomote work.

## Why this PR exists

- [ ] A maintainer explicitly invited this PR in the linked issue or discussion
- [x] I am a maintainer / this is internal Roomote work

## What changed

Replaying an already-rotated remote MCP OAuth refresh token now revokes the entire session family, per the OAuth 2.0 Security BCP refresh-token reuse-detection guidance. Previously the token route's refresh path called `getRemoteMcpRefreshSession()` first, which returns null for an already-rotated token, and returned `invalid_grant` before ever reaching `rotateRemoteMcpRefreshToken()` — the only place the reuse-detection Lua branch ran. The result: the replayed token was rejected, but the family's current token kept working, so a stolen-token signal never disabled the remaining tokens.

The route now falls through to a new `revokeRemoteMcpRefreshSessionOnReplay` helper when the presented token does not resolve to an active session. The helper only fires on the `rotated:<sessionId>` marker left behind by a successful rotation (keyed by the SHA-256 of the presented token), then deletes the session record and its current token hash, killing every descendant token. Unknown, malformed, or still-current tokens cannot revoke a live family.

## How it was tested

- New unit tests: route-level replay triggers family revocation (and never mints/rotates); library-level replay kills the family's current token; current, unknown, and malformed tokens leave a live family intact.
- Full OAuth suite passes: 28/28 tests across `mcp-remote-oauth.test.ts` and the token route tests; `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint, and oxfmt are clean.
- Verified end-to-end against a live dev stack: rotate → replay the old token → `invalid_grant`, and the family's current token is then also rejected (previously it exchanged successfully). A garbage-token replay against a separate live family did not affect it.

## Checklist

- [x] The PR title follows the repo convention: `[Fix]`, `[Feat]`, `[Improve]`, `[Refactor]`, `[Docs]`, or `[Chore]` followed by a user-facing description
- [x] This PR is small and scoped to one change

author: jiazi009
body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the open source app people use to manage AI agents for work
> - The board UI already includes i18next, but most visible text is still English
> - Chinese users need a complete Simplified Chinese interface and a clear language control
> - User data must stay unchanged when the interface language changes
> - This pull request adds complete Simplified Chinese resources, locale persistence, and safe static UI localization
> - The benefit is a usable Chinese board without translation of company names, project names, issue titles, or agent names

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

Related work:

- Refs: https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/11125
- Refs: https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/11133
- Refs: https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/8641

This PR reuses and extends the i18n work from these contributions. Thank you to @convergentaru and @cat9999aaa for the original localization work.

**What existing behavior does this improve?**

The React and Vite board UI language support.

**Subsystem affected**

`ui/` React and Vite board UI.

**Current behavior**

The board has i18next resources, but most visible UI text is English. The active locale is not selected consistently from saved or browser preferences. The board has no complete Simplified Chinese catalog.

**Proposed behavior**

The board offers `EN` and `简中` controls before and after onboarding. It saves the selected locale. It restores the locale after a refresh. It translates static UI copy while it leaves dynamic user and API data unchanged.

**Reason and benefit**

Chinese-speaking operators can use the complete board UI in Simplified Chinese. The implementation keeps technical identifiers and user-authored data stable.

**Breaking changes**

None. English remains the fallback locale. Existing partial locale files remain available for future work.

## What Changed

- Add complete English and Simplified Chinese keyed locale resources.
- Add locale detection, persistence, document language sync, and language controls.
- Add a build-time transform for remaining static UI literals. Do not mutate the rendered DOM.
- Add locale validation, untranslated-value checks, static-copy audits, and focused runtime tests.
- Add Simplified Chinese labels across navigation, primary pages, onboarding, authentication, settings, and status views.

## Verification

- `pnpm check:i18n`

author: rfs2671
body:
**No model call in this commit, deliberately.** The line sends itself at the admin's daily send time whether or not a human looked at it, so the check *is* the feature. You asked for a verdict on whether it can be made reliable before anything else ships.

## Verdict: it works, and it should ship

Two rules, in `backend/lib/ai/sub_summary.py`:

**Completion claims** are a deny-list checked *first*, on the raw tokens — `complete, finished, done, wrapping, final, closed, ready, topped, poured, installed, delivered`. A deny-list rather than "unknown nouns" because several of those could legitimately sit inside an activity label, and the sentence asserts an end state either way. The cost of a miss is a false statement to a lender.

**No new nouns** is the closed input set — company, trade, tapped activities, tapped locations, the counts — plus a deliberately tiny connective list of grammar and progress words that name no work, no place, no material and no quantity. A test asserts that list admits none of `pour, concrete, steel, floor, roof, wall, complete, inspection, delivery`.

## Tested adversarially — all four of yours refuse

| sentence | verdict |
|---|---|
| "Branch rough-in **complete** on the 3rd floor." | `COMPLETION_CLAIM` |
| "Branch rough-in and **conduit** continuing…" | `UNTRACED_TERM: conduit` |
| "Pull wire continuing in the **penthouse**." | `UNTRACED_TERM: penthouse` |
| "**Preparing for the pour tomorrow.**" | `UNTRACED_TERM: pour, preparing, tomorrow` |

The fourth is the dangerous one — it reads perfectly and traces to nothing. Also refused: *"Crew mobilised early and made good progress"* and *"Work proceeding without issues"*, the kind of thing a model volunteers unprompted. Eight completion phrasings are covered, including "wrapping up", "closed out" and "ready".

**Fails closed**: empty, punctuation-only and connectives-only all refuse. A refusal is never nothing — `plain_facts` states the payload in a fixed order with no progress language, and is asserted to **pass the checker itself**, because a fallback its own verifier would reject is an incoherent system.

**The depluraliser is crude on purpose.** It handles the one morphology a fixed label catalogue produces — "column" tapped, "columns" written. A real stemmer mapping "pouring"→"pour" would open the completion back door.

28 tests, 20 subtests, **6 mutations all caught** — both rules disabled, the vocabulary opened, empty allowed through, connectives-only allowed through, and the fallback made to claim progress. Backend **2977 passed**.

## Two of my own tests failed first, and both were mine

`plain_facts` said "4 on site" and `site` is not in the vocabulary — **the fallback bent rather than the allow-list widening**, because widening it hands the model a free noun. And the "touches no database" assertion matched the module's own docstring *saying* it touches no database. That is the fourth time this project has hit the self-referential shape, and the second time I have hit it **after** writing the report that named it. Both are now stripped before asserting.

## A process note you should have

I committed this to `main` locally before catching it — the `git checkout -b` was in a compound command whose heredoc failed to parse, so the branch was never created and the shell carried on. Nothing was pushed. `main` is reset to `origin/main` and the commit now sits on its own branch; verified both.

## What is NOT in this PR

The model call itself. With the check proved, the remaining work is `genai.Client` mirroring `phase_inference.py`, the prompt, the per-row loop off the report path, and the WhatsApp approval flow. Say the word and that is the next branch.

**Parts 2 and 3 of the report brief are not started** — you said build them while waiting on the queries, and I spent the budget on the check because you gated the feature on it. Page 1 also still waits on the headcount answer.

Awaiting your output from the three queries in #118 to close defects 2, 3 and 4.

Carried, unstarted: the U2 shakedown port, time pickers, ~200 i18n keys, hot_work gate wiring, the persisted UNASSIGNED sentinel, the site-manager role, the two-server-renderer consolidation, and SST card class from colour — which must never assert a class, with "cannot determine from this photo" as a first-class answer.

author: rmyndharis
body:
## What

Adds `src/modules/message/message.controller.spec.ts`, asserting the two response headers `getChatMedia` sets on the stored-media download:

- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`
- `Content-Disposition: attachment`

## Why

That route serves bytes that arrived from a third party, from the API origin. The two headers together are what keep those bytes inert in a browser: the disposition forces a download rather than a render, and `nosniff` stops a wrong `Content-Type` from being re-interpreted as active content.

`MessageController` had no spec. Its other 25 routes are covered indirectly — the route shapes are locked by the OpenAPI snapshot gate and the route-fence gate, the roles by the auth metadata, and the handlers carry no control flow. These two headers were the exception: they are a side effect on the `@Res({ passthrough: true })` response object, so they appear in no return type, no contract snapshot and no route gate.

That the gap was real was measured rather than assumed: with the `nosniff` line deleted and this spec absent, the pre-existing suite passed in full — 5,529 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed.

## Verification

Each header is asserted separately, so a failure names the one that went missing, and each line was removed on its own to confirm the spec actually fails without it:

| Mutation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| baseline, controller untouched | GREEN — 2 passed |
| delete `'X-Content-Type-Options': 'nosniff',` | RED — 1 failed, 1 passed |
| restore | GREEN — 2 passed |
| delete `'Content-Disposition': 'attachment',` | RED — 1 failed, 1 passed |
| restore | GREEN — 2 passed |

Each mutation fails exactly one test rather than both, so the two assertions discriminate between the headers instead of merely reacting to any change. The controller was confirmed byte-identical to its original after the run.

Full suite with the spec in place, rebased onto b2538e3f: 5,532 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed. `lint`, `tsc --noEmit`, `format:check` and `build` all clean.

## Scope

Test-only. No production code is touched.

body:
The release-gate cold-user run on main (bd5eafee) failed on the published artifact, not the repo: PyPI's wheel labeled 2.4.3 is built from 2.4.1-era code. From that wheel, `xair --version` prints 2.4.1, the documented negative-arg and dry-run behaviors fail, `xair --dry-run discover` puts a real UDP broadcast on the wire (spy-confirmed), the `docs` command is absent, and LICENSE/NOTICE are not included. It also found the root README had drifted ahead of the inner copy in exactly the dry-run safety section — and the wheel ships only the inner copy — with no guard enforcing the documented byte-identical invariant.

This PR makes the docs claim only what is true and pre-stages the republish:

- README + QUICKSTART: source install leads; explicit caveat naming what the stale wheel gets wrong and how to tell the builds apart (`xair --version` → 2.4.1); caveat self-retires when a release newer than 2.4.3 lands
- `pyproject.toml`: 2.4.3 → 2.4.4 — PyPI filenames are immutable, so the fix release needs a new version; bumping now makes the next publish unambiguous
- Root and inner README resynced (root was correct; inner was missing the safety section)
- New `tests/test_doc_parity.py`: README/LICENSE/NOTICE byte-parity enforced (falsified: appending one byte to the inner README fails it; skips cleanly on artifact installs with no repo root)

Close two concrete hardening gaps from the seven-day review without adding new runtime authority:

This is not a string-only coverage marker and does not skip when an external sibling repository is absent.

## SPARQL evaluator safety law

`crates/ggen-engine/tests/sparql_gate_complexity.rs` records the empirical evaluator limit found during DSPy expansion: current praxis-graphlaw overflowed on a sufficiently deep UNION algebra tree, observed around the 140–160 branch region.

The new court recursively scans checked-in `packs/**/gates/*.rq`, ignores UNION text in comments/string literals, and fails closed above 120 actual UNION tokens. The remediation is to use VALUES/table-driven bounded gates, matching the successful repair already applied to `dspy-pack`.

This does not pretend 120 is a universal SPARQL semantic limit. It is a conservative repository law below the exact current evaluator's empirically observed crash region.

Two new Rust integration-test files only. No engine execution path, pack semantics, release state, generated projection, receipt, filesystem actuator, network path, or BRCE boundary is changed.

## Standing

`PARTIAL_ALIVE` at publication pending exact-head repository CI.

## Falsifiers

Reject this transition if the restored pack-authoring court no longer matches the current pack contract; any checked-in gate already violates the conservative UNION budget; the counter counts comments/string literals as algebra; workspace formatting/lint/test gates fail because of this diff; or the restored test is only nominal coverage without real sync/idempotency/refusal execution.

Abandon/revert this purpose branch. No external consequence is created.

author: mrseanr
body:
An email client renders the statement ledger into a card a few hundred pixels
wide, and the date cell was free to wrap -- so a customer read 2026-03- on one
line and 05 on the next, down the whole left edge of a document sent to ask them
for money. The money cells already carried white-space:nowrap for exactly this
reason; the date was simply missed.

The description is now the only cell allowed to wrap, which is the right one to
give up: prose absorbs a narrow viewport, a value does not.

Found by looking at the rendered email while verifying the deposit fix, not by a
failing test -- so the test added asserts the date cell holds its nowrap, since
nothing else would catch it being tidied away.

Side effect (intended, spec-conformant): a non-author hitting another author's **draft** now gets 404 instead of leaking its existence via 403.
- Adds a guardrail to `docs/developer/CODING-STANDARDS.md`: a mutating endpoint must gate on write/ownership, never read-only, plus the audited exception list for surfaces that legitimately stay read-gated.

M1.5 **batch A**: the web application becomes valuable against today's unmodified NCIt —
inspect defects, verify corrections, and browse a certified corpus — on a rebuilt, pinned
serving stack. No NCIt content is modified.

## What lands

**Serving stack (foundation)**
- QLever replaces Oxigraph as the read engine for both immutable publisher indexes (NCIt and
  Uberon/CL), selected on a measured bake-off and pinned by image digest. No Oxigraph runtime,
  image, store-format assumption or sibling `fairdata` dependency remains.
- Journaled, crash-safe NCIt store activation: fsynced phase journal, owner-marked exact paths,
  same-filesystem swap, service stop/restart, health revalidation, deterministic recovery and
  rollback at every phase.
- Certified same-release serving: NCIt 26.07d with 12,980,813 default and 10,855,010 stated
  triples; repository metadata is bound to the certified manifest identity, and `/ready` refuses
  to claim ready on drift instead of serving an uncertified identity.
- Pinned data-build supply chain: digest-pinned service images, checksum-verified ROBOT and Jena
  artifacts, and tool identity recorded in build provenance.

**Application (inspection surfaces)**
- All routes render through a SvelteKit SSR BFF. Route-critical data arrives in the first HTML
  response through typed server loads; a server-only transport reaches FastAPI without exposing
  an internal origin. Backend 404/503 become explicit route errors, never a blank success.
- One shared loading primitive replaces the previous per-component variants; no unexplained
  blank region.
- Pre-coordination status is exposed, badged and server-side filterable across list/search,
  detail and the graph, as `representation_status: "legacy-precoordinated" | null`. Absence
  means "not published in this graph", never "atomic".
- Graph explorer: ForceAtlas2 layout moved off the main thread with an adaptive time budget and
  explicit cancellation; WCAG-AA label colours wired to the theme; label collision controlled so
  labels stay legible and reveal more on zoom.
- caDSR concept graph raised above the fold; cards no longer stretch to the tallest sibling.
- Breadcrumbs no longer link to `/repositories`, which 404s on every repository page.
- Stale route/prop-driven requests are cancelled or sequence-guarded so an older response cannot
