body:
## Summary

`klt synthesize` (and `place_and_route`) fail to resolve the nominal liberty
corner for `gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu9t5v0` when `pdk.corner` is omitted, because
`list_cell_libraries()`'s `nominal_corner` field is inconsistently shaped
across PDKs:

- sky130's `.lib` files' `default_operating_conditions` attribute is already
  bare (`tt_025C_1v80`).
- gf180mcu's real `.lib` files' `default_operating_conditions` attribute
  already carries the `<cell_library>__` prefix
  (`gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu9t5v0__tt_025C_1v80`) -- that's how the vendor's
  Liberty file is written.

`synthesize._resolve_liberty` and `place_and_route`'s identical copy both
unconditionally build `f"{cell_library}__{corner}.lib"` when `corner` came
from `nominal_corner` -- correct for sky130's bare shape, but doubling the
prefix for gf180mcu, producing a bogus path and a "liberty not found for
deck" error.

## Fix

Per the issue's curator enhancement, normalize in the single reporting
location (`pdk.py`'s `_nominal_supply`) rather than patching both
`_resolve_liberty` copies -- this also matches the already-documented
contract (`docs/cli/pdk.md:340` already describes `nominal_corner` as the
bare corner name). Added `_strip_library_prefix()`, applied to the `corner`
value `_nominal_supply` returns.

## Tests

- `tests/test_pdk.py`: new regression test reproducing the real gf180mcu
  shape (bare on-disk filename suffix, prefixed
  `default_operating_conditions` attribute) plus a sky130-shape no-op check.
  Extended `_make_cell_library`'s `corners` tuples to optionally carry a 5th
  `attribute_corner_name` element so the filename suffix and the attribute
  value can diverge.
- `tests/test_synthesize.py`: new test mirroring
  `test_run_synthesize_nominal_corner_default`, exercising
  `_resolve_liberty(cell_library, None)` against a gf180mcu-shaped fixture.
  Same `_make_pdk_install` extension as above.
- `tests/test_place_and_route.py`: this module had **no** synthetic-fixture
  unit test for the nominal-corner-default path at all (only the
  CI-skipped real-toolchain integration test) -- added both a sky130
  baseline test and the gf180mcu-shaped regression test, plus the same
  `_make_pdk_install` extension (`attribute_corner` param).
- `tests/test_equiv.py`: removed `_find_any_cell_library()`'s now-redundant
  prefix-stripping workaround and its stale "unrelated pre-existing
  behaviour" docstring -- `nominal_corner` is bare unconditionally now.

All four suites pass locally (`uv run pytest tests/test_pdk.py
tests/test_synthesize.py tests/test_place_and_route.py tests/test_equiv.py`).
`docs/cli/pdk.md:340`'s `nominal_corner` description was already accurate
for the fixed behavior -- no doc change needed.

The issue's secondary observation (gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu9t5v0 reporting
`nominal_supply_v: 1.8`/`voltage_class: "core"` while also shipping
`tt_025C_5v00` views) is triaged as expected, working-as-designed behavior
per #537's "report the lowest characterised supply as nominal" -- already
covered by `test_cells_reports_every_characterised_supply_gf180mcu_shape`.
No follow-up needed.

Note: `tests/test_synthesize.py::test_integration_real_yosys_gcd_worked_example`
fails locally on an unrelated, pre-existing exact-area-number mismatch tied
to this host's real Yosys micro-version (`0.68+post` vs. the pinned `0.68`
baseline) -- not caused by or related to this change. Full local run of the
rest of the repo suite also surfaced pre-existing failures in `test_gen.py`/
`test_functional_verification.py` unrelated to this change's scope (this
PR touches none of those files).

Closes #820

author: saranshisatgit
body:
## The miss

The negative-level sweep from #1257 reported:

```
No negative stock levels found across 194 level(s)
```

…while the admin UI showed **−2.5** on one of those very rows.

It wasn't wrong about what it saw. **It was reading one half of the value.**

`model.bigNumber()` persists a field **twice** — `<field> numeric` and `raw_<field> jsonb` — and on `FAB-TWO-BLU-001` at Shramdaan the two had drifted apart:

| surface | reported |
|---|---|
| `/admin/inventory-items/:id/location-levels` | `0` |
| item's `location_levels` relation (what the UI renders) | `-2.5` |

A healthy row agrees on both — the muslin read 19/19. **That comparison is the cheap discriminator**, and it's what proved this was a row-level fault rather than a serialization quirk.

## Two changes

**1. The sweep reads both columns and takes the worse.** A level is bad if *either* side is negative. A test pins the exact live shape — `numeric: 0`, `raw: -2.5` — so this specific miss can't recur.

**2. Divergence is reported in its own right.** It's worse than a wrong number, because it defeats the check that would catch a wrong number: whichever side a tool happens to read, it is confident and it may be wrong.

**Reported, never auto-resolved.** Neither column is inherently authoritative — the numeric side is what most queries filter on, the raw side is what the UI renders — so choosing between them is a judgement about what really happened to the stock. That belongs to a human. Same reasoning as refusing to guess a null `quantity_basis` (#1248).

## Prod state

The live row was already corrected by hand via `POST /admin/inventory-items/:id/location-levels/:location_id`, which rewrites both columns. Both surfaces now read `0`, and a full re-sweep is clean: **0 negatives across 194 levels / 219 items**.

⚠️ That manual write **bypassed the ops audit log** — no `ops_maintenance_run` row exists for it. Which is the other reason this class of fix belongs in a job.

## Tests

```
npx jest --testPathPattern="reset-negative-inventory-levels"   # 19 passed
npx tsc --noEmit                                               # 79 — baseline
```

author: ihoffmann-dot
body:
Fixes #36916

## Problem

The legacy "Select a file" / "Select link" dialog used to pick a **redirect target page** from a Page's Properties returned zero results for every folder — "No files found" even for folders that visibly contain pages. `BrowserAjax.getFolderContentWithDotAssets(...)` came back as `{total: 0, list: []}`.

`application/dotpage` is a **synthetic, display-time-only** MIME type. It is stamped onto a page's view map in memory (`PageViewStrategy`, `ContentletAjax`, `BrowserAjax`) and is **never persisted** to `contentlet_as_json`. The SQL MIME predicate added in #34217 tests for an asset-metadata `contentType`, so it matched **zero** HTMLPAGE rows and every page was filtered out in SQL before it could be transformed.

Regression origin: `f4ff8039` — *"feat(Content Drive) #34205: Support mimeTypes filtering in /api/v1/drive/search endpoint"* (#34217). That change targeted the new Content Drive endpoint but landed in the shared `selectQuery(...)` path the legacy DWR browser also uses.

## Fix

`BrowserAPIImpl.appendMIMETypeQuery(...)` now routes each requested MIME type to the only clause that can actually match it, OR'd together inside the existing `AND (...)` wrapper:

- exact `application/dotpage` → `struc.structuretype = BaseContentType.HTMLPAGE.getType()`
- anything else → the existing `jsonb_path_exists(...)` asset-metadata check

`struc` is already joined by `buildSelectBaseQuery(...)`, so this needs no new join, no new bound parameter and no caller change.

### Why not simply exempt HTMLPAGE rows from the predicate

That was the spec's original idea and it was **rejected during Phase 0 research**. The in-memory `filterReturnList(...)` pass runs on only **one of the three** consumers of `getContentUnderParentFromDB(...)` — Content Drive (`/api/v1/drive/search`) and `getFolderContentList(...)` have no in-memory MIME filter at all. Exempting pages in SQL would have leaked pages into `image/jpeg` browses on Content Drive, a new regression. The per-MIME translation is correct on all three paths and is a strictly smaller behavioural change.

### Generated SQL per request shape

| `mimeTypes` | Emitted fragment |
|---|---|
| `["application/dotpage"]` | ` AND (struc.structuretype = 5)` |
| `["image/jpeg"]` | ` AND (META(image/jpeg))` — unchanged |
| `["application/dotpage","image/jpeg"]` | ` AND (struc.structuretype = 5 OR META(image/jpeg))` |
| `["image/jpeg","application/pdf"]` | ` AND (META(image/jpeg) OR META(application/pdf))` — unchanged |

For any request that carries no `application/dotpage`, the emitted fragment is **byte-identical** to before this PR. The `5` is emitted from the `BaseContentType.HTMLPAGE` enum, never written as a literal. The match on the synthetic value is exact, so `application/dotpage-foo` still takes the metadata branch.

## Testing

TDD, Red confirmed before any implementation. The Red run failed with exactly the expected signature — 5 failures, all and only the `application/dotpage` cases, every one an `AssertionError` on an empty result set:

```
BrowserAPITest.test_getFolderContentList_dotPageMimeType_returnsPages
  AssertionError: Pages must be returned for an 'application/dotpage' browse, but got: []
BrowserAjaxTest.test_getFolderContentWithDotAssets_dotPageMimeType_returnsPages
  AssertionError: The dialog must report at least one item ... but reported: 0
```

The real-MIME regression guards were green before and after.

After the fix: `BrowserAPITest` 40/40, `BrowserAjaxTest` 7/7.

```bash
./mvnw verify -pl :dotcms-core,:dotcms-integration -Dcoreit.test.skip=false -Dit.test=BrowserAPITest,BrowserAjaxTest -Dtest=NumberUtilTest -DfailIfNoTests=false
```

New coverage:

- `BrowserAPITest` — `application/dotpage` returns pages; `image/jpeg` returns matching file assets and **no pages**; `["image/jpeg","application/pdf"]` unchanged; `application/dotpage-foo` not routed to base type; mixed request returns both; MIME order independence; nested sub-folder; language + default-language fallback.
- `BrowserAjaxTest` — the legacy DWR entry point the dialog actually calls.
- `Browser_Resource` Postman collection — two new requests against `POST /api/v1/browser` (it had no MIME coverage at all). `ContentDriveResource` already covers MIME filtering and is untouched.

> **Postman not run locally.** Both collections aborted on their first setup request with `Timeout connecting to [es/172.17.0.3:9200]` — the OpenSearch container died mid-run from Docker memory pressure on the dev machine. No browse request executed, so nothing about this change was exercised either way. They need to go green in CI before merge.

Manual confirmation still pending: selecting a page in the dialog and saving it as a redirect target, and comparing the dialog listing against the Site Browser for the same folder.

## Risk

Rollback-safe: no DB schema change, no ES mapping change, no REST/API contract change, no `@Schema` change, no `openapi.yaml` regeneration, no data migration or reindex. One private method in one class.

## Out of scope

Flagged during planning, deliberately not fixed here:

- `appendMIMETypeQuery` emits PostgreSQL-only `jsonb_path_exists` with no dialect branch — on MS SQL any MIME-filtered browse fails outright. Pre-existing, separate issue.
- Caller-supplied MIME strings are interpolated into the SQL string rather than bound. Pre-existing from #34217, unchanged here.
- The `PURE_ES` path builds its own `+mimeType:(...)` clause and has the same synthetic-MIME blind spot if it ever becomes the default heuristic. Not the default today.
- The three legacy `application/dotpage` string literals are left in place; only the modern class gets a constant.

## ADR alignment

ADR-0018 (*Database-First Search for Content Drive*, proposed) assigns MIME-type resolution to the DB via `jsonb_path_exists`, scoped to **file assets**. This PR *implements* that scoping rather than deviating from it: MIME stays DB-resolved, and the asset-metadata check simply stops being applied to rows that structurally cannot carry asset metadata. Nothing moves to the index.

author: homelab-agents-1234[bot]
body:
Fixes #353

The pushgateway markers are `AgentCoordinateScanWedged`'s **second** single-replica dependency, and PR #347 deliberately left them alone because #332's test gives them a **different answer** than it gave KSM. This is that answer, and it is **two answers**, because the two arms fail in opposite directions.

## Why the KSM verdict does not transfer — and what the class actually splits into

KSM is a **mirror**: a fresh replica re-lists the API and republishes the same facts, so a range selector bridges a hole that **ends**. The gateway is a **store**, and the scan pushes once per phase *transition*, so what the gateway loses nothing republishes. The failure therefore splits in two, and **only one half is bridgeable**:

| class | what happens | data | fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| **(a)** scrape gap / container restart | persistence file survives; at most one `--persistence.interval=5m` of pushes lost | **returns, identical** | `max_over_time(...[5m])` — #332's case in its pure form |
| **(b)** pod reschedule | the emptyDir goes with the pod; every group **destroyed** | **never returns** (until the next transition, which for a pod streaming a ride can be the rest of its life) | no range fixes it — `[5m]` postpones the consequence and the data is still gone |

**Measured, 2026-08-12, against live Prometheus @`192.168.40.13` over the 8 days it retains:** the pushgateway target had **11461 of 11461 scrape-minutes present — zero gaps >60s**, 0 container restarts, one pod generation, process up **15.5 days**. It is quieter than KSM itself (2×120s in the same window, #347). So class (a) is rare and class (b) has not happened inside retention — `[5m]` here is headroom, not a fit to observed damage.

`[5m]` and not `[10m]` for #347's reason unchanged: `for:` is **2m**, and the range is also how long this alert keeps ringing after the pod it names is gone, while **deleting the workflow is this alert's own containment**.

## The three reads, dispositioned separately

**Arm 1 — `unless on(pod) agent_scan_phase_start_timestamp`: fails OPEN.** It is a *guard*, so losing it does not silence the alert, it removes the thing that keeps a healthy >15m ride from raising one — the exact pre-FU-145 behaviour #283 exists to kill (2026-08-06: #120 and #134, two false issues in one hour). **Bridged, and guarded**, one mechanism per class:

- **(a)** `max_over_time(agent_scan_phase_start_timestamp[5m])`. The wrinkle the issue asked to be stated is stated in the manifest: a marker that legitimately went away keeps suppressing arm 1 for up to 5m. It is bounded, it can only *delay* a firing, and only for a pod that had already pushed. (Observed live: two generations of `platform-agents` markers visible in one 5m window, because a new scan's push **replaces** the namespace group.)
- **(b)** `kube_pod_start_time >= <the gateway's own process start>`. What (b) needs is not a longer range but a way to **know the store was emptied**. Absence of a marker is only *evidence* if the store has been up since before the pod could have pushed into it; if the gateway's current process started after the pod did, "no marker" means nothing. `process_start_time_seconds` also moves on a container restart, which is right — a restart can lose one persistence interval of pushes.
  **Positive evidence only:** `or vector(0)` makes an *absent* gateway self-metric read as "no roll observed" — today's behaviour — never as suppression. A guard that silenced the alert whenever its own input went missing would trade a rare false page for an unbounded silent one, and nothing watches the guard.

The guard is **arm 1's alone**: arm 2 reads the markers positively, so a lost store silences it rather than mis-firing it, and there is nothing for a guard to add.

**Arm 2 — `(time() - agent_scan_phase_start_timestamp) > 900` and `agent_scan_in_deterministic == 1`: fail CLOSED.** Both are required conjuncts, so a hole means arm 2 cannot fire at all. **Both bridged at `[5m]`** for class (a) — the wedge outlives the gap and the marker comes back unchanged.

`last_over_time` on the **gate**, `max_over_time` on the **clock**, deliberately: the clock is a monotone epoch so max *is* the newest transition, while the gate is a **state**, and `max_over_time(...) == 1` would read "was deterministic at some point in the last 5m" — a fail-open reading of the one conjunct that keeps a streaming ride out. Today the clock conjunct masks the difference (both are pushed together, so a dispatch moves the timestamp too and the `>900s` test fails first), so **no fixture row can separate them** — the choice is made on meaning, not on a red row, and the manifest says so.

**No `max by (...)` on the marker reads**, unlike #347's KSM half: verified live 2026-08-12, the marker series carry **no `instance`** (the gateway serves pushed groups with an empty instance and `honorLabels` keeps it), so there is no #288 identity churn to aggregate away — and aggregating would drop `job` from the alert's published labels.

## The ceiling, and the trade behind it

Past the bridge, a **destroyed** store leaves this alert **silent** for that pod: arm 2 has no data and arm 1 is suppressed by its own guard. That is the cost of this decision. It is **asserted, not assumed** (witness row 4), and bounded — the pod dies at `activeDeadlineSeconds: 1800`, and every scan pod started after the new gateway generation is covered again from its first evaluation.

The alternative was to leave arm 1 unguarded. Witness rows 1 and 4 are why that is not the cheaper trade it looks like: **the same gateway roll pages on a healthy ride (row 1) and on a real wedge (row 4), with gateway-side inputs that are indistinguishable.** The marker was the only thing separating them and the reschedule destroyed it. Silence that ends with the pod beats a page that cannot be believed.

**The FU-145 claim is not merely preserved, it is extended:** "a healthy >15m ride cannot raise this alert" previously held only while the gateway held its store; it now holds across a gateway roll too (row 1), which is the one input that could still break it.

## The witness

`argocd/resources/pushgateway/scan-wedge-pgw-witness.promtool-{rules,test}` — a **non-deployed** group holding the shipped expr and the pre-#353 one, asserted on **identical series**, six rows:

| # | input | shipped | pre-#353 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | class (b) under a **healthy ride** | silent at 23m (bridge) **and 27m (guard alone)** | **fires** — the FU-145 false page |
| 2 | class (a) under a healthy ride | silent | **fires** at 22m |
| 3 | class (a) under a **real wedge** | keeps firing, one identity | resolves, **re-keys onto arm 1**, resolves, re-fires — 3 notifications, 2 identities, one unbroken wedge |
| 4 | class (b) under a real wedge | fires to 23m, then **silent for good** — the ceiling, written to meet it | fires, on row 1's evidence, for the opposite condition |
| 5 | no gateway self-metric at all | **fires** (#103 no-marker wedge) — the `or vector(0)` default | identical |
| 6 | gateway **older** than the pod (the live steady state) | fires on pod age, unchanged | identical |

**Anti-vacuity, since a hand copy that tests the old expr passes for free.** Four mutations, each reverted one mechanism in the fixture's rules copy; **all four turn the fixture RED**, then restored byte-identical (`cmp`): arm-1 bridge, arm-1 guard, arm-2 clock bridge, arm-2 gate bridge. The hand copy was also diffed against the manifest via the `yq` recipe in its own header (a one-liner, so #344's wrapping bug does not bite) — **faithful on `expr`/`for`/`labels`**.

**This witness is not a second behaviour home** and its header says so: `agents/scan-wedge-alert-test.sh` remains the authority because it extracts the expr out of the shipped manifest at run time. What is pinned here is the **difference between two exprs**, which is a statement about this PR and cannot be made in a file holding only one of them. If the two ever disagree, t

author: bee404
body:
## Why A 10-round live QA pass found the preview mounted a real, interactive component in only **2 of 10 rounds**. The other 8 were not crashes — they were *silences*. `PreviewFrame` only rendered the "couldn't render this as live UI" fallback banner for mount/transpile failures on a `complete` generation. A generation that ended in `status: "error"` — overwhelmingly a `truncated_response` from hitting the output-token ceiling — fell straight through to a bare read-only source view with **no failure signal at all**. From the outside, a broken generation and a deliberately source-only one looked identical. Three distinct causes sat behind those 8 rounds: the silent stall itself (7 rounds), a token ceiling too low for dense full-page directions, and one JSX-children parse error. ## What **1. No bannerless failure is possible.** The typed codegen error is threaded from `CodeSheet` into `PreviewFrame`, and an `error` status now *always* resolves to the fallback banner regardless of cause. The decision is extracted into a pure, DOM-free helper — `errorFallbackNotice` / `PREVIEW_FALLBACK_PREFIX` in `lib/preview/preview-fallback.ts` — so the guarantee is unit-testable rather than an implicit property of JSX branching. **2. Token ceiling raised 4096 -> 16384** in `lib/providers/codegen/claude-provider.ts`. Dense directions (checkout, dense tables, settings, CRM detail) reliably produced ~30k characters and hit `stop_reason=max_tokens`. `stop_reason` is now parsed off the terminal `message_delta` and raised as a typed `truncated_response`, so the failure reads as "the model ran out of room" instead of a mystery `Unexpected token`. Re-tested at 4/4 mounting after the bump. `max_tokens` is a ceiling, not a reservation — billing is on tokens actually produced, so the raise costs nothing unless a component needs the room. **3. JSX-children parse error -> prompt rule, not auto-repair.** Object-literal-shaped children (`
{count: 5}
`) were reproduced and deliberately **not** auto-repaired: distinguishing intended text from an inline-style object from a typo requires the same JSX parser that is already failing, and naive regex escaping corrupts `<`/`>` inside strings and expressions. The fix is a targeted rule in `IMPLEMENTATION_REQUIREMENTS`, with the always-on banner from (1) as the safety net for residual cases. ### Rebase note: reconciled with PR #19 PR #19 (streaming panel + load-once incremental iframe mount) landed on main after this branch was cut and rewrote the same dispatch, producing real conflicts in `components/preview-frame.tsx` and `components/code-sheet.tsx`. Worth flagging: **#19 did not just collide with this fix, it entrenched the bug.** It refactored the dispatch into explicit branches and gave the silent stall its own dedicated code path: ``` // main today if (status === "streaming") return ; if (status === "error") return ; // <- no notice. the silent stall. return ; ``` The merged dispatch keeps both behaviours — #19's `StreamingSourceView` and `LiveMount` are untouched; only the bannerless `error` branch is replaced with `errorFallbackNotice`: ``` if (status === "streaming") return ; // #19, intact const errorNotice = errorFallbackNotice(status, error); // #16 if (errorNotice) return ; return ; // #19, intact ``` **Adds `lib/preview/preview-frame-dispatch.test.ts`.** `preview-fallback.test.ts` pins the pure helper, but a helper is only a guarantee if the component calls it — which is exactly what #19's refactor broke without failing a single test. The new tests render `PreviewFrame` across all three statuses. They fail against main's dispatch and pass here, so a future refactor cannot quietly reopen this. ## How to Review - `components/preview-frame.tsx` — the merge resolution. Confirm #19's streaming/incremental-mount path is intact and only the `error` branch changed. - `lib/preview/preview-fallback.ts` — the pure guarantee. - `lib/preview/preview-frame-dispatch.test.ts` — new regression guard on the wiring. - `lib/providers/codegen/claude-provider.ts` — the ceiling and its reproduction comment, plus the JSX prompt rule. - Intentionally excluded: deterministic JSX-children auto-repair (rationale above). ## Test Evidence - **30/30 unit tests pass** (21 original + 5 inherited from #19's merged test file + 4 new dispatch tests). Lint clean; `next build` + TypeScript pass. - **New guard verified to bite:** temporarily restoring main's `error` branch fails exactly 2 of the new tests; restoring the fix returns 30/30. - **Original scenario re-verified post-#19**, replaying the committed real captured truncation fixture (`truncated-max-tokens.raw.txt`, 16,459 chars, cut off mid-file at `fontSize: '`) through the full chain — provider -> typed error -> `PreviewFrame` render: ``` STEP 1 provider -> status=error code=truncated_response STEP 2 transpile -> false ("Unexpected token, expected ";" (10:42)") // nothing mountable STEP 3 render -> main today (pre-fix) banner : false <- the silent stall this PR (merged) banner : true banner names the reason : true ``` Not re-run: a live end-to-end dense-page generation against the Anthropic API (needs one of Bryan's real screenshots as input). The ceiling change is pinned by a test asserting the request sends `max_tokens: 16384`. ## Design QA — what to look at - **Failure banner on error states.** Open a direction that errors. You should always get the notice line above the source view, never a bare source dump. Check the banner's tone and prominence in the sheet at full height, and that the reason text reads like an explanation rather than a stack trace. - **Dense-page live mount.** Generate a dense direction (checkout, settings, CRM detail). It should mount as live interactive UI, not fall back to source. - **The two states together.** Streaming (compact partial-height panel) -> settled. Confirm #19's eased expansion to 85vh still plays correctly when the stream settles into an *error* banner, not just into a successful mount — that transition is the one this merge touches. Human author: Bryan (bryan@bryanlew.is) 🔗 [Obvious Project](https://app.obvious.ai/p/coqui-bvVRu4l0) · 🧵 [Obvious Thread](https://app.obvious.ai/p/coqui-bvVRu4l0?thread=th_Ws0Ekmzx)

author: juanlentino
body:
**PATCH.** Batches three un-versioned changesets from two sessions, coordinated across both before cutting.

## What is in it

| from | change |
| --- | --- |
| peer, [#584](https://github.com/juanlentino/signal-and-noise-tools/pull/584) | WordPress 7.1 readiness — a lifecycle guard hooked to a name WordPress never shipped, and a no-undo force-delete hidden from the Site Editor |
| peer, [#585](https://github.com/juanlentino/signal-and-noise-tools/pull/585) | `⌫ Clear DB Overrides` asks before it force-deletes |
| this session | the contrast scan's admin exclusion keys on the enqueue hook, not a filename substring |

#584 and #585 are **two halves of one hazard** and ship together deliberately: #584 fixed *where* the button renders, #585 *what happens when it is clicked anywhere else*. #584 alone reads as "we moved the dangerous button"; together they read as "we made it safe."

Mine is unrelated and small: `uptime-status.css` is admin-only but not named `admin`, so it leaked through the old filename proxy and put two wp-admin status colours (`#00a32a` at 3.35:1, `#dba617` at 2.22:1) into the live contrast report, scored against a public page they never appear on.

## PATCH — checked, not assumed

The renamed global in #584 (`sn_ability_guard_on_invoked` → `sn_ability_guard_filter_pre_execute`) is the *letter* of a breaking change. Not the substance: it was registered against `wp_ability_invoked`, a hook that ships in no WordPress release, so nothing has ever called it on any install. **You cannot break a caller of a function that was never reachable.**

The confirm gate guards an existing action rather than adding a capability, so it fails the MINOR test — and "requires user action" means adapt-or-migrate, not "adds a click".

**`Tested up to:` stays 7.0**, deliberately. There is no 7.1 install here, and asserting untested compatibility is the exact failure this batch exists to fix.

## Test plan

- [x] **Sweep on the combined tree: 422 suites, 16,548 assertions, 0 ERROR, exit 0** — matching the peer's *independently predicted* figure (16,530 base + 11 for #585 + 7 for mine). Hitting it exactly is the evidence the three changesets do not interact; a different number would have meant stopping to find out which two were touching.
- [x] My fix test-first: six assertions watched fail, then mutation-fired **in both directions** — dropping a sheet from the exclusion list and adding a front-end sheet to it each red the suite, so the guard can neither fail open nor over-reach
- [x] The drift test derives the admin-enqueued set from the plugin's own source and asserts it equals what the function excludes, so a new admin sheet reds CI instead of seeding false positives
- [x] Measured effect of my fix: 15 → 12 plugin sheets, 17 → 6 pairings, both sub-AA false positives gone
- [x] CHANGELOG conflicts (twice, same anchor) resolved keeping **every** entry, the peer's prose byte-for-byte, in the order they asked for
- [ ] CI green

author: jeffredodd
body:
Fixes #1572

## Cause

There is exactly one `/health` registration (`src/api_server.py:1030`, verified via `grep -n "\"/health\"" src/api_server.py`):

```python
@app.api_route("/health", methods=["GET", "HEAD"], response_model=HealthResponse)
async def health():
```

A single `api_route` carrying two methods becomes one `APIRoute` whose `unique_id` is computed once, not once per method. FastAPI's default `generate_unique_id` derives it from route name, path, and `list(route.methods)[0]` — and `route.methods` is a `set`, so which method lands in the id is non-deterministic. That one id is then emitted for both the GET and HEAD operation in the OpenAPI schema.

## TDD

Per the repo's test quality bar, I wrote the regression tests first and watched them fail before touching production code.

Added to `tests/test_api_docs.py`:
- `test_openapi_schema_has_unique_operation_ids` — asserts no duplicate `operationId` values anywhere in `/openapi.json`
- `test_openapi_schema_operation_ids_are_deterministic` — forces two fresh schema rebuilds (clearing `app.openapi_schema`) and asserts the `/health` operationIds are stable, since the root cause is `set` ordering

**Observed failure before the fix** (`pytest tests/test_api_docs.py -v`):

```
tests/test_api_docs.py::test_app_has_api_root_path PASSED
tests/test_api_docs.py::test_openapi_json_served PASSED
tests/test_api_docs.py::test_docs_page_references_prefixed_openapi_url PASSED
tests/test_api_docs.py::test_openapi_schema_has_unique_operation_ids FAILED
tests/test_api_docs.py::test_openapi_schema_operation_ids_are_deterministic PASSED

=================================== FAILURES ===================================
_________________ test_openapi_schema_has_unique_operation_ids _________________
tests/test_api_docs.py:62: in test_openapi_schema_has_unique_operation_ids
    assert not duplicates, f"Duplicate operationId(s) in /openapi.json: {sorted(duplicates)}"
E   AssertionError: Duplicate operationId(s) in /openapi.json: ['health_health_get']
E   assert not {'health_health_get'}
=============================== warnings summary ===============================
tests/test_api_docs.py::test_openapi_json_served
tests/test_api_docs.py::test_openapi_schema_operation_ids_are_deterministic
tests/test_api_docs.py::test_openapi_schema_operation_ids_are_deterministic
  .../fastapi/openapi/utils.py:303: UserWarning: Duplicate Operation ID health_health_get for function health at /app/src/api_server.py

1 failed, 4 passed, 3 warnings in 0.86s
```

This confirms the failure is a genuine duplicate id, not a typo/import error.

## Fix

Split the single `@app.api_route(methods=["GET", "HEAD"])` into two handlers with distinct names, `health()` (`@app.get`) and `health_head()` (`@app.head`), so each HTTP method gets its own `APIRoute` and its own deterministic `operationId`. `health_head()` delegates to `health()` (`return await health()`) to keep byte-identical response behavior. This was the option the issue called "clearest" over a per-route `operation_id` override or a global `generate_unique_id_function`.

## Verification

All run via the isolated container recipe:
```
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/app -w /app python:3.11 sh -c \
  "pip install -q -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt && pytest tests/test_api_docs.py -v"
```

- After the fix: all 5 tests in `tests/test_api_docs.py` pass, no warnings.
- Ran the broader set (`tests/test_api_docs.py tests/test_api_extended.py tests/test_service_lifecycle.py tests/test_auth_routes.py`, 291 tests) with `-W error::UserWarning` — all pass, confirming the `Duplicate Operation ID` warnings that were previously raised in `test_openapi_json_served` and `test_middleware_public_paths_when_enabled` are gone.
- Confirmed existing `/health` GET and HEAD tests (`test_api_extended.py::TestRootAndHealth`, `test_service_lifecycle.py::TestHealthEndpoint`) still pass unchanged.
- `ruff check` passes on both changed files.

**Vacuity check** (per the test quality bar): stashed the `src/api_server.py` fix only, re-ran `tests/test_api_docs.py` — `test_openapi_schema_has_unique_operation_ids` failed again with the identical `AssertionError: Duplicate operationId(s) in /openapi.json: ['health_health_get']`. Restored the fix and re-ran to confirm green. This proves the test is not vacuous.

body:
Make the monorepo auto-bump workflow respond to `repository_dispatch` events sent by submodule repos, so pin bumps land within ~a minute of a submodule merge instead of waiting for the 30-minute cron (which remains as a backstop).

## Changes

- `.github/workflows/auto-bump-submodules.yml`: add `repository_dispatch` with `types: [submodule-update]` alongside the existing `schedule` + `workflow_dispatch` triggers. No script changes — drift detection in `scripts/auto-bump-submodules.sh` is trigger-agnostic.
- `AGENTS.md`: document the new immediacy path in the Phase 2 auto-bump section — submodule repos notify the monorepo on push to `main` via `repository_dispatch` (`submodule-update` event) using the `MONOREPO_DISPATCH_TOKEN` secret (stored in each submodule repo; fine-grained PAT with contents:write on `intent-hq/monorepo`; fail-soft when absent, with the cron backstop still advancing pins).

## Verification

- `actionlint .github/workflows/auto-bump-submodules.yml` — clean (actionlint 1.7.12).
- Grepped `AGENTS.md` for `MONOREPO_DISPATCH_TOKEN` / `repository_dispatch` / `submodule-update` consistency with the workflow trigger.

The companion notify workflows in the submodule repos (senders of the dispatch event) are being added separately.

author: gapul
body:
## なぜ

バックアップの稼働確認をしていて2点見つかった。

1. **監視が実質効いていない**: `restic-monitor` は `restic snapshots --latest 1` を**リポジトリ全体**で見ていた。共有リポジトリなので、homeserver/macmini/rpi4 のどれか1台が毎日書いていれば「最新は今日」と判定される。母艦だけ何週間止まっても通知は飛ばない。
2. **homeserver の forget が他ホストのスナップショットまで対象にしていた**: `pruneOpts` に `--host` が無いため、自分が書いていないホストにも保持ポリシーが適用される。ポリシーは `restic-common.nix` で全ホスト同一なので今すぐ何かが消えるわけではないが、**書き込む側が居なくなったホスト**（畳んだ pve の vzdump、移行時の cold/warm pass）は keep-monthly 6 の期限切れで消える。

## なにをした

- `monitoredHosts` を `nix/lib/restic-common.nix` に置き、monitor は一覧を1回取って**ホスト別**に鮮度判定。未知ホスト（一度も書いていない）も別文言で通知。
- `nix/homelab/backup.nix` の `pruneOpts` に `--host homeserver` を追加。
- リポジトリ側（この PR の外・実施済み）: `restic tag --add archive --host pve` と `--host homeserver-migration` で3本を保持対象から外した。
- `docs/HOMELAB.md` §10 に、monitoredHosts の足し忘れ／退役ホストの外し忘れの罠を追記。

## 確認

- `nix build .#homeConfigurations.gapul.activationPackage` 通過。生成された restic-monitor の中身を目視。
- 生成後のループを実データ（`restic snapshots --json`）に対して実行。max_age=2 で無警告、max_age=0 で4ホストとも stale 検知、存在しないホスト名で「no snapshots」経路も発火することを確認。
- `nix eval .#nixosConfigurations.homeserver.…pruneOpts` → `[ "--keep-tag archive" "--keep-daily 7" "--keep-weekly 4" "--keep-monthly 6" "--host homeserver" ]`
- `nix fmt` / `just docs` 差分なし。

author: joacomarquez
body:
## Qué arregla

Lote operativo del análisis del 11/8 (hallazgos 3, 10, 11 y menores) — elegido para **no colisionar** con la sesión de fixes estructurales (menú/0-0/exactos) ni con el PR #170 (calendario, sigue abierto).

### Hallazgo 3 — la planilla envenenada por el rerun (el gordo)

El rerun T-2h versiona la planilla nueva aunque el gate por valor descarte el cambio (regla de trabajo #2). Nadie recarga esos picks en la web, el partido cierra… y `load_frozen` congela los picks de la planilla — **picks que nunca jugamos**. El optimizador diversifica contra una posición propia falsa el resto de la temporada, y el postmortem atribuye puntos con los mismos picks fantasma. Ya pasó el 10/8 (7 picks en amarillo con Δ −456).

**Fix:** `drift_audit` ahora ADOPTA — igual que ya hacía con los goleadores. Post-cierre los picks propios son públicos por API y son la verdad inmutable: si difieren de la planilla, versiona una planilla realineada, avisa una vez por Telegram, y si la causa fue el gate lo dice ("esperado, no es error de carga"). Idempotente: sin desvíos no versiona.

### Red de seguridad

- **`safe_pull.sh`** validaba los imports del stack del Mundial (apagado desde el 29/7) — un ImportError en `picks`/`rerun_cierre` pasaba limpio y explotaba al día siguiente con la fecha corriendo. Ahora valida `src.clausura` completo. Y `sync_units` avisa de units `clausura-*` del repo que el VPS no tiene instalados (gate-watch y heartbeat nacieron después del setup inicial).
- **`heartbeat`** vigila también `clausura-gate-watch` (el vigía caído era el silencio exacto que el heartbeat existe para cerrar), su propio timer y el servicio del dashboard (uvicorn muerto = sin modo carga el sábado).
- **`gate_watch`** traga cualquier fallo de tick (antes solo red: un cambio de shape del API = crash + OnFailure **144 veces/día**) pero escala una vez tras 12 ticks consecutivos fallados (~2h) — ni silencio eterno ni fatiga de alarma.
- **`sync`** escribe el YAML con rename atómico (lo leen 4 procesos concurrentes) y rechaza un config sin eventos en vez de mutilar la fuente de verdad de todos los cierres.

## Tests

323 pasan; 5 nuevos: adopción reescribe solo cerrados-distintos / idempotente / reporta causa gate, escalación del vigía, y el heartbeat exige gate-watch en la lista. (El rojo local de `fastapi` es ambiental, preexistente.)

## Deploy

Post-merge: `safe_pull.sh` en el VPS. La primera corrida del drift-audit (13:20 UTC) va a realinear la Fecha 1 si quedó alguna versión con picks descartados — el Telegram va a decir exactamente qué realineó y por qué.

author: tobe2111
body:
상인회·전자계약에 이은 **세 번째 제품**과, 앞으로 제품을 계속 늘리기 위한 **토대**입니다.
프랜차이즈 본사에 파는 것은 예쁜 홈페이지가 아니라 **상담 신청이 쌓이는 화면**이라서, 화면 자랑보다 DB가 들어오고 관리되는 경로를 먼저 세웠습니다.

커밋 5개입니다.

| # | 내용 |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | 가맹점 모집 랜딩 + 상담 DB |
| 2 | 실제로 굴려 보면 비는 열 가지 보강(전환율·광고출처·초안발행·사진·사본·자동파기 등) |
| 3 | `wrangler.toml` 위치 조정 (자동 배포 실패 대응) |
| 4 | **제품 유형 레지스트리 + 업종 프리셋 + 사이트 복제** |
| 5 | **보안 검토 반영** |

---

## 1. 제품 유형 레지스트리 (`src/kinds.js`)

`kind === "esign"` 같은 분기가 네 파일 50여 곳에 흩어져 있어, 제품을 하나 더 만들 때마다 열 군데를 고쳐야 했습니다. 한 곳으로 모았습니다.

| kind | 공개 화면 | 관리자 화면 | 제품 소개 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `merchant` | 상인회 홈 | 승인·공지·회비·홈 구성 | `/` |
| `esign` | 계약 창구 | 계약서·서식·담당자 | `/esign` |
| **`franchise`** | **모집 랜딩 한 장** | **랜딩 편집 + 상담 DB** | **`/homepage`** |

홈 분기·상단 메뉴·콘솔 패널·슈퍼 콘솔 선택지가 전부 이 표를 읽습니다.

### 업종 프리셋 — 같은 엔진, 다른 제품

모집형은 **업종 문구**만 갈아 끼웁니다: 프랜차이즈 · 학원 · 헬스장 · 병원 · 분양.
`terms`("가맹 상담" ↔ "입학 상담" ↔ "진료 상담")가 메뉴·고정바·폼·공지에 함께 반영됩니다.
안 채운 문구는 대표 프리셋에서 빌려오므로 **업종 추가는 항목 하나**면 됩니다.
→ [`docs/새-제품-유형-추가하기.md`](../blob/claude/seocho-homepage-service-w3t0h0/docs/새-제품-유형-추가하기.md)

## 2. 사이트 복제

슈퍼 콘솔에서 잘 만든 사이트를 본으로 새 고객사를 찍어 냅니다.
- 따라오는 것: 유형·업종·대표색·홈/랜딩 구성·캠페인 사본
- 따라오지 **않는** 것: 회원·점포·상담 신청·계약 — 남의 개인정보가 새 고객사 화면에 뜨면 안 됩니다(테스트로 고정)

## 3. 랜딩페이지

히어로 · 흐르는 띠 · 브랜드 소개 · 강점 · 후기 · 메뉴 · 절차 · 비용(가리기) · **상담 폼** · 매장 안내 · FAQ · 공지 · 마무리 배너 + 손님 화면 전체에 붙는 **고정 하단 바**.

- 섹션 켜기/끄기·순서·문구를 관리자가 직접 수정, **초안 → 미리보기 → 발행**
- 사진은 파일 선택 또는 **사진 보관함**에서 주소 복사
- **캠페인별 사본** `/l/:campaign` — 광고 소재별 전환율 비교(색인 제외)

## 4. 상담 DB

- 상태·메모·CSV·삭제, 50건씩 쪽 나눔
- **광고 출처 자동 기록**(UTM·referrer·사본) + **30일 전환율** + **랜딩별 성과**
- 새 상담 → 담당자 알림톡·메일, 신청자 접수 확인 알림톡
- 상담 건에서 **계약서 만들기** → 서명 링크까지 정보가 따라감

## 5. 보안 검토 결과 반영

감사에서 나온 4건을 모두 고쳤습니다.

- **[높음]** 공개 폼이 **임의 번호로 알림톡을 쏘고 조직 크레딧을 태울 수 있었음**(Turnstile 미설정 시 fail-open) → 조직당 하루 200건 상한 + IP 제출 제한(15분 20건, CGNAT 감안)
- **[중간]** 지운 상담 건의 이름·번호가 **알림함·감사로그·주소창에 남았음** → 전부 제거(건 번호로 대체). "파기한다"는 방침과 코드가 일치하게
- **[낮음]** 방문 계측 남용 → 크롤러·1분 내 재조회 제외(중복 창을 짧게 둔 이유: CGNAT에서 서로 다른 방문자가 합쳐지면 전환율이 거짓말을 함)
- **[낮음]** 공개 폼이 심은 값이 관리자 화면을 채우던 문제 → 없는 사본 이름 미기록, 집계 상한

**깨끗했던 항목**: 테넌트 격리 · XSS(`safeSrc`가 `javascript:`/`data:` 차단) · 가린 금액이 HTML에 실리지 않음 · 복제가 개인정보를 옮기지 않음 · 새 POST 경로의 CSRF·권한 등급

## 확인

- `npm test` — **415건 통과**(신규 33건) · `npm run test:e2e` — 27건 통과
- 데스크톱·모바일 실제 렌더 확인(랜딩·상담 DB·편집기·학원 프리셋)
- ⚠️ Workers 빌드 체크 실패는 **코드가 아니라 계정/빌드 설정** 쪽입니다. 깨끗한 클론에서 `npm ci` → `wrangler deploy --dry-run` 모두 성공합니다 — [상세](https://github.com/tobe2111/website/pull/13#issuecomment-5262537736)

author: clabonte
body:
Replaces the blanket `specfuse/loop/` prefix in `arm_eval.JUDGE_PATHS` with a named registry of the modules a merge/arm/close verdict actually reads.

## Why

The prefix was right in intent and far too wide in reach. It covered **all 44 modules** of the driver package plus **every shipped document**, so in the one repository where it applies — this one — no gate shipping documentation could arm, and no bug fix touching any driver module could auto-merge, whether or not it went near a decision.

Both halves are observed, not predicted:

- FEAT-2026-0053's close recorded the first as a structural limit making `auto` *"currently unreachable for a large class of features"*, and said narrowing it *"needs a decision with evidence, not a one-line prefix edit, and it has no home yet."* This PR is that home.
- The first unattended agent run hit the second, declining two of eight items `judge_path_touched`.

## What is a judge now

`JUDGE_MODULES` — **24** modules, each classified against one rule: *a merge/arm/close verdict, or the evidence a verdict reads, can change because of an edit to it.*

- the predicates — `arm_eval`, `arm_sweep`, `arm_txn`, `gate_eval`, `bug_lane`, `bug_lane_run`, `bug_lane_state`, `upgrade_merge_gate`
- what a verdict is measured against — `agent_policy` (the automerge dial, the caps), `cost`, `gate_commands`
- what a WU or a close must satisfy — `closing_requirements`, `criteria_state`, `lint_closing`, `lint_plan`, `plan_baseline`
- the driver's own guards — `loop`, `prerun`, `prerun_capture`
- trail integrity — `validate_event`
- evidence pipes — `_miniyaml`, `_wu_sections`, `triage`, `rearm_migration`: none signs a verdict, each can change one (`triage.parse_marker` decides `REASON_UNTRACEABLE`; `_miniyaml` parses the automerge dial; `rearm_migration` rewrites the cost fields `budget_projection` measures). Three of these were in `NON_JUDGE_MODULES` in the first push and moved on review — `triage` was plainly misclassified, its reason reading "sets no gate and merges nothing", which is false.

`JUDGE_DATA_PREFIXES` — package data seeding a judge surface downstream: `rules/`, `rules-local/`, `schemas/`, `templates/`, `workflows/`, `verification.yml.example`. Editing a shipped rule is editing what becomes `.specfuse/rules/` in every consumer.

The five universal surfaces (`.specfuse/verification.yml`, `.specfuse/hooks/`, `.specfuse/rules/`, `.github/workflows/`, `pyproject.toml`) are **unchanged** — and they are the only entries that match at all in a project that installed Specfuse rather than holding its source.

**`specfuse/loop/data/docs/` is the one deliberate exclusion**, on the evidence that no predicate reads it. That mirror is precisely why any documentation-shipping gate fired the class.

## The counterweight

An allowlist stops protecting the moment someone forgets to extend it — which the blanket prefix, for all its bluntness, could not do. That regression is not acceptable on a safety predicate, so the narrowing does not ship alone:

- `NON_JUDGE_MODULES` / `NON_JUDGE_DATA_ENTRIES` record **every** unlisted file with a written reason
- `tests/test_judge_path_registry.py` enumerates `specfuse/loop/*.py` and the data tree and **fails when anything appears in neither**

A new decision module cannot escape by omission; it has to be classified, in writing. Same shape as the `DEPENDENCY_MANIFEST_COVERED` / `_NAMED_UNCOVERED` pair directly beside it in the same file.

## Read this before merging

**This widens what may proceed without a human.** A PR editing a driver module outside the 20 is now eligible to auto-merge where it previously was not. That is the intended effect, and it is a judgement call about a safety predicate — the module classification above is the thing to review, not the mechanism. If any of the 20 modules in `NON_JUDGE_MODULES` looks to you like it decides something, say so and it moves. A hand review after the first push already moved four that way, so treat the remaining 20 as reviewed once, not as proven.

Note also that neither of the two items which triggered this actually becomes mergeable: issue #240's fix touched `specfuse/loop/loop.py` and #795's touched `specfuse/loop/gate_eval.py` — both are real judges and both still decline, correctly. The class this frees is the fix to notification, liveness, changelog, scaffolding or escalation-rendering code that was blocked while deciding nothing.

## Verification

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` — **3166 tests, OK** (1 skipped)
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` — **OK** (full declared gate set including bats)
- `ruff check specfuse tests .specfuse/scripts scripts` — clean
- `bandit -r specfuse .specfuse/scripts -ll` — 0 medium, 0 high
- `coverage report --fail-under=90` — **93%**
- `tests/test_scaffold_data_in_sync.py` — the docs edit was made canonical in `docs/` and re-synced to package data; parity guard green
- Registry tests verified **red against the pre-change `arm_eval.py`** (7 failures, 5 errors), not merely green after

Two existing tests were updated rather than deleted: both asserted the old behaviour using an invented path (`specfuse/loop/some_module.py`, `specfuse/loop/a.py`) that no longer resolves to a judge. They now name real decision modules, which is what they were always trying to express.

## Unrelated observation

While running the gates concurrently I hit `FileExistsError` on `~/.claude/session-env/.specfuse-preflight-probe` in `loop.require_session_env_writable`. The probe directory has a **fixed name**, so two concurrent `specfuse run` invocations can fail each other's preflight. Not touched here — it needs its own issue.


Separately filed while verifying this PR: #1951, a fixed-name preflight probe that makes two concurrent `specfuse run` invocations fail each other with a wrong diagnosis.

The issues screen becomes a real My Work view, verified live on the iOS simulator against the dev Redmine 7.

## What changed

- **Mine / All filter**: a segmented control scopes the list and map to the signed-in account. Identity comes from core `/users/current.json`, fetched once per session and tolerated to fail (a narrow token or role hides the filter instead of breaking); matching is by Redmine display name, which is what bundle summaries carry.

Pull-to-refresh walks `GET /gtt_sync/changes` pages, upserts by id, reconciles deletions via `known_ids`, and advances the cursor; the sync logic is pure (`IssuesState.applyPage`) and unit-tested. The app-bar refresh stays a full reload.

Filter defaulting to Mine with real assignments, instance status colors (blue Resolved, yellow In Progress, green New...), resolved names, red overdue dates, geometry icons; then a server-side subject edit appeared in the list after a single pull-to-refresh, synced as a one-issue delta through the feed.

author: cheeseprince
body:
## What this changes

Three related fixes to the Bluetooth adapter flow, from two reports on real hardware:

> *"Forget adapter: click on it and it goes 'Forget adapter?' and then nothing happens."*
> *"I keep on getting bluetooth connection requests on my mac."*

### 1. The Forget-adapter acknowledgement was invisible

`forget()` only sets a flag that core 0 processes on its **next** poll, so at the moment of
confirmation the link is still up and the gauges render instead. By the time it drops, the dash
has re-bonded — about a second on the bench — so the branch was skipped again. The
acknowledgement was effectively never displayed.

Moving it ahead of the link-up branch was necessary but **not sufficient**: confirming did not
close the menu, and `statusLabel`/`menuLabel` are both full-screen `LV_OPA_COVER` children of
`lv_layer_top()` with the menu built second, so it drew on top. Confirming now closes the menu,
exactly as the Close row does.

### 2. Destructive rows get a real confirm dialog

`Reset trip` and `Forget adapter` were click-to-arm / click-again, and **any knob turn silently
cancelled** the pending confirm. Nothing on screen said a second click was needed.

Now: click opens `< No >`, the knob selects No/Yes, a click acts on the highlighted choice. The
mapping is **absolute** (right = Yes), not a toggle — a toggle made the outcome a parity function
of how fast the knob was spun, which is a poor property for a destructive action.

### 3. The dash no longer re-probes devices it already rejected

The connect path detected *"no known BLE-ELM327 profile"* and gave up, but never recorded the
address, so the next scan ranked the same stranger just as highly and probed it again — a laptop
in range got a connection request roughly every minute.

An 8-entry RAM ring now records those peers and folds into the existing `bleShouldSkip()`
predicate. **RAM only, deliberately**: persisting would be per-device learned state, and two
identical dashes must behave identically out of the box. Cleared on reboot and on Forget-adapter,
which stays the universal "try everything again" escape hatch.

Only the "connected but exposed no ELM327 profile" outcome is recorded, and only while the link
is still up. A connect timeout, a failed bond or a failed `ATE0` is **not** evidence a device is
not an adapter — it can be the real dongle having a bad moment, and banning it would break the
one device the user actually wants.

### Escalation, corrected

`connFails_` drives both `recoverBleStack()` (8) and `ESP.restart()` (20). The reboot is the only
escalation that wipes the RAM ring, and it fired even when the adapter was simply absent —
reboot-looping every few minutes and re-probing every stranger from an empty ring each time.

The **reboot** is now gated on the scan also failing; the counter is not. Gating the counter
would have disabled stack recovery for a wedge that breaks connecting while scanning still works
— which is precisely the shape of the `v0.1.0` failure (NimBLE 2.x changed `setConnectTimeout`
from seconds to ms, giving a 4 ms connect budget: scanning fine, connecting always failed).
Recovery now re-fires every 8 consecutive failures rather than once at exactly 8.

### Also

`std::string bleAddrs[64]` would have added 1536 B to a `connectAndSetup()` frame already at
4496 B of an 8192 B task stack, and every 17-char address exceeds libstdc++'s 15-char SSO, so all
64 would heap-allocate per scan. Uses `char[64][18]` — exact for NimBLE's fixed-width address
format, and allocation-free. Skipped candidates also no longer consume the 12-attempt connect
budget.

## Verified on hardware

Bench pass against the HIL emulator, 2026-08-11 — all six checks:

1. Connects normally after the connect-path changes (~28 queries/s) — the regression check
2. Dialog opens on `< No >`
3. Knob toggles to `< Yes >`; the cursor does not leave the row
4. Three detents in one direction land on Yes — no parity flip
5. **Click Yes → the menu closes and "Adapter forgotten…" appears** — the reported bug
6. Re-bonds afterwards; the wire shows the disconnect/reconnect and a VIN re-read, confirming the
   bond was genuinely cleared

## Known limits

- **The Mac will get fewer prompts, not zero.** The rejection is recorded *after* bonding, so the
  first probe of any address still prompts, and macOS rotates its address (~15 min), which the
  ring cannot follow. Expect roughly one prompt per rotation rather than one per minute.
- **The row reads `Forget adapter?`, not the adapter's name.** No adapter *name* is cached
  anywhere in the firmware — only a MAC — and `g_obd` is file-scope `static`, so identity is not
  reachable from `ui.cpp`. Naming it needs the name captured at connect time; deliberately
  deferred rather than faked.
- Only the NimBLE 2.x arm was compiled; the 1.x arm mirrors an already-shipped pattern in the
  same file.

## Checklist
- [x] Host tests pass locally (`cd test && make` — exit 0, zero failures)
- [x] Any image I added has no metadata — no images added
- [x] Docs updated if behavior changed — behaviour is UI-level; no doc claims went stale
- [x] For a new vehicle: n/a
- [x] **Arduino core / IDF / NimBLE / BLE source / WiFi / TLS:** `src/ble_obd_source.cpp` IS
      touched, so the on-hardware gate applies and was run — see "Verified on hardware" above.
      Linked to an adapter (the HIL emulator) and saw live gauge values plus the full
      Forget-adapter flow.

author: lear111
body:
## Summary

Add a Codex weekly quota value estimate below the Codex weekly meter. It correlates locally observed official OpenAI Codex quota cost with continuously observed percentage transitions so users can sanity-check the approximate API-price value represented by their subscription quota.

Only `Estimated weekly quota` is shown; no local-device spend total is presented.

## User-visible behavior

- Show `Estimated weekly quota` directly below the Codex weekly limit.
- Show the estimate row for every identified Codex account; a newly added account starts in the collecting state.
- Restore each account's own persisted estimate for the matching weekly reset cycle without borrowing samples from the active account.
- Publish after three percentage points of valid continuously observed transitions, then update at each new boundary.
- Separate observations by Codex `accountKey` and weekly reset cycle.
- Preserve valid estimate evidence across updates and account switches.
- Normalize persisted segment state so an account switch cannot leave duplicate active segments.
- Start a new cycle after a natural or manual quota reset.
- Apply Codex Fast service-tier credit multipliers without changing ordinary API-cost totals elsewhere.

## Estimation model

Observations are grouped into uninterrupted local segments. The first usable percentage boundary in each segment is an anchor; later boundaries extend its endpoint.

```text
segment net cost = endpoint cumulative quota cost - anchor cumulative quota cost
segment span = endpoint used percentage - anchor used percentage

estimated weekly value =
  100 * sum(segment net costs) / sum(segment spans)
```

Temporary negative counter observations remain inside the segment, so a regression and its later rebound cancel through endpoint netting instead of creating another anchor.

A segment ends only when the active account changes, the weekly quota resets, or a directly observed percentage jump spans more than 1%. The first boundary in every new segment is normally an anchor. When the reset-cycle `100%` point was directly observed, it is instead retained as the exact endpoint-net start: `100% -> 99%` contributes to the accumulated span but cannot publish an estimate by itself, and `100% -> 97%` uses the total net cost across all three percentage points. A segment first observed below 100% still excludes its initial partial bucket. Jumps larger than 1% are retained for diagnostics but excluded from the formula.

Third-party or relay Codex sessions that cannot be attributed exclusively to OpenAI are excluded.

## Persistence and migration

State is stored locally in `codex-weekly-quota-samples.json`, grouped by hashed account key and quota cycle. Records contain aggregate percentages, token/cost counters, timestamps, segment identity, status, and diagnostic reason; they do not contain prompts, responses, credentials, or raw account identifiers.

Version 1 state migrates while retaining valid estimate evidence. Legacy current-device usage accumulators are discarded because transient counter regressions could inflate them.

Storage is bounded to 200 important observations and 32 segments per cycle, plus 12 cycles per account. Older closed segments are compacted into aggregate estimate offsets; old anomaly diagnostics are pruned before boundary records.

## Limitations

The calculation uses local official Codex session usage only. It cannot observe quota consumed on another device, and local token records do not contain an account id. Local counter intervals are therefore attributed to the `accountKey` reported as active by the Codex limits provider during that interval. An inactive newly added account can display its own saved estimate, but cannot collect new local cost evidence until it becomes the active local account.

## Validation

- Rebased onto current `main` and resolved the collector integration with the upstream Qoder CN adapter.
- `npm run lint` passed.
- Codex estimator, persistence, migration, pricing, multi-account selection, segment normalization, and presentation tests passed (21 focused tests).
- GitHub CI passed on Windows, macOS, Ubuntu Node 22/24, the macOS Widget build, and CodeQL.
- The full local suite completed 3,312 tests with 3,302 passing, 4 skipped, and 6 unrelated Windows permission, timing, and watcher-fixture failures.
- Windows NSIS and portable builds passed before the rebase; release artifact names were verified.

## Screenshot

The multi-account Codex panel keeps each account's estimate independent: one account restores a ready estimate while a newly added account starts in the collecting state.

![Codex weekly quota estimate for multiple accounts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lear111/token-monitor/agent/codex-weekly-quota-estimate/.github/assets/codex-weekly-quota-estimate.png)

author: the-turtle-from-1871
body:
`/items` led with rows nobody was scrolling for: devices with **no name at all**, and the `BE-XXXXXXXXXXXX` names an MDM re-enrolment invents. On the current fleet that is ~160 of ~1,200 entries that cannot be told apart at a glance.

They are now hidden by default. **A search lifts the hide**, so a hidden device is never reported as missing from the property book, and a **Show unnamed / BE- devices** toggle in *Sort & filter* turns it off for good. The count line reads `933 items · 126 hidden` rather than a total that quietly omits them, and the closed menu carries a `· Unnamed` chip whenever the hide is not in effect.

### The match rule is a `BE-` prefix, not the importer's anchored pattern

Deliberately **not** `isAutogeneratedDeviceName`'s `^BE-[A-Z0-9]{12}$`. Prisma 7.9.1 has no regex operator and no length constraint — `StringFilter` is `equals/in/notIn/lt/lte/gt/gte/contains/startsWith/endsWith/mode/not`, read from the generated client — so the strict rule is reachable only in raw SQL. Since the hide is the **default**, that would drag the ids *and* the `count` onto `$queryRaw` for nearly every `/items` load.

On the live fleet both rules select the same 91 devices, and the asymmetry justifies the looser one: a false positive in the importer refuses a genuine rename permanently, while here it hides a row that a search or a checkbox brings straight back.

### Two shapes worth keeping

- **The hide defaults OFF in `listItems` and ON in the page.** A shared service that dropped rows unless a caller opted out is a trap for the next caller; the default is a view decision. The *"a search lifts it"* rule does live in the service, because the rows, the total and the hidden count all have to agree about which filter ran — so `ItemsPage` echoes the **effective** value back rather than the request.
- **`hidden` is a real second `COUNT`**, issued in the same `Promise.all` and only while the hide is on.

### Verification

Driven in a real browser against 1,059 dev rows (27 unnamed, 99 `BE-`):

| view | count line | summary chip |
|---|---|---|
| default | `933 items · 126 hidden` | `Newest` |
| `?q=BE-` | `102 items` | `Newest · Unnamed` |
| toggle on | `1059 items` | `Device Name ▲ · Unnamed` |

Ticking and unticking the checkbox moved it between 1,059 and 933 both ways, and `showUnnamed=1` survives paging and re-sorting.

Tests: 3 new cases in the filter/sort **parity** suite (hide alone, hide + uic, and the search lift — all asserted across *both* query paths), 5 service tests, 4 summary tests. Full suite **167 files / 2,068 tests** passing, `next build` clean.

### Notes

- **No migration.** Nothing to apply to Supabase before merging.
- This changes the default view of the property book for everyone — worth telling the desk it is coming.

author: claude[bot]
body:
Two ways a clinical document loses what it was trying to tell us: a refusal the import report never mentions, and an observation filed in the wrong shape.

## Audit — both reproduce on current main (`21b1131`)

| # | Verdict | Evidence on main |
|---|---------|------------------|
| **2411** | **Reproduces, exactly as written.** | `observationRecords` (`lib/fhir/resources.ts`): `for (const comp of components) { const val = readFhirObservationValue(comp); if (!val) continue; … }`. The bare `continue` is the whole drop. `fhirDropReason` (`lib/fhir/bundle.ts`) is reached only through the `Observation` mapper's `recs.length > 0 ? { records: recs } : { record: null }` — i.e. only when the resource maps to **nothing** — so a BP that kept its systolic never consults it and its refused diastolic reaches neither `drops` nor `considered`. |
| **2411**, CDA sub-question | **No matching gap — confirmed, no change needed.** | The issue asked to confirm `lib/cda/coverage.ts` visits the nodes the kept path visits. `observationNodesOf` (coverage.ts) and `observationsFromEntries` (`lib/cda/extractors/observations.ts`) build the identical node set — `entry.organizer.component[].observation` plus `asArray(entry.observation)` — and coverage re-runs `mapObservation` itself to decide kept-vs-dropped. |
| **2321** | **Reproduces; one issue-body spelling is stale.** | The instrument substrate is intact (`recordInstrumentScore` in `lib/instrument-records.ts`, `INSTRUMENTS` in `lib/mental-health.ts`, migration 066's `instrument_responses`), and nothing in either clinical parser mentions it — `grep -rn "instrument-records\|recognizeInstrument" lib/cda lib/fhir` is empty. `mapObservation` routes a questionnaire item to the `assessment` category via `isNonAnalyteObservation` (#2318's identity guard) and stops there. **Stale in the body:** it says #2318 "stops" the per-question pseudo-biomarkers — #2318 withholds *identity*; the rows still store, one per question, which is what this changes. |

Both landed. No migration was needed or taken: the fix is at the import door in each case, and #2321's `instrument_responses` rows are children of an existing `medical_records` row.

---

## #2411 — a component refusal now reaches the report

Only the mapper can classify a component-level refusal. `fhirDropReason` is asked about a **resource**, and only about one that mapped to nothing; a panel that kept its systolic maps to something, so nothing anywhere ever asked about the diastolic. So the drops travel **out** of the mapper with the readings: `observationOutcome` returns `{ records, drops }`, and `observationRecords` stays as the back-compat accessor over it.

Each drop carries:

- the **component's own** printed label, resolved the way `fhirReadingFromCode` resolves a kept component's name — never the parent panel's;
- its **own** classified reason — an explicit `dataAbsentReason` is FHIR's null flavor (`null_flavor`); the #2322 duration door's refusal stays `unparsable_value`, because "no value" says the opposite of what happened; anything else is `no_value`;
- the **kind its own LOINC disposition implies**, so a refused diastolic is a `vitals` candidate exactly as the systolic beside it is a `vitals` reading.

A resource that keeps nothing but refuses components takes the container path too, so N component drops are the whole accounting and no resource-level "no value" is counted on top of them — `considered` counts each candidate once. The same outcome threads through `recordsFromDiagnosticReport`, so a component refused inside a report-only Observation reports identically.

The disposition filter at the tail of the mapper is covered on the same principle, but **only for components**: a scalar reading it refuses is still classified from the resource, which already reports exactly those two reasons.

## #2321 — a screening instrument imports as a score

A CCD files a screening as its individual **questions**: the question text as the observation's name, a free-text answer as its value, no number, no unit, no range. #2318 stopped those rows coining analyte identity. This recognises them.

**EPDS** joins `INSTRUMENTS` with its published items, its per-item option labels, the two published cut-offs (10 and 13) as band edges, and **item 10 declared as its self-harm item** — the role PHQ-9 item 9 plays, so a positive answer escalates whatever the total. Seven of its ten items are **reverse-scored**, which is what forces per-item options onto `InstrumentDef`: "which option is worth 3" is an item-level fact, and an inverted item is a silent, plausible-looking scoring error — the total still lands in a real band, just the wrong one.

- `lib/instrument-recognize.ts` (pure) answers "do these questions spell out an instrument, and what did it score?"
- `lib/instrument-import.ts` (pure) applies that to the parsers' `ImportedRecord`s: a score **replaces** the questions it consumed with ONE `instrument`-category record under the curated canonical name, carrying its per-item answers into the same `instrument_responses` the in-app tap-through writes. An imported score and an administered one are indistinguishable downstream — band, item 9 / item 10, crisis decision, undo.

Curated: an `EPDS` entry in `canonical-biomarkers.json` (rangeless, like PHQ-9 and GAD-7), the `mental-health` panel, a biomarker description, and `CANONICAL_ALIASES` routes for the spellings and the abbreviation. It stays a **third distinct identity** — never folded onto PHQ-9, whose items, range and cut-offs are all different.

### Both refusals are safety decisions, and both are reported

- **subject** — post-natal screening is administered to a *parent* and routinely filed in the *child's* chart, which is where these rows came from. The document must **say** the subject is its own patient (`<subject><relatedSubject classCode="PAT"/>`); a stated other subject **and an unstated one** both refuse, per the issue's decision. A misattributed crisis-escalating score is worse than an unimported one.
- **partial** — a partial total is not a smaller total, it is a different measurement, and cannot be banded against cut-offs derived from the whole. An answer the parser cannot map onto one of the item's own options counts as unanswered, so the instrument refuses rather than banding a total that is short some points.

Neither deletes anything. The question rows keep their #2318 `assessment` treatment — stored, dated, viewable on their document, no identity — and the **SCORE** is what is reported as a drop, under two new reasons (`other_subject`, `incomplete_instrument`) because "no value" and "other" would each say something untrue about a document that carried plenty of value.

A set-level refusal is invisible in any one node, so it cannot be re-derived in `lib/cda/coverage.ts` the way every other CDA drop is; it travels out of the extractor through a new `SectionExtractorOutput.drops`.

### Footprint

`instrument_responses` is a **child** of the score row: delete and reprocess reach it through `ON DELETE CASCADE`, and the extracted count already counts its parent — so it is allowlisted in `import-footprint-inserts.test.ts` with that justification rather than added to `IMPORT_FOOTPRINT_TABLES`. A **reassign** moves the parent's `profile_id`, which a child does not inherit, so `moveImportedDocumentRows` carries it explicitly.

## Tests, at the tier that can see each bug

- **#2411** — pure: a component's own label/reason/kind, the duration-door case, one-drop-per-candidate when the whole panel is refused, and a component inside a `DiagnosticReport`. **DB**: `lib/__db_tests__/fhir-component-drops.test.ts` drives the real persist path (which is where `considered` is rebound onto the live footprint tally) and asserts the refusal is in the **stored** report with `imported: 1, considered: 2`.
- **#2321** — pure: each EPDS item's orientation pinned **individually** rather than through a total, plus the self-harm claim the issue asked for — a p

author: paiwandkarem
body:
Alt is the only thing that can turn a cert number into a card, and Alt only knows a cert once it has appeared in a sale it indexed. A genuine slab that has never been listed resolved to nothing, and the page offered a blank submission form **without anybody asking the company whose label is on the case.**

PSA already works here through Parse. It was wired as an enrichment step that runs after a card exists, so the one situation where it is the only source that can answer was the one situation it was never asked.

- **Second, not first.** Alt brings the comps and PSA brings none, so asking PSA first would spend 5 to 20 seconds and a credit on every lookup to learn what Alt was about to say anyway.
- A card resolved this way has no Alt asset id, so no Alt comps, history or listings. It matters less than it sounds: PPT and the eBay Australia search both match on the card's **identity** rather than on Alt's handle, so it can still reach a price, Australian listings, the population census and photographs of the actual slab.
- Where PSA answers, its populations and price estimate are stored from that same response rather than spending a second credit on the deferred path a moment later.

**Unproven against the case it exists for.** Two certs were tried and Alt knew both, one of them a baseball card, which says something about how wide that index is. The path is covered by the type system and the suite; the real world case needs a cert PSA has and Alt does not.

790 tests pass.

author: thebehera
body:
Four CI defects that each produce a **green run that is silently wrong or silently expensive**. None fails loudly on its own, which is why all four survived this long.

## 1. The fuzz lanes ran a libquiche disconnected from the rest of the run — closes #338

`setup-linux-fuzz` used read-**write** `actions/cache` on keys differing from the canonical writer (`build-linux`'s `natives` job) in *both* the version token (`-v7-`/`-v2-` vs `-v8-`/`-v3-`) **and** the `hashFiles` set — it omitted `socket-quic-quiche/build.gradle.kts`, the very file whose SHA-256 *is* `quichePatchDigest`.

So it wrote and re-read its own orphan lineage. Receipt: run `31526973512` created `quiche-linux-x64-v7-dd62aee…` at 19:29:58Z **from a fuzz job**, alongside the live `-v8-` entries. The issue called this "guaranteed misses"; it is worse — those lanes fuzzed a binary nobody else in the run shipped.

malloc-check and fuzz-jvm now use `linux-quiche-env` and consume the natives artifact. `cargo-fuzz-bin` stays the one read-write cache (`natives` doesn't build cargo-fuzz, so this composite really is its only writer).

## 2. The cache was over quota — and the prior diagnosis was wrong

Measured **10.01 GiB / 64 entries against a 10 GiB cap**, so every write evicts something. That is why "cached" natives still cost 339s (Apple) / 204s (Linux).

The AVD cache was **not** the dominant driver (17.3%). `~/.gradle/caches` stored under **three overlapping mechanisms** was, at **65.8%** — seven `setup-java cache: gradle` sites duplicating an explicit `actions/cache` on the identical path. The key hashes collide exactly, which is the proof rather than an inference from sizes.

| driver | share | action |
|---|---|---|
| gradle-home, 3 mechanisms | 65.8% | read-only restores |
| already-merged PR refs | 80.7% of bytes | new `purge-pr-caches` |
| AVD, per PR ref | 17.3% | deleted |

AVD deletion is on the numbers: **~0.07 s saved per MiB cached**, vs 1–4 s/MiB for the quiche/Konan/gradle entries it evicts, and android_integration (13–16 min) is nowhere near the 48–55 min critical path.

`purge-pr-caches` deliberately lives in **its own workflow**, not under merged.yaml's `concurrency: group: deploy` — there, a newer pending run cancels the older one, so it would never have run during exactly the multi-PR merge burst that overruns the quota.

## 3. `QUIC_TEST_TIME_SCALE` reached one lane out of three

Set only in build-apple.yaml, yet the `timeScaleEnv()` actuals exist for Linux and JVM/Android — so the two lanes carrying live flaky issues (#292 linuxX64, #291 API-35) had **no deadline scaling at all**. Added to build-linux and android_integration.

The two `timeout-minutes: 8` step lids on the most deadline-heavy lanes go to 24: a step timeout cancels the step and destroys the report, turning a clean assertion failure into an opaque cancellation.

⚠️ This does **not** help #291's own suite — see #342, filed separately: `Http3LoopbackTestSuite` has 63 fixed deadlines, zero scaling calls, and no `:socket-testsuite` dependency.

## 4. A release published to Central and then could not tag itself

v4.3.2 shipped tonight and `finalize` died on:

```
! [remote rejected] v4.3.2 -> v4.3.2 (refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or
  update workflow .github/workflows/build-apple.yaml without workflows permission)
```

That is the documented `RELEASE_PAT` fallback firing — the same way v3.1.0 and v3.1.1 failed and were backfilled by hand. **v4.3.2 has since been tagged and released by hand**, so the repo agrees with Central again.

The tag is now created through the REST API as a side effect of `gh release create --target`, which is not subject to the workflow-file check. No PAT needed; the vestigial checkout is gone.

Idempotence is keyed on the **release**, not the tag — the state this exists to repair (tag present, release absent) is exactly what a hand-backfilled tag leaves behind, and v4.3.2 is now in that state, so the next run meets it for real. A **draft** release is a hard error rather than a skip: a draft carries no tag, so skipping would silently recreate the bug.

## Also

- Every `actions/cache/save` is gated on `cache-hit != 'true'`. `cache/save` has no restore state, so an unguarded save tars 258 MB–1 GB and *then* fails to reserve, swallowed by `continue-on-error`.
- Single-writer discipline restored on the Konan keys; the two quiche-env composites move to cache v6.
- **No `restore-keys` added to any quiche *library* cache** — a partial restore there silently yields a wrong native. The one pre-existing violation is removed.

## Verification

- **ruamel round-trip, 20/20 YAML files.** The only tool that catches the duplicate-key failure that once made GitHub schedule *zero* jobs while unrelated workflows still posted green checks. actionlint does not catch it.
- **actionlint: 31 diagnostics on this branch, 31 on main**, all pre-existing shellcheck noise, zero new — baseline taken from `git archive main .github`, normalised for line drift.
- **Both tools mutation-tested** so a vacuous pass can't fool them: an injected duplicate `env:` makes ruamel raise `DuplicateKeyError`; a deleted required `with:` input makes actionlint report `input "version" is required`.
- **The rewritten release block was executed against a mock `gh`** across all four reachable states (published / draft / neither / tag-only), verifying exit codes and whether `--target` is passed.

## Known limitation

merged.yaml's classifier treats `.github/*` as a non-code path, so merging **this** PR resolves to `flow=skip` and never exercises build-linux/build-apple. The first real test of the `cache-hit` guards and of a warm main-scoped read is the **next code-bearing merge** — worth watching that run rather than this one.

body:
# What does this implement/fix?

Synchronizes the Yandex Station provider from v1.5.6 to v1.5.6 and fixes two
regressions affecting current Music Assistant and Yandex Station installations.

## Authentication borrowing

- Reads linked Yandex Music credentials from guided setup data, while retaining
  the legacy provider-config fallback.
- Waits briefly when the linked Yandex Music provider has not finished loading,
  avoiding a startup-order race that previously left the Station provider
  unavailable.
- Updates the shared authentication dependency to
  `ya-passport-auth[ma]==1.8.0`.

## Stream playback on current Station firmware

- Detects the advertised `audio_client` capability and sends `audio_play` with
  track/HLS metadata on current firmware.
- Retains `radio_play` as a fallback for older firmware.
- Uses the matching pause/stop behavior for each playback mode and consumes
  progress reported by `audio_play`.
- Attributes Glagol state transitions to the requested track, so stale state
  from the previous source cannot turn a normal track handoff into a reported
  physical pause.
- Uses the same firmware-aware stream command for announcements and preserves
  compatibility with cores that do not expose the announcement-duration
  resolver.

The PR also includes the corresponding authentication, setup-flow,
announcement, protobuf, player-state, and project-consistency tests, plus a
small return-type normalization for generated QR data URIs.

**Source provider:** [trudenboy/ma-provider-yandex-station](https://github.com/trudenboy/ma-provider-yandex-station), version 1.5.6

**Related issue (if applicable):**

- N/A

## Types of changes
