author: billykshowalter
body:
## Summary

Completes the one Costbook CRUD gap C001-C004 left: `Division`, `Category`, and `Subcategory` previously had only list + create (unlike `CostItem`, which already had full CRUD). Adds `GET :id`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` for all three under the existing `app/modules/costbook` workspace boundary, following the exact permission split (`costbook.read`/`write`/`manage`) and soft-delete pattern C002 (materials) and C003 (labor rates) already established. See `docs/architecture/COSTBOOK_IMPLEMENTATION_RECONCILIATION.md` (#147) for the reconciliation this continues.

## Backend / API changes

- `app/modules/costbook/{types,repository,service}.ts` gain Division/Category/Subcategory CRUD. Division scopes directly by `orgId`; Category/Subcategory inherit organization scope through their parent join (`Category -> Division.orgId`, `Subcategory -> Category -> Division.orgId`), matching how `CostItem` already inherits scope. Category/Subcategory create rejects a parent id that doesn't belong to the authenticated organization.
- New routes: `GET/POST /api/v1/costbook/{divisions,categories,subcategories}`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE .../:id`. `categories`/`subcategories` list support an optional `divisionId`/`categoryId` filter.
- Legacy `/api/v1/cost-database/{divisions,categories,subcategories}` list+create routes remain mounted unchanged.

## Schema changes

- Migration `20260812120000_add_costbook_hierarchy_foundation` adds `isActive` (default `true`) to `divisions`, `categories`, `subcategories` — the one net-new schema change in this slice, and the only three catalog tables in this hierarchy that didn't already have a soft-delete flag.
- The same migration tightens `divisions_write_policy`/`categories_write_policy`/`subcategories_write_policy` from the generic app-wide `current_app_can_write()` (owner/admin/legacy-`estimator`) to the Costbook-specific `current_app_can_manage_costbook()` (owner/admin only), matching the C002/C003 precedent. Legacy `estimator` loses direct database write access to these three tables as a result.

## Frontend changes

- `/costbook/divisions`: an expandable Division → Category → Subcategory tree (all three levels loaded in one server pass, not per-level client fetches), with inline create/edit forms and deactivate controls at each level, gated on the same Costbook permission summary as materials/labor-rates. Linked from the Categories count on `/costbook`.

## Testing

- `cd app && npm test` — 1581/1581 passed
- `cd app && npm run test:integration` — 74/74 passed (Docker-backed live Postgres, includes new cross-org RLS coverage for the hierarchy tables and the tightened write boundary)
- `cd app && npm run lint && npm run build` — clean
- `cd web && npm test` — 62/62 passed
- `cd web && npm run lint && npm run build` — clean (`/costbook/divisions` present in build output)
- `npm run docs:test` — 39/39 passed
- `npm run docs:check -- --base origin/main` — PASS
- `git diff --check` — clean

## Follow-up

Assemblies and supplier modules remain outside the Costbook boundary — not touched here. Labor engine, equipment workflows, assembly builder, pricing calculations, estimate integration, price-history engine, supplier sync automation, and Athena recommendations remain future work, unchanged from every prior C-slice's stated exclusions.

Note: PR #128 (C004, equipment catalog) is still open as of this PR. This branch was cut from `main` after #128 was opened but before it merged, so this migration's timestamp (`20260812120000`) is safely after C004's (`20260811150000`) with no overlap — worth a quick reverify if #128 lands first.

## Purpose

Adds Costbook hierarchy management for Divisions, Categories, and Subcategories. The feature provides organization-scoped CRUD, parent filtering, soft deactivation, and an expandable management UI.

## Affected domains

- Costbook API, controllers, services, and repositories.
- Costbook database schema and row-level security policies.
- Costbook web workspace.
- Costbook documentation and architecture records.
- Legacy cost-database routes.
- Assemblies and supplier modules remain unchanged.

## Major changes

- Adds `GET`, `POST`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` routes under `/api/v1/costbook` for hierarchy management.
- Enforces `costbook.read`, `costbook.write`, and `costbook.manage` permissions.
- Aligns legacy hierarchy create routes with the `costbook.write` authorization boundary.
- Validates organization ownership and parent relationships.
- Adds `isActive` fields and soft deactivation.
- Adds hierarchy indexes and active-category inventory counts.
- Adds `/costbook/divisions` with expansion, sorting by `sortOrder`, inline mutations, permission-gated controls, loading states, and mutation error handling.
- Publishes shared hierarchy types and frontend API functions.
- Documents legacy read behavior, authorization rules, schema changes, and route compatibility.

## Security and data risks

- RLS policies restrict hierarchy writes to Costbook owners and admins through `public.current_app_can_manage_costbook()`.
- Application and database layers enforce organization scoping.
- Cross-organization parent relationships and updates are rejected.
- Deactivation does not cascade. Downstream consumers must handle inactive parents and children.
- Legacy create handlers now reject unauthorized estimator, technician, and dispatcher requests.
- The migration adds non-null `is_active` columns with a default of `true`.

## API and schema impact

- Adds Division, Category, and Subcategory DTOs, records, inputs, and update inputs.
- Category lists accept `divisionId`.
- Subcategory lists accept `categoryId`.
- Category and Subcategory updates cannot change parent identifiers.
- Adds hierarchy CRUD endpoints and soft-deactivation behavior.
- Replaces hierarchy write policies and adds supporting indexes.

## Validation

Coverage includes controller, service, RLS integration, migration, legacy controller, frontend route, build, lint, and documentation checks. Tests cover permissions, validation, organization isolation, parent validation, deactivation-only errors, active-category counts, sorting, loading, error, and empty states. Reported application, integration, frontend, documentation, lint, build, and diff checks pass.

- Confirm deployment sequencing for the Prisma schema and RLS migration.
- Monitor inactive hierarchy behavior in downstream Costbook consumers.
- Add explicit cascade or reassignment rules if business workflows require them.

author: volkermauel
body:
Refs #98 (sub-item **A1** — shared-key fallback removal). Does **not** close #98; A2 (broker NetworkPolicy) and A3 (rate limiting) are follow-ups.

## Summary
The per-session runtime-key change promised a hard cutover with no backward-compat, but `rust/broker/src/proxy.rs` still fell back to the shared `BROKER_RUNTIME_API_KEY` when a sandbox's per-session key was absent/unreadable — re-opening the cross-sandbox lateral-movement risk per-session keys were meant to eliminate. This PR removes that fallback: a missing/unreadable key is now a hard `502`, with the upstream runtime never contacted.

## Changes
- `rust/broker/src/proxy.rs` — the `read_runtime_key` match now returns `ApiError::BadGateway` on `Ok(None)` (no key) and on `Err` (unreadable), instead of cloning `config.runtime_api_key`.
- `rust/broker/tests/proxy_resolve.rs` — new regression test `proxy_rejects_when_no_per_session_runtime_key`: a pre-existing Ready sandbox without a per-session key yields `502` and the upstream mock is never hit.

Newly-created sandboxes are unaffected — `ensure_runtime_key` still mints a key in the resolve path; only pre-existing/misconfigured sandboxes hit the new error.

## Verification
- `cargo fmt --check` ✅ · `cargo clippy -p broker --all-targets` ✅ (no warnings)
- `cargo test -p broker` ✅ — all suites green, incl. the new test and the existing forwarding tests (which go through the create path and mint a key).

## Notes / follow-ups (remaining under #98)
- `rust/broker/src/terminal.rs::ensure_pty` and the S3 offload/restore hop (`rust/broker/src/s3.rs`) still reference the shared key on runtime hops — same boundary, to be hardened next.
- A2 (opt-in broker NetworkPolicy) and A3 (per-token rate limiting) are separate follow-up PRs.

author: kalenkevich
body:
### Link to Issue or Description of Change

**2. Or, if no issue exists, describe the change:**

**Problem:**

When a node threw, `Workflow.runLoop` marked it FAILED, cancelled its in-flight siblings and rethrew. `WorkflowAgent` turned that into `channel.fail(err)` and the Runner propagated it — leaving the session with **no event recording which node broke or why**. A UI had nothing to show, and on resume a node that failed was indistinguishable from one that never ran, even though every other significant thing a workflow does produces an event.

**Solution:**

Emit a `NodeErrorEvent` before the rethrow. It is a **record, not a control-flow signal**: the error still propagates and still cancels siblings, so no existing behaviour changes.

Emitting *before* the rethrow is what makes it observable — `AsyncQueue` delivers buffered items before it surfaces a failure, so a consumer draining the channel sees the event and only then the rejection.

The type reuses the `errorCode`/`errorMessage` that `Event` already inherits from `LlmResponse`, so consumers that know nothing about it (A2A conversion, the logging plugin) surface a node failure anyway; it adds `errorType` and `attemptCount`. The **stack trace is deliberately excluded** — events are persisted to session storage, where a stack is bulk, leaks internal paths, and is useless to a resumed run.

Two details worth a reviewer's attention:

- **Cancellation is not failure.** A node stopped because the workflow is already unwinding must not mint its own event, or one real failure would produce a burst of misleading ones. Siblings cancelled by `cleanupPending` never reach the report (their rejections are swallowed there), so the guard is really catching an invocation-level abort — arriving either as `InvocationAbortedError` or, for a node under a deadline whose timer shares a signal with the external abort, as a `NodeTimeoutError`. A genuine timeout with nothing having cancelled the run **is** a failure and is reported.
- **`attemptCount` must come from the engine's `NodeState`, not the child context.** When a node throws, its context is never returned, so a node that burned through its `retryConfig` would otherwise report 1 attempt instead of all of them. `executeChildNode` now accepts the caller's state for this.

`errorName` in `retry_utils` is exported rather than reimplemented, so the label on a failure is exactly the name `retryConfig.exceptions` matches on and the two cannot drift.

### Testing Plan

**Unit Tests:**

- [x] I have added or updated unit tests for my change.
- [x] All unit tests pass locally.

New `core/test/workflow/node_error_event_test.ts` — 13 tests covering: a thrown node produces exactly one event with its path and message while the run still rejects with the original error; the event is delivered to the consumer *through `WorkflowAgent`* before the rejection surfaces (the queue-ordering linchpin); a cancelled sibling produces none; an exhausted `retryConfig` produces one event reporting every attempt rather than one per attempt; a timeout is reported and identified; and — added in review follow-up — a nested failure is recorded once at the deepest path, three-level nesting still yields one event, an inner workflow's own `finalize` failure is reported at the parent, and the same error instance is re-reported in a different invocation.

```
npx vitest run --project unit:core
 Test Files  208 passed (208)
      Tests  2857 passed (2857)
```

`tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors repo-wide. eslint and prettier clean on all 7 files.

**Manual End-to-End (E2E) Tests:**

Not run. The failure path is fully covered by unit tests through the public `WorkflowAgent` surface; what is unverified is how a client (dev UI, A2A) renders the new event in practice.

### Checklist

- [x] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/google/adk-js/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) document.
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code.
- [ ] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas.
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works.
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes.
- [ ] I have manually tested my changes end-to-end.
- [x] Any dependent changes have been merged and published in downstream modules.

### Additional context

**This type is TypeScript-first, by explicit decision.** The roadmap's `NodeErrorEvent` lives in the ADK 2.0 Python repo, whose `workflow` module is not published (public `adk-python` is 1.28.0 and has no such module), so the fields were chosen here rather than ported. When Python's version lands, expect naming differences and treat the Python definition as authoritative for the wire format.

Per repo-owner instruction this change carries no explanatory code comments — which is worth knowing given the two subtleties above (the cancellation guard and the `attemptCount` sourcing) are no longer explained at their call sites.

author: nestor-deeptempo
body:
Closes #630. Based on `agent-refactor`, rebased onto `0d14372`.

`_run_phase_loop` is deleted, not deprecated. `execute_workflow` now begins the run record, enqueues a compose job naming the workflow, and hands back the id the UI follows. A playbook already states its steps in order, so compose takes no decision: it calls the harness once per phase with that phase as the role, and the run ends when the list does. That is the lead loop with the decider removed, which is why `arch/compose.yaml` declares no roles and no actions.

**Why a sequencer rather than a vestigial lead.** Putting a playbook through `runLead` spends a model call per phase choosing what an analyst already wrote down, and leaves a model free to choose otherwise. For a forensic or compliance playbook the ordering *is* the product: evidence is acquired before it is analysed, and the report is last because it rests on everything above it. The Python loop being replaced walks `for idx in range(start_index, len(phases))` and cannot reorder — an approval may abort a run but never reroute it. Determinism is the faithful port, not a simplification of one. The cost is that `roles.lead` becomes optional in the loader and the lead-specific assembly (`roster()`, `constrainWorkerId()`) is skipped rather than fed an empty roster.

The job carries a reference (`workflow:<id>`), not resolved content, so an edited definition reaches the next run and Python never writes to the ledger. Four internal endpoints carry the boundary, all loopback plus a shared secret; the token check moves out of `tools_router` into `core/agents/internal_auth.py`, because a security check written twice is one edit from a hole. The approvals table stays the inbox and the agent layer keeps its single writer — Python records the analyst's decision and hands it back, that side journals it.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | |
|---|---|
| `_run_phase_loop` is deleted in this PR | ✅ |
| Custom workflow CRUD is untouched | ✅ |
| Run records are untouched | ✅ |
| Definition loading is untouched | ❌ — see below |
| The definitions run end to end on the harness | ⚠️ not provable until #635 |
| Phase progress reaches the UI at the same granularity | ✅ |
| The threat-hunt definition is removed, its UI entry point routes to hunt | ❌ deferred |
| Only one hunt path is reachable, asserted by a test | ❌ deferred |

**Definition loading is not untouched, deliberately.** The front matter is now read with PyYAML rather than the regex reader, which could not carry a phase list. `agents` and `tools-used` are dropped from the front matter: the phase list already states both, and two copies agreeing is luck rather than a guarantee. All five definitions are rewritten to carry their phases, and `scripts/create_workflow.py` and the README emit the same shape — a workflow scaffolded from either previously loaded with no phases, no agents, no tools and a blank use case, then ran as a silent no-op. If the "playbook is the single source for a workflow" trade is wrong, this is the thing to change.

**Two of the ticket's premises are wrong and worth correcting on #630.** `_run_phase_loop` ran *custom* workflows, not the file playbooks — those took `_execute_oneshot`. And there are five definitions, not four. The threat-hunt AC is unsatisfiable as written, because nothing currently executes `hunt`: the UI runs every workflow as a chat prompt, so there is no entry point to reroute yet. Relatedly, nothing in `clients/web/src` calls `workflowApi.execute` at all — compose is reachable only by hitting the endpoint directly until #631 decides where the Workflows screen points.

## What refuses rather than stalls

Four ways a run could previously hang or mislead instead of stopping. All four now fail loudly, which matters more than usual for a queue-backed path where the failure is otherwise invisible.

- **An unanswerable gate.** Three of the five shipped definitions have an `approval_required` phase. Run where no mirror is configured, such a phase raised its checkpoint into a void — nothing created the approval action and nothing could ever answer it, so the run parked forever with its record stuck at `running`. A `Mirror` now declares whether it is `answerable`, and compose refuses such a playbook before the ledger opens.
- **An unset shared secret.** `AGENT_INTERNAL_TOKEN` answered exactly like a wrong token, and the worker read the same secret under a second name. The endpoints now answer 503 naming the variable, the worker reads `AGENT_INTERNAL_TOKEN` first (still falling back to `VIGIL_TOOLS_TOKEN`), and `env.example`, `docker-compose.yml` and the chart all carry it.
- **A run that dies before its terminal.** A resolver 404, a bad token or a queue flap left the record open forever. The worker mirrors a terminal on the way out.
- **A playbook with nothing in it.** A definition with no phases resolved to an empty list and completed instantly having done nothing, which reads exactly like a run that worked. Refused in the resolver, and again before a run record exists.

Two sizing bugs went with them. `max_calls` was a flat 24 against `max_turns` 8 per phase, so a five-phase playbook whose steps actually iterate died `budget_exhausted` part-way through; it is derived from the phase count now, and cost and wall clock are what bound a run. And grants were keyed by agent, so an agent running two phases got the last phase's tools for both — the opposite of the per-step deny-by-default intended. Keyed by phase id now, which is also the right unit for attributing spend. One visible consequence: the tool-approval question names the step rather than the agent ("*response* wants to call `update_case`"), which is correct for grants but worth a look if the human-facing string should name the agent.

## Known gaps, and where they belong

Deferred to their own tickets, not missed here:

- **Nothing consumes the queue yet.** Python enqueues onto `agent-runs`; `services/agent/worker.ts` consumes it, and no container runs it — there is no `Dockerfile.agent` and no service in `docker-compose.yml` or the chart. That is #635, and it is why the "runs end to end" AC cannot close here. `AGENT_INTERNAL_TOKEN` reaches the backend in this PR; the worker's own `VIGIL_PLAYBOOKS_URL`, `VIGIL_RUNS_URL` and `VIGIL_TOOLS_URL` are documented in `env.example` and wait on that container. **`VIGIL_RUNS_URL` is not optional telemetry** — it carries the approval decision back, so a gated playbook refuses to start without it.
- **The `/internal/*` loopback check blocks a containerised worker.** `internal_auth.authorise` requires a loopback client address, so a worker in its own container gets a 403 on every call. #635 needs either a shared network namespace or a trusted-CIDR notion — a design decision, not a config line.
- **A run nobody picks up still sits at `running`.** The terminal-on-throw above covers a run that dies *inside* the worker; it cannot cover one no worker ever claims. That, and a second worker resuming a run already in flight, are #633's lease, watchdog and reaping.
- **Answering the same checkpoint twice** is deduped by the BullMQ job id (`{run_id}:{action_id}`), but full idempotency is #634.

## Behaviours the old loop had and this one does not

Five, all of them regressions of shipped features, none currently ticketed. Flagging them here rather than letting them go quietly:

1. **Per-component model assignment** (#89) — `playbook_resolver.resolve()` takes a `model` argument and is never passed one, so every phase runs on `DEFAULT_MODEL`. The old path resolved per agent through `resolve_model_for_component`.
2. **Pre-flight cost estimates** (#184/#191) — the projected USD band written into `trigger_context` and each phase's `input_context` is gone. Arguably obsolete since #593 made Bifrost the authority on spend, but that is a decision nobody has made.
3. **Cancel semantics** — `cancel_workflow_run` on a paused run now ends as

author: jsoyer
body:
#500 wired the branch name to the **wrong run id** and severed the chain between stages on the first pipeline that used it.

`record_run_start` mints a run id **per task**, so `<prefix>/<project>/<run_id>` produced one branch per **stage**.

Measured on a real greenfield run:

```
developer      -> hivepilot/greenfield-probe/473   (pushed)
documentation  -> hivepilot/greenfield-probe/477   (local only)
reviewer       -> a branch with no commits
```

The reviewer is the stage carrying `create_pr: true`. It ran on an empty branch, so:

- no PR was opened,
- no adversarial review ran,
- **no verdict was recorded**,
- the release manager (`promote_pr: true`) had nothing to promote.

Ten stages reported `success` and nothing connected them. Worse, the run *read* as though the release gate had blocked — the gate was never reached.

## The fix

The pipeline run id is held for the duration of the run, beside `_governing_verdict` and cleared on the same outermost-scope boundary. `_branch_run_id` prefers it over the task's; a standalone task has no pipeline and keeps its own id.

Full elicitation: compositional addressing grammar - [@{scope}][/{path}]({**{slug}} | {/{exact-path}})[§{section}][[{start}-{end}]]. Chained multi-project @-scoping is deliberately excluded here (that's UC-005's job, since extraction already knows where it's going). §section and an explicit line range compose rather than being alternatives. Three distinct non-content outcomes: no wildcard match succeeds empty; more than one match fails with the candidate list; a missing section in an otherwise-resolved document fails but includes a pointer to the closest match. Content is always read verbatim from the source .md file, never reconstructed from index data.

body:
## Summary
- Replace `MultiLn` dependency inside `SNN` with a local, private `BatchEnsembleLinear` primitive implementing the TabM factorization: shared `W ∈ ℝ^{out×in}` + per-member rank-1 `R`, `S` adapters + per-member bias `B`. `MultiLn` is untouched (still used by `MultiMLP` multitask paths).
- Apply the TabM init recipe via the new layer's own `reset_parameters`: LeCun-normal `W`, Rademacher `±1` `R` on the first layer (deterministic 1 elsewhere), ones `S`, zero bias. Docstring now cites both SNN (arXiv:1706.02515) and TabM (arXiv:2410.24210).
- Fix the MC-dropout submodule-counting bug: `nn.SELU` / `nn.AlphaDropout` are now instantiated fresh per hidden position instead of a single shared instance appended N times.
- Delete the obsolete module-walking `SNN._reset_parameters` (init now lives inside `BatchEnsembleLinear`) and enforce `num_parallel >= 2` (raises `ValueError` — the HPO grid already floors at 2). Old SNN checkpoints are incompatible.
- Add `tests/torch/predictors/test_snn.py` — 42 test cases across `TestBatchEnsembleLinear` (21) and `TestSNN` (17 after parametrization) covering shapes, init recipe, param-efficiency vs naive ensemble, MC-dropout regression, gradient flow, and edge cases.

body:
### Which Issue(s) This PR Fixes(Closes)

- Fixes #9285

### Brief Description

Replace host-side model-test substitutions in the Kubernetes fault matrix with bounded, live operations against the running RocketMQ cluster.

The change adds reusable helpers for Broker PVC exhaustion, port-scoped network impairment, Broker role discovery, Controller snapshot observation, metrics capture, and residue checks. It runs live ENOSPC and HA promotion scenarios, makes Controller snapshot thresholds configurable while preserving production defaults, and adds a test-only authenticated gRPC Proxy load driver. author: dhh
body:
The notification history was a pair of in-memory lists mirrored into `notifications.json`, split into "pending" and "past" by a seen/unseen distinction no surface exposed, capped at 100, deduped by an id that repeats across server generations, and pruned by a 15-minute TTL. Replaying it showed five rows drawn from whichever list happened to hold them.

Every toast already writes a file under `~/.local/state/omarchy/notifications` so it can survive a shell restart. That file is now the history record.

- A popup leaving the screen — expired, dismissed, or clicked — **moves into `notifications/history/`** instead of being deleted, and the directory is trimmed to the newest ten in the same shell job.
- `showHistory` (SUPER + SHIFT + ALT + comma) replays exactly what is in there, plus the toasts still on screen when it was asked for, newest first.
- A notification DND silenced is written straight into the same directory: a toast that never showed is the one worth looking back at.
- A notification superseded on screen through `replaces_id` is deleted rather than archived, so history holds one entry for what the sender means as one notification.
- `notifications clear` now forgets the recorded history instead of emptying a "past" bucket that nothing displayed.

Gone with it: the pending/past models, the history payload in `notifications.json` (which keeps only `{version, dnd}` and rewrites itself once on load if it still carries the old rows), the past pruning, and the `~/.cache/omarchy/notification-images` copies that existed to keep long-lived history thumbnails alive. A migration removes that cache directory.

— 🤖 Claude, posting on behalf of @dhh

author: kickthemoon0817
body:
Closes #89. Closes #105.

## What changed

`IsaacTools` renders Isaac Sim scripts as Python source, but embedded call
parameters went through `json.dumps`, which spells `None`/`True`/`False` as
`null`/`true`/`false`. Those are undefined names once they land in the generated
script, so three tools raised `NameError` **on their default argument path**:

- `get_isaac_logs` (`isaac_tools.py:4562-4563`)
- `list_isaac_graph_node_types` (`:4343`)
- `query_usd_typed_prims` (`:3947`)

`get_isaac_logs` failed 23 of 24 recorded calls in `~/.simul/logs/tool_usage.jsonl`
between 2026-03-27 and 2026-06-14; the single success passed both optional filters
explicitly.

- Adds `_pyval(value) -> str` (`repr`-based) and routes **all 87 embed sites**
  through it. This collapses three hand-rolled idioms that had grown up around the
  same problem — `json.dumps(x)`, `json.dumps(x or "")`, and
  `json.dumps(x) if x else "None"` — into one, so the bug class stops being
  reachable rather than being patched at three sites.
- The two conditional sites that mapped a falsy value to `None`
  (`texture_file`, `prim_type`) keep that mapping explicitly as `_pyval(x or None)`
  rather than inheriting `repr("")`, which would have been a silent behaviour change.

## Verification

`pytest tests/` — **498 passed, 6 skipped, 3 deselected** (baseline before this
branch: 495 passed; the 3 new tests are the added harness). The 6 skips are
`tests/unreal/test_live.py`, which needs a running Unreal editor.

The new harness (`tests/isaac/test_generated_scripts.py`) renders every generated
script at default arguments and checks two things: that it parses, and that no JSON
literal is loaded as a free variable. Run against the parent commit it fails with
exactly the three known-broken tools, which is what makes it a regression test
rather than a coverage exercise:

```
AssertionError: generated scripts reference JSON literals that are undefined names
in Python: {'get_isaac_logs': ['null'], 'list_isaac_graph_node_types': ['null'],
'query_usd_typed_prims': ['null']}
```

It also carries a coverage floor (`_MIN_EXPECTED_SCRIPTS = 60`, against ~80 script
generating methods today) so a future change to script dispatch fails loudly
instead of silently sweeping nothing.

The check is deliberately **static** rather than exec-against-stubs: it needs no
`omni`/`pxr` stubs, and it sees embeds sitting on branches an `exec` would never
reach — a `true`/`false` leak inside an untaken `if` is caught here but would not be
caught by executing the script.

**Scope:** script *generation* only. Runtime behaviour inside Kit is not covered by
this harness, and no Isaac Sim instance was available, so the end-to-end fix for
`get_isaac_logs` is verified by generated-source inspection, not a live call.

**Pre-existing, untouched:** `black --check` and `mypy` both already fail on
`isaac_tools.py` at the parent commit (17 mypy `ErrorResponse` `call-arg` errors,
905 repo-wide). None of them reference `_pyval`, and reformatting the file would
have buried this diff.

## Follow-ups

`_pyval` is the helper `IsaacScriptBase` will own when #103 splits `IsaacTools`.

## Summary

FinRedOps v0.2 turns the simulation-only MVP into a durable assurance control plane for regulated financial-institution security assessments.

- add transactional SQLite snapshot revisions, audit-prefix verification, and idempotency records

author: copilot
body:
The framework had no way to build a topological map interactively while driving the robot — maps had to be hand-authored or captured via the joystick-driven `manual_topomapping.py` tool, with no support for loop closure, live preview, or programmatic control.

## New ROS 2 interfaces (`topological_navigation_msgs`)
- `action/RecordMap.action` — start recording (goal: `map_name`, `node_distance`), cancel to stop; feedback carries `num_nodes`, `last_node`, `status`
- `srv/LoadTmap.srv` — load a (partial) map file so recording can continue from it

## Core recording logic (`map_recorder_utils.py`)
Pure-Python, no `rclpy` dependency, fully unit-tested in isolation:
- New node created once the robot moves `node_distance` from the last recorded node
- **Loop closure**: reuses an existing node (via `networkx_utils` influence-zone check) instead of duplicating it when the robot re-enters a known zone, linking it to the previous node
- Nodes connected successively with **bidirectional** edges
- Recorded nodes tagged `properties.map.source: recording`
- Step history lets `delete_last_node` correctly undo either a new node or just a loop-closure link, without corrupting nodes still referenced earlier in the recording

## New `map_recorder` node
- `record` action server driving the above logic from robot odometry
- Services: `add_node`, `delete_last_node`, `reset_map`, `save_map`, `load_map`
- Publishes the in-progress map on latched `/recorded_tmap`
- Inherits map metadata (transformation, actions, definitions) from the currently active `/topological_map_2`
- Registered as `map_recorder.py` console entry point

```bash
ros2 action send_goal /record topological_navigation_msgs/action/RecordMap \
  "{map_name: 'my_map', node_distance: 1.0}"
ros2 service call /map_recorder/save_map topological_navigation_msgs/srv/WriteTopologicalMap \
  "{filename: 'my_map.tmap2.yaml'}"
```

## Documentation
README updated with the new node's parameters, topics, services, action, and a dedicated "Recording Maps" walkthrough.

author: juanmahidalgo
body:
## Changes

`setMonitoringUser` has existed since monitoring was wired, with a docstring that says *"Call on sign-in / disconnect"* — and it was never called. The only thing that ever set the Sentry user was a one-shot read inside `initSentry()`, which runs before the first render and therefore before the session is restored, so it resolves to `null` in practice and nothing updates it afterwards.

Every error report we have is attributed to the visitor's IP.

- `store/wallet.ts` `restore()` → `setMonitoringUser(session.address)`, on the same line as the Segment `identify` that already sends the same address. Both lowercase it, so the two systems share one id.
- `store/wallet.ts` `disconnect()` → `setMonitoringUser(null)`, next to `resetAnalytics()`. The Sentry user is global and outlives the session: without this, the next visitor's errors — anonymous, or a different account on the same device — are reported as the account that signed out last.

## Why it matters

Three things are broken without it, and the third is the reason for the PR:

1. **"Users impacted" is not a user count.** It counts IPs. A rotating mobile IPv6 makes one person look like several; a shared NAT makes several look like one. That number is what we use to rank severity.
2. **You cannot follow one account.** `user.id:0x…` returns nothing today, so an error cannot be placed in the context of that person's session.
3. **There is no join key to anything else.** The address is what links a report to the purchase history, to the on-chain state, to the funnel and to the warehouse. Without it, "did this buyer actually complete what they were doing?" is unanswerable — which came up on a real production purchase that reverted, where we could see the failure and had no way to find out what happened to the buyer afterwards.

A wallet address is a public, pseudonymous identifier and is already treated as safe to attach (the scrubbing block in `monitoring.ts` says so explicitly, and Sentry receives the geolocated IP today, which identifies more).

Not retroactive — existing issues stay anonymous.

## Test plan

- [x] `wallet.spec.ts` 10/10 — new cases assert the address on restore, `null` on disconnect, and no call when there is no session to restore
- [x] `tsc -b`, eslint and prettier clean on the changed files
- [ ] After deploy: confirm a production event carries `user.id` as an address instead of `ip:…`

author: kile-thomson
body:
## What

When a phone joins the device's WiFi AP, its OS fires a connectivity probe (Android `generate_204`, Apple `hotspot-detect`, Windows NCSI, Firefox `canonical`) to decide whether the network has internet. The AP answered those unmatched URLs with the first-run `/setup` redirect, which the phone OS reads as a captive portal ("Sign in to WiFi") and can use to push the phone off cellular. While joined to the device that meant missed messages/calls and a stalled OTA download.

The `onNotFound` handler now detects those probe paths and answers a bare `404` (no `204`, no redirect), which the OS reads as "no internet, not a captive portal", so the phone keeps its own 4G/5G alive and only routes device-UI traffic over the AP.

## Why a bare 404

- A `204` would tell the OS "internet works here" - a lie; the phone would route everything through us and go dark.
- A redirect / `200`-with-body reads as a captive portal and can trap the phone off cellular.
- A bare `404` is neither, so the phone keeps cellular in charge.

The probe answer runs *ahead* of the setup redirect, so it behaves the same whether or not the AP is provisioned (during first-run, the probe is often what auto-opens the setup page, so we still want the no-internet signal there).

## Implementation

- Pure, host-tested `is_captive_probe(const char*)` seam in `OpenHaldexC6_Calculations` (case-insensitive, query-string tolerant, no prefix false-matches).
- Called from the `onNotFound` handler in `OpenHaldexC6_API.cpp`.
- Firmware-only, no web-UI change. Bumped to v8.00.18.

## Tests

New `test/test_captiveprobe` suite (12 cases): every known probe URL, case-insensitivity, query-string tolerance, prefix non-match, real routes (`/`, `/index.html`, `/api/dashboard`, `/setup`) rejected, and null-safety. Full native suite: **250/250 pass**.

- **New Features**
  - Improved device Wi-Fi handling for Android, Apple, Windows and Firefox connectivity checks.
  - Captive-network checks now receive a simple 404 response, preventing unwanted setup-page redirects and helping preserve cellular connectivity.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Fixed phones connected to device Wi-Fi being incorrectly treated as connected to a captive portal.

- **Tests**

author: guillaume-osmo
body:
Replaces #314, which I closed. Your objection there was right and this takes it as the specification: `peroxy` can only do functional replacement where there is an oxygen to replace. Rather than argue that per group, this puts the test in the code.

### The rule

`peroxy` has two meanings — a bivalent joiner (`peroxydibenzene`) and replacement of an `-O-` by an `-O-O-` (`peroxybenzoic acid`). In front of a functional group standing alone, only the second yields a monovalent anion, and only if the group has an oxygen to expand.

That distinction was previously encoded one token at a time, so `peroxycyanate` was right (#309) while its equally oxygenated siblings were not:

```
peroxycyanate            [O-]OC#N                        token
peroxyfulminate          O(OO[N+]#[C-])O[N+]#[C-]        neutral bis compound
sodium peroxyfulminate   O(OO[N+]#[C-])O[N+]#[C-].[Na]
peroxyhydroxide          O(OO)O
```

Now the decision is made where the interpretation is actually chosen, in `buildMonovalentFunctionalGroup`: if the ide atom is a singly bonded terminal oxygen, that oxygen is what the peroxy replaces and the group stays an anion, so its salts ionise the metal exactly as they already did for cyanate.

```
peroxyfulminate          [O-]O[N+]#[C-]
sodium peroxyfulminate   [O-]O[N+]#[C-].[Na+]
peroxyhydroxide          [O-]O
```

### It deliberately does nothing for the chalcogen siblings

This is the part #314 got wrong. `thiocyanate` has no oxygen for the peroxy to replace — the thio already replaced it — so an `-O-O-` would be an addition rather than a replacement, and the joiner reading is left in place:

```
peroxythiocyanate         O(OSC#N)SC#N            unchanged
sodium peroxythiocyanate  O(OSC#N)SC#N.[Na]       unchanged
phenyl peroxythiocyanate  C1(=CC=CC=C1)OOSC#N     unchanged, still your mis-spaced ester
```

Same for `peroxyselenocyanate`, `peroxytellurocyanate` and the isocyanates. No token, no `[O-]OSC#N`, nothing invented — the exclusion falls out of the rule rather than being a judgement I made.

### Scope, measured

Exactly eight names change, and every one has an oxygen ide atom:

```
peroxyfulminate  peroxyisofulminate  peroxyhydroxide      peroxyalcohol
peroxyalcoholate peroxydeuteroxide   peroxyhydroperoxide  peroxyperoxycyanate
```

plus their salts. I ran every token in `functionalTerms.xml` through both builds to get that list rather than reasoning about it.

Guards checked, all unchanged:

```
peroxydifulminate       O(OO[N+]#[C-])O[N+]#[C-]   explicit multiplier still forces the bis reading
isophthaloyl chloride   C(C1=CC(C(=O)Cl)=CC=C1)(=O)Cl   the duplication leniency is untouched
peroxydibenzene         O(OC1=CC=CC=C1)C1=CC=CC=C1
phenyl peroxyfulminate  C1(=CC=CC=C1)OOO[N+]#[C-]  esters unaffected
```

These are consistency fixes, not a recall win. **No PubChem name uses any of the eight** — zero hits across all 123,543,538 generated IUPAC names and zero across the 117,515,989 synonyms (control: the same scan finds 6,881 `peroxybenzoate`/`peroxyacetate`/`peroxide` names, so it is not a dead pattern). The chalcogen siblings this PR deliberately leaves alone are likewise absent from both dumps, which is the other half of why I am not inventing a structure for them.

### Testing

Suite 684 + 1072 + 3, green, including `DtdTest`. The 500,000-name differential is **byte identical to master**; against 2.9.0 it shows only the 195 names master has already gained since the release, with zero newly rejected and zero changed structures.

Six cases added to `functionalClasses.txt`, including `peroxythiocyanate` and `peroxycyanate` as controls so both sides of the rule are pinned.

author: mekenthompson
body:
## Why / job spec

`reference/jobs/fleet-stays-healthy.md` — *"the fleet detects, ranks, and
tracks its own recurring failures… the operator never has to hand-audit
turns to find what is quietly breaking."* This PR removes a case where the
detector itself was the thing quietly breaking: a broken job that reported
`{"status":"ok","breaches":0}` for as long as it stayed broken is exactly
the silent failure the spec exists to prevent.

## The defect

`consolidation-failure-streak` (R6) admitted a `(bank, operation_type)`
streak as a live breach only when its newest FAILURE was under 2 h old
(`CONSOLIDATION_STREAK_RECENCY_S`). That guard is a proxy for "still
broken", and it was tuned against `consolidation`, which failed roughly
every 87 s during the 2026-07-29 incident.

A **demand-driven** operation type produces no new failures while it is
broken, because it only runs when work is enqueued. So the proxy
structurally cannot hold its streak. Live on the production database,
2026-08-12:

| bank | op type | streak | newest failure | last success |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `overlord` | `graph_maintenance` | **19** | 37.2 h | 220 h |
| `klanker` | `graph_maintenance` | **9** | 91.3 h | 220 h |

The page line is 10. Running the **unmodified `origin/main`** evaluator
against those rows:

```json
{"state":"ok","detail":"longest live consolidation-failure streak 0 across 2 bank/op pair(s) — warn ≥3, page ≥10","measured":{"streak":0,"pairs":2}}
```

Both pairs failed the 2 h recency filter, the candidate list emptied, and
the signal reported a streak of zero while the job was 100 % broken.

**The consequence is general.** Any permanently-broken sparse operation
type reads green forever. `graph_maintenance` is the instance that
surfaced it, not the scope of the bug.

## The fix

The per-pair psql pass also reads the age of the pair's most recent
`completed` op (`lastCompletedAgeS`; empty when the pair has never
completed one). A streak counts as live when EITHER:

1. its newest failure is under `CONSOLIDATION_STREAK_RECENCY_S` (the old
   condition, byte-for-byte unchanged), **or**
2. the streak has reached the warn line (3) **and** nothing has succeeded
   for `CONSOLIDATION_STREAK_NO_SUCCESS_S` (48 h).

Asking "has anything SUCCEEDED lately?" instead of "is the failure
recent?" still clears the instant a completion lands — which is what the
recency guard existed to protect.

### This is a behaviour change, not a no-op for dense jobs

The second arm is **not** scoped to sparse types; nothing in the data
distinguishes them. A `consolidation` pair with ≥3 failures and no
completion for 48 h therefore breaches where it previously read `ok`.
That is intended — a dense job broken for two days should page — but it
is a real behaviour delta and is called out in both doc blocks and the
changelog rather than glossed as "unchanged".

### Where 48 h comes from, and what it cannot claim

Per `thresholds.ts`'s contract, the constant carries its derivation —
including the parts that are *not* measured:

- **The window is 30 days, and that is a hard ceiling.**
  `async_operations` `min(created_at)` is 2026-07-13; `memory_units` goes
  back to 2026-04-15. No terminal row is older than 30 days. Nothing about
  a longer horizon is knowable from this table.
- **Floor, from every self-resolving episode in the window** (58 episodes,
  56 recovered, all operation types, ≥1 failure): p50 0.88 h, p95
  16.16 h, max 27.67 h (`retain`/`batch_retain`). 48 h clears the observed
  max by 73 %.
- **Ceiling**: the two live `graph_maintenance` streaks are 220 h without
  a success — 4.6× the line.
- **What is NOT measured, and cannot be**: there is **no recovered sparse
  ≥3-failure episode on record**. The six ≥3 episodes that did recover are
  5 `refresh_mental_model` + 1 `consolidation` (spans 2.01 / 4.82 / 5.99 /
  8.70 / 9.75 / 17.64 h; median 7.35 h continuous, 5.99 h discrete). Their
  self-heal distribution is a **dense** distribution being applied to a
  type whose healthy inter-completion gap has p99 28.47 h and max
  145.17 h. 48 h clears that p99 by 69 %, which is why it is the line
  rather than 24 h. It does not clear the max, and nothing sensible would.
- **Residual exposure, stated rather than argued away**: a pair that is
  already breaching and then goes idle stays breaching. The recovery clock
  is bounded by demand arrival, not by a cron. That exposure is real and
  bounded by three things: it needs a genuine >=3 streak first, it enters
  at warn (3) not page (10), and it clears on the next completion.
- **What the doubling costs**: worst-case detection latency for a broken
  sparse job doubles with the constant — a job that breaks just after its
  last success is invisible for up to 48 h rather than 24 h. Paid
  deliberately, against a status quo of *never* and against a 24 h line
  that a measured 27.67 h self-heal would have false-paged.

An earlier revision of this PR derived 24 h from the six-episode
population alone. That was a margin artefact — the review caught it, a
27.67 h counterexample sits above that line, and the honest answer was to
re-derive against a defensible population *and* document the irreducible
limit, which is what the doc block now does.

## Three-state field semantics

`lastCompletedAgeS` is deliberately tri-state, and the distinction is
load-bearing:

- `number` — age of the last completion.
- `null` — no `completed` row is **visible**, which is not the same as
  "never completed". `docker/hindsight-maintenance.sh:136` deletes
  `status='completed'` rows older than `SWITCHROOM_HINDSIGHT_RETENTION_DAYS`
  (default 30, unset in the fleet) and, per that script's header at line 23,
  **never touches failed rows** — confirmed live in the logs (`pruned 40
  completed async_operations older than 30d`) and in the table (oldest
  completed row 30.008 days, oldest failed row 25.110 days and ageing).
  Breaches only if the streak is *also* older than the window; absence alone
  must not page.
- `undefined` — the row predates the field (older state file, older
  container emitting the 5-field row). **Abstains.** Reading unknown as
  "never" would page on hydration alone.

The probe *abstains* rather than dropping a row whose sixth field is
garbled or missing — a dropped streak row reads as HEALTH, which is the
very failure mode this PR removes. Row arity is pinned at exactly 5 or 6;
any other arity is a row we did not understand and is skipped.

## Cost

The added correlated subselect is a real second `SubPlan` over
`async_operations` — it is not free. Measured on the production database
with `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, TIMING OFF)`: the whole statement runs 20.3 ms,
against a 5 s probe budget.

## Test plan

- [x] **Blindness reproduced on unmodified `origin/main` first** — the
      live-shape fixture returns `{"state":"ok","streak":0}` before the
      change and `breach`/`page` after.
- [x] **No dense regression** — a long-resolved streak (100 h-old failure,
      completion 46 h ago) still reads `ok`.
- [x] Boundary trio at 48 h − 1 s / exactly 48 h / + 1 s.
- [x] Never-completed pair, legacy row abstain, warn-line conjunction,
      garbled-field abstain, 5-field legacy arity, 7-field rejection.
- [x] End-to-end through `run.ts`: pages and the DM carries
      `"19 consecutive FAILED graph_maintenance"` / `"last SUCCESS 220.0h ago"`.
- [x] **Mutation battery, 15 mutants, 15 killed** — including flipping the
      constant in both directions, deleting either liveness arm, loosening
      `=== null` to `== null`, emitting the `measured` key
      unconditionally, collapsing the "unknown" phrase to "NEVER",
      opening the probe arity to `>= 5`, and reverting the abstain to a
      row drop. Every fixture is hard-coded in seconds and independent of
      the constants it exercises, with a pin assertion as the tripwire —
      the defect class where fixture and expectation both derive from the
      constant under test cannot recur here.
- [x] `vitest run sr

author: erikfortune
body:
**Unblocks the rest of Stream A (#612–#615).** No behavior change, no public API change.

## Why now

CI failed on #612 for a `max-lines` warning — `fileTreeMemoryStore.ts` crossed the repo's 2000-line limit (1872 on `release` before this stream → 1991 after #611 → 2086 with #612).

The reason it got that far without being caught is worth recording, and this PR records it: **`rush rebuild` exits non-zero on "SUCCESS WITH WARNINGS", while a per-project `rushx build` exits 0 on the same warning and prints `Finished`.** I checked the exit code locally, saw 0, and dispositioned this as advisory tech debt. That disposition was wrong about the facts, not just the priority — there is no advisory tier in this repo's CI. `CODING_STANDARDS.md` now says so, next to the existing lint-gate section.

## The change

The extraction that the tech-debt entry had already sketched. Moved out of `FileTreeMemoryStore` into a `VectorMaintenance` collaborator in the same packlet:

- `embedOnWrite` / `embedFragmentsOnWrite`
- `pruneStaleVector` / `removeEvictedVectors` / `removeAll` (the two best-effort removals, which every caller used as a pair)
- `tryVectorOp`
- `declineEmbedding` — already `static` and pure, now a module-level function
- `IEmbedOnWriteOutcome`

## Why this seam and not another

The store's write path is **fallible and fatal at every step** — a body/codec/policy failure, a persist failure, a codec mismatch all fail the `put`. Vector maintenance is **best-effort by contract**: the durable store is authoritative, both indexes are derived and rebuildable, and *nothing* in the moved code can turn a committed write into a `Failure`.

That is a real difference in kind, not just a convenient line count. It also means the collaborator needs nothing back from the store except a `warn` callback, so it holds no store reference and cannot quietly grow one.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `fileTreeMemoryStore.ts` | 1991 | **1766** |
| `vectorMaintenance.ts` | — | 306 |

That leaves the whole remaining stack under the limit with room to spare (#612 adds ~95 lines to the store, #615 ~19).

## Behavior-preserving — the evidence

**No test file changed.** The same 762 tests pass unmodified at **100%** coverage on both files. `etc/ts-agent-memory.api.md` is **byte-identical** — the collaborator is `@internal` and deliberately not re-exported from the packlet barrel, so nothing new reaches the public surface.

That combination is the argument: a refactor that altered behavior would have had to touch a test, and one that altered the surface would have moved the API report.

| | |
|---|---|
| `rushx build` / `lint` / `test` | ✅ green, **zero warnings** |
| coverage | ✅ 100% statements / branches / functions / lines |
| `etc/ts-agent-memory.api.md` | unchanged |
| change file | `type: none` — internal only |

## Follow-up

The stale `[P3] max-lines` entry in `docs/TECH_DEBT.md` was added on #612's branch; it is removed there as part of rebasing that PR onto this one, so the two land consistently rather than leaving a debt entry describing something already fixed.

## Summary

- keep the top-left triangular veil text black in both dark and light themes
- remove the light-theme override that changed `--site-on-accent` to white
- add a regression test that locks the CSS token cascade

## Root cause

The root theme defined `--site-on-accent: #000000`, but `:root[data-theme='light']` overrode the same token with white. `LogoVeil` consumes that token, so its text color changed with the theme.

## User impact

The triangular veil text now remains `#000000` regardless of the selected public-site theme.

## Validation

- `npm run test:copy`
- `npm test` — 333 passed, 0 failed
- `npm run build`
- `git diff --check`

author: frankischilling
body:
## Summary

Represent HolyC switch syntax without reducing it to an ordinary C switch. The parser preserves bounded `switch (...)` and no-bound `switch [...]` headers, implicit and ranged cases, source-spelled `default:`, ordered body statements, and recursive `start:`/`end:` sub-switch regions.

Closes #117

## TempleOS source references

- `Compiler/PrsStmt.HC:PrsSwitch`: header modes, case handling, sub-switch stack, and jump-table path
- `Compiler/PrsStmt.HC:PrsStmt`: switch dispatch and ordinary region statements
- `Compiler/CompilerA.HH`: internal keyword IDs 20 through 24
- `Compiler/OpCodes.DD`: checked source spellings, including `default`
- `Compiler/UAsm.HC`: bracket mode, ranges, and a sub-switch region
- `Kernel/Compress.HC`: bracket switch in kernel code
- `Kernel/StrPrint.HC`: nested switch and sub-switch use
- `Demo/NullCase.HC`: implicit cases
- `Demo/SubSwitch.HC`: a braced sub-switch
- `Doc/HolyC.DD`: switch modes, ranges, implicit cases, and front-porch restrictions

Reference commit: `c26482bb6ad3f80106d28504ec5db3c6a360732c`

## Implementation

- add public AST records for switch modes, case patterns, default labels, and recursive sub-switch regions;
- retain both header delimiters, body braces, every label delimiter, ordinary statements, and source order;
- parse switches through the shared statement path in both compiler modes and every current recursive statement context;
- preserve definition and include provenance in human and `holyc-ast-v1` JSON dumps;
- stop recovery at case, default, start, end, and enclosing switch boundaries;
- reject malformed delimiters, labels, ranges, regions, and excessive nesting with stable diagnostics;
- keep switch and sub-switch recursion under separate 256-level hosted limits.

## Compatibility impact

This change implements syntax and provenance only. It does not evaluate case expressions, assign implicit values, swap range endpoints, detect duplicate cases or defaults, bind `break`, enforce front-porch restrictions, construct jump tables, lower control flow, or execute a switch.

The source spelling is `default`. `KW_DFT` is the pinned compiler's internal keyword constant, not a separate HolyC spelling.

## Tests

Passing on this branch:

- `dune build @fmt`
- `dune build @generated-check`
- `dune build @all`
- `dune runtest` (586 tests, including 231 parser cases)
- `dune build @install`
- `powershell -File tools/verify-reference.ps1` (61 audited checksums)
- canonical Dune syntax comparison for `test/dune`
- JSON parsing for the reference manifest
- `git diff --check`

Focused coverage includes both compiler modes, empty bodies, all three case shapes, default labels, ordinary statements before a case, stacked labels, nested switches, nested and empty sub-switch front porches, every current recursive statement context, definitions, includes, deterministic dumps, malformed children, label-boundary recovery, CLI goldens, and hosted nesting limits.

## Documentation

The README, architecture notes, language guide, compatibility table, source map, testing guide, reference manifest, and traceability registry now state the implemented boundary and the pinned sources behind it.

## Generated files

No generated files changed.

## Security considerations

Switch and sub-switch recursion have independent 256-level hosted limits. Recovery consumes rejected nested switch structure without executing source code.

## Checklist

- [x] Source behavior audited at the pinned commit
- [x] AST and parser implementation complete
- [x] Unit, negative, provenance, recovery, and deterministic tests pass
- [x] Human and JSON CLI goldens reviewed
- [x] Reference checksums and traceability updated
- [x] Documentation updated
- [x] Full local checks pass
- [x] GitHub Actions pass

author: yukouf
kentwelcome
body:
## Summary

The dashboard can report Working for a session that is actually waiting on you. DRC-4134 has one measured instance, roughly one in five.

The rate is not the expensive part. **Nobody finds out.** The product exists so that nobody opens every session, so a row wrongly reading Working is precisely the row nobody visits. The one instance we have was found by a person deliberately holding a gate open under `tmux` while reading the API, which is why we have one. An hour later there is nothing left to read either: overlays expire and the ledger is memory.

This makes the server record its own contradictions instead.

## What it does

`Application._apply_overlays` already holds both halves at the moment they conflict: the row a collector produced, and the patch the ledger reduced to. When the collector says `needs_input` and the patch says `working` or `idle`, that is written to a bounded ring on `RuntimeState` with the ledger attached, and `/api/overlays` serves it beside the live ledger.

```
row after patch : working event
dispute_total   : 1
record keys     : ['at', 'collector_state', 'harness', 'last_activity',
                   'overlay_state', 'overlays', 'own_activity', 'sid']
states          : needs_input -> working
ledger attached : ['working']
leaks title?    : False
leaks detail?   : False
```

The evidence now collects itself, from ordinary use, on every machine running the dashboard, with nobody watching.

## The four decisions worth reviewing

**Only one direction counts.** A collector `idle` row an overlay promotes to `working` is the ordinary path; counting it would bury the case worth finding under every ordinary one. Both `working` and `idle` count as overruling a wait, because idle is as wrong as working for a session holding a question, and the dwell makes it the likelier of the two to arrive late.

**A ring, not a refusal.** The ledger and pending caps refuse rather than evict, because they hold live alerts and dropping the oldest could drop a standing prompt. This holds evidence: losing the oldest costs a sample, and refusing new records would stop collecting exactly when the fault got worse. The running total is separate and never resets.

**It records, it does not decide.** The patch is applied either way. Letting the collector's `needs_input` win is the tempting change and is deliberately not made: DRC-4095 and DRC-4097 are this same disagreement resolved the other way, with tests pinning it. The two directions cannot both be loosened, and which way to move is a question about how often each side is right. Nobody has that number; this produces it.

**One response, not a new route.** A dispute is read against the ledger that produced it. Two requests would be two instants.

## Privacy

A record holds the session key, both states, the two activity timestamps the reducer compared, and the ledger. The row's `title` and `state_detail` are deliberately absent, since a state detail can carry a permission prompt's own text. There is a test asserting both stay out.

## Test plan

- [x] Ran the pre-PR suite in `AGENTS.md` § Pre-PR Checks against a venv pinned to `requirements-dev.txt`, clean
- [x] 1134 tests pass (up 10), coverage 89.3% over the `fail_under` threshold
- [x] Verified the new tests are not vacuous: with the recorder call deleted, 7 of the 9 fail
- [x] Live check on a real application object, output above
- [x] Preserved Python 3.11 compatibility; CI's `runtime-floor` job covers the floor
- [x] Ran `/sync-docs`; N-6 added, SKILL.md and SECURITY.md updated
- [x] No version field was touched
- [x] Commits are signed off (`git commit -s`, DCO)

## What happens next

Once this is running, DRC-4134 stops needing a staged reproduction: read `dispute_total` after a few days of ordinary use, and the records say which of N-5's four readings each one was. The fix follows from the counts.

Closes DRC-4139

author: loom-fleet-dispatch[bot]
body:
## Summary

Epic #704 Phase 2b (issue #874): Liberty-driven cell selection for
technology mapping, implemented against issue #873's contract
(`docs/design/synth-techmap-stage-contract.md`, PR #881). A new
`native/techmap/` crate maps a `klt.synth.generic-netlist/1` + resolved
Liberty onto a mapped standard-cell netlist, benchmarked against
Yosys/`abc`'s own technology mapping on the `gcd`/`mult8`/`modexp` corpus
— the same 3-design proxy for the #520 Tiny Tapeout corpus every prior
Epic #704 phase (#809/#822/#830/#873) already measures against (#520
itself is `loom:operator-only`, not yet ingested, and no dedicated
synthesis-corpus harness exists yet per
`docs/design/synthesize-qor-improvements-survey.md` section 4.1).

**Not (yet) a `klt` subcommand** — per the contract's section 1, wiring
this into `klt synthesize`/a future `klt synth` and gating it with `klt
equiv` is issue #875's job. This is a standalone crate + CLI
(`klt-techmap <request.json>`), following `native/statime/`'s own
precedent (issue #809).

### What's implemented (`native/techmap/`)

- `liberty.rs` — a `.lib` parser fork (not shared dependency) of
  `native/statime/src/liberty.rs`, extended to capture `area`, per-pin
  `function`, and each cell's `ff (...)` group.
- `boolfn.rs` — a Boolean-expression parser/evaluator over `function` text.
- `celllib.rs` — classifies every liberty cell against the 10-primitive
  vocabulary **by truth table** (combinational) / `ff`-group shape
  (sequential) — not by cell-name pattern matching — then scores
  candidates by `area_um2 + delay_weight * delay_ns` (`delay_weight`
  driven by `constraints.clock_period_ns`, the contract's own "tunable
  cell-selection scoring function").
- `map.rs` — the mapping algorithm: realises a generic `$dff`'s `RST`/`EN`
  pins, including via an inserted `$mux2` feedback chain when no single
  liberty cell combines async-reset and clock-enable (`sky130_fd_sc_hd`
  has none — `dfxtp`/`dfrtp` are plain/reset-only, `edfxtp` is
  enable-only) — the majority case in this repo's own corpus (`gcd`'s 50
  flops: 48 reset+enable; `modexp`'s 127: 110+16 reset+enable). Resolves
  `"$const0"`/`"$const1"` tie-net references to a single shared tie-cell
  instance — this issue's proposed answer to the contract's section 8
  "constant nets" open question (recorded back into the contract doc in
  this PR).
- `verilog.rs` — emits the mapped netlist in **exactly** the dialect
  `native/statime/src/netlist.rs` already parses — verified against the
  real parser end to end for all 3 corpus designs, not just argued from
  the spec text.
- A measured correctness pitfall, fixed: `sky130_fd_sc_hd__lpflow_inputiso1p_1`
  (a power-domain isolation cell) has `function : "(A) | (SLEEP)"` — a
  functionally exact 2-input OR the truth-table classifier alone can't
  distinguish from a real `or2` cell, and it was in fact selected as the
  cheapest `$or2` candidate in an earlier pass. `celllib.rs` now excludes
  the whole `lpflow_*` family by name — this stage's own minimal
  equivalent of `abc -dont_use`.

### Benchmark corpus (`tests/corpus/techmap/`)

- `yosys_to_generic.py` — the interim on-ramp converter
  (`docs/design/synth-techmap-stage-contract.md` section 2.4): Yosys's
  `synth -run coarse:fine; techmap; simplemap; opt -full; opt_clean;
  write_json` output → `klt.synth.generic-netlist/1`, normalising Yosys's
  clock/reset/enable polarity encoding to the vocabulary's active-high
  convention.
- `regenerate.sh` — regenerates the 3 checked-in `*_generic.json`
  fixtures from real Yosys (never a CI step).
- `compare.py` — the benchmark harness: `klt synthesize` (oracle) vs.
  `klt-techmap` (this crate), both mapped netlists timed by the *same*
  tool (`klt-statime critical-path`, issue #809's accepted native STA
  engine) so the delay comparison isn't confounded by two different STA
  engines/settings.

## Benchmark results (measured, not asserted)

### Area-only cell selection (`constraints.clock_period_ns: null`)

| design | cells (oracle/techmap) | Δ% | area µm² (oracle/techmap) | Δ% | delay ns (oracle/techmap) | Δ% |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gcd` | 366 / 551 | +50.5% | 3263.1 / 4678.2 | +43.4% | 3.0676 / 3.8529 | +25.6% |
| `mult8` | 249 / 347 | +39.4% | 2037.0 / 2448.6 | +20.2% | 3.5751 / 4.5377 | +26.9% |
| `modexp` | 710 / 1326 | +86.8% | 7126.8 / 11051.8 | +55.1% | 6.0345 / 6.3007 | +4.4% |

### Delay-driven cell selection (`constraints.clock_period_ns: 5.0`)

| design | area µm² (oracle/techmap) | Δ% | delay ns (oracle/techmap) | Δ% |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gcd` | 3263.1 / 5241.3 | +60.6% | 3.0676 / 3.7473 | +22.2% (improved vs area-only) |
| `mult8` | 2037.0 / 3039.2 | +49.2% | 3.5751 / 4.6455 | +29.9% (**worse** vs area-only) |
| `modexp` | 7126.8 / 12619.6 | +77.1% | 6.0345 / 5.8797 | **-2.6%** (faster than oracle) |

**Reading these honestly**: this v1 mapper uses meaningfully more
cells/area than Yosys/`abc` on every design, growing with design size.
The primary reason: the generic vocabulary is deliberately the ten
technology-independent 2-input primitives the contract defines, while
`abc` uses a much larger compound-gate library (AOI/OAI/MAJ3/etc., which
this repo's own oracle netlists use extensively). A compound gate
collapses several 2-input-equivalent logic levels into one cell; this v1
mapper can't do that — matching multi-level patterns onto compound cells
is QoR work for a later phase, not this issue's scope. The delay-weighted
score is a real, working knob but not uniformly winning (`mult8` got
worse under it) — the expected signature of a representative-
operating-point heuristic rather than a true critical-path-aware sizing
loop (Phase 3's job). Full discussion: `native/techmap/README.md`
"Reading these numbers honestly".

Reproduce: `uv run python3 tests/corpus/techmap/compare.py` /
`--delay-driven`.

## Acceptance Criteria Verification

| Criterion | Status | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Technology mapping produces a mapped gate netlist from a generic netlist + PDK Liberty | ✅ | `native/techmap/src/map.rs` + `verilog.rs`; verified end to end against all 3 corpus designs, mapped netlist parses with `native/statime`'s real parser with zero code change |
| Benchmarked against Yosys/abc mapping on ≥3 #520 corpus designs for gate count and delay, results measured and reported (not asserted) | ✅ | `tests/corpus/techmap/compare.py`; results table above and in `native/techmap/README.md` "Results" |

## Test Plan

- `cd native/techmap && cargo test` — 27 unit tests, all passing (no
  PDK/Yosys required): boolean-function truth tables, cell classification
  (combinational, sequential, tie cells, the `lpflow` denylist
  regression), mapping (plain/reset/enable/reset+enable `$dff` chains,
  constant-net resolution, unrealizable-cell errors), NLDM interpolation,
  Verilog emission shape.
- `cargo fmt --check` / `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `uv run --extra dev ruff format --check .` / `ruff check .` — clean
  (full repo, not just the new files).
- `uv run --extra dev pytest tests/test_synthesize.py
  tests/test_synthesize_equiv_gate.py` — 88 passing (targeted re-check;
  this PR touches no Python source).

author: jandddddd
body:
## Root Cause

The CLI main guard called `pathToFileURL(process.argv[1])` unconditionally. When the module is imported from `node --input-type=module`, `process.argv[1]` can be `undefined`, so the import crashes before any exported function can be used.

## Fix

- require `process.argv[1]` to exist before converting it to a file URL
- apply the same minimal fix to the one other identical unsafe guard in `atlas-pr-supervisor.mjs`
- preserve normal direct CLI execution
- add subprocess regression coverage for pure `--input-type=module` imports and direct Repair Plan CLI execution

No policy, allowlist, workflow, permission, trigger, fixture, environment, secret, label, or Pilot PR #43 changes are included. Repair Execute #1 was not rerun and no repair was executed.

- `npm ci`: passed

author: inernoro
body:
## 摘要

接一个上游以前要用户自己去搜供应商文档、把 API 地址抄进输入框。这些值系统本来就知道——本 PR 内置 18 个上游预设，用户只提供系统无从得知的那一样东西：密钥。配套补上「加了密钥之后怎么知道对不对」的三件事：自动测连接、查看上游模型清单并勾选导入（价格由上游给，不内置价目表）、以及 Provider 删除。

同时落一条规则 `minimal-user-input.md`，把「用户少填的每一项，系统都欠他一个『我填了什么、对不对』的交代」写成硬约束。

### 本 PR 的单一目标与不变量（范围基线，规则 5.5）

- **目标**：把「接入一个上游」的用户输入压到只剩密钥，并让用户当场看得见接得对不对。
- **不变量**：不内置价目表（价格只认上游给的）；用途推断拿不准就留空不猜；删除不级联。
- **明确不做**：放开密钥必填校验面、模型池语义改动、导入时编辑用途、跨系统删 MAP 权威数据。
- **首轮基线**：14 文件 / +2207 −49。当前与基线同量级，未扩出首轮文件清单。

## 改动 diff

**网关控制台 API（llmgw/console-api）**

- `Provisioning/ProviderPresets.cs`（新增）：18 个上游预设（openai / anthropic / openrouter / deepseek / siliconflow / dashscope / moonshot / zhipu / volcengine / minimax / stepfun / xai / groq / mistral / together / fireworks / ollama / vllm），每条带中英文与拼音搜索词。含 `ResolveModelsUrl`（版本号后缀判据与网关 `OpenAIGatewayAdapter.BuildEndpoint` 共用同一条正则）、`InferCapabilities`（只做高置信推断，拿不准返回空）、`ReadPricing`（只认上游给的价格，`-1` 视为 N/A 而不是免费）
- `Program.cs`：新增 `GET /gw/provider-presets`、`POST /gw/platforms/{id}/test`（回报可达性 / HTTP 状态 / 耗时 / 探测地址 / 模型数 / 失败类型 / 逐状态的下一步建议）、`GET /gw/platforms/{id}/upstream-models`、`POST /gw/platforms/{id}/models/import`（单批上限 200）。探测客户端在**建立连接那一刻**校验对端 IP（`SocketsHttpHandler.ConnectCallback`），堵住 DNS rebinding；响应体边流边数、超 8MB 中止；发现条目上限 2000 并如实告知被截断
- `Provisioning/GatewayConfigurationProvisioning.cs`：把用途 / 价格 / 币种 / 名称长度的校验抽成公开 SSOT，批量导入与单模型端点共用同一份口径；`ToCapabilityCode` 负责模型类型名到存储层能力码的映射
- `Models/Dtos.cs`：上述端点的请求/响应契约

**网关控制台前端（llmgw/web）**

- `components/ProviderSetup.tsx`（新增）：预设搜索选择器、连接测试结果条、上游模型勾选面板（默认只勾未导入且推断出用途的，单批上限 200）、密钥前缀提示、拉取时间
- `pages/PlatformsPage.tsx`：创建流程重排为「先选平台 → 只填密钥 → 其余收进高级区」；保存后自动测一次连接并直接列出上游模型；行操作新增「测试连接」「查看模型」
- `lib/api.ts` / `lib/types.ts`：新增端点与类型
- `theme.css`：控制台底部留 72px 净空，让开右下角固定的「提交缺陷」浮标

**测试与 CI**

- `prd-api/tests/PrdAgent.Tests/GatewayDataDomainGuardTests.cs`：新增守卫覆盖探测地址判据同源、禁止内置价目表、每个预设都有走得通的密钥路径、连接时 IP 校验、导入口径同源、停用 Provider 拒绝导入、拉取时间透出、用途推断必须过导入端校验、根节点类型判定、换 Provider 重挂选择器
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`：server job 的 path filter 登记 `llmgw/console-api/**`。不登记的话，只改 console-api 的 PR 根本不会触发上面那些守卫（形状 7：守卫自己没接上线）

**规则与文档**

- `.claude/rules/minimal-user-input.md`（新增）
- `doc/debt.platform.llm-gateway.md`：记留尾（console-api 无单测工程；用途推断覆盖率 71%；下方两条 Review B 类）
- `changelogs/2026-08-11_网关上游接入最小输入.md`（本 PR 全部变更收在这一个碎片里）

## 验收报告修复

验收智能体报了三条，都成立：

| 报告项 | 根因 | 修法 |
|---|---|---|
| Ollama 界面提示「无需密钥」，保存时却报「Provider 通讯密钥不能为空」 | 文案是本 PR 加的，判据（`GatewayConfigurationProvisioning.cs` 拒空）一直没变——拿一份在真实校验下不成立的声明当成「已经支持」的证据（形状 8） | 预设声明 `KeylessPlaceholder`，选中即预填占位值 + 一行说明。没有放开密钥必填（那要动所有上游的校验面）；Ollama / vLLM 的 OpenAI 兼容接口本就忽略 Authorization 头 |
| 测试 Provider 没有删除入口，只能停用并清密钥 | 后端压根没有删除端点 | 合并 main 后发现 main 已独立实现了更完整的一版（同时查模型池引用、要求输入平台名确认），**删掉我这版，用 main 的** |
| 反馈浮层遮挡底部按钮 | `BugReportDialog` 的右下角固定 FAB（z-index 1100）压在按钮落点上 | `.lg-console-content` 底 padding 22 → 72px |

报告里另外两条是验收提示词写错，不是功能问题：指定的样本页本就不存在；「应有 7 个模型」是提示词写死的数字，不是契约。两个「验收-」测试 Provider 已从共享 Mongo 清干净。

## Review 处置（规则 5.5 分类）

A 类（可证明违反本 PR 目标 / 真实调用契约）——已修并补守卫，每条都做过红绿闭环：

- 上游清单根节点不是对象时（回 `[]` 或标量），`JsonNode.Parse(body)?["data"]` 抛的是 `InvalidOperationException` 而非 `JsonException`，穿过 catch 变 500——而端点自己声称这种情况给 `UPSTREAM_SHAPE`。改为先 `as JsonObject` 再索引。**这是同一类坑第三次出现**，本次横扫了 `Program.cs` 全部 `Parse(body)` 取值点
- `UpstreamModelPicker` 缺 `key`：勾选集是 `useState` 初始值只算一次，换 Provider 时组件不卸载，上一个平台的勾选会被带进下一个（同名模型很常见），用户可能导进自己没勾过的选择
- 更早几轮：池同步触发条件、导入端能力码词表、pricing 非对象、密钥解不开仍探测、8MB 上限、`ModelNameNormalized`、停用 Provider 拒绝导入等

B 类（建议合理但引入新语义类别）——记入 `doc/debt.platform.llm-gateway.md`，不在本 PR 展开：

- 预设拉取失败无 loading / error / retry 三个 UI 状态
- 探测耗时只算到响应头（挪 `sw.Stop()` 会改变失败分支口径，等于重新定义「探测耗时」的语义）
- 删除与导入之间的 TOCTOU 竞态（已并入既有的「带模型的 Provider 删除」条目）

本 PR 曾触发范围熔断（Review 轮次多、且我自己在级联删除上引入过一次回归），熔断后的动作是**移除**那段级联删除代码而不是继续叠加。

## 测试

- [x] 前端 `pnpm --dir llmgw/web tsc --noEmit` 通过
- [x] 红绿闭环：把 ollama 预设改回事故状态（文案说免密钥、无占位值），守卫两条断言各自命中；新增的根节点判据与 `key` 判据也各自验过「改回事故写法即变红」
- [x] **真实预览端点自测**（`https://llmgw-provider-presets-claude-prd-agent-llmgw.miduo.org`）：
  - Ollama 用预设自带占位值提交 `POST /gw/platforms` → **HTTP 201**，`hasKey: true`（用户一个字没敲）
  - `DELETE /gw/platforms/{id}` 删两个测试 Provider → **HTTP 200** ×2
  - 对名下有 13 个模型的 openrouter.ai 删除 → **HTTP 409** `PLATFORM_HAS_MODELS`，且它仍在列表里（拒绝不是假拒绝）
  - 自测新建的 Provider 已自行删除，共享 Mongo 恢复到验收前状态
- [x] 价格自动填的实证：OpenRouter 402/402 个模型都带 pricing，按每百万 token 换算核对过
- [x] 用途推断在 402 个真实模型 id 上跑过：287/402 = 71% 覆盖，0 例可疑误判，其余 115 个如实留「用途待定」不猜
- [ ] 真人通过预览域名验收：https://llmgw-provider-presets-claude-prd-agent-llmgw.miduo.org/platforms

## 风险与已知边界

- **视觉层未验证**：沙箱内 Chromium 无外网，双主题未做真机截图。上述自测走的是 API 层。
- **本预览环境与生产共用 Mongo**：验收时新建的 Provider 请以「验收-」开头并用删除按钮清干净，不要执行模型导入。
- `llmgw/console-api` 不在 `PrdAgent.sln` 里，没有自己的单测工程，唯一编译验证是 CI 的 Docker 构建 job。已记 `doc/debt.platform.llm-gateway.md`。
- 用途推断覆盖率 71%，剩余模型留「用途待定」由用户自选。同上台账。
- 删除 Provider 不级联删模型/池成员，这是刻意的：静默连坐删除不可逆。
- `host.docker.internal` 在 Linux 宿主上不可解析，Ollama / vLLM 预设的默认地址在这类部署上要用户改成实际 IP。已记台账。

## 后续事项

- P2：给 `llmgw/console-api` 建独立单测工程，让守卫不必都寄生在 `prd-api/tests`
- P3：用途推断覆盖率提升（当前 71%）

author: mszczepanowski11
body:
## Summary

Wdraża pozycję "🔴 Deduplikacja między źródłami (VIN-first, potem rozmyta)" z Etapu 2 audytu CTO — "AKOL i 44FOX prawdopodobnie odsprzedają nakładający się inwentarz dealerski", czyli ten sam fizyczny samochód może trafić do CARIZO dwa razy przez dwóch różnych partnerów.

- Nowe kolumny na `CarAdvert`: `DuplicateOfId` (self-referencing FK, `SetNull` przy usunięciu kanonicznego ogłoszenia) i `DuplicateMatchReason`.
- `PartnerImportService.DetectDuplicateAsync` wywoływane wyłącznie przy TWORZENIU nowego ogłoszenia (nie przy update — zaktualizowany `ExternalId` to z definicji to samo ogłoszenie, nie nowy kandydat):
  1. **VIN-first**: dokładne dopasowanie po znormalizowanym numerze VIN wśród aktywnych, jeszcze nieoznaczonych jako duplikat ogłoszeń — najstarsze pasujące staje się kanoniczne.
  2. **Fuzzy fallback** (tylko gdy marka+model+rok rozwiązane — nieistotne dla części/maszyn): ta sama marka+model+rok, cena w tolerancji ±5%, przebieg ±10%. Celowo konserwatywne — oznacza tylko gdy istnieje DOKŁADNIE jeden kandydat, żeby nie zgadywać między kilkoma naprawdę różnymi autami tej samej marki/modelu/rocznika.
- `AdvertService.SearchCarAdvertsAsync`/`GetMostViewedAsync`/`GetPremiumCollectionAsync` pomijają teraz oznaczone duplikaty w wynikach publicznych — ale TYLKO gdy `dto.UserId` nie jest ustawiony (ogólne wyszukiwanie), więc partner/użytkownik nadal widzi WSZYSTKIE swoje zgłoszone ogłoszenia we własnym panelu, oznaczone czy nie.
- Nic nie jest nigdy ukrywane/kasowane automatycznie bez śladu — oznaczenie jest odwracalne (ręczna korekta w bazie), a duplikat pozostaje w pełni widoczny dla admina.
- Nowa sekcja `duplicateAdverts` w `GET /api/admin/quality-report` — lista oznaczonych duplikatów z powodem dopasowania i partnerem źródłowym, do ręcznego przeglądu przez admina.

## How verified

`dotnet build` (0 błędów), migracja EF Core wygenerowana i zastosowana lokalnie. Pełny e2e przez curl: dwóch NIEZALEŻNYCH partnerów (różni `LinkedUser`, symulujący AKOL/44FOX):
1. **Ten sam VIN** → drugie ogłoszenie poprawnie oznaczone "duplikat #X (VIN)", widoczne w quality-report, ZNIKA z publicznego wyszukiwania (`POST /api/Advert/search`), podczas gdy kanoniczne ogłoszenie zostaje widoczne.
2. **Bez VIN**, ta sama marka/model/rok/cena±5%/przebieg±10% → poprawnie oznaczone "Fuzzy: marka+model+rok, cena ±5%, przebieg ±10%".

## Test plan
- [x] `dotnet build` bez błędów
- [x] Migracja EF Core zastosowana lokalnie
- [x] E2E: VIN-match między dwoma niezależnymi partnerami działa
- [x] E2E: fuzzy match (bez VIN) działa
- [x] E2E: kanoniczne ogłoszenie widoczne, duplikat wykluczony z publicznego wyszukiwania
- [x] Quality-report poprawnie surfacuje oba przypadki
- [ ] CI

body:
The screen an 8-year-old met each morning carried 32 numbers and 237 words
across five cards, and needed scrolling on a tablet to reach the button. Most
of it was the same facts repeated: each dial had a paragraph restating its own
tiles, and a third card underneath restated both paragraphs. On day three
"$3.05" was on screen three times.

The two dials and the gap are now ONE card. Money coming in is the top row,
money going out is the bottom row, and the gap sits in the space between the
two sets of tiles that make it, with the two amounts it is made of underneath
the number they make. Change a tile and the gap moves — one glance instead of
three cards. Both restating paragraphs are gone.

The loan card was a seven-row table for a yes-or-no question. "They want
$62.50" repeated the sentence above it; two rows were the working for a third;
and two more were numbers the child had to subtract to reach a conclusion the
line underneath already stated in words. Two rows now: what saying yes earns,
and when the money comes home.

Smaller things, all the same complaint — a fact stated where it was already
visible:

- The vault's bottom line read "$153.25 of the money in this bank belongs to
  other people", which is the blue bar spelled out directly beneath the blue
  bar. It is only ever a warning now, so a line that turns red is a line
  somebody still reads.
- The coach box repeated the vault's own red warning, and repeated the gap
  card's "tonight COSTS you" in longer words. Both branches are gone; what is
  left is only ever something the screen does not already show.
- Three loans coming home on one morning was three board rows all ending "that
  money is in your vault again", which on a phone pushed the dials — the only
  decision on the screen — below the fold. One row per kind of news now.
- On day one nothing is out on loan, so all three loan tiles priced at $0.00 —
  three identical zeros at the moment the child first picks a loan rate. With
  nothing to price the tile is the rate and who it brings through the door.

Copy through the game and the five how-to pages cut to shorter sentences.

Measured over a full 10-day run, driving the real page: the morning is down
from 32 numbers and 237 words to 26 and 153, the loan card from 17 and 139 to
13 and 108. The morning no longer scrolls on a tablet on any day of a run
(was up to 138px over); on a phone the worst day is 139px over, down from 944.
bank.js is untouched — 2,140,993 harness assertions still pass.

Evidence-gated review of the `microsoft/aspire` skill catalog (issue #4905). Pins the source, inventories and classifies all 23 Aspire skills, and applies one small generic augmentation to SkillForge: a Phase 0 guardrail for adapting a foreign skill catalog.
