author: mwelwa-cyber
body:
Two commits, both removing Anthropic spend while keeping (or improving) what it bought. Together they take **automatic GitHub-side AI spend to zero**.

> **Note on scoping:** these were authored as separate changes and ended up stacked on one branch. `82f6401` (CodeQL) and `6bd2846` (Ledger) are independent and reviewable on their own.

---

# 1 · Add CodeQL (`82f6401`)

#2295 made the AI security review opt-in behind a label. That took spend to zero but left **nothing looking at application logic by default**. CodeQL fills it back in for free — this repository is **public**, so both CodeQL and Actions minutes cost nothing.

Scans `javascript-typescript` under `security-extended`, `build-mode: none`. Findings land in the **Security tab**. Already proven on this PR: the job completed in **3m 14s**.

**Three decisions worth reviewing:**

- **Not a required check, and must not become one.** Code scanning reports against the whole repository, so a pre-existing alert unrelated to a PR would block that PR indefinitely.
- **No `push: [main]` trigger**, for the runner-contention reason `ci.yml` documents — a job on the merge commit makes deploys queue behind it. A weekly cron baselines the default branch instead. Stated cost: for up to 7 days an alert already on `main` can surface on a PR as if that PR introduced it, and one fixed on `main` stays open until the next run. Both self-correct; neither blocks.
- **Complementary, not a swap.** CodeQL follows taint across the whole codebase rather than reading one diff, but cannot reason about authorization semantics ("this callable never checks the caller's role"). That gap is covered behaviourally by the rules emulator jobs, and the `security-review` label remains as the escape hatch.

`test:codeql-scope` (8 checks) guards the three silent ways it stops covering anything while still reporting green: a source root added to `paths-ignore`, a `paths:` filter on the trigger, or a `config-file` pointing nowhere. The first two were exercised by injection to confirm the test goes red.

---

# 2 · Make Ledger deterministic (`6bd2846`)

#2294 fixed Ledger to actually select commits. Measuring what the model then *did* with them showed it wasn't earning its call.

**Over the 54 commits since the last changelog entry:**

| | Count | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Conventional prefix | 21 | 39% |
| — of which Dependabot | **15** | |
| **Human + machine-readable** | **6** | **~15%** |
| No prefix at all | 33 | 61% |

Two conclusions. First, **conventional-commit tooling does not fit this repo** — release-please or changesets would bucket 6 entries and dump 33 into "Miscellaneous". Second, and more useful: the unprefixed 61% are **already well-formed sentences** —

```
Move the admin shell into src/features/adminShell (#2286)
Integrity guard: count brackets in code, and catch the truncation it was missing (#2289)
```

— so the model was mostly paraphrasing good prose into different good prose.

**What it does now:** buckets what carries a prefix (`feat`→Added, `fix`→Fixed, `docs`→Documentation, `ci`/`build`/`chore`→Internal, `!`→Breaking, scope `security`→Security), prints the rest **verbatim** under `Changed`, and collapses Dependabot to one line with its PR refs.

Unprefixed commits go to `Changed` because Keep-a-Changelog defines it as "changes in existing functionality" — the honest claim about a commit nothing classified. Inventing `Added` or `Fixed` for it would not be. The draft PR reports how many entries were **classified** versus **merely listed**, so a human knows which to check.

**Real output**, rendered from actual history:

```markdown
## 2026-08-12

### Fixed
- Walk --first-parent, and run daily instead of per push (#2294)

### Changed
- Gate (b) factories: read the builder inside the factory, not the words "guarded elsewhere" (#2290)
- Move the admin shell into src/features/adminShell (#2286)
  … 31 more
### Documentation
- Record the `register` migration outcome, and mark it merged (#2292)

### Internal
- Make the scan label-triggered (#2295)

_Dependencies: 15 automated bumps (#2288, #2287, #2285, …)._
```

The workflow now holds **no secret** — `ANTHROPIC_AGENTS_KEY` is removed from it, and the header says not to re-add one without reading the measurement. When a release genuinely wants polished prose, invoke the `release-notes` subagent on the drafted section; that runs on a session, not an API key.

9 new checks in `test:release-notes` (20 total), including that an unprefixed subject survives word for word, that Dependabot collapses rather than printing 15 bullets, and that the classified/listed counts in the PR body are real.

---

## Where this leaves GitHub spend

| Tool | Trigger | Anthropic cost |
|---|---|---|
| CodeQL | every PR + weekly | **$0** |
| Ledger | daily cron | **$0** (was ~$0.10/day) |
| Dependabot, `npm audit`, rules emulators, `test:secret-hygiene` | automatic | **$0** |
| AI security review | `security-review` label | $0 unless asked |
| Mendi | `bug` label / `/mendi` | $0 unless asked |

**Automatic Anthropic spend on GitHub is now zero**, with *more* security coverage than at the start — CodeQL scans the whole codebase every PR, where the AI reviewer only ever saw the diff.

## Verification

- `npm run lint` — 0 errors (11 pre-existing warnings, unrelated files)
- `npm run build` — clean
- `npm run test:all` — **706/706 node scripts pass**
- `npm run check:integrity` — clean
- CodeQL ran green on this PR in 3m 14s
- Ledger rendering dry-run against real history (output above)
- Negative testing on both new guards

Not run: Vitest — no `src/` behaviour changed (only two roster string literals).

author: jiaweihan88
body:
@
## Why

The **Bypass approvals** chip silently does nothing on the Claude driver for at least one user. Approval cards keep appearing — on a brand-new chat, with the mode pinned before the first message.

Argus was not at fault. Every layer carried the mode faithfully. The Claude CLI refuses it: `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode: "disable"` is set by org policy, which blocks the mode **and** the `--dangerously-skip-permissions` flag, silently, with no diagnostic. Measured with Arguss exact option bag on two machines:

| requested | init reports (policy Mac, CLI 2.1.222) | init reports (clean Win, CLI 2.1.220) |
|---|---|---|
| `bypassPermissions` | **`default`** — `canUseTool` fires for every tool | `bypassPermissions` — 0 calls |
| `auto` | `auto` — 0 calls | `auto` — 0 calls |

Two defects follow, both independent of the policy:

1. **A mode can be refused and nothing says so.** Diagnosing this took two days and a cross-machine comparison.
2. **`auto` was unreachable** — permitted under the policy, honoured on both machines, and it delivers the outcome the user wanted.

## What this does

- Adds **`auto`** as a selectable permission mode, Claude driver only. Copilot/ACP/Codex advertise a narrowed list.
- Adds `auto` to the **unattended downgrade** set. It skips the `canUseTool` seam exactly as bypass does, so an unattended routine on `auto` would otherwise execute ask-level tools with no operator.
- Carries the CLIs **adopted** mode (from its `system/init` message) onto `session.started` — previously discarded.
- Records a refusal per provider instance when adopted ≠ requested, exposes it on `ProviderStatus`, and **disables that option in the picker** with "Disabled by your organization". Cleared by the providers **Refresh** button, then re-learned from the next session.
- Restores `tool_calls` **audit rows** for modes where `canUseTool` never runs, via the existing `onToolObserved` seam.

## Notable findings during review

- **The audit dedup had the race backwards.** A reviewer probed the real SDK: the observation seam fires **7-8ms before** `canUseTool`, deterministically (the CLI emits the finished assistant message before its tool-execution phase; the SDK preserves wire order). "First writer wins" would have recorded every **denied** call as `decision: auto, risk: LOW`. Now gated on the adopted mode instead of racing.
- **`refreshAll()` is not the Refresh button.** It also runs at boot, on a 5-minute interval, and on *every* settings write — clearing refusals there would have made them evaporate within five minutes. Moved to the IPC handler, with read-time overlay so a refusal also does not wait for the next probe.
- **`default` must never be recorded as refused.** `queryOptions.ts` deliberately omits `permissionMode` when it is `default`, so Argus asks for nothing — on an enterprise-configured CLI that would have disabled "Ask approvals", the safest mode.

## Deliberately not in scope

- **A local `bypassPermissions` short-circuit** in `handleToolRequest`. It would make the chip work, but on a policy-gated machine it grants what the organization withholds. `auto` reaches the same outcome inside policy. The three non-Claude drivers keep their existing short-circuits by decision; only their (false) "parity with the Claude SDK" rationale was corrected.
- **The `acceptEdits` audit gap.** Do **not** close it by adding `acceptEdits` to the same gate — `canUseTool` still fires for non-edit tools there, which would reintroduce the Critical above. It needs the PreToolUse-hook migration the spec names.
- **Deny enforcement under `auto`.** The classifiers deny verdicts are lost; only the audit trail is restored. Same follow-up.
- **The chip label for a refused mode.** The picker tells the truth; the chip still shows the refused modes label. Needs a UI design call.

## Testing

`npm test` 7210 passed / 13 skipped / 0 failed · `npm run typecheck` clean · `npm run lint` 0 errors (7 warnings, identical count to base — none added).

⚠️ **The live exit check has not been run.** jsdom proves none of this — a green renderer suite is exactly what existed while the bug was live. Still needed: a real Claude session confirming `auto` opens no card and writes its audit row, and the policy-gated Mac for the refusal path and the Refresh-clears behaviour.

Spec: `argus-docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-11-permission-mode-auto-and-refusal-design.md`
Plan: `argus-docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-11-permission-mode-auto-and-refusal.md`

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
@

- [x] Existing behavior assumptions verified by tests and exact aggregate diff
- [x] Untested gap documented below

### Data Flow Trace

1. Authenticated request enters `executionRoutes.get('/:triggerId/executions/:executionId')` in `apps/api/src/routes/triggers/executions.ts`.
2. `requireProjectTaskRead()` validates active `task:read` membership for the route project through `apps/api/src/routes/task-project-auth.ts` and `apps/api/src/middleware/project-auth.ts`.
3. The Drizzle query joins `trigger_executions.trigger_id` to `triggers.id` and requires execution ID, route trigger ID, execution project ID, and parent trigger project ID to match.
4. A miss emits `trigger_execution.access_miss_rejected` with only supplied IDs, then throws the standard `Trigger execution` not-found error.
5. Only a scoped row reaches the unchanged `toExecutionResponse()` serializer and HTTP JSON response.

### Untested Gaps

Staging/live verification is intentionally omitted by explicit instruction. The complete changed data path is covered locally with real SQLite through the repository D1 adapter, and GitHub CI is terminal green on the final PR head.

## Post-Mortem

### What broke

An active project-A member could place project A in the route while supplying a valid project-B trigger/execution pair and receive project B's execution detail, including rendered prompt, error metadata, task linkage, timestamps, and an existence signal.

### Root cause

The detail route introduced in `394b47f4f8` treated route-project membership as equivalent to child-resource ownership. Later membership authorization in `736b6e2178` did not extend the final execution lookup beyond caller-supplied execution and trigger IDs.

### Class of bug

Cross-project IDOR caused by authorizing a container scope without binding the requested child and parent resources to that scope at the database boundary.

### Why it wasn't caught

The nearby mocked Drizzle route harness ignores `.where()` predicate semantics. No prior multi-project route test executed the predicate against a real SQL engine with owner and attacker controls.

### Process fix included in this PR

`.claude/rules/11-fail-fast-patterns.md` now requires project-scoped reads, parent/child relationship agreement, uniform non-disclosing misses, real-SQL owner/attacker controls, and structured rejection diagnostics.

`tasks/archive/2026-08-12-trigger-execution-detail-project-idor.md`

## Summary

Adds a durable enforcement layer for the writing conventions established by the earlier docs-and-comments cleanup, so future contributions (from any tool, Claude Code included) don't quietly reintroduce essay-length comments, AI-slop vocabulary, or third-person voice.

Three pieces:

- **`CLAUDE.md`** at the repo root. Claude Code auto-loads it at session start, so the rules reach every Claude session editing this repo with zero dev config.
- **"Writing style" section in `CONTRIBUTING.md`** — the durable rules for humans, mirrored from CLAUDE.md.
- **`tools/test/style.test.mjs`** — greps user-facing docs and source-file comments for banned slop terms and third-person voice. Runs as part of `npm test`.

`.gitignore` un-ignores `CLAUDE.md` so it ships.

## Scope of the style test

**In scope**
- `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/*.md`
- Source comments and docstrings under `plugin/` and `tools/` (excluding `plugin/examples/`, `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `.venv/`, `__pycache__/`, and test files)

**Deliberately out of scope**
- `SETUP.md` and everything under `plugin/{commands,agents,skills}/` — these are Claude-instruction files where "the user" is the correct third-person reference (Claude is being told what the user's experience should be).
- `docs/walkthroughs/`, `examples/*/passes/` — historical records.

## No shipped code changed

Only 4 files touched: `.gitignore` (3-line removal), `CLAUDE.md` (new), `CONTRIBUTING.md` (new section), `tools/test/style.test.mjs` (new). No plugin code, no adapters, no policies, no scripts.

## Test plan

author: dejeune
body:
<!-- Template from https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/main/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md?-->
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:
1. Consider creating this PR as draft: https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

> ### Branch strategy
>
> - Active development targets `main`.
> - v1 maintenance targets `v1`; forward-port fixes to `main` separately when needed.

### What this PR does

Before this PR: every Agent session spawned the bundled Claude Agent SDK CLI with telemetry left at its defaults, so the subprocess kept calling `api.anthropic.com` in the background — `POST /api/event_logging/v2/batch`, `GET /api/claude_cli/bootstrap`, `GET /api/claude_code_penguin_mode`, `GET /api/claude_code/organizations/metrics_enabled` — even for users on a third-party provider (see the packet capture in #18429).

After this PR: `buildEnvironment` sets `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1` in the subprocess env, the CLI's umbrella privacy switch that covers Statsig-style event logging, Sentry-style error reporting, the bootstrap/fast-mode config fetches, GrowthBook feature flags and the autoupdater.

Fixes #18429

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made: the value is set in the base env *before* the agent `env_vars` merge and is deliberately **not** added to `BLOCKED_ENV_KEYS`, so a user who wants telemetry back can set `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC: ""` on an agent (per the docs, empty = off) — that keeps the escape hatch without shipping a new settings surface for a one-line default.

The following alternatives were considered: (a) a dedicated Settings toggle + Preference key, rejected as unnecessary given the `env_vars` override already exists; (b) the narrower `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` / `DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING` pair, rejected because they leave `/api/claude_cli/bootstrap` and the fast-mode config fetch running — the umbrella flag is a strict superset.

Links to places where the discussion took place: https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/18429, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars

### Breaking changes

None for users. Anyone who *wants* the SDK's telemetry (or an org relying on Anthropic-side Claude Code metrics) must now opt back in with an agent `env_vars` entry of `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC: ""`.

### Special notes for your reviewer

Two things were verified against the bundled CLI binary (`claude-agent-sdk` 0.3.220 → claude-code 2.1.220) rather than assumed:

- **Local dev tracing is unaffected.** `ClaudeCodeTraceBridgeService` drives the trace bridge with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY` / `CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA` / `ENABLE_BETA_TRACING_DETAILED` + OTLP endpoints; none of those gates consult the essential-traffic flag. The only thing the flag removes from the OTel pipeline is the first-party metric reader that exports to `api.anthropic.com/api/claude_code/metrics`, not anything bound for the local collector. The 1P event pipeline that *is* switched off (`logEventTo1P`) is a separate logger from the one the local collector reads.
- **Fast mode still works.** The org check behind `/api/claude_code_penguin_mode` is skipped, but because Cherry passes `settings.fastMode` explicitly, the CLI forgives the resulting "unknown" state and keeps fast mode enabled — no extra env var needed.

`buildEnvironment` is the single source of the subprocess env for every spawn path (turn, warm query, prewarm), so this one line covers them all. The Code page's external CLI is untouched: it runs under the user's own config, where this key is already exposed as a managed key.

`pnpm build:check` passes except for a pre-existing flake in `scripts/__tests__/fix-tailwind-canonical-classes.test.ts` (20s timeout under full-suite load; passes in isolation, unrelated to this change).

### Checklist

This checklist is not enforcing, but it's a reminder of items that could be relevant to every PR.
Approvers are expected to review this list.

- [x] Branch: This PR targets the correct branch — `main` for active development, `v1` for v1 maintenance fixes
- [x] PR: The PR description is expressive enough and will help future contributors
- [x] Code: [Write code that humans can understand](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Martin_Fowler#code-for-humans) and [Keep it simple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KISS_principle)
- [x] Refactor: You have [left the code cleaner than you found it (Boy Scout Rule)](https://learning.oreilly.com/library/view/97-things-every/9780596809515/ch08.html)
- [x] Upgrade: Impact of this change on upgrade flows was considered and addressed if required
- [x] Documentation: A [user-guide update](https://docs.cherry-ai.com) was considered and is present (link) or not required. Check this only when the PR introduces or changes a user-facing feature or behavior.
- [x] Self-review: I have reviewed my own code (e.g., via [`/gh-pr-review`](/.claude/skills/gh-pr-review/SKILL.md), `gh pr diff`, or GitHub UI) before requesting review from others

### Release note

```release-note
Agent sessions now run the Claude Agent SDK with non-essential traffic disabled, so the bundled CLI no longer sends telemetry, error reports or background config fetches to Anthropic.
```

body:
## Hvad

Første delopgave mod automatisk PL-facit (opgave #7) — og fundamentet for kickoff-synken (#10). Ren server-side; ingen klient-, rules- eller dataændringer.

- **`syncProviders.js`**: alt kilde-specifikt (URL'er, parsing, status-oversættelse, dokument-genfinding) bor nu i én provider pr. kilde bag en fast kontrakt: `hentFaerdige`, `hentLive`, `hentStandings`, `resolveDocs`. Superliga-provideren er flyttet herover uændret; pulselive (PL) er næste PR.
- **Kernerne i `superligaSync.js`** (vagter, batching, heartbeat, rækkefølge, tidlige exits) er adfærdsmæssigt urørte: **alle 117 eksisterende synk-tests kører grønt uden én rettet linje.**
- **`SYNCED_GAMES`**: statisk liste over synkede spil — nul Firestore-opslag pr. minut, og et produktionsdokument uden `sync`-felt kan ikke tabe et spil ud af synken. Paritetstest mod `scripts/games.mjs` med en tripwire: implementeres en provider, kræver testen at dens spil kommer med i listen.
- **Minut-synk, sweep og strandede-alarmen** løber over hele spil-listen — før dækkede alarmen kun Superligaen.
- **`syncSuperligaResultsNow`** tager valgfrit `gameId` (kun fra listen); uden argument Superligaen som altid.
- **Runde-Botten** er liga-neutral ("en rundes egen uge") med indholds-assertion.
- **`scripts/probe-pulselive.mjs` + fixtures**: pulselives shapes dokumenteret i repoet (period/matchWeek, tidszone-løs kickoff + Europe/London, compSeason-opslag, standings).

## Rollernes konklusioner

Alle fire roller kørt; alle fund lukket og modbevist:

- **Test Manager** ("ikke klar" i første runde): 7 mutationer dræbt, 3 overlevede — snittets bærende klausul (kernerne bruger providerens `resolveDocs`) var ubevist, fordi Superligaens oversættelse er en identitet. Lukket med en fake provider med `sourceKey ≠ dokument-id` i begge kerner + bevis for at flerspils-kørslen kører ALLE spil. Alle 5 mutationer kørt igen som modprøve — røde.
- **Quality Control** ("land med forbehold"): adfærds-diff for Superligaen efterprøvet led for led — ingen. Fund lukket: `games.mjs`-kommentaren beskrev et hul, denne gren netop lukkede (omskrevet til det tilbageværende); `sync.tournamentId` var dekorativt (bruges nu i URL'en); forældet `architecture.md`-tekst rettet. **Efter-deploy-tjek til operatøren: logtekster skiftede fra "Superliga-synk:" til "Synk superliga2627:" — evt. log-baserede alarmer i GCP på de gamle strenge skal opdateres.**
- **Security Reviewer** (ingen blokerende fund): `gameId`-argumentet PoC-testet mod 13 fjendtlige input — alle afvist, brugerens værdi når aldrig en Firestore-sti; auth-tjek urørt foran. Hærdning gennemført: `Object.hasOwn` i de tre `PROVIDERS`-vagter. Fixtures indeholder ingen hemmeligheder.
- **Release Manager**: deploy STRAKS efter merge (onsdag/torsdag — ikke fredag, hvor SL spiller) via `deploy-platform.yml` med kun `deployFunctions: true` (deployer bekræftet hele platform-codebasen; den misvisende label er rettet i denne PR). Verifikation: time-sweeps kl. xx:25 som røgtest mod den ægte SL-API; fredagens første SL-kamp er facitprøven. Rollback: `git revert` + redeploy.

## Test

- `npm --prefix functions-platform test` — 436 tests, inkl. nye: paritet SYNCED_GAMES ⇄ games.mjs, provider-tripwire, fake-provider-kontrakten i begge kerner, flerspils-kørslen, liga-neutral recap-prompt

author: pengcuo
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #314. Adds a four-line TODO at each of the four DROID forward-dynamics notebooks, next to the block that normalizes actions outside the dataset.

No behavior change — comments only.

## Why

#314 made the notebooks normalize DROID actions themselves. That works, but it is a workaround at the wrong layer: `DROIDLeRobotDataset` ignores `action_normalization` and cannot resolve its own bundled stats, so the notebooks compensate. The real fix is **NVIDIA/cosmos-framework#182**.

Two reasons to say so in the notebooks rather than only in the PR:

- **Cookbooks get copied.** Without a note, five lines of stats loading and normalizer construction become the reference way to load DROID actions, and it spreads into user code.
- **It will silently rot.** All four notebooks construct the dataset relying on `action_normalization` defaulting to `None`. That default was `"quantile"` before cosmos-framework#86 changed it. If it is ever restored, these notebooks would normalize twice — no error, just actions off by the same order of magnitude that #314 fixed.

## After cosmos-framework#182 lands

Each block collapses to one keyword argument:

```python
droid_dataset = DROIDMergedLeRobotDataset(
    root=droid_dataset_root, chunk_length=chunk_length,
    action_normalization="quantile_rot",
)
```

and `assets/actions/droid_normalization_stats.json` can be deleted — its values are bit-identical to the framework's bundled `droid_lerobot_stats.json` (verified, `max|diff| = 0.0000000000`).

## What & why

Residual task #48 — rider RJM realignment. `offer_food` (a HIGH-risk accept-offer screen) is **deferred**, recorded in `adopted.mjs` (registry-only; `food-offer.tsx` byte-identical/untouched — `acceptFoodDispatch`/`declineFoodDispatch`/the offer poll are provably unchanged). Guarded count unchanged at **36/36** congruent; depcruise 0 errors.

**Why (a safety wall, not a codegen gap):** the RJM `offer_food` mock draws ONE static variant — cash-collect. The live screen is a three-way money-variant decision (`foodOfferVariant` from `merchantPaymentMethod`/`merchantCashRule`):
- `cash_collect` — the mock's case;
- `cash_upfront` — **the rider fronts their own cash**: a danger-wash "this kitchen asks you to pay first / only accept if you're carrying $X" warning + a variant-aware accept label `Accept · front $15.50`;
- `wallet` — customer already paid.

Restructuring to the single-variant mock would **drop the cash_upfront own-cash danger warning and the money-commitment accept label** — a money-safety regression on the accept path. `not-drawn⇒not-rendered` governs cosmetic extras, not a live money-risk differentiation the backend drives. The app is in fact aligned to the richer sibling current mock `RR.offer_cash` (see `docs/parity/PHASE5-riderjobs.md`); `RJM.offer_food` is the no-countdown flag branch and is a simplification of it.

**This reads as a mock gap:** the app correctly *exceeds* the RJM mock for money-safety. The sanctioned resolution is a `docs/DESIGN-DEVIATIONS.md` entry (user-approved) + reporting the missing cash-upfront variant upstream — held for owner decision.

## Risk & rollout

author: copybara-service[bot]
body:
PR #47084: [XLA] Treat unknown custom calls as dynamic in value inference instead of erroring

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/47084

## 📝 Summary of Changes

Fixes #45839.

`ValueInference::AnalyzeIsDynamic` returns an `InvalidArgument` error when the graph contains any custom call other than `SetBound` or `Sharding`. That includes custom calls XLA emits itself: `tf.linalg.qr` is lowered by the builder library (`xla/hlo/builder/lib/qr.cc`) to the `Qr` and `ProductOfElementaryHouseholderReflectors` custom calls, so asking value inference about anything downstream of a QR decomposition kills the whole compilation with an error carrying a raw proto dump (that's the "goo.gle/debugstr" in the issue title, it is just protobuf redaction).

This change makes the unknown-custom-call case answer conservatively instead: everything in the result is dynamic, via the existing `CreateAllDynamicResult` helper. That is the same fallback the function already uses for `kWhile`, `kSend`/`kRecv` and unhandled opcodes, and it is what `AnalyzeConstant` already expects: its custom-call case returns a garbage literal with a comment saying it "will be masked out later" by exactly this dynamism mask. Since every `AnalyzeConstant` mode computes the dynamism mask first, the fix also stops the same error coming out of constant/bound queries.

## 🎯 Justification

With this fix, tf2xla's compile-time-constant resolution gets a clean "this value is not a compile-time constant" answer for values coming out of a QR decomposition, and reports its normal actionable diagnostic instead of an internal error. Programs where a custom call only sits near (not on) the queried path now compile. The conservative answer can never be wrong, it can only miss a folding opportunity, and before this change the same query errored anyway.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

Three new tests in `xla/hlo/builder/value_inference_test.cc`, all failing before the fix and passing after:

- `UnknownCustomCallIsConservativelyDynamic`: `AnalyzeIsDynamic` on an unknown custom call returns all-dynamic instead of an error.
- `QrCustomCallsAreConservativelyDynamic`: the issue's graph shape (Qr tuple custom call, GTEs, reflectors custom call, reduce), the exact question tf2xla asks for `Range`'s limit, plus direct queries of the tuple-shaped custom call and of a tuple element.
- `AnalyzeConstantOnCustomCallReportsUnknown`: `AnalyzeConstant` in all three modes reports "unknown value" instead of erroring.

`bazel test //xla/hlo/builder:value_inference_test` and `bazel test //xla/hlo/builder:xla_builder_test` pass.

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

Not applicable, the change is in builder-level analysis and fully covered by the unit tests above (CPU-only, no GPU needed).
Copybara import of the project:

--
e77d9a8585849ae77445169929d7a574a7efb87f by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

[XLA] Treat unknown custom calls as dynamic in value inference instead of erroring

ValueInference::AnalyzeIsDynamic returned InvalidArgument for any custom
call other than SetBound/Sharding, killing compilation even for custom
calls XLA emits itself (tf.linalg.qr lowers to the Qr and
ProductOfElementaryHouseholderReflectors custom calls). Since every
AnalyzeConstant mode computes the dynamism mask first, the error escaped
from all value-inference queries, and AnalyzeConstant's own custom-call
handling already assumed the mask would cover its garbage literal.

Answer conservatively instead: an opaque custom call's result is fully
dynamic, the same fallback already used for kWhile and unhandled opcodes.

Fixes #45839.

Merging this change closes #47084

author: huajq
body:
## What

Two small changes that reduce the API server's idle/background memory
footprint:

1. Tune jemalloc through an embedded `malloc_conf` string
   (`dirty_decay_ms:1000,muzzy_decay_ms:1000,background_thread:true`).
2. Pin the Firecracker warm pool's private Tokio runtime to a single
   worker thread.

## Why

A production memory audit showed two server-side hygiene issues:

- After bursts (RocksDB opens, image resolution, template builds),
  server RSS climbs and is slow to fall back: jemalloc's default
  dirty-page decay is 10s (`muzzy_decay_ms` defaults to 0, i.e.
  immediate), so burst pages linger as retained RSS well after the
  burst. Shortening both to 1s returns them within ~2s.
  Note on mechanism: background purging threads are already active —
  the `background_threads` cargo feature makes `tikv-jemalloc-sys`
  bake `background_thread:true` into the jemalloc build via
  `--with-malloc-conf` (build.rs). It is included in the string only
  for explicitness; the effective change here is the decay tuning.
- The Firecracker pool's owned runtime uses the default multi-thread
  builder, parking one worker thread per CPU core for the process
  lifetime, although it only drives occasional I/O-bound `block_on`
  calls from the maintenance thread.

## Related issue

N/A — small performance hygiene change from a direct memory audit; no
tracking issue.

## Scope and non-goals

- In scope: server allocator decay tuning; pool runtime thread count.
- Out of scope: ublk-daemon memory (it does not use jemalloc), guest
  memory, and any pool watermark/sizing changes.

## Design and behavior changes

- `malloc_conf` is jemalloc's link-time configuration mechanism and is
  parsed at allocator init, before `main()`; the TOML config system
  therefore cannot express these settings. Precedence (lowest first):
  build-time `config_malloc_conf` (already carries
  `background_thread:true`), link-time `malloc_conf` symbol (this
  change), `/etc/malloc.conf`, `MALLOC_CONF` env var — later sources
  win per key, so deployments keep an env-level override hatch.
- The pool runtime keeps `new_multi_thread()` with `worker_threads(1)`,
  so the existing spawn-based fill logic behaves identically on one
  worker; pool refill concurrency is unchanged (driven by
  `fill_concurrency`, cooperative on the single worker).

## Compatibility and operations

- Public API or generated protocol: N/A — untouched.
- Configuration or defaults: no config changes; `MALLOC_CONF` remains
  available as a per-environment override.
- Snapshot manifest, artifact layout, or storage format: N/A.
- Upgrade and rollback: revert-safe; no state migration.
- Host requirements, permissions, ports, or dependencies: none added.

## Validation

- [x] `make fmt`
- [x] `make clippy`
- [ ] `make test-unit` 
- [ ] Relevant Rust integration tests — skipped: no sandbox-lifecycle
      behavior change; changes are allocator tuning and a runtime
      worker-count setting covered by existing unit tests.
- [ ] `make -C services test` — N/A: `services/` untouched.
- [ ] Generated clients/server regenerated — N/A: no generated code.
- [ ] Documentation updated — N/A: no user-facing configuration added;
      `MALLOC_CONF` is jemalloc's built-in override channel.
- [ ] Benchmarks or performance comparison completed — skipped: change
      affects memory retention timing and idle thread count, not a
      latency/throughput path.

Commands and results:

```text
$ make fmt          # cargo fmt --all -- --check — clean
$ make clippy       # workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings — clean
$ make test-unit    # 700 passed, 1 failed (pre-existing, see above)
$ nm target/release/server | grep malloc_conf
000000000397c378 d config_malloc_conf   # build-time baked conf (background_thread:true)
000000000396bc40 D malloc_conf          # this change (link-time symbol)
$ MALLOC_CONF="abort_conf:true" ./target/release/server --setup-only
# exit 0 — embedded config string parses; all options valid
```

Skipped checks and reasons: integration tests and benchmarks (no
lifecycle or latency-path change); test-unit failure is pre-existing on
the base commit in a root test environment, unrelated to these files.

## Risks and reviewer notes

- jemalloc: shorter decay means more frequent `madvise` purging after
  bursts; the purging runs on jemalloc's background thread (already
  enabled at build time), so the allocation path is unaffected. Config
  validity verified with an `abort_conf:true` smoke run.
- Pool runtime: single worker serializes maintenance `block_on` work;
  refill stays I/O-bound and off the sandbox critical path.
- Review focus: `src/bin/server.rs` (new exported symbol),
  `src/sandbox/firecracker/pool.rs` (`worker_threads`).

## Checklist

- [x] The PR contains one coherent change and no unrelated formatting or
      refactoring.
- [x] New behavior is covered by tests, or I explained why testing is
      impractical.
- [x] Logs and examples contain no credentials, tokens, or private
      registry information.
- [x] I did not manually edit generated code without updating its
      source and regenerating it.

author: copilot
body:
The Deploy job intermittently fails with `curl` exit code 22 (HTTP error) when triggering Render deploys — runs 17–19, 21, and 26 failed while 20, 22–25 succeeded with no workflow changes between them. The workflow syntax was correct throughout; the failures are transient Render API errors.

## Changes

- **Retry on transient failures**: Added `--retry 3 --retry-delay 10 --retry-all-errors` to both curl calls (trigger + status poll), so transient 4xx/5xx responses from Render are retried up to 3 times before failing the job.
- **Safer status polling**: Refactored the status-check curl from a direct pipe into `python3` to capture the response first, avoiding a cryptic JSON parse error if curl ultimately fails after all retries.

```yaml
# Before
STATUS=$(curl -sf \
  "https://api.render.com/v1/services/.../deploys/$DEPLOY_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: ****** secrets.RENDER_API_KEY }}" \
  | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['status'])")

# After
DEPLOY_RESP=$(curl -sf --retry 3 --retry-delay 10 --retry-all-errors \
  "https://api.render.com/v1/services/.../deploys/$DEPLOY_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: ****** secrets.RENDER_API_KEY }}")
STATUS=$(echo "$DEPLOY_RESP" | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['status'])")
```

author: ardalanazimian
body:
## What

Follow-up to the merged `#1` (Rezv AI Agency OS). The user asked for a deep
review of `backup/`, `deploy/`, `e2e/`, `loadtest/`, `observability/`,
`standalone/`, `tools/`, `shared/`, `.env.example`, and ~15 root-level docs
that hadn't been touched by the prior update. This PR is the result — real,
live-verified fixes where things were actually broken, and an honest
"checked, no change needed" for the things that weren't.

## Real bugs found and fixed

1. **`tools/build-standalone.py` — `standalone/customer.html` was
   completely broken, only caught by opening it in a real browser:**
   `CUSTOMER_ORDER` was missing 11 of 29 real modules (`analytics.js`,
   `api-core.js`, `data/booking.js`, `waitlist.js`, 7× `features/*`).
   Since `api.js` imports `httpJson`/`resolveApiBase` from `api-core.js`,
   every real API call in the standalone build threw `ReferenceError`.
   After adding the missing modules, two more real collisions surfaced —
   `pull-refresh.js` and `swipe-actions.js` both declare top-level
   `THRESHOLD`, `_busy`, and functions `reduced`/`onMove`/`onStart` — fine
   as separate ES modules, but a hard `SyntaxError` (or silent function
   overwrite) once concatenated into one classic script. Fixed at the
   class level, not just those two files: any module with zero `export`
   statements now gets auto-wrapped in an IIFE, simulating ES module
   isolation for every current and future zero-export module.
   **Verified live**: all three `standalone/*.html` opened via Playwright/
   real Chromium on `file://`, zero console/page errors.
2. **`docker-compose.observability.yml` — Prometheus alerts were silently
   dead**: `prometheus.yml` requires `rule_files: /etc/prometheus/alerts.yml`,
   but no volume ever mounted that file into the container. Added the
   mount.
3. **`HTTPS-SETUP.md` — DNS instructions were for the pre-ADR-0002
   architecture**: told readers to point one root A record at their
   server; checked against the actual `deploy/caddy/Caddyfile` — Caddy has
   no block for the bare domain at all today (root is intentionally
   Vercel's), it needs 4 subdomain A records (`api.`/`app.`/`business.`/
   `admin.`). Rewrote the DNS and verification sections to match reality.

## Flagged, not fixed (needs a human decision)

`PROJECT-KNOWLEDGE.md` claimed "35/35 tables have RLS enabled" — true for
the live DB as of 2026-07-19, but **not reproducible from this repo's
migrations**: a database built fresh from `prisma db push`/`migrate deploy`
+ `apply-sql.sh` (verified both paths locally, plus checked
`0_init/migration.sql` directly) only gets RLS on 15 of 49 tables — the
ones migrations 023/024/029/031 explicitly touch. The ~34 original tables
(`restaurants`, `reservations`, `users`, `staff`, `tenants`, …) have RLS on
production but no migration file that does it — same "DB drift written up
after the fact" pattern this repo already documents for
`payments`/`platform_settings`/`restaurant_closures` before migration 023,
just never closed for the original tables. Documented in full in
`PROJECT-KNOWLEDGE.md` §2 and `agency/knowledge/KNOWLEDGE_SYSTEM.md`
§SECURITY_MEMORY. Deliberately not fixed here — writing an RLS migration
for ~34 tables is exactly the DB/security change class that needs explicit
human sign-off before an agent touches it.

## Smaller fixes

- `QUEUE.md` was missing the `webhook` job kind entirely (real, active
  handler in `worker.ts`, called from `events.ts`) — added.
- `DEPLOY-COMMANDS.md` had the wrong repo name in its own "corrected" note
  (`ardalanazim/RezervnoOSv2` instead of `ardalanazimian/Rezv`) and a stale
  table count — fixed both.
- Removed stray root `package.json`/`package-lock.json` — `CLAUDE.md`
  explicitly says the repo root has none; these were unused leftovers from
  an earlier, since-reverted architecture (traced to commit `e0d14c8`, no
  `node_modules`, nothing references them).

## Checked, confirmed accurate — no change needed

`backup/` + `BACKUP-GUIDE.md`, `deploy/caddy/Caddyfile` (already fixed two
documented bugs in an earlier session), `docker-compose.prod.yml`,
`.env.example` (root + `api/`, cross-checked every `process.env.X` used in
`api/src` against both files), `DATABASE-OPS.md` (all 7 claimed
`dbRead`-routed endpoints verified with `grep`), `COMPANY-PANEL-API.md`.

## Tested

- All three `standalone/*.html` opened with Playwright against a real
  Chromium build on `file://` — zero console/page errors (screenshots
  taken, match the live-hosted UI).
- `python3 -m py_compile tools/build-standalone.py` — clean.
- `python3 -c "yaml.safe_load(...)"` on `docker-compose.observability.yml`
  — valid.
- Full link/path-reference sweep re-run across all 106 `.md` files — zero
  new breakage.
- `sh tools/sync-design-system.sh --check` — clean (no `shared/` changes
  this round).
- RLS/table-count claims verified against a live local Postgres 16
  instance (`prisma db push` and `migrate deploy` both tried), not assumed.

author: zhhyu7
body:
## Summary
In udp_input()'s broadcast/multicast fan-out loop, each iteration calls netdev_iob_replace(dev, iob) to swap in a freshly cloned iob before handing the packet to the next matching connection. That function unconditionally sets dev->d_len = iob->io_pktlen, which is the full frame length (IP + UDP headers + payload), undoing the 'dev->d_len -= udpiplen' done once before the loop to strip the headers off for udp_input_conn().

As a result, every connection after the first sees a d_len that is udpiplen (IP+UDP header length, eg 28 bytes for IPv4) too large. This value flows into udp_datahandler() as buflen (it reads dev->d_len directly) and is stored as the queued packet's declared length in the connection's read-ahead iob chain. Once more than one such oversized entry has queued up in the same chain, the consumer (udp_readahead() in udp_recvfrom.c) parses the following entry's metadata starting at the wrong offset, so whatever byte happens to land on src_addr_size is trusted as-is. That single byte (0-255) is then used as the length in iob_copyout(srcaddr, iob, src_addr_size, ...), which fills a fixed-size stack buffer with no bounds check outside a DEBUGASSERT - compiled out in release builds - so an oversized value overflows that stack buffer.

Re-apply the same '-= udpiplen' header-stripping after each netdev_iob_replace() call in the loop, matching what's already done once before the loop for the first connection.

Inside udp_input_conn, d_appdata is always set first, and since neither the ICMP nor ICMPv6 process accesses d_appdata, the redundant d_appdata settings have been removed.

## Impact
Affects any target with CONFIG_NET_SOCKOPTS + CONFIG_NET_BROADCAST where two or more SO_REUSEADDR UDP sockets are bound to the same port and receive broadcast/multicast traffic — a normal, non-adversarial configuration (the issue reporter hit it without any malicious input). Security-relevant: stack buffer overflow in the network receive path.

## Testing

body:
LP07 Gate 6 closeout candidate.

Base `main`: `dc78ff4ddd0d90b25e1781f13ffd7794787dd3d7` (merged Gate 5 / PR #50).

## Gate 6 target

Prove the accepted reusable project asset lifecycle crosses the real LP05/LC01 -> LP06 Windows package -> named Runtime boundary, including updated-product use after explicit reimport and last-good preservation on failure.

## Implemented Gate 6 scope

- Renegade-owned persistent reusable-asset instance wrapper using existing serialized Wicked metadata + hierarchy; no Wicked format/source changes.
- Gate 5 Studio placement now uses `PlaceReusableModelCommand`, preserving stable `.rasset` identity and creator-authored wrapper transform through Undo/Redo and WISCENE Save/Open.
- `ReusableAssetDependencyProvider` projects scene stable IDs into the normal LP05/LC01 graph and exposes current `.rasset` payload dependencies through that same graph.
- Build preparation retains authoritative FBX/GLTF source only as an EditorOnly freshness root after Runtime transitive discovery, so stale-product validation remains authoritative without leaking source input into `GameData`.
- Packaged Runtime resolves stable asset IDs from `GameData/content-manifest.json`, validates the governed `.rasset`, prepares replacements before scene mutation, replaces only child payloads, and never consults/reconverts original source.
- Story Flow Runtime evidence accumulates reusable-asset refresh records across level loads.
- Failed Runtime refresh preserves the prior saved payload/wrapper; failed reimport preserves last-good `.rasset`; stale/failed builds preserve prior owner-visible output.

## Acceptance proof

Headless Gate 6 proofs execute in both Debug and Release:

- `RenegadeReusableAssetInstanceTests`
- `RenegadeReusableAssetRuntimeTests`

The full creator -> LP05/LC01 -> LP06 -> named Runtime acceptance is intentionally Release-only because representative FBX conversion and the real standalone Runtime require Wicked graphics initialization on the hosted Windows runner.

`RenegadeReusableAssetPackageAcceptance` proves:

- representative animated/skinned FBX import and catalogue/tag state;
- persistent placement + Save/Open;
- failed reimport leaves last-good `.rasset` unchanged;
- changed valid source makes the imported product stale at build freshness;
- stale owner build fails before smoke and preserves prior final output;
- explicit reimport retains source/product stable IDs and changes payload hash;
- the saved scene is deliberately **not** resaved after reimport;
- LP05/LC01 reaches the current `.rasset` while retained source remains EditorOnly;
- LP06 packages the `.rasset` but not the source FBX;
- staged named Runtime launched from unrelated CWD reports the current reimported payload hash and not the old payload hash;
- safe promotion + package integrity succeed;
- source project is deleted; and
- promoted `<GameName>.exe` launches directly a second time from unrelated CWD and proves the same current packaged `.rasset` identity/hash.

Mandatory proof fixtures fail CMake configuration with `FATAL_ERROR` if absent; Gate 6 cannot silently disappear while CI stays green.

No `.rentity`, no thumbnails, no stock Wicked Editor UI, no Wicked source/pin change, no LC01 schema change, no Gate 2 metadata schema change, and no `Tools/Windows-Build.Common.ps1` change.

Implementation/proof is complete. **Do not merge yet.** The final documentation head must pass:

author: lassiheikkila
body:
## What

The bare-metal *Run* section of `DEPLOY.md` told hosters:

> For production add `--workers 2` (or use gunicorn with uvicorn workers).

Replace that with an explicit statement that the backend is single-process by design, and why.

## Why it matters

Following the old advice breaks things **today, on one box** — no horizontal scaling involved:

- The **bridge pollers** and the **token-expiry sweep** are `lifespan` asyncio tasks with no
  leader election, and a poller claims an event only *after* processing it. A second process
  reprocesses the same pending events: duplicate activity imports, duplicate LLM analyses,
  duplicate spend.
- The **startup stranded-run sweep** settles every `pending` LLM row on the premise that whatever
  wrote it is gone. With two processes that premise is false — starting the second settles the
  first one's live runs.
- **`AGENT_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS`** is an in-process counter, so N processes allow N× the
  concurrency against the LLM.
- **Rate limits are held in memory**, so each caller gets N× their allowance. For login and
  password reset that is a weakened brute-force defence, not just a looser quota.
- The **per-user activity lock** guarding sync dedup is an `asyncio.Lock`, which spans one process.

The line also contradicted the rest of the same document, which already describes the stranded-run
sweep as inheriting "the same single-process assumption as the bridge pollers" and
`AGENT_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS` as bounding runs "in flight at once in **this process**".

**No deployed instance was affected** — `backend/scripts/docker-entrypoint.sh` execs a single
uvicorn worker with no `--workers` flag, and the three systemd units each run one process. This
was a documentation hazard, not a deployed defect.

A bare deletion would have left the next reader to rediscover the idea and re-add it, so the
replacement gives the reason and points at
[`openkoutsi-ops/SCALING.md`](https://github.com/openkoutsi/openkoutsi-ops/blob/main/SCALING.md)
for the vertical scaling path.

## Scope

One hunk in `DEPLOY.md`. The `uv run uvicorn …` command itself is unchanged. No code, no API
surface, so no `openapi.json` regeneration; no feature change, so no README summary.

## Testing

`SECRET_KEY=… uv run python -m pytest tests/` — **2245 passed, 2 skipped**. Nothing outside a
Markdown file changed, so this confirms the tree is untouched rather than exercising the change.

## Context

Stage 0 of openkoutsi/openkoutsi#49, which inventories what would block running the backend as
multiple replicas. This was the one finding in that investigation that is a live defect rather
than a future concern; the rest of that issue is deliberately not addressed here.

## Summary The document tools row (Content / People / Comments / Citations / Attributes) no longer pins to the top of the scroll container: it stays where it is in the page and scrolls away, with a hairline `border-b` in place of the `IntersectionObserver`-driven `shadow-md`. That deletes the sentinel, `isToolsSticky`, the observer effect, the mobile-only stuck-shadow bug, and the hover-card vs `z-10` conflict. What must stay reachable now lives in a **48px `DocumentTopBar`** that is a *sibling* of the content scroll area, not a `sticky` child of it — persistence is a layout fact rather than a paint trick: ```tsx
{mainPageContent}
``` Left: file-explorer reveal + breadcrumbs. Right: the same `documentContentAction` composition (publish/save, `...` menu) the old floating overlay rendered. Mobile web scrolls the document itself, so there the same bar is `sticky top-0` and pins under the site header as it scrolls away — which replaces both mobile workarounds: the `fixed` actions overlay (which drifted, keeping its `--site-header-live-h` offset after the header was gone) and `MobileBackToTop`, both deleted. Three non-obvious pieces: - **Breadcrumbs moved out of the header.** `DocumentHeader`/`EditableDocumentHeader` lost their `breadcrumbs` prop, and the home-doc-only trail that rendered view labels in the page body is gone. `Breadcrumbs` renders a single crumb now instead of `if (breadcrumbs.length <= 1) return null`, so a home document reads as just the Home icon, `aria-current`, not a link. - **The reveal button's state belongs to `SiteFileBrowserLayout`,** which now publishes it through context rather than the page duplicating it. The bar *claims* the button while it renders one, so the layout keeps its floating fallback on routes that have no bar instead of losing the affordance: ```tsx {collapsed && revealClaims === 0 ? : null} ``` Electron has no such layout, so `useSiteFileBrowserControls()` returns `null` there and the bar is breadcrumbs-only on the left (its sidebar toggle stays in the titlebar). - **Scroll offsets retuned.** `STICKY_HEADER_OFFSET` 88 → `SCROLL_TOP_MARGIN` 16 (the 88 was tuned to chrome that no longer exists), and the outline sidebar's `sticky top-24` → `top-4`. On the window-scroll path (mobile web) the hook now scrolls explicitly and subtracts the bar height *only when it is actually pinned*, measured off `[data-document-top-bar]` rather than hardcoded — this is what keeps `#blockRef` deep links from landing under the bar. author: ldwghm
body:
两个由 2026-08-12 午报（git 通道首次实战）暴露的问题。

## 一、合并把当日盘中数据换成了昨收 🔴

GitHub Actions 13:42 抓到了完整的当日盘中数据（50/50 行 `data_date=2026-08-12`），但 `realtime_indices` / `watchlist_rt` / `sectors` / `index_5day_kline` 四个键**都不在 `MERGE_KEYS` 里**，合并后被 CCR 会话自己那份 klines_cache 昨收盖掉：

```json
"quote_source": "none",
"provenance": {"by_source": {"klines_cache": 50}, "fallback_rows": 50}
```

用当天真实归档复现，把未修复的合并结果送进 `evaluate_liveness`：

```
('block', '午报无任何当日数据：观察池 0 条实时报价，且无板块/资金流盘中层')
```

**这封午报本该被阻断、不发送（exit 3）。** 当天三个板块盘中层（`ai_boards_rt` / `board_stocks_rt` / `capital_flow_top30_rt`）恰好都是空数组，所以连 DEGRADE 都不是。

今天没出事，只因为模型自己去核对了 `data_quality`、发现异常、现写 overlay 脚本救了回来。那是运气，不是控制。

### 改法

新增 `INTRADAY_KEYS` 与 `apply_intraday_merge`：按 `as_of` 比时点，取新的那份，**四层整组一起换**——混用会造出「13:42 的指数 + 昨收的个股池」这种自相矛盾的快照。

`intraday_as_of` 逐级降级取时点：行级 `as_of` → 指数 `as_of` → 快照日期 + 指数 `time`（Actions 那份只有 `time`，没有 `as_of`）→ `data_date` 当日收盘。

**关键的一步是 `overlay_technicals_prices`**：只换 `watchlist_rt` 不够——verify 的活性判定、覆盖率、provenance 统计读的都是 `watchlist_technicals`。只覆盖价格字段，`ma`/`macd`/`rsi` 仍出自缓存序列，并把 `technicals_source` 标成 `klines_cache`，别让人以为整行都是今日的。

`quote_source` 随之区分：采用 Actions 盘中层时报 `efinance@github_actions (盘中快照)`，不再混报成 `efinance_backfill`。

### 验证

同一份真实数据，修复后 `liveness` 转 `pass`（50/50 当日实时）。反向也测了——CCR 哪天能连上新浪，本地更新的那份不会被昨天的盖掉。

## 二、轮询走 CDN，一次都没读到自己那份快照

```
05:38:45  抓数 workflow 提交 f336545（带本次 request_id）
05:38-05:42  poller 每 10 秒拉一次 raw.githubusercontent —— 一次都没看到
05:42:23  同一条 workflow 的 13:50 定时任务提交 45aba72（无名），覆盖
05:45:31  poller 终于读到，但读到的是被覆盖的那份 → by_freshness
```

`?t=<uuid>` nonce 没能绕过 CDN 缓存。

读取改走 git 协议：`ls-remote` 拿 HEAD（几百字节，可高频问）→ HEAD 变了才 `fetch` → `git show FETCH_HEAD:<path>`。没有 CDN 这一层。临时 clone 从 dispatch 复用到轮询结束，`finally` 里 `close()`。

同时修掉暴露出的第二个洞：**已经确认过的 `by_request_id` 匹配不该被随后那份无名快照顶掉**。新增 `_better()`，只在匹配等级不降的前提下替换手上的快照。

## 其他

测试 **223 → 238**。

顺带说明：昨天开的 #4 里说「by_freshness 是给 Codex 抢 trigger 文件准备的」——方向对了，但真正的竞争者是这条 workflow 自己的 13:50 cron。

Четвёртый срез ратчета `BLE001`/`S110`/`S112`: пакет `providers` (6 мест) разобран и ушёл из
`per-file-ignores`. Общего правила «сузить типы везде» снова не нашлось — и это сам результат разбора.

## Дефект

`cost_method` ×3: `except Exception: pass` выбрасывал **целую категорию совета** — гигиена сессии,
делегирование, выбор runtime. Человек читал 4 совета вместо 5 и не имел способа узнать, что список
неполон. Инструмент, чья работа — советовать, советовал меньше и молчал об этом: тот же класс, что
заниженное число в `kit_observability`.

Исправлено **без новых полей**: канал вывода уже есть — сама выдача советов, — поэтому пропуск
называется в ней же (`НЕ ОЦЕНЕНО: <категория> — <причина>`). fail-open сохранён.

## Верное поведение, причина записана

`orchestrator`: `except Exception: return False` вокруг проверки вердикта **ревьюера** — fail-closed

наружу, то есть в падение вместо отказа — для `writer ≠ judge` это хуже.

author: guan404ming
body:
## Related Issue

Fixes #139989.

## Why

- A graph break inside a checkpointed function made Dynamo skip the entire frame.
- The outer forward and the checkpointed function both ran eager, losing all speedups.
- Implements the fallback design @zou3519 proposed on the issue: turn `compile(ac(f))` with a graph break in `f` into `ac(compile(f))`, which already works.

## How

- Fall back to an eager checkpoint call that re-enters Dynamo on the checkpointed function.
- Run forward and backward recompute through the same compiled code, keeping recompute consistent.
- Keep raw `tag_activation_checkpoint` usage and `fullgraph=True` behavior unchanged.

Authored with an AI assistant. Reviewed by me.

## What (A7.20 — PR 3; stacked on #695)

Migrates audience Q&A and follow codes to the storage call convention (`docs/reference/storage-scope.md`). Behaviour-preserving; org semantics untouched (D5 boundary).

**11 exports**, exactly the brief's PR-3 cut:

- `questions.js` (8): `getQuestion`, `listQuestions`, `createQuestion`, `upvoteQuestion`, `cancelQuestion`, `removeQuestion`, `promoteQuestion`, `attachQuestionsSseClient` — plus the internal `broadcastQuestions` carrier.

author: ybcoder01
body:
## Summary

- authorize both the registry owner and pricing-policy owner for secure admin sessions
- move the admin ownership check from the replaceable registrar to the persistent registry
- show current registry owner, policy owner, treasury, quote signer, USDC contract, payment switches, policy version, and delayed-update status
- allow the correct connected owner to transfer registry or policy ownership
- allow the policy owner to propose, cancel, and activate delayed operational configuration updates
- require ownership-transfer addresses to be entered twice
- preserve every price and discount when changing operational roles
- document the public pricing-policy address required by the admin UI

## Contract impact

No new contract, redeployment, activation, or gas is caused by this PR. The controls call functions already present in `XNSRegistry` and `XNSPricingPolicy`. Transactions occur only after the connected owner explicitly confirms them in their wallet.

## Security boundaries

- no private key, signer key, API key, or RPC credential is accepted, stored, or logged
- changing the quote signer authorizes only a public address on-chain
- the matching Vercel signer secret must be updated separately after the delayed configuration is activated
- ownership transfers are immediate and cannot be undone by the old owner
- treasury, signer, USDC and payment switches retain the existing 48-hour policy delay
- policy activation remains permissionless only after the delay, as designed in the contract

## Validation

GitHub Actions should run contract and SDK tests and the production frontend build. The PR remains draft until CI and Vercel succeed.

author: bishalsingh153
body: ## What this does Adds an Export dropdown with **Export as PNG** and **Export as PDF**, downloading a high-resolution image of the current graph — alongside the existing AI-generated architecture diagram export. Closes #26. ## How it works - Renders the graph at its true **native resolution** by resizing the capture area to the graph's actual content bounds, rather than shrinking everything to fit the screen and upscaling afterward (which produced blurry results on large graphs during testing). - Excludes UI chrome from the capture (search box, controls, minimap, hover tooltip, Large Repo Mode banner, and the Legend — the last one specifically because its fixed position could otherwise overlap real content depending on the graph's shape). - Capture area is capped at **4000px** on the longest side to prevent browser crashes — confirmed via testing on a 400+ node repo, where an earlier higher cap + pixelRatio multiplier crashed the tab. - An **in-app confirmation modal** (styled to match the rest of the UI, not a native `confirm()`) warns users before exporting graphs with **>150 nodes**, since those are capped and may render at reduced clarity. ## Known limitation (discussed with @armannhansda above) This is single raster-image export, which has a real ceiling for very large graphs — full native-resolution rendering at that scale risks browser crashes, so large graphs are capped and export at somewhat reduced clarity instead. This is a fundamental limitation of DOM-to-raster capture, not something fixable by tuning `pixelRatio` further (tested and confirmed). Long-term direction (tiled/paginated or vector-based export) filed as a separate follow-up issue: #33 **Also noted for the record:** while debugging label clarity, found that a node's rendered width can measure ~96px via `getBoundingClientRect()` despite `CustomNode.tsx` setting `min-w-[240px]` in CSS — not fully root-caused within this PR's scope. The "zoom in before exporting" tip in the dropdown is a practical workaround in the meantime. ## Testing done - ✅ Small/medium repos export cleanly at full native resolution - ✅ Large repo (217+ nodes) — confirmed warning modal appears, Cancel/Continue both work correctly - ✅ Large repo (400+ nodes) — confirmed no browser crash with the current cap (previously crashed with a higher cap + pixelRatio multiplier) - ✅ Legend no longer overlaps graph content in exports - ✅ UI chrome (search box, controls, minimap) correctly excluded from captures

author: jaimito-asuntos-gringuenos
body:
Closes #521 · silences the false alarm in #520

## What this changes

**#520 has been open since 2026-08-10 saying "Deployed app does not draw a trail". The app draws a trail.** Every other check in that run passed. What failed was `bucket-errors`, on a 404 for `elevation_profile.json`.

That 404 is correct behaviour. `lib/trailData.ts` fetches it through `fetchOptionalArtifact`, whose own docstring says an optional artifact is one *"a release may predate"*, where a 404 means *"this release has no such file" rather than a failure* — so that a phone pointed at an older release still gets its map. The bucket does not publish it today, so the app asks, gets a 404, and carries on as designed.

`check-deployed-app.mjs` flagged **any** 4xx as `failed`. So a designed-for absence became a daily alarm claiming the map was broken.

That file's own header quotes #431 about a check that cries wolf one morning in four being precisely the thing to avoid — and then did it every morning for three days. An alarm red for a non-reason is one people learn to close without reading, which is how the next real one gets missed. This alarm's whole job is catching a recurrence of #427.

### The list is read, not restated

The optional keys come out of `lib/trailData.ts` and `lib/config.ts`. A copy in the check would be a second home for the contract whose drift is invisible from both sides — the same argument `verify_release.py` check 2 makes about the client's key contract. It **throws** rather than returning an empty list, because a regex that quietly stopped matching would put every optional 404 straight back to looking like an outage.

The absence is still surfaced, as `noted` rather than `failed`: the app working without the file is by design, but the file being missing means the elevation ribbon ships dark, and somebody should know that without it being called an outage.

**One bug found by running it rather than reading it**: the first pattern also matched the *declaration* of `fetchOptionalArtifact` and captured its parameter name, which resolved to no key and tripped the guard. Requiring `await` distinguishes a call from a declaration.

## How it was checked

- The contract reader run against the real sources: `['SPURS_KEY', 'ELEVATION_KEY']` → `['spurs.json', 'elevation_profile.json']`, guard passes.
- **client** 2320 passed / 148 files, typecheck, lint and format clean · **.github/tests** 143 passed / 12 skipped · **pipeline** 1185 passed / 6 skipped.
- **Not verified: a live daily run.** That is tomorrow's 09:30 UTC run, which is what should close #520 by transition.

Merges clean against `main`.

## Adjacent, deliberately not folded in

**`elevation_profile.json` arguably should be published** — that is the `include_elevation` dispatch #133 needs anyway, and it would remove this 404 at source. But the check has to be right either way: an optional artifact is optional whether or not this particular one is present today.

author: ahmedhamedaly
body:
Closes #60

Step 3 of the portfolio charts plan (follow-up to #57): reconstruct the data both charts need from the accounting `/history` endpoint and the local `earn_transactions` table.

- `AccountingClient.get_user_history()` pages through `/v1/accounting/history` with the caller's SIWE token, oldest page first so the walk stays stable while new entries append. Verified against the staging deployment.
- `services/portfolio/reconstruction.py`: pure replay of history entries into per-token available/locked change-points. Kind semantics are documented in the module — notably `transferFromLockOut` debits **locked** (the counterparty is paid out of the lock), `transferFromLockIn` credits available, and `modifyLock` is treated as a lock top-up funded from available.
- `services/portfolio/earn_positions.py`: completed earn deposits/withdrawals as per-pool flows and net-principal change-points, timestamped at settlement. Amounts stay in asset units — share conversion needs the pool rate at each instant and belongs to the rate provider (step 2).
- Balances can go negative when history predates the accounting service's deployment (unbackfillable, same caveat as #57). Preserved, not clamped, so valuation (step 5) can decide how to baseline.

Two assumptions worth a sanity check from @buberdds:
- `modifyLock` amount is read as a delta, not the new lock total
- `transferFromLockIn` credits the receiver's available balance

author: surveit
body:
Per-project **Terms**: the nouns and verbs a methodology runs on, so every agent that writes about a project uses the owner's words instead of picking its own. This PR is the model and storage layer only — no prompts, no injection, no UI, no generation. Those follow on this branch. ## Why Three prompts already tell an agent to use the methodology's wording — `REVIEW_GUIDE_SYSTEM_PROMPT`'s VOCABULARY section, `REVIEW_GUIDE_NOTE`, `HOW_YOU_WORK_NOTE` — with nothing to point at. Each agent re-reads raw prose and derives its own vocabulary. Measured on `venezuela_lda_lobbying`, document vs its 30 compiled stages: | word | in the document | in the stages | |---|---|---| | `incidental` | 0 | 9 | | `core` | 0 | 23 | | `flag` | 0 | 40 | | `alias` | 0 | 56 | | `registrant` / `firm` | 3 / 16 | 311 / 66 | Six words the workflow runs on that the methodology owner never wrote once. ## Shape ```mermaid graph LR NS["NamedSchema
kind now optional"] --> SL[SchemaLibrary] SL --> T[Terms] V[Verb] --> T T --> SVC["services/terms.py
(was data_model.py)"] SVC --> D1["<project>/schemas/*.json"] SVC --> D2["<project>/verbs.json"] T --> WF[WorkflowFile export/import] ``` A **noun** is an existing `NamedSchema` with its columns left empty. `columns` already defaulted empty; `kind` did not, and `reference | input | computed | ground_truth` is a claim about where rows come from. The word *registrant* makes no such claim, so forcing one would write a fabricated fact to disk — hence `kind: SchemaKind | None`. A **verb** is new: `name`, `definition`, `also_written`. `Terms` composes both and refuses a word that carries two meanings across every `name` and `also_written`. That check is the artifact's whole point. ## Known gap, fixed in the stacked PR 🟣 #587 The noun half cannot record an alias — `NamedSchema` has no `also_written`, so *registrant / firm* has nowhere to go. Fixed in 🟣 #587, which is stacked on this branch.

author: lordvicky
body:
## Summary

Adds a multi-device desktop battery widget using the existing ii-vynx desktop-widget design language. This is intentionally a **Draft PR** and is stacked on `feat/weather-widget-layouts` so it can reuse the same desktop-widget layout work without merging anything into `main`.

## Implemented

- Adds a unified battery device source for:
  - the shell's existing laptop/UPower battery service
  - connected Bluetooth devices that expose battery information
- Adds the approved **List** layout:
  - fixed icon rail for consistent device-icon alignment
  - connected-device battery percentage per row
  - charging state handling where the source exposes it
  - dynamic vertical growth/shrink as devices connect and disconnect
  - smooth device row/state transitions
- Adds the approved **Compact** layout:
  - circular battery progress indicator
  - device-type icon in the gauge
  - large percentage readout
  - device name + connection/charging status
  - on-widget layout switcher following the existing desktop-widget interaction pattern
- Compact device selection prioritizes the device that needs attention:
  - lowest battery is preferred
  - 5 percentage-point switch threshold prevents constant swapping
  - values within 2 percentage points are treated as a tie
  - ties prefer the most recently connected device for the current shell session
  - disconnecting the displayed device immediately selects the next best candidate
- Uses the existing shell design primitives, typography, semantic colors and animation timings rather than introducing a separate visual language.
- Keeps the implementation intentionally small: laptop and Bluetooth are the only battery sources for this first version.

## Runtime testing

Tested on Fedora/Quickshell with live Bluetooth devices:

- Bluetooth battery discovery works.
- Multiple connected devices render correctly.
- Widget height updates dynamically when devices connect/disconnect.
- Compact layout switches to the lower-battery device as intended.
- Compact device name/status rendering was runtime-debugged and fixed by ensuring the widget imports `qs.services` for `Translation.tr()` bindings.

Laptop/UPower rendering has not been hardware-tested yet because the development machine is a desktop. The implementation deliberately reuses the shell's existing `Battery` service rather than adding a second polling implementation.

## Design constraints

This follows the previously approved battery mockups and the existing ii-vynx desktop-widget language. The implementation intentionally avoids adding a new design system or unrelated UI changes.

## Base branch

`feat/weather-widget-layouts`

This PR should stay draft until the stacked desktop-widget work is ready and laptop battery behavior has been verified on hardware.

author: handokei
body:
Closes #2309

## 문제
2026-08-12 아침 실기기 trip: 07:46:09 destination imminent 발사(뚝섬 34m — 정확) → 3초 뒤
07:46:12 사용자 "안내 종료"(user-delete) → 정답지(ground truth) 확정 창이 완료되지 못해
miss로 self-report되어 dump `alarmAccuracy(local)=0/1`. 08-10에도 동일 패턴 관찰. 정확한
발사를 실패로 계수하는 지표 왜곡.

## 옵션 검토 (이슈 지정 2개 + 조사 결과)
1. **user-delete 시 미확정 알람을 분모에서 제외** — 구현은 간단하지만 결과가 `0/0`(무응답
   제외)이 된다. 이슈 Acceptance("다음 검증 탑승에서 동일 행동 시 alarmAccuracy 1/1")를 만족
   시키지 못한다 (기각).
2. **발사 시점에 fusion arrival-confirmed 상태였으면 hit로 즉시 확정** — 채택. 코드 조사 결과
   destination `imminent` phase 발사(`useStationAlarm.ts` `isImminentByArrivalCode` /
   `stationPipeline.ts` 동일 phase 게이트) 자체가 이미 arrival-code 기반 fusion 확인 신호라,
   발사 성공 = 객관적 hit 증거다. 사용자에게 다시 물을 필요가 없고, 정확도 확정 창을 기다리다
   조기 종료로 미완료되는 구조적 결함도 함께 제거된다. 결과가 acceptance(`1/1`)와 정확히 일치.

## 변경
- `src/features/alarm/utils/alarmLog.ts`: `logFiredAlarm`에서 `kind==='destination' &&
  phaseId==='imminent'` 발사 시 in-memory flag(`accurateDestinationFired`) stamp.
  `consumeAccurateDestinationFire()`로 1회 읽고 즉시 리셋(trip 간 leak 방지). 활성 trip은
  항상 최대 1개이므로 corrId 매칭 없이 안전(기존 `fireAlarmOnce` in-memory ledger와 동일 패턴).
- `src/features/debug/utils/triggerTripGroundTruthPrompt.ts`: trip 종료 시 flag가 서 있으면
  기존 수동 Yes/No 정답지 modal(`enqueuePrompt`)을 건너뛰고 `recordAutoConfirmed`로 즉시
  'accurate' 확정. 이 함수는 4개 trip-end 경로(setDestination/silent push/launch
  reconciliation/state rehydration)의 단일 gateway라 호출부 변경 없이 전체 적용.

author: smana
body:
## Why

  The Security landing page was one sentence:

  > The read-only default, the action gate, and the trust model.

  The pages beneath it are strong. The index did no work. Someone deciding whether to point an LLM-driven agent at their production cluster landed there and got a table of contents.

  ## What

  It leads with the invariant that answers that question — **the model proposes, the server decides** — then the four controls that bound the blast radius, each independent of the model's cooperation and each one
  click from its enforcement in the architecture doc.

  **"What it does not claim" sits above the routing table, deliberately.** A prompt injection can still bias an answer; redaction is best-effort; RCA is sub-50% on real incidents; configured endpoints are trusted.
  That is where most agent security pages stop being useful, and putting it first is the only version of this page consistent with an agent whose selling point is preferring *"I don't know"* to a guess. Someone who
  reads only the top should come away with an accurate picture, not a flattering one.

  The rest is a **question-to-page table** rather than prose — a reader arrives with one specific question (what RBAC does it need, what can I prove afterwards, what happens if I connect a third-party MCP server),
  not an appetite for two long documents.

  The receipts — Scorecard, the nightly eval, how to report a vulnerability — are linked rather than summarised, since the point of a receipt is that it is checkable somewhere other than here. It closes by naming
  the single-maintainer risk, because that belongs in a security assessment and stating it in the README while omitting it here would be choosing where to be honest.

  **Content only — no new claims.** Every statement summarises `security-model.md` or `security-architecture.md` and links the section it came from.

  ## Verification

  - `hugo --minify --gc` builds — a bad `relref` is fatal (`refLinksErrorLevel: ERROR`).
  - `hack/check-anchors.sh` passes.
  - The page's **13 cross-page anchors were each resolved against the rendered target headings** by hand. That is not something the anchor guard on `main` covers — which is the subject of the companion PR, and how
  one of these was caught before it shipped.
