author: itzyanick
body:
## What

Every package this repository has ever published lost its **setuid, setgid and sticky** bits between the builder and the client.

`add-to-repo` did not copy the incoming package. `PkgOpen` extracted it with `tarUtils.DefaultUntarOptions` — whose `PreserveSetuid` is false, so `sanitizeMode()` starts from `.Perm()` and masks all three away — and `PkgCopy` then re-tarred that sanitised tree as the artefact clients download. The old comment on `PkgCopy` said as much without anyone connecting it to the missing bits:

> Note this re-tars the extracted contents rather than copying the input file: the published archive is not byte-identical to the one handed to add-to-repo

## The measurement

Against the live index, both architectures, every subversion — not against any recipe:

| | |
|---|---|
| payloads fetched and listed | **622 / 622**, 0 failures |
| entries examined | 251,608 |
| carrying setuid, setgid or sticky | **0** |
| owned by anything but root | **0** |

The instrument was verified against a known-positive tar before the zero was believed.

**The builder is not at fault**, which is where everyone looked first. `duct-filesystem` built end to end with the real `tape-builder` in *both* builder images produces `drwxrwxrwt` on `/tmp`; a path-and-mode diff of that archive against the published payload of the same subversion is 48 entries each side, identical, differing in exactly those two directories.

## The fix

**The bits are the symptom. The defect is that publishing rebuilt the artefact**, so anything the extractor normalised was silently dropped from the thing users install — modes today, and whatever the extractor learns to normalise next.

`PkgCopy` now copies the input bytes. What the repository serves is exactly what the builder produced and CI uploaded, and the recorded digest is a digest of that same artefact. It writes to a temporary name in the destination directory and renames, so an interrupted publish cannot leave a short package where a complete one is expected.

`PkgOpen` keeps its extraction, which now exists only to read `TAPEPACKAGE.toml` and is thrown away. `PreserveSetuid` **deliberately stays false** there — it is the right default for writing a stranger's archive into a temporary directory as root, and it no longer costs anything, because the sanitised tree is not what gets served. Turning it on would recreate the privilege-escalation shape without buying back a single bit. It also moves to `os.MkdirTemp` at 0700 instead of a `math/rand` name under a shared 0755 parent — the same hardening `daemon/utils/downloadPkg.go` already had and this end did not.

## Why the install path is untouched

A closed-world audit of every consumer of `DefaultUntarOptions` found exactly three entry points:

| call site | verdict |
|---|---|
| `common/tarUtils/untar.go:50` `Untar()` | convenience wrapper, **zero callers** anywhere; keeps the safe default |
| `daemon/utils/install.go:88` | **must preserve — already does** |
| `repo/utils/pkgOpen.go:35` | **the defect, and the only one** |

Publish was the whole of it: a republished-correct payload lands correct on disk with no other change. The install path has always been the careful one, and its reasoning is the reasoning this end was missing — quoted into `PkgCopy` so the next reader learns why `PreserveSetuid` is true there and false in the wrapper:

> Setuid is off by default because an arbitrary archive that can set those bits can hand out root. A package is not an arbitrary archive: its digest was checked against an index carrying a valid signature from a trusted key before we got here [...] Dropping the bits instead would silently ship a broken su, mount or ping — the file is present and executable and simply does not work.

It is careful past extraction too: `fullMode()` exists because "`.Perm()` masks to 0777 and discards all three without a word, which is why an installed su lost its setuid bit and /tmp came out 0777 instead of 1777", and `place()` chmods after `MkdirAll` because `MkdirAll` applies the umask.

## Tests — both arms, both levels

A test that only checks the setuid file passes just as well against a publish step that sets it on *everything*, which is a worse bug than the one being fixed.

- **publish** — special bits survive; a plain file stays 0755; published bytes are unchanged; the name comes from the manifest, not the input filename; a failed copy leaves nothing behind
- **install** — the existing `TestInstallPreservesSetuidSetgidAndSticky` gains the negative arm it lacked: a plain file and a plain directory that must *not* gain privilege. This is a new guard over behaviour that works today and that nothing proved would keep working.
- **witness** — `TestTheOldRetarPathLosesSpecialBits` reproduces the old extract-and-re-tar path and asserts the bits **are** lost, so the assertions above are demonstrably capable of failing rather than merely passing. It also fails loudly if `tarUtils` ever starts preserving by default, which is the moment someone would otherwise conclude the publish path had been safe all along.

Verified with the **real binary against a real published payload**: the experiment that produced 0755 on every entry before this change now gives `4755` on the setuid probe, `0755` on the plain probe, `1777` on both sticky directories, and a published file byte-identical to its input.

## ⚠️ Sequencing — this cannot be merged and forgotten

Merging this changes nothing on its own. **Already-published payloads stay wrong**, and the six packages that own an affected path have to be rebuilt — but only *after* the fixed `tape-repo` is the one actually running in the publish workflow. `publish.yml` runs `tape-repo` out of `ghcr.io/duct-linux/builder:latest`, which is assembled from the **published** `tape` package, so the order is forced:

1. merge this
2. `tape` package rebuilt and **published**
3. `duct/builder` rebuilt from that tape, `:latest` pushed
4. **only then** bump dbus, linux-pam, polkit, fuse3, shadow, duct-filesystem

Bumping at step 1 or 2 republishes the identical defect through the old stripping `tape-repo`, burns six subversions, and looks exactly like success — a name-and-version presence check passes at every moment.

Two things this fix does **not** cover, tracked separately:

- **dbus needs a recipe change regardless.** `dbus-1.16.2/bus/meson.build` installs the launch helper with no `install_mode`; the whole tarball has zero hits for `install_mode`/`chmod`/`4750`/`add_install_script`, and a seeded local build stages it at 0755. The autotools `install-exec-hook` that used to `chmod 4750` did not survive the meson port, so there was never a bit here for publish to destroy.
- **Ownership is still unexpressible, by design and by a second mechanism.** `tar.go` zeroes `header.Uid/Gid`, and the ISO build packs with `mksquashfs -all-root`. So `4750 root:messagebus` cannot work on a Duct system in either path, and setuid helpers must be restricted by mode rather than group.

author: tec2612
body:
## Summary

Fixes what a user hit right after pairing succeeded: two computers showed as paired, but moving the mouse did nothing. Four real, separate gaps, not one bug:

1. **Nothing ever launched `mouse-share-daemon`** (the process that actually owns input capture/injection and `CoreService`) — the installer copies it but nothing runs it. Fixed: the UI now spawns it as a background process on startup if it's present next to the UI executable.
2. **The UI and the daemon resolved their config directories differently** (Tauri's `app_config_dir()` vs. `ms_config::ConfigStore::default_path()`), so even a running daemon would see an empty trust store and layout. Fixed: the UI now uses the same path the daemon uses.
3. **Nothing ever dialed out for a live session** — both daemons only ever listened, so paired devices never actually connected to each other. Fixed: `ms-daemon` now runs a mesh-connect loop that browses mDNS (reusing the UI's pairing-port advertisement for address discovery), reloads the trust store periodically, and dials every paired device it can reach.
4. **Pairing never registered either device as a `ScreenLayout` node**, and there was no way in the UI to link two devices' edges — so even a connected session had nothing telling `EdgeStateMachine` which edge maps to which peer. Fixed: `commit_pairing` now registers both ends as layout nodes, and Computer Setup has a simple "my edge ↔ paired device" linking form as an interim substitute for the not-yet-built drag-and-drop canvas.

Also fixed a real bug found while in this code: `layout.nodes` is a Rust `HashMap<Uuid, ComputerNode>`, which serializes to a JSON *object* keyed by device id, not an array — the existing frontend called `.map()` on it directly, which would have thrown at runtime the first time any layout ever had nodes (which, until fix #4, was never).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --workspace` — 103 tests passing
- [x] `cargo build -p ms-daemon --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` — real linked Windows binary with the new mesh-connect code
- [ ] `app/src-tauri` can't be `cargo check`ed in this sandbox (missing Linux GTK/webkit2gtk packages); CI on `windows-latest`/`macos-latest` is the real compiler validation, as for every prior PR in this series
- [ ] Manual test on the reporting user's two real Windows machines once installers are rebuilt from this PR

## Summary
- explicitly enable the default alpha buffer for all newly created Qt Quick windows before `QGuiApplication` starts
- preserve the existing surface format while requesting an 8-bit alpha channel
- add a regression check ensuring the Turbo overlay alpha policy is configured before window creation

## Why
The dynamically created transparent `TurboChromeWindow` could receive a premultiplied-alpha D3D11 swapchain while its `QQuickWindow` format reported no alpha buffer. Qt then warned that the swapchain had alpha without an `alphaBufferSize`, and the Turbo interface could render incorrectly.

The native VLC child remains opaque with an alpha size of 0.

body: ## Why PR #15 merged the earlier `--auto` version of `.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml`, which only works after you enable "Allow auto-merge" + a branch protection rule in the GitHub UI. author: sinity
body:
## Summary

Make the resumable testmon seed operationally bounded on the current correctness corpus.

## Problem

The merged seed protocol split 20,964 nodes into 82 serial 256-node controllers. A single property-heavy shard took 9.5 minutes, making a complete seed multi-hour despite healthy tmpfs, memory, and xdist workers. Fixed node chunks also left expensive tests unevenly scheduled.

## Solution

- increase the resumable checkpoint size to 4,096 nodes, producing six shards for the current corpus;
- use xdist `worksteal` within each shard to keep workers productive around long property fixtures;
- retain per-node event/outcome recording and resumability;
- align the shard determinism regression with the canonical lexicographic node ordering.

## Verification

- `.venv/bin/python -m devtools test tests/unit/devtools/test_verify.py` — 150 passed;
- `.venv/bin/python -m devtools verify --quick` — all 25 steps passed at `a1b78b775`;
- terminal baseline diagnostic on merged master demonstrated the prior 256-node serial-shard bottleneck and preserved its partial ledger.

This is a self-contained test-harness performance fix; it does not claim the full suite is green.

author: fabianh1994
body:
Sex ändringar som blev klara efter att PR #10 mergades. Tre av dem rättar något som står live på alpkoll.se just nu.

## Sluta låta ortsidan vara en återvändsgränd (`a14485d`)

Från en ortsida fanns ingen väg till någon annan ort — de 83 parsidorna nåddes bara från väljaren och sitemapen. Mätt i renderad HTML på alpkoll.se: noll länkar till `/jamfor/` från en ortsida.

Ett block längst ner listar nu de jämförelser orten förekommer i, grupperade i Norden och Alperna, med motpartens pistkilometrar och veckokostnad i länken. Åre och Sälen får 24 var, en nordisk ort tio, en alport två. De fem orter som inte ingår i något kuraterat par får rubriken ändå, med en väg till väljaren.

## Sluta visa ett snöfall vi inte kan belägga (`430b84c`)

`avg_snowfall_cm` står live på 30 ortsidor och i jämförelsetabellen. Fördelningen väckte misstanken — alla 30 värden delbara med tio, elva unika tal bland trettio — men beviset kom av att gå till källan: skiresort.com bär ingen säsongssiffra för snöfall alls, bara aktuellt snödjup. Kolumnen ligger kvar i databasen; fält slutar visas, de raderas inte.

## Visa priserna i kronor med ortens eget belopp bredvid (`1f4befa`)

Kronbeloppet är huvudtal, ortens eget belopp står bredvid. Kurserna hämtas från ECB via frankfurter.dev i `lib/valuta.js` — ingen nyckel, en timmes cache, daterade reservkurser om den inte svarar. Beloppet lagras i ortens valuta och räknas om vid visning; en omräkning i databasen hade varit samma fälla som `lift_pass_week_eur` gick i. Avrundning till närmaste femtio med "ca" på talet.

## Rätta Tignes och spara prisarbetet i repot (`af346ea`)

Migration 015 sätter Tignes nybörjarpoäng till 7 — orten har 55 % blå pist och stod kvar på 5 efter att 014 missat den. **Migrationen är redan körd i produktion**, kontrollerat mot databasen: Tignes står på 7 och efterkontrollen ger noll rader.

`docs/liftkortspriser.md` är arbetsdokumentet för omhämtningen av liftkortspriserna.

## Skapa valutakolumnen och lås veckokostnaden vid euro (`dd081d4`)

Koden läser `lift_pass_currency` på sju ställen men kolumnen har aldrig funnits. Migration 016 skapar den, med CHECK på de fyra valutor `lib/valuta.js` kan räkna om och alla rader satta till EUR — exakt vad fallbacken redan gör, så ingenting i vad sidorna visar ändras.

Innan kolumnen får ett annat värde måste en koppling bort: `est_weekly_cost_eur` skickades genom `pris()` med `lift_pass_currency` som valuta på sex ställen. Fältet är inte ett liftkortspris utan en researchad uppskattning av hela veckan, i euro för alla orter. Dagen Åre fått SEK hade 1 600 € renderats som "1 600 kr" — en elftedel av beloppet, utan att en rad om veckokostnaden ändrats. Migrationen bär också regeln som gör kolumnen ofarlig: valuta och belopp ändras i samma UPDATE, aldrig var för sig.

Kvar som beslut: `lift_pass_day_eur` och `lift_pass_week_eur` heter `_eur` och kommer att innehålla CHF, NOK och SEK. Skälen och rätt ordning för ett namnbyte står i migrationen.

## Rätta döda utgående länkar och skriv ner prisläget (`7afd4b7`)

Samtliga trettio orters `resort_url` hämtades och följdes. Hemavans båda länkar pekar på hemavan.se, som svarar 200 men vidarebefordrar till en samtyckessida hos Google — domänen är parkerad, vilket är varför felet överlevt. Migration 017 rättar den till hemavan.nu och tar även Geilo och Zermatt, som bytt domän, plus fyra fall som ser ut som döda länkar men inte är det.

Prisdokumentet gick från sexton till tjugo av trettio orter, och skälet står per ort för de tio som återstår.

## Verifierat

`npm run build` går rent: 125 sidor, 83 par, 30 ortsidor. Zermatt visar dagskort ca 1 350 kr, veckokort ca 6 450 kr och veckan ca 28 500 kr (2 600 €); Åre mot Sälen ca 17 550 kr mot ca 16 450 kr. Inga konsolfel på en nystartad server.

Migrationerna 016 och 017 är **inte körda** — de kräver Fabian i Supabase SQL Editor. Ingen av dem behöver köras för att koden ska fungera.

author: seanmorris
body:
## What changed

- pin the Docker builder to the official Emscripten 6.0.6 SDK and carry the remaining `sm-updates` behavior as a local patch
- preserve preload naming, `locateFile` fallbacks, IDBFS modes, duplicate-export handling, and async `dlopen` behavior
- preserve the source -> object -> archive -> side-module path used by dynamic extensions
- link the C++ ABI/runtime required by dynamically loaded ICU libraries and export `HEAPU8` for VRZNO
- keep compiler-rt's profiling runtime out of ordinary `MAIN_MODULE` builds and link it only for instrumented builds
- expose unambiguous CGI, CLI, and phpdbg entrypoints for Emscripten 6, null-terminate CLI/phpdbg `argv`, and return CLI exit statuses without terminating the JS host
- replace regex-based `??=`/`||=` rewriting with a syntax-aware Babel transform for generated CommonJS runtimes
- retry transient Emscripten port and PECL downloads without masking real build failures
- update GD/WebP, iconv, libzip, and Tidy recipes for the current toolchain

## Why

The previous image replaced the SDK checkout with the old `sm-updates` fork. Moving to Emscripten 6 lost local loader and dynamic-linking changes, while new generated-code and entrypoint behavior exposed several assumptions in the PHP wrappers.

In particular, Emscripten 6 renames PHP's argc/argv `main` export while PIB also supplies a no-argument `main`. CLI and phpdbg calls therefore selected PIB's no-op function. Explicit SAPI entrypoints avoid that ambiguity. Emscripten 6 also began emitting logical-assignment expressions whose left-hand sides were corrupted by the old Perl post-processing regex; the AST-based transform preserves them.

The compiler-rt split prevents non-instrumented main modules from creating `default.profraw`, while preserving profile output when instrumentation is explicitly enabled.

## Validation

- built `seanmorris/php-emscripten-builder:latest` locally from the updated Dockerfile
- verified source -> `.o` -> `.a` -> `.so` -> `dlopen` with a side module returning `42`
- verified plain `MAIN_MODULE` produces no profile file and an instrumented build does
- built all six dynamic PHP artifacts in Actions; all dynamic SDL verification jobs passed
- applied the explicit CLI/phpdbg patches cleanly to PHP 8.0 through 8.5
- relinked PHP 8.1 dynamic CLI against the failing CI artifact and passed output, version, and `exit(7)` tests
- incrementally relinked PHP 8.1 dynamic phpdbg with Emscripten 6.0.6, verified the named Wasm export, and passed its real Node prompt/script/quit test
- transformed and syntax-checked eight real Emscripten-generated JS variants from the CI artifact
- ran the repaired CommonJS CGI runtime and passed its hello-world and PHP-version requests
- focused Node regression suite: 13 passed, 0 failed
- focused Deno regression suite: 6 passed, 0 failed
- `git diff --check` passes

Replacement full-matrix CI for the latest commit is in progress.

author: oblinder
body:
## Summary

First PR in a series toward **#646** (AIAC phase 2 — platform integration: live onboarding trigger + live enforcement). This PR delivers **OPA plugin integration within the AIAC system plus live enforcement**: AIAC now publishes the rules it generates to the enforcement layer's policy resource, and real requests are allowed/denied by the deployed AuthBridge OPA plugin.

Later PRs in the series will cover the remaining #646 scope (e.g. the live IdP-event onboarding trigger path).

## What's in this PR

**PDP OPA policy writer → live enforcement**
- Rewrote the OPA policy writer from a filesystem stub into an always-on writer of per-agent `AuthorizationPolicy` Custom Resources (`agent.rossoctl.dev/v1alpha1`) on the live Kubernetes API via server-side apply; the bundle-service composes these CRs into per-pod OPA bundles the plugin loads.
- Reworked the Rego generator: fixed `authbridge.client.{inbound,outbound}.request` packages matching the live AuthBridge OPA plugin input shape (`input.identity.*`, `input.mcp.params.name`), with de-prefixed outbound scope values.
- Removed the superseded Keycloak composite-role writer and fixed every dangling reference across the PRD, specs, and the k8s deployment guide.
- Rego dump to `REGO_OUTPUT_DIR` is now purely additive local-debug output, gated by `POLICY_WRITER_DUMP_REGO` (default off); it never gates the CR write. Error mapping: malformed `agent_id` → 400, k8s API failure → 502, delete of an absent CR → 204.

**AuthBridge OPA plugin + token exchange**
- Plugin changes to support outbound Rego rules (in addition to inbound).
- Token-exchange plugin/delegation changes supporting scoped token exchange for the agent's onward call to the tool.

**Kubernetes wiring**
- Added the `aiac-pdp-policy-writer` ServiceAccount + cluster-scoped RBAC (`get,list,create,update,patch,delete` on `authorizationpolicies`, no watch) and wired the SA into the aiac-interface pod.
- Turned the prod Rego dump off (dropped `REGO_OUTPUT_DIR` + `/rego` mount), kept read-only rootfs + `/tmp`; added `PLATFORM_SOURCE_CLIENTS`.

**Integration tests — real OPA loop**
- Rebuilt the OPA integration tests to close the **real** enforcement loop through the AuthBridge OPA plugin on a live Kind cluster: onboard → poll bundle-service → real HTTP request through AuthBridge → assert allow/deny from the deployed plugin over bare tool names. Retired the `opa eval` / probe model (`opa` no longer needed on PATH). Suite skips cleanly when the cluster is not wired.
- Added `scripts/opa-kind-{enable,disable,driver,restore}.sh` to stand up / tear down the OPA pipeline on Kind.

**Docs**
- Rewrote the `pdp-policy-writer-opa` spec to match the CR-writer implementation.

**Supporting refactors carried in this branch**
- Renamed *Policy Store* → *Policy Model Store* across specs, code, and tests.
- Renamed *kagenti* → *rossoctl* (realm, operator contract, brand, repo paths).

## Testing

- `.venv/bin/pytest test/ -m "not integration"` — green.
- Integration tests (`-m integration`) close the real OPA loop against a live rossoctl/Kind cluster with the AuthBridge OPA pipeline wired in (see `docs/opa-kind-runbook.md`); they skip cleanly when the cluster/env is absent.

## Related

Part of #646. Sub-issue of the AIAC epic #643; depends on phase 1 (#645).

author: gmasria
body:
Solo documentación. **Nada de código**, ninguna migración, nada que desplegar.

Daniel pidió recorrer el sistema proceso por proceso *"para ver todos los detalles, pantallas que aún faltan"*, con la meta de sacar la primera versión cuanto antes. Se revisó en **siete tramos paralelos verificando contra el código**: que existan las pantallas, que exista **el botón** que lleva al paso siguiente, qué falta, qué sobra y qué no tiene sentido.

## Qué trae

**`docs/DIAGNOSTICO-FLUJO-COMPLETO.md`** — los 7 tramos, **24 bloqueantes** con evidencia `archivo:línea`, más lo que duele y lo que puede esperar. Se declara explícitamente lo no verificado, incluido que **ningún hallazgo se probó ejecutando la app**.

El bloqueo #1: **ninguna orden de compra nueva se puede autorizar**. El estatus `pendiente_autorizacion` no lo escribe nada en el sistema, pero es el único desde el que el frontend ofrece autorizar — y la bandeja lo usa de filtro, así que está vacía para siempre. No se ve al probar porque el ETL deja las OC históricas ya autorizadas; solo truena al crear una nueva. El test unitario usa ese mismo estado de fixture, por eso el CI tampoco lo veía.

El patrón de fondo: **casi ningún hallazgo es una función que falte** — los motores están construidos y bien construidos. Falta **la puerta**.

**`DECISIONES.md` §Post-F9.36 y §Post-F9.37** — las nueve decisiones que cerró Daniel. Las dos que más cambian el camino: **Ruta Crítica apagada en la v1** (retira cinco bloqueantes) y **se arranca sin conteo físico**, cargando el inventario sobre la marcha (el importador Excel deja de ser bloqueante — era el mayor riesgo de fecha, aunque agrava el bloqueo de compras).

**`HOJA-DE-RUTA.md`** — dos decisiones que llevaban meses abiertas quedan cerradas (el nº interno de producción y las 6 empresas viejas) y se agregan las nueve con su efecto en el plan.

**`docs/hoja-de-ruta/V1-etapas.md`** — las 7 etapas del empujón de cierre, cada una con qué entrega, **qué no entra** y su criterio de cierre. No es una fase nueva: F0–F10 no cambia.

## Pregunta abierta

Si la **salida de tela a una orden** debe generar un documento «nota de salida» como en el viejo, o basta el movimiento de kardex. Hoy la nota solo puede documentar avíos.

author: vahid-ahmadi
body:
Response to a full economics referee report (major revision). The referee's core objection was that the manuscript "does not have a thesis that survives its own honesty" — its headline is arithmetic the author derives himself, its displacement side rests on ~6 effective survey records, its trade calibration earns a rank correlation of 0.00, and its Discussion names unfinished items that would "exceed the 10.0-point gap outright" if added.

## The reframe

**Retitled** to *"Loss Concentration, Not Job Loss: What Tax–Benefit Stabilisation Coefficients Measure"*. The old title advertised the extensive margin as the organising axis when the paper's own finding is that the margin contributes 0.1 of 10 points and that this near-zero is mechanical.

The paper now leads on the measurement claim: the automatic-stabiliser literature reports a proportional income shock and an unemployment shock side by side and reads the difference as the extensive margin. That difference mixes a concentration effect with a margin effect and reports the sum under the margin's name — and the margin component is near-zero **by construction** in any annual static model, because every status-contingent institution lies outside one. The result is about measurement and does not depend on the UK.

## Where I depart from the referee

He put the wage-bill-weighted schedule wedge at ~15.7 points against a realised 9.9, implying **~6 points** of household offsets. That mixes bases: 15.7 is on the five-seed channel split, 9.9 is the fifty-draw step. On a consistent basis it is 15.7 against 13.5 — **2.2 points**, not 6. His framing was right and is adopted; his arithmetic was not. The manuscript now reports the weighted wedge (roughly twice the single-worker figure it previously quoted), states that the household system works *against* the tax schedule, and warns that comparing across seed bases overstates the offsets by more than a factor of two.

## Cuts

EPD counterfactual and pharmaceutical sections (both carried riders saying not to believe them); the decile figure (six of ten deciles are exactly zero on a representative draw); the product-destination panel compressed to what the estimand needs; four secondary adjustment families moved to the supplement. Results 6,083 → 5,284 words.

## Literature

Fourteen entries added where the mechanism actually lives — **Heathcote, Storesletten and Violante** above all, since their progressivity parameter τ *is* this paper's marginal–average wedge — plus Blundell–Pistaferri–Preston and the partial-insurance strand, Varian, Eaton–Rosen, Kniesner–Ziliak, Lyon–Waugh, Antràs et al., Rodrik, and a proper take-up literature. A new subsection ties them to the mechanism rather than listing them.

**Two citations corrected:** Garin and Silvério report 10–15 per cent pass-through of an *idiosyncratic export-demand* shock into incumbent *wage growth*, not a "0.13–0.14 elasticity to firm-specific output shocks". Atkin et al. compute *economic* incidence in Chile, so claiming their framing as "the one I adopt" was backwards when this paper computes only the statutory half.

## New machinery — implemented, disclosed as unrun

- `analysis/concentration_sweep.py` — holds each division's aggregate loss invariant while sweeping concentration continuously, and **nests both existing endpoints exactly** (reproduces the diffuse cut record-for-record at low φ, and the concentrated cell bit-identically at φ=1 under Bernoulli). This separates concentration from worker selection, which the three-cell design cannot. `make concentration-sweep`.
- `analysis/write_welfare_results.py` — the conditional-on-affected poverty statistics, which the referee noted are computed but unreported (5.0% → 31.3% under displacement). It **refuses to emit below 50 draws** rather than quote the existing 5-draw run, whose SD exceeds its mean. `make poverty-gap-production`.

Both need licensed FRS data, so neither is reported. They are named in the Discussion as the two largest gaps in the draft.

## Housekeeping

Seven stale internal memos removed from the replication package; `.pytest_cache` gitignored; the two dangling references the deletions created repaired.

## Verification

263 passed, 3 skipped. Writers idempotent. Manifest valid. Every macro, cross-reference and citation key resolves in both documents.

**Not addressed:** the paper still cannot be compiled or its artifacts regenerated here (no LaTeX, no licensed FRS file, no `policyengine-uk`, no HMRC panel). Run `make reproduce` and `make paper` before submission.

author: pablo-afterlife
body:
## Summary

The desktop **Tasks panel (Tasks X/N)** stays frozen at `0/N` for entire sessions: agents create the todo list once and never call the tool again, so the panel only moves — if at all — on the final call. This is the root cause of "tasks created but never progressing" reports.

The tool schema said only `Mark items completed immediately when done`, which models treat as optional bookkeeping. The panel is a pure mirror of the last `todo` tool result (live events in `use-message-stream`, hydration from the last todo tool-call message), so there is no UI bug — the agent simply never reports progress. The fix makes the rule explicit in the tool description: call with `merge=true` **the moment any item changes state** (in_progress when started, completed when done), never batch at the end, and state why (the panel only moves when the tool is called).

## Changes

- `tools/todo_tool.py`: reworded `TODO_SCHEMA` description — added a "KEEP THE LIST MOVING" section explaining the live `Tasks X/N` panel and requiring incremental `merge=true` updates on every state change; removed the weaker "mark completed immediately when done" phrasing.

## Validation

| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| `pytest tests/tools/test_todo_tool.py tests/tools/test_todo_tool_type_coercion.py tests/agent/test_display_todo_progress.py` | 33/33 passed |
| Schema text change is static (cached), no code paths altered | n/a — description-only diff |

No functional code changed: `TodoStore` already supports incremental merges and the display layer already renders progress fractions (`2/4 ✓`) on update calls — this PR only makes the model actually use that path.

author: yellowcap
body:
## The error

Production, `2026-08-12T09:30:47Z`. Langfuse trace: [`d4c0aa713e096b7958d7cdcd9cdfeea9`](https://langfuse.globalnaturewatch.org/project/wri_lcl/traces/d4c0aa713e096b7958d7cdcd9cdfeea9?observation=c07b1325f270c8cb). Langfuse session: [81dbede5-ec64-4099-9e87-85339af777b3](https://langfuse.globalnaturewatch.org/project/wri_lcl/sessions/81dbede5-ec64-4099-9e87-85339af777b3)

```
{"tool_name": "pull_data", "event": "tool_execution_failed", "logger": "src.agent.graph",
 "level": "error", "query": "Paris, Île-de-France, France - (district-county) [FRA]", ...}

  File "/app/src/agent/tools/pull_data.py", line 123, in pull_data
    aoi_names = [a["name"] for a in state["aoi_selection"]["aois"]]
                                    ~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
KeyError: 'aoi_selection'
```

Note what did *not* fail: line 100, `dataset = state["dataset"]`. The thread had a dataset but no AOI.

## Cause

`AgentState` is a plain `TypedDict` — keys exist only once a node writes them. `aoi_selection` was absent because no `pick_aoi` call ever completed a selection.

The `query` field is the giveaway. `"Paris, Île-de-France, France - (district-county) [FRA]"` is generated by `_format_aoi_candidate` — it's a nudge option, verbatim. The sequence:

1. `pick_aoi` ran on "Paris"; `check_duplicate_aois` found the same name in several countries.
2. It returned the `aoi_choice` nudge, whose `Command` writes **only** `nudge` and `messages` — not `aoi_selection`.
3. The user clicked an option. Clicking resubmits the option string as the next human message; there is no dedicated resolver tool.
4. The model saw a fully-qualified place name in the user's turn and called `pull_data` directly instead of re-running `pick_aoi`.
5. `KeyError`.

A `*_choice` nudge records the options offered, never a selection. `pick_dataset`'s `dataset_choice` branch has the identical write-free shape, so `state["dataset"]` was exposed to the same crash.

`pull_data` was the only unguarded consumer — `middleware.py`, `create_dashboard.py`, `show_imagery.py` and `pick_dataset` all use `.get()` with a fallback.

## Changes

**Guard both selections in `pull_data`.** Missing `dataset` or empty `aoi_selection.aois` now returns a `human_feedback` message naming the tool to run, instead of raising. When a matching `*_choice` nudge is pending, the message appends the offered options so the model re-resolves the user's actual click rather than guessing a different area.

This matters because of how the crash surfaced: `handle_tool_errors` returned `Tool 'pull_data' failed unexpectedly (KeyError)` to the model, with no hint that the fix was to call `pick_aoi`. That is the input condition for the guess-and-retry thrashing tracked separately (repeated `pick_aoi`/`pick_dataset`/`pull_data` calls after an uninformative failure).

**New i18n keys** `pull_data.no_aoi` / `pull_data.no_dataset`, all 15 languages, matching `show_imagery.no_aoi` — so no runtime LLM translation call on a hot path.

**Told the model a nudge reply is unresolved**, in the two places it reads: `NUDGE_ALREADY_SET_NOTE` (shared by `pick_aoi` and `pick_dataset`) and the system prompt's Nudges section, which now points at the session block as the check — if it still says `AOI: none`, resolve first regardless of what the user's message looks like.

**Documented that the option format is load-bearing** (`_format_aoi_candidate`). The re-resolution round-trip terminates only because the option carries the full comma-joined hierarchy: re-querying with it scores 1.0 by trigram similarity against the same `name` column, while same-name rows in other countries fall below `pg_trgm.similarity_threshold = 0.2`, so `check_duplicate_aois` finds no rivals and the nudge does not re-fire.

```
1.000  Paris, Île-de-France, France
0.182  Paris, Ontario, Canada          filtered
0.154  Paris, Texas, United States     filtered
0.143  Paris, Kentucky, United States  filtered
```

Shortened to a bare `"Paris"`, every Paris would match again and the nudge would re-offer the same choice indefinitely — with the new guard, on a loop.

**Refactor:** the repeated `Command(update={"messages": [ToolMessage(...)]})` block in `pull_data` is extracted to `_human_feedback`. It was written out three times; the guards would have made it five.

## No frontend change needed

`ChatNudge.handlePick` optimistically adds the picked dataset's layer to the map for `dataset_choice`, which round-trips into `ui_context.dataset_selected` and lets the backend set `state["dataset"]` without `pick_dataset`. There is no `aoi_choice` equivalent — which is why `dataset` was present and `aoi_selection` was not.

That asymmetry is a latency optimization, not the mechanism. The intended flow works on its own: click → text → `pick_aoi` → `aoi_selection` in state → streamed → `pickAoi.ts` adds the area layer and flies to it. The only defect was the model skipping `pick_aoi`, which is what this PR fixes.

## Tests

`TestMissingSelectionGuards` in `tests/tools/test_pull_data.py` — five cases: missing `aoi_selection` (the production case), missing `dataset`, present-but-empty `aois`, pending `aoi_choice` options echoed to the model, and an unrelated pending nudge *not* echoed. All five fail against `main` with `KeyError` and pass here.

`tests/unit` (418) and `tests/api` (294) green; ruff and mypy clean.

author: parkerron1971-hash
body:
**"Six rooms. One brain."** was a headline over a carousel. The carousel proves the six rooms. Nothing proved the *one brain* — you clicked through six separate-looking screens and took the sentence on faith.

Section 04 now ends with a board **whose stops are the rooms**. One decision walks the whole spine in the order it really touches them:

> **You decide to sell something new** → The Academy *(decide it)* → The Studio *(dress it)* → Smart Sites *(house it)* → Clients *(tell it)* → Operate *(sell it)* → Autopilot *(keep it)* → **It's live, and it sells**

Reaching a stop swaps the panel beneath it to that room. The rooms stop being six things you click through and become six places the system walks you through.

### Not the hero board again

That one is a *branched* spine over generic surfaces arguing "these parts are connected." Showing the same picture twice would have halved both. This is a **straight** spine whose nodes are the six rooms — a different diagram, a different argument, in the one place on the page already about rooms.

### Paced by the visitor, never a timer

- **Desktop** — the section pins for one screen; the distance you scroll is the distance the current travels.
- **Phone** — nothing pins. Progress is read from where the section sits in the viewport, so it moves exactly as fast as your thumb. Arriving at it can never start a race already half run. Ramp measured at an even two stops per quarter of scroll.
- The phone drops the room panel: it would sit under a board taller than the screen, so the two could never be seen together — and each stop already names its room and says what it did beside its own dot.

### The one risky change, and why it's safe

`.rooms` moves from `overflow:hidden` to `overflow:clip`. Both contain the 3D ring identically, but **`hidden` makes the section a scroll container, which silently kills `position:sticky` in every descendant**. `clip` never creates one.

Verified after the change:
- pin holds at `0` across the entire scrub (0 / 30 / 60 / 90%)
- six ring faces intact, 3D transform still applied
- document has **no horizontal overflow**, zero offending elements

### Notes

- **Self-contained** — own `rm-` prefix, own script, so it cannot destabilise the hero board that is already live. Reuses only the `#bdglow` filter that board emits once per page.
- The scroll handler is **deliberately not rAF-throttled**. The obvious guard leaves the board frozen for good if the scheduled frame is ever dropped, because the flag never clears — I hit exactly that while measuring an earlier version.
- `?rooms=m` forces the phone path for review, since window resizing isn't reliably available here.

### Verified

- All 7 marketing pages render (shared CSS touched, so checked not assumed)
- Driven in Chrome on the real rendered page: pin, scrub, room-panel swapping, and the phone path
- **Tests: 3456 passed, 15 skipped — identical to main, zero regressions**

### Still open, and yours

On desktop this sits **alongside** the existing six-room carousel rather than replacing it. If the board is now walking people through the rooms, the carousel underneath may be redundant. I left it in rather than delete something you hadn't agreed to lose.

## Summary

Follow-up to #8. The smoke job failed on `main` (run [#31592180044](https://github.com/oimlsmart/studio/actions/runs/31592180044)) — the preview server never became ready.

## Root cause

`npm run preview &` captured the wrapper's PID, not the daemon's. Astro preview detaches by default in v7, so the wrapper exits immediately. The readiness curl was hitting port 4322 (hardcoded) but the daemon was on 4321 (astro's default).

## Fix

- Use `npx astro preview --port 4322 --host --background` — explicit port, explicit daemon
- Stop via `npx astro preview stop` (not the captured PID, which was the wrapper's)

author: riverdave
body:
mem2reg gives up on a slot if any use lives in a nested region whose parent op doesn't implement PromotableRegionOpInterface. No CIR op implements it. So this doesn't promote:
```mlir
%a = cir.alloca "a" align(4) : !cir.ptr<!s32i>
%c = cir.const #cir.int<42> : !s32i
cir.store %c, %a : !s32i, !cir.ptr<!s32i>
cir.if %cond {
  %v = cir.load %a : !cir.ptr<!s32i>, !s32i
  cir.call @use(%v) : (!s32i) -> ()
}
```
You have to run -cir-flatten-cfg first, which is why mem2reg.cir does. That's a lot of destruction for a value that never leaves the region.

This implements the interface for cir.if and cir.scope. Both regions are entered straight from before the op, so they see the reaching definition unchanged. Nothing to merge, nothing to yield.

Stores inside a region are refused. A new definition has to exit through a result,  cir.if has none, cir.scope has one it may already be using. Supporting that means giving those ops results. Separate patch.

My use case specifically:
Downstream, I'm propagating constants into CUDA kernel arguments.[ Every launch site sits inside a cir.if, the __cudaPushCallConfiguration guard](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/5bf59e2c4b54a85e4e7f0e188b99061beb2708f6/clang/lib/CIR/CodeGen/CIRGenCUDARuntime.cpp#L33), so the argument reaching the device stub call site is always a cir.load. In particular this allows other MLIR passes like sccp, determine if such value is in constant form through the call graph. So the argument flow would be like this: mem2reg turns it into the block argument, sccp turns that into a cir.const, and you get the constant at the call site.
 
Claude assisted with this patch.

author: archer30
body:
…tension

## Summary

Improve System Options Extension behavior when leaving combat through ERA's `FastQuitToGameMenu`, while preserving the existing upstream dialog behavior.

## Problems fixed

- `FastQuitToGameMenu` unwinds combat without firing `OnAfterBattle`. Temporary Quick Combat and Auto Spells settings could therefore persist after loading, restarting, or leaving the game from combat.

- FastQuit is a local exception-based unwind and is not safe for a real network battle. Using Load, Restart, Main Menu, or Quit during network combat could leave the remote peer waiting or cause synchronization problems.

- The dialog's temporary `networkGame` member is part of the nested-dialog cleanup contract and is not a reliable way to determine whether the current game is actually a network session.

## Changes

- Extract the Quick Combat restoration into `RestoreOriginalQuickCombatSettings()`.

- Restore temporary combat settings from both `OnAfterBattle` and `OnGameLeave`. This covers normal battle completion and FastQuit.

- Clear the restoration flag after applying the original settings, making the cleanup idempotent.

- Detect an actual network game using the engine network-session state.

- Disable Load, Restart, Main Menu, and Quit actions during real network combat.

- Add a second network guard before calling `FastQuitToGameMenu`.

- Preserve the existing nested network-dialog cleanup performed around the System Options dialog.

- Build the Release configuration with `v141_xp`, `WINVER=0x0501`, and `_WIN32_WINNT=0x0501` for Windows XP compatibility.

## Scope

This change repairs state owned by System Options Extension and prevents its unsafe FastQuit entry points during network combat. It does not attempt to provide general cleanup for all engine or third-party plugin state skipped by ERA's FastQuit mechanism.

body:
## Summary

- Store each type constructor package ID, module name, name, arity, and kind.
- Store structured package, module, and name fields in each global term key.
- Remove the special type-name identity rules.
- Receive the `aihc-prim` package ID from each type-checker caller.
- Use resolver identities for ordinary types, including user-defined `Int` and `Bool` types.
- Define `Int` in `aihc-prim:GHC.Types`.
- Re-export `Int` from `aihc-base:GHC.Int`.
- Retain type identities during type checks and System FC generation.
- Keep each bundled REPL module with its source package during module loading.
- Use `aihc-prim:GHC.Types.Bool` for System FC case binders.

## Reason

Type constructors with the same name and arity had the same identity.
This error caused types from different modules to conflict.
Special type-name rules also removed the defining package and module.
The REPL loader also discarded each source package after it found the module path.
System FC desugaring found `Bool` through the current term scope.

## Effect

All resolved types retain their defining package and module.
The type-checker only needs the caller-provided `aihc-prim` package ID for compiler-known types.
Bundled REPL modules retain the `aihc-base` or `aihc-prim` package identity.
System FC desugaring uses the caller-provided prim package ID for `GHC.Types.Bool`.

author: cmettler
body:
Follow-on to #125. `CommitWriteAsync` hardcodes `isBlindAppend: true` for any plain append, which is a claim only the caller can make.

## The claim

```csharp
bool blindAppend = mode == DeltaWriteMode.Append && !dynamicPartitionOverwrite;
if (blindAppend)
{
    // "A plain append takes its rows from the caller and reads no file of this table to decide
    //  what to write, which is Delta's definition (readPredicates.isEmpty && readFiles.isEmpty)."
    committedVersion = await CommitOccAsync(..., isBlindAppend: true);
}
```

The comment is true of what the library does and not of what the field means. `isBlindAppend` describes the **transaction**, and Delta's definition is conjunctive — `onlyAddFiles && !dependsOnFiles`. `DeltaWriteMode.Append` establishes the first conjunct and says nothing about the second: it describes the commit's output shape, while the flag describes what was read to produce the rows.

#125's own `DeltaTransaction.IsBlindAppend` states the rule this needs:

> This library cannot derive it for a host with its own data plane. A transaction records the reads made THROUGH it, but a host that scanned the table itself and then staged the result has made a read this library never saw — which is exactly the case the claim exists for.

That rule is applied on the staged surface — `EffectiveIsBlindAppend` derives only `false`, never `true` — and skipped on the auto-committing one. `WriteAsync` is the host-facing append API, so it is precisely the surface the rule is about.

## The measurement

fabricator drives engineered-wood as a host with its own data plane. Codec engine, autocommit, `delta.isolationLevel = write_serializable`:

| version | statement | recorded |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | `INSERT INTO t VALUES (100)` | `true` — correct |
| 3 | `INSERT INTO t SELECT max(id) + 1 FROM t` | **`true` — wrong** |

Both reach `WriteAsync(batches, DeltaWriteMode.Append)` as identical calls: a list of `RecordBatch` and a mode. Nothing in either records that v3's rows came from scanning the table it is appending to.

v3 is the anti-join incremental shape, i.e. the `insert_select_self` row #125's own interop tier singled out:

> its operation is WRITE, exactly like the genuine blind append above it, and its commit carries nothing but adds, exactly like the genuine blind append above it. The recorded flag is the ONLY thing that tells them apart.

So the reader now believes a flag the writer emits falsely, for the one commit shape the flag exists to distinguish. Under WriteSerializable another engine skips the `concurrentAppend` check it owed — the direction #125 itself names as unsafe, against "saying nothing costs only spurious conflicts".

## The change

`bool? isBlindAppend = null` threaded through both public `WriteAsync` overloads into `WriteCoreAsync` and `CommitWriteAsync`, replacing the hardcode. +37/−13, one file.

- **Default `null` = absent**, the pre-#125 behaviour for a caller that says nothing. The library stops answering a question only the caller can answer.
- **The overwrite branch keeps its hardcoded `false`.** That one the library genuinely knows: it reads the active-file set to decide what to remove. The asymmetry is the point — engineered-wood can prove "not blind" from its own actions, but never "blind".
- **`DeltaTransaction.EffectiveIsBlindAppend` is untouched.** Its one-directional derivation (a recorded read proves `false`; no recorded read proves nothing) is right, and is the model this mirrors.
- Internal DML (`DeleteAsync`/`UpdateAsync`) stages through a transaction and keeps deriving `false` — unaffected.

Cost to a caller that was getting `true`: pass `true`. That is a one-line change at a call site which, by construction, knows whether it read.

## Anticipated objection

That `WriteAsync` means "you hand me rows, I append them", so a caller has implicitly asserted blindness. `DeltaWriteMode.Append` is a *mode* argument rather than a read-set assertion, and the two shapes above pass the identical mode. Delta itself computes `onlyAddFiles` separately and then pointedly does not use it alone, which reads as the same conclusion reached independently.

## Testing

Gated downstream in fabricator's `verify_delta_catalog_transactions` §42, run against both write engines: a declaration pin for the versions the host states, a positive control counting blind claims, and a safety property asserting no other version claims blind. Mutation-tested by restoring the hardcode — it dies with three blind claims where one is true.

No engineered-wood test is added here, since the behaviour needs a host that reads outside the library to exercise it. Happy to add one driving `WriteAsync` with an explicit `false` and asserting the field is absent by default, if that shape is wanted.

Draft: opened for the argument rather than to merge as-is. If you would rather the parameter live somewhere else — an option on `DeltaTableOptions`, or a property mirroring `DeltaTransaction.IsBlindAppend` — the placement is not the part I care about.

body:
## Summary

#973 shipped `0-for-3` as a fact. **It is not verifiable, and the framing was wrong.**

`
dd57241c  audit-snippet-lines=0     <- index landed here (#965)
6ecb984d  audit-snippet-lines=0
2fd31fc1  audit-snippet-lines=0
bccce831  audit-snippet-lines=1     <- first executable audit (#971)
`

**No executable audit existed until #971.** At the time of the two earlier catches the
file carried prose only. So the bullet credited an instrument that did not exist, and I
wrote it from memory — two PRs after recording that *an author auditing his own claim
consults his intent, not the artifact*.

## What survives

- **One confirmed miss**, verified: the `But a gate means ask, not refuse` row was live
  in `main` from #967 through #969, absent at `bccce831`. That is enough to carry the
  corollary.
- **Two unattributable catches.** No instrument existed and no artifact records what found
  them. Verdict is the third state this document keeps insisting on — **UNATTRIBUTED**,
  not zero.

## What replaces it, and is sharper

The prose said *grep every row against the headings* — table-derived, and correct. What
was executed was keyed to a hand-maintained list. The record came from an undocumented
substitute while the credit went to the prose. Hence:

> **Prose describing a check is not a check.** It has no output, so it can never be
> observed to fail, and nothing forces the thing actually run to resemble it.

Which is the whole reason #971's snippet is executable.

## Also corrected, in the other direction

The peer's amplification — no input from the subject, every PASS carrying zero bits — is
too strong. The check read the headings and would have fired had one been renamed. Its
blind spot is one direction: substring matching lets a row with **extra** text pass, so
only row text drifting from intent is invisible.

## Changes

- `0-for-3` retracted **at the point of assertion**, per the `#929` standard.
- Corollary rests on the one confirmed miss.
- `prose describing a check is not a check` recorded.
- The "no input" overstatement scoped to the direction that is true.

## Issues

Closes #974

## Testing

- [x] Table-derived reference audit after `prettier --write`: `rows=9 broken=0`
- [x] Corollary count check: declared `Three` / 3 bullets
- [x] Retraction verified present within the corollary block, not as a banner
- [x] No surviving `0-for-3` claim outside the retraction itself
- [x] `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm copy:check`

author: vedant-simulacrum
body:
Closes part of SR-017 (P-1140F-3). Does **not** close the finding — this unit cannot cite its own merge commit, and the state and verdict are the owner's. SR-017's `closure_evidence` is written in the next PR.

## What was wrong

SR-017 names seven conflicting artifacts. PF-017, its only serving unit, opened one of them (`source-receipt-v1.schema.json`). Two held the contradiction:

- `verifier-appraisal-v1` carried seven classification dimensions as unnamed integers.
- `appraisal-result-v1.schema.json` carried the same seven by name, plus the claim digest, evidence digest, validity interval and supersession chain.
- `verifier_appraisals` stored three states — `provenance_state`, `continuity_state`, `integrity_state` — that appeared in neither.

## Why it lasted

`appraisal_wire_ranges()` matched `0..<n>` and nothing else, so it parsed ten labels of twenty-three. Labels 3, 5, 14 and 18–22 were invisible to every check built on it. A field could be added to the record and to no label, or dropped from the grammar entirely, and the only thing looking would report that ten dimensions were still in range.

## The repair

`appraisal_cddl_labels()` reads every label and its declared type. `appraisal-policy-v1.json` gains `wire_binding.labels` (label → record field) and `record_only_fields` (the six deliberately off the wire, each with a reason). `validate_evidence_chain` now fails **in both directions** on field set, on per-field nullability, and on ordinal density — and runs the same shape against the DDL via `column_bindings`, `column_only`, and `unbound_fields` split from `unpersisted_fields`.

The CDDL gains the evidence-bundle digest, both halves of the supersession chain, the certification state and the three evaluated bundle identifiers; labels 5 and 18 admit nil. `verifier_appraisals` goes from 9 columns to 31, with a unique index making one appraisal current per claim.

## Three things found while repairing

- **Three slack integer ranges.** Tightening `>` to `=` exposed `capture_class` and `accounting_class` declared `0..4` against four values and `device_key_class` `0..6` against six. Each had one integer that encoded successfully and resolved to nothing — the shape PF-070 found once in the gap declaration's cause label, here three times in the rule nothing parsed. The test that widens `capture_class` back was confirmed against the pre-repair validator: it passed there.
- **`bound_columns` was a second spelling.** It listed column names beside `unbound_fields`' record-field names with nothing connecting the two vocabularies — which is how `evidence_profile_id text not null` sat in the bound list, declared reconciled, while contradicting both other authorities. It is nullable now: a rejected claim is awarded no profile, so the table could not store the outcome of a rejection.
- **`source_limb` excused nothing.** It named no field of the record, no label of the CDDL and no column of the table.

## One aggregate, one owner

`evidence_assessments` and `verifier_appraisals` both held this aggregate with nothing saying which won. `verifier_appraisals` is the owner. The three assessed states leave it rather than being redeclared beside the seven dimensions, and their `SQL_LOCAL_VOCABULARIES` entries are deleted rather than left pointing at columns that no longer exist.

## Validation

- `make validate` — pass, zero FAIL lines
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` — **1111 tests, OK** (1097 before; +14 drift-injection tests)
- `scripts/repository/doctor.py` — PASS
- `validate_repair_task_binding.py` — SR-017 now **2/2**
- `validate_finding_artifact_coverage.py` — pass
- Scope check prints nothing: no `apps/`, `crates/`, `migrations/` changes

Postgres DDL skips locally (no Docker); CI is its first real execution of the new `verifier_appraisals` shape.

## Claim scope

`validate_evidence_chain` proves the three authorities agree about the record. It does not prove any implementation produces it — no verifier evaluates a dimension and no row is written. There is still no instance-level CDDL conformance execution, so `verifier-appraisal-v1` remains a grammar nothing decodes against.

author: spydon
body:
## What

Renames the pure Dart client package from `supabase` to `supabase_dart`, and its library entrypoint from `supabase.dart` to `supabase_dart.dart`.

The `supabase` name reads like the umbrella name for the whole SDK, so people keep adding it to Flutter projects instead of `supabase_flutter` and then report that things do not work. The new name makes the split obvious at the point where a dependency is picked.

## Changes

- `packages/supabase` moved to `packages/supabase_dart`, with `name: supabase_dart` in the pubspec and the repository link updated.
- `lib/supabase.dart` renamed to `lib/supabase_dart.dart`. Every internal import and the `supabase_flutter` re-export now point at `package:supabase_dart/supabase_dart.dart`.
- `supabase_flutter` depends on `supabase_dart` instead of `supabase`. Nothing in its public surface changes, it re-exports the same symbols.
- The Dart example package is renamed to `supabase_dart_example` and depends on `supabase_dart`.
- Root `pubspec.yaml` workspace entries, the test/pana workflow package lists and coverage carryforward flags, the issue-form library dropdown, and the issue label mapping all use the new name. The label mapping keeps the old `supabase` key so existing reports still land on the same label.
- READMEs, `AGENTS.md`, `MIGRATION.md` and the `sdk-compliance.yaml` header comment updated. Nothing inside the package is renamed, so `SupabaseClient` and everything it exposes keeps its name, and no capability statuses change.
- `MIGRATION.md` gains a v2 to v3 section covering the dependency and import rename.

## Follow-up outside this repo

Publishing `supabase_dart` and marking `supabase` as discontinued on pub.dev, pointing at the new name, has to happen at release time.

## Testing

- `dart analyze` clean across the workspace, and `dart analyze --fatal-infos` clean in `packages/supabase_dart`.
- `dart test` passes for the offline `supabase_dart` suites (`api_key`, `mock`, `stream_filter`, `trace_propagation`, `utilities`).
- `flutter test` passes in `packages/supabase_flutter`.
- `dart format -l 80 --set-exit-if-changed` reports no changes.

## Summary

- keep setup-only GitHub credentials out of the Codex Cloud agent credential store; native GitHub connector/task controls remain the supported control plane
- pin the task merge base and prevent recursive Cloud node/npm command shims
- retain credential-free origin validation and document the exact Cloud capability boundary

RAG impact: no retrieval behaviour change — Cloud bootstrap, GitHub control-plane policy, and environment documentation only.

## Verification

- [x] `npm run check:codex-cloud` — `[Codex Cloud Check] PASS: static Cloud contracts match.`
- [x] `npm run docs:check-inventory` — current at 226 script files and 236 npm scripts
- [x] `npm run check:branch-review-ledger` — passed

- [ ] `npm run test -- tests/codex-cloud-setup.test.ts` — not rerun after the final security repair because the repository run coordinator was at focused-test capacity; the earlier PR head passed 24/24, and CI will exercise the pushed head
- [ ] local lint/typecheck — the pre-push guard reported the repository heavyweight coordinator busy; hosted CI remains authoritative for this pushed head

## Risk and rollback

- Risk: Cloud tasks without native GitHub connector tools may still lack some hosted GitHub operations. This is an explicit platform limitation rather than a reason to persist a setup-only PAT into agent-accessible storage.
- Rollback: revert the final security repair only if a future platform-owned credential broker exposes narrowly scoped GitHub capabilities without making the underlying credential retrievable by the agent.
- Provider or production effects: pushed only this non-protected feature branch and updated this PR. No deployment, protected-branch push, PR merge/close, branch deletion, rebase, or force-push.

## Review disposition

The prior fix rejected plaintext `hosts.yml`, but OS-backed storage still allowed the same agent user to run `gh auth token` or otherwise use the persisted setup credential. Head `6ba68ffed2a3f7b36afa06067f5b2e04800b398e` removes that persistence path and adds a static regression guard while retaining the independent base-refresh and command-shim repairs.

author: mrdntgrn
body:
Part of [DMVP-9656](https://tutorbot.atlassian.net/browse/DMVP-9656). Speckit package: `specs/001-terraform-test-native-support/`.

## Three defects, not one

1. **No `terraform init` step**, despite the action description claiming "init, test". Verified empirically: a provider-less module passes without init; one declaring `required_providers` fails with `Missing required provider`. Every real module repository hits this
2. **`terraform_version` defaults to 1.3.6**, which predates the native test framework. The experimental `terraform test` from 1.3 was *removed* in 1.6, so the old default could not run either generation correctly
3. **Existence-only tests check.** It verified `tests/` existed but not that anything discoverable was in it. Since `terraform test` does not recurse, a repo with files at `tests/<case>/main.tftest.hcl` passed the check, ran zero tests, and reported success

Also: `path` defaulted to `/`, so the default config would `cd /` to the filesystem root.

## The new guard

Counts discoverable files at depth 1 and nested files below. Fails when discoverable is zero, naming the nested paths so the layout can be fixed. Warns without failing when both exist, so partial migrations are not blocked. Exercised against discoverable / nested-only / empty fixtures.

## ⚠️ Merge last — this is live for consumers on `@main`

Six first-party repos pin `terraform-test@main`, so merging takes effect immediately with no tag gate:

| Repo | `tests/` | discoverable `.tftest.hcl` | effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `terraform-aws-dns` | yes | 0 | **newly fails** at the guard |
| `terraform-aws-frontend-app` | yes | 0 | **newly fails** at the guard |
| `terraform-any-shared` | no | 0 | already failing today |
| `terraform-any-wireguard` | no | 0 | already failing today |
| `terraform-aws-iam` | no | 0 | already failing today |
| `terraform-aws-sns` | no | 0 | already failing today |

The four without `tests/` already fail on the existing check, so nothing changes for them. The two with `tests/` but no native test files will go from green-but-testing-nothing to red — which is the intended signal, but should be a deliberate choice rather than a surprise.

Repos pinned to `@4.1.1` / `@4.2.x` / `@4.3.0` are unaffected until a new tag is cut and adopted.

## Suggested sequencing

Either pin those six to a tag before merging, or merge and accept the two red builds as the correct signal.

Raising the Terraform default is a behavior change, judged safe because the previous default could not run tests in either generation. Consumers can still pin `terraform_version` explicitly.

author: claussa
body:
Dans la lignée de #25 (hébergeur) et #26 (volontaire) : le tour guidé de l'espace unité.

## Ce que ça fait

- **Proposé une seule fois sur « Jumelage »** (la liste des unités, où redirige la publication de l'annonce), quand `User.unitTourStatus` est null et qu'une annonce est ACTIVE. Refus, croix ou abandon en cours → `SKIPPED` (jamais re-proposé) ; parcours complet → `DONE`.
- **Un seul tour pour les deux sens d'annonce** : chercher un jumelage ou pouvoir jumeler traversent la même interface — seul le wording s'adapte au sens (`kind`) de l'annonce (titre/description de la liste, message de la demande d'exemple, étape finale).
- Le parcours (9 étapes) : liste des unités du sens opposé avec une **annonce d'exemple « 1re Exemple »** injectée côté client (compteur ajusté, lien neutralisé, jamais d'appel API) → demande de mise en relation → « Demandes de mise en relation » avec une **demande d'exemple à accepter soi-même** (badge « Demande d'exemple », carte « En relation » aux coordonnées fictives) → accepter/ignorer (ni refus ni expiration, jumelages multiples) → échange de coordonnées et limite de la plateforme → retrait d'annonce (mises en relation acquises) → retour sur la liste.

## Backend

- Nouveau champ `User.unitTourStatus` (enum `TourStatus` partagé, migration `20260812170000`), exposé dans `MeSchema`, le select DTO et l'export RGPD.
- `PATCH /me` : écrit `unitTourStatus` pour les comptes `SCOUT_UNIT` uniquement — symétrique des champs host/seeker réservés aux `INDIVIDUAL` (chaque type ignore les champs de l'autre).
- Événements PostHog `unit_tour_*` (proposed/declined/started/completed/abandoned), sans PII.

## À savoir pour la review

- Infrastructure commune aux trois tours : `tour-lib.tsx` (`TourStatusField` étendu), aucun changement de comportement des tours existants.
- **Piège driver.js documenté dans `Jumelage.tsx`** : l'ancre de l'étape 1 (`data-tour="unites"`) n'est posée que pendant le tour. La liste existe avant l'injection de l'exemple ; une ancre permanente serait mesurée par driver.js sur ce rectangle périmé (popover posé SUR la carte au lieu d'en dessous).
- Les gardes `demo` neutralisent tout appel API sur les cartes d'exemple, en plus du `disableActiveInteraction` global du tour.

## Tests

- Test d'intégration `PATCH /me` étendu (112/112 verts) : null au départ, `unitTourStatus` ignoré pour INDIVIDUAL et host/seeker ignorés pour SCOUT_UNIT, progression SKIPPED→DONE.
- Testé de bout en bout dans le navigateur, **dans les deux sens d'annonce** : proposition, refus→SKIPPED, abandon en cours→SKIPPED, tour complet→DONE (9/9, wording SEEKING puis HOSTING), cohabitation exemple/annonces réelles dans la liste, non-réapparition après chaque issue.

author: xylar
body:
The first half of the `plan` layer — DESIGN.md §3.3.1–§3.3.4. Attribution, provenance, removals and the gates follow in a second branch off `main`.

## `python_min` (§3.3.3)

Read from what the pull request already contains — the recipe's own `context.python_min` where it sets one, `.ci_support` otherwise — never fetched. That removes the staleness problem rather than solving it.

DESIGN says any single `.ci_support` file will do because `python_min` cannot differ per architecture. That is now **measured**: across the 217 feedstock checkouts on this machine carrying it, no feedstock's build variants disagree. The same survey shows the fleet mid-migration — **82 checkouts on 3.9, 135 on 3.10** — which is the concrete argument for reading it per feedstock rather than pinning DESIGN's stated 3.9.

An unquoted `python_min: 3.10` is refused: in YAML that is the float `3.1`, a whole Python release out and otherwise indistinguishable from meaning 3.1.

## Marker reconciliation (§3.3.1–§3.3.4)

Discard variants gated below the floor, intersect what survives, stop on an empty intersection, comment the line where a marker-qualified variant supplied the binding bound.

**Two bugs the tests caught, not the reading:**

- `SpecifierSet` intersects by *unioning* clauses, so the three `pandas` declarations came out `>=2.1.2,>=2.2.3,>=2.3.3` when only the last binds.
- `str(SpecifierSet)` orders clauses alphabetically, putting the ceiling first — where every recipe in the corpus writes `>=2.21.0,<3.0.0`, floor first.

Rendering now reduces the bound operators and orders them as recipes are written. An `==`, `~=` or `===` anywhere leaves clauses exactly as they came: simplifying those is version-range algebra, and untidy is recoverable where subtly wrong is not.

Satisfiability is decided by trying the versions the set mentions plus a point either side, which also gets `>1.0,<=1.0` and `~=2.1,<2.0` right. Reachability samples both ends of each minor release so a window like `python_full_version >= "3.12.4"` is not mistaken for unreachable — being wrong in the *discard* direction would silently drop a real constraint.

## Verification

Swept over every real provider: **688 dependency groups across 89 `pyproject.toml`, 684 reconciled, zero crashes.** All 4 stops are genuinely `sys_platform`-conditional (`kerberos`, `winkerberos`) — exactly §3.3.4.

Against the golden corpus, **every marker-reconciliation line is reproduced exactly** — constraint *and* comment wording — matching the published output of the tool being replaced. That is now a parametrized test, with a guard so it cannot silently cover nothing:

```
pandas >=2.3.3          # more restrictive for python >=3.14
psycopg >=3.3.3         # more restrictive for python >=3.14
psycopg2-binary >=2.9.10  # more restrictive for python >=3.13
asgiref >=3.11.1        # more restrictive for python >=3.14
pyarrow >=22.0.0        # more restrictive for python >=3.14
```

Both stops assert on the **message**, per §11 — the contradiction quotes the conflict, names the Python range and where that number came from, and names the config file to resolve it in; the platform stop names both resolutions, since "swage cannot" and "swage will not choose for you" send the reader somewhere very different.

485 tests; both commits independently green.

body:
Fixes #538

## Проблема

Админка → редактирование категории → вкладка «Сетка товаров». Клик по удалению (строка **или** «Удалить выбранные») показывал **два диалога подтверждения сразу**.

## Причина

Страница `category/update` монтирует **два независимых Vue-приложения** (`update.class.php:70-71`): `category-products` (`CategoryProductsGrid`) и `category-options` (`CategoryOptionsTab`). PrimeVue вынесен в общий Import Map (externalized в `vite.config.js`) → один экземпляр модуля на страницу, а `ConfirmationEventBus` внутри PrimeVue — **модульный singleton**. Значит `confirm.require()` без `group` ловится **всеми** смонтированными ungrouped `<ConfirmDialog>` на странице, в каком бы приложении они ни были. На этой странице их было два → два диалога.

## Решение

Namespace обоих приложений через confirm-`group` (паттерн уже используется в `ExtraFieldsManager`, `GridFieldsConfig`, `ModelFieldsGrid`, `ProductDataConfig`):

- `useActions` / `useSelection` — новая **опциональная** опция `confirmGroup`, подставляется в `confirm.require({ group })`. По умолчанию `null` → ungrouped (полная обратная совместимость).
- `ActionsColumn` — новый проп `confirmGroup`, проброс в `useActions`.
- `CategoryProductsGrid` — `group="category-products"` на `<ConfirmDialog>`; группа прокинута в `useSelection` и `ActionsColumn`; убран висячий `useConfirm()` (мусор от рефактора).
- `CategoryOptionsTab` — `group="category-options"` на `<ConfirmDialog>` и в обоих `confirm.require`.

Остальные гриды (Customers/Orders/Deliveries/Payments/…) **не тронуты**: `confirmGroup` opt-in, по умолчанию ungrouped — поведение прежнее.

## Проверка

- ESLint (5 файлов) ✓
- `npm run build` ✓
- Проверено на DEV после hard-reload: в сетке товаров и в опциях категории теперь **один** confirm, удаление (строчное и bulk) работает.

## Связанное

Системный риск той же природы (общая шина PrimeVue на страницах с несколькими Vue-приложениями/табами, потенциально `product-tabs`, а также `ToastEventBus`) вынесен отдельно: #539.

author: jcschaff
body:
The nightly posted a thousand-line report to Slack and was green regardless of what it found. Nobody reads it, and nothing enforces it.

## Why it never failed

Three causes, none of them a missing feature:

- `TestReportCommand.call()` ended in an unconditional `return 0`
- the only alarm could never fire — `grep -q PATTERN "$(cat report.md)"` passes the file's **contents** as the filename. It already carried a `# Not currently working` comment
- nothing else in the job could fail (no `continue-on-error` involved — nothing ever exited non-zero)

## The comparison already existed

`vcell-cli/src/main/resources/test_cases.ndjson` is the documented baseline — 1072 `SYSBIO_BIOMD` cases, 893 PASS + 179 FAIL, exactly the report's "Historical" column — and `OmexTestReport` already classified every deviation. It simply had no way to say so. This gives it one.

## What now fails a run

| condition | meaning |
|---|---|
| **changed** | an undocumented failure, a documented failure that has started passing, or a documented failure that now fails a *different* way |
| **stopped running** | a documented case that did not execute |
| **undocumented** | an execution with no baseline entry |

A newly *passing* case fails the run too: the baseline is now wrong, and left alone it masks the next real regression.

**"Stopped running" is the one that matters most**, because it reads as good news. Last night is the example: passes 893→889 and failures 179→172 looked like an improvement, but the entire delta was 11 models that did not run (4 passes, 6 `SOLVER_FAILURE`, 1 `TOO_SLOW`). Nothing actually improved.

## Those 11 turned out to be deliberate

They are exactly the workflow's own hard-coded skip list at line 179 — `235|255|595|711|1008|1013|1022|1025|1030|1035|1042`, commented *"too slow or otherwise misbehaved"* — never reconciled with the baseline. The gate would have gone red every night for an intentional exclusion.

`SKIP` already means "known not to run", so documented-SKIP cases are exempt from "stopped running", and those 11 are marked `SKIP` with the reason recorded (11 lines changed, formatting preserved).

## Keeping the gate survivable

`--update-test-cases` writes the baseline the run implies — across **all** collections, so it stays diffable against the committed file rather than dropping the 110 rows this run doesn't cover. Accepting a legitimate change becomes a reviewable diff instead of a hand-edit of 1182 lines. That is what decides whether a hard gate survives contact.

## Verified against real data

Against last night's actual `exec_summary.ndjson` (1061 lines, downloaded from run 31574242739):

- reports `FAIL: 3 changed` and names them — `BIOMD0000000459/460/461`, `SBML_IMPORT_FAILURE → UNCATEGORIZED_FAULT`
- `--update-test-cases` produces a file differing in **exactly those 3 lines** out of 1182
- re-running against that file exits **0**, `PASS: no changes`, and the report's Historical column now agrees with Current (889/172 both sides) instead of the misleading 893/179

So the first run goes red for a genuine reason, with a 3-line diff to accept.

## Slack is now two or three lines

```
🔴 *BMDB nightly: FAIL* - 3 changed
Accept these results by committing the `test_cases.updated.ndjson` artifact over `vcell-cli/src/main/resources/test_cases.ndjson`.
<run details, full report and updated baseline>
```

Green is one line plus the link. The full report and the updated baseline are artifacts of the run.

body:
## Problem

Eight internal links point at `/fhe-library` and `/client-sdk/quick-start`. Neither is a page — they are section prefixes. Neither exists as an `.mdx` file, and neither appears as a nav entry in `docs.json`, so all eight 404:

| File | Link text | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`fhe-library/introduction/best-practices.mdx:205`](fhe-library/introduction/best-practices.mdx#L205) | encrypted data types | `/fhe-library` |
| [`fhe-library/introduction/best-practices.mdx:206`](fhe-library/introduction/best-practices.mdx#L206) | FHE operations | `/fhe-library` |
| [`fhe-library/introduction/best-practices.mdx:207`](fhe-library/introduction/best-practices.mdx#L207) | access control mechanisms | `/fhe-library` |
| [`fhe-library/introduction/best-practices.mdx:208`](fhe-library/introduction/best-practices.mdx#L208) | common pitfalls | `/fhe-library` |
| [`fhe-library/introduction/quick-start.mdx:324`](fhe-library/introduction/quick-start.mdx#L324) | FHE Library documentation | `/fhe-library` |
| [`fhe-library/introduction/quick-start.mdx:327`](fhe-library/introduction/quick-start.mdx#L327) | access control mechanisms | `/fhe-library` |
| [`client-sdk/introduction/overview.mdx:96`](client-sdk/introduction/overview.mdx#L96) | Quick Start (Card) | `/client-sdk/quick-start` |
| [`client-sdk/introduction/installation.mdx:119`](client-sdk/introduction/installation.mdx#L119) | Quick Start | `/client-sdk/quick-start` |

All eight sit in "Next steps" / "What's next" blocks — the exact place a reader clicks after finishing a page, so this is the worst spot for a dead end. `best-practices.mdx` is the clearest case: four consecutive bullets with four different link texts all resolving to the same non-existent path.

## Change

Retargeted each link by its own link text, to the page whose existing title/description already matches — no page was renamed, added, or reworded:

| Link text | New target | Why that page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| encrypted data types | `/fhe-library/reference/fhe-sol/overview` | its description is "Encrypted data types, imports, and general usage of the FHE Solidity library" |
| FHE operations | `/fhe-library/core-concepts/encrypted-operations` | titled "FHE Encrypted Operations" |
| access control mechanisms | `/fhe-library/core-concepts/access-control` | titled "Access Control" |
| common pitfalls | `/fhe-library/core-concepts/common-errors` | titled "Common Errors" |
| FHE Library documentation | `/fhe-library/introduction/overview` | the FHE Library section's own landing page |
| Quick Start (both) | `/client-sdk/quick-start/javascript` | first page of the "Quick Start" nav group in `docs.json` |

Link targets only — 8 lines across 4 files, no prose changes.

## Verification

- Re-ran a scan over every `href="/..."` and `](/...)` across all 113 `.mdx` pages: **no broken internal links remain**.
- All six new targets exist on disk **and** are nav entries in `docs.json` (checked both, since a page can exist without being routed).
- Also swept `docs.json` the other way — every nav entry resolves to a real page, so there is nothing of the #17 kind outstanding.

This is the same class of fix as #15 ("Fix 11 broken internal links across docs") and #17; these eight accumulated after those landed.

## Note on overlap

`client-sdk/introduction/installation.mdx` is also touched by #35, but that PR only edits the version pins around lines 14–40 while this touches line 119, so the two do not conflict. Happy to drop that one file if you would rather keep the PRs fully disjoint.

author: tepalmafia
body:
사장님 「**상태창 광학창 레이더 등 모든 창들을 마우스로 위치를 자유자재로 옮길 수 있게** 해줘」

## 무엇이 생겼나

**U** 를 누르면 배치 모드입니다 — 마우스가 풀리고 창을 **끌어서** 옮깁니다. 놓는 순간 저장되고 껐다 켜도 그 자리입니다. **R** 로 되돌립니다.

- 격자 0.005 에 붙습니다 — 손 떨림은 먹고 「거기 두고 싶다」는 살립니다
- **화면 밖으로 안 나갑니다** — 판의 **반쪽 크기를 세고** 막습니다 (복판만 보고 막으면 가장자리에서 절반이 잘립니다)
- 안 옮긴 창은 **아무것도 안 들고 있습니다** — 그래야 기본값을 고치면 따라 움직입니다
- 옛 저장에 못 옮기는 창이 들어 있으면 버립니다

## 조준경은 못 옮깁니다 — 까닭을 적었습니다

취향이 아니라 **규칙**입니다: 조준경은 표적 상자와 락온 고리를 **하늘의 진짜 자리 위에** 그립니다 (`space-align.js` 가 0.01도로 지킵니다). 판을 옮기면 그 그림이 통째로 어긋나 **「창밖의 저것」과 「계기의 저것」이 갈라집니다** — v91·v93·v95·v98 네 판을 태운 그 병입니다.

## 만들면서 세 번 데었습니다 (다 재서 잡았습니다)

**①** 「Cannot access 'layout' before initialization」로 **게임이 안 떴습니다.** 상태를 다른 상태들 옆(1107줄)에 두었는데 `placePanels()` 가 **484줄에서 이미 한 번 돕니다.** 이 파일의 오랜 규약 그대로입니다 — 여러 곳이 읽는 값은 읽는 곳들보다 위에. `panePicks` 로 **한 번 더** 같은 데 데었습니다.

**②** **집히는데 안 끌렸습니다.** 진짜 마우스로 끌어 보니 창을 잡기는 하는데 자리가 안 바뀌었습니다. 원인은 `input.js` 가 **단추를 누를 때마다 포인터를 다시 잠그는 것** — 잠기면 `clientX/Y` 가 안 움직여 **첫 이동만 먹습니다.** 푸는 것만으로는 모자랐고 **다시 안 잠기게** 막아야 했습니다 (`input.noLock`).

> 코드로 옮기는 것(`SPACE.putPane`)은 처음부터 됐습니다 — **진짜 마우스로 해 보지 않았으면 못 잡았을 자리**입니다 (v49 가 남긴 가르침 그대로).

## 검사

`tools/space-layout.js` (새로) — 여섯 절 전부 ✔. 그리고 **진짜 브라우저로** 확인했습니다: U 로 열고, 왼쪽 아래 상태창을 화소로 잡아 오른쪽 위로 끌고, 놓고, **새로고침해도 그 자리**였습니다.

전부 ✔: layout · screen · save · fit · nav · hud · loot · story · keys
