author: swamp-ig
body:
## Proposed change

Adds **Enter host** to the iZone user config flow alongside **Search for devices** (builds on the Search shelf handoff from #178721).

Supersedes #177163, which tried to keep probed controllers out of Discovered and claim unique_id in the user flow instead, which doesn't work cleanly.

- User start always shows a menu: Search / Enter host (even when an entry is already loaded).
- Enter host HTTP-probes via `async_discover_by_host`, then hands off to a Discovered-shelf confirm (or shelves one first). Matching a shelf card by host skips the probe; after probe, match by UID. If the shelf still has a stale host, that card is replaced so confirm/create use the probed address.
- Probe failures stay on the form (`cannot_connect`, `unpaired_bridge`, `already_configured`, YAML exclude / shelve miss → `no_devices_found`) instead of aborting the flow.
- Empty Search nudges to the Enter host form with `no_devices_found` rather than aborting.
- Ignored controllers: confirm in the user flow without claiming `unique_id` until `CREATE_ENTRY`, so Ignore is replaced on create.

Note: Two concurrent Ignore confirms for the same UID can both sit on the confirm step (HA only dedupes in-progress flows once `context["unique_id"]` is set); the second create aborts `already_configured`. No better option without changing when we claim the UID.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  user[async_step_user]
  menu["menu: Search / Enter host"]
  search["Search for devices (#178721)"]
  manual[Enter host form]
  shelfHost{"already Discovered?"}
  probe["async_discover_by_host"]
  shelve["shelve + hand off to shelf confirm"]
  ignoreConfirm["in-flow confirm; unique_id at CREATE_ENTRY"]
  confirm[shelf confirm]
  create[CREATE_ENTRY]

  user --> menu
  menu -->|Search| search
  menu -->|Enter host| manual
  search -->|found| confirm --> create
  search -->|none| manual
  manual --> shelfHost
  shelfHost -->|yes| confirm
  shelfHost -->|no| probe
  probe -->|ok new| shelve --> confirm
  probe -->|ok ignored| ignoreConfirm --> create
  probe -->|fail| manual

  classDef existing fill:#f5f5f5,stroke:#666,color:#333
  classDef new fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1e3a8a
  class user,search,confirm,create existing
  class menu,emptyNudge,manual,shelfHost,probe,shelve,ignoreConfirm new
```



### Next tasks

- Reconfigure / moved-host repair: typing an already-configured controller’s new IP currently stays on Enter host with `already_configured`. Follow-up should let the user update `CONF_HOST` (dedicated reconfigure step, or `updates={CONF_HOST: …}` on the unique-id abort) so UDP-blocked installs can recover without deleting the entry.

author: bertpl
body:
**Problem**: The reusable `build` job in `_package_check.yml` produces the exact artifact the release path publishes, yet its setup-uv used the default `auto` cache — which on hosted runners restores a `main`-scoped cache that any push-to-`main` run can write into.

**Solution**: Set `enable-cache: false` on that job's setup-uv, so the published bytes never build from a cache other runs can poison. Scoped to the `build` job (the one whose output ships); the install/test job is unaffected.

- **Attention:** The reusable workflow also runs on PRs, where the build output is discarded — so PR builds lose uv caching too, a negligible cost for a job that only runs `uv build`.
- **TEST:** `make lint` clean (actionlint, zizmor, and workflow validation all pass); no code changed, so the Python test suite is unaffected.

**Changelog** (Security):
```
- the published release artifacts are no longer built from a CI cache that other pushes to `main` can write into, closing a supply-chain path
```

author: mel-64
body:
This fixes tests which don't cleanly fail (e.g. with a stacktrace) not counting towards the total. This happens due to tests resulting in a stacktrace or similar non-panic runtime errors not printing a result.

Example:
```
running 4 tests
test tests::test_greet_empty ... ok
test tests::test_greet_other_name ... ok
test tests::test_greet_simple ... ok
//  no `failed` to capture here???
thread 'tests::test_hello' (1698933) has overflowed its stack
fatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting
zsh: abort      ./main
```

This is fixed by changing the formula from `score = (score / (score+failed))` to `score = (score / total)` and capturing the total via the `running 4 tests` line.

Fixes #8

author: amitcse
body:
### Motivation

- Implement the M2 broker durability and local boundary so the broker can persist lifecycle state, run versioned migrations, and derive requester identity from the kernel rather than RPC payloads.
- Provide a deterministic, testable seam for planning/approval receipts without enabling any real APT execution until later milestones.

### Description

- Add versioned SQLite migrations and metadata tables (`crates/rp-broker-core/migrations/0001_initial.sql`, `.../0002_credentials.sql`) and wire a migration runner into `BrokerStore::from_connection` with integrity checks and `user_version` tracking.
- Implement durable open/migration helpers and reboot handling in `crates/rp-broker-core/src/lib.rs` including `BrokerStore::open` (secure `0600` DB open with symlink/permissions rejection) and `start_boot` to expire non-executing work from prior boot epochs.
- Add a bounded length-prefixed Unix-domain socket transport (`LocalSocket`, `read_frame`, `write_frame`) in `crates/rp-broker-api/src/lib.rs` that enforces safe socket modes, exact framing, and automatic socket cleanup.
- Introduce a minimal, narrowly-scoped Linux `SO_PEERCRED` adapter crate `crates/rp-peercred` to obtain PID/UID/GID from the kernel and use it to construct `PeerCredentials` rather than trusting RPC fields; update the API crate to use it.
- Make supporting fixes and polish: workspace `Cargo.toml` updates, `rp-cli` UTF-8 arg handling, package-name parsing boundary tweaks, protocol/vector test fixes, WebAuthn RP-ID-hash comparison fix, and unit tests and migration tests added to `rp-broker-core`.

### Testing

- Ran the full Rust unit test suite: `cargo test --workspace --offline`, which completed successfully (all unit tests and protocol vector tests passed).
- Exercised `rp-broker-core` unit tests and added an integration-style migration/reopen test that passed under the test runner.
- Ran `git diff --check` (no whitespace/format errors) as part of validation.
- Attempted linting with `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, but repository-wide pedantic documentation rules in the protocol crate produced doc-markdown warnings that block a full pedantic-clippy clean run; functional tests remain green.

author: j2teamnnl
body:
## Summary

TablePro already shows a per-tab database picker in the query editor toolbar (`QueryContainerPicker`), and its own doc comment says "the tab owns the new database for the rest of its life and the sidebar's browse cursor stays where the user left it."

Autocomplete ignored that picker. This makes completion honour it, and fixes the second half of the same defect class in plugin metadata.

## Root cause

One mechanism, two surfaces: the app resolved "which database is this work for?" from **ambient** state rather than from the identity that owns the work.

- `SchemaProviderRegistry` keyed providers by `connectionId` and sourced every fetch through `withBrowseMetadataDriver`, which is the **sidebar's** cursor. Every tab of a connection shared one provider bound to whatever the object browser last pointed at.
- Metadata reads keyed by `pluginTypeId`, the **primary plugin's** id rather than the type's own. A variant (Redshift, CockroachDB, PGlite) was served the primary's facts.

Both are a key that cannot express a distinction the app needs.

## What changed since the first version of this PR

The metadata half is no longer a 6-site patch. `snapshot(forTypeId:)` is renamed `snapshot(forRegisteredTypeId:)`, so every site that passed a `DatabaseType` stopped compiling until it was classified: **83** now ask `snapshot(for:)` and **6** remain genuine plugin-identity lookups, each commented as such.

Letting the compiler enumerate the sites rather than a regex found **8 multi-line calls that a line-based grep missed**, including `DatabaseManager.canPool()` reading `postConnectActions`, which decides pooling eligibility. The real count was 70 collapsed sites, not the 57 first estimated.

Three corrections came from measured probes rather than from reading the code:

- Cancelling a caller that awaits a shared `Task.value` neither cancels that task nor returns early, so a superseded resolution always runs its tail to the commit. Refusing to cache was half a guard; the stale value must not be **returned** either.
- `@Observable` tracks the whole stored property, and `dict[k, default: 0] &+= 1` notifies through the ungated `_modify` even when nothing changed. The per-scope `revisions` dictionary bought nothing over one counter while costing a body re-evaluation per editor, so invalidation now uses one observable box per scope inside a plain container.
- SwiftUI re-runs a `.task` at an **unchanged** id when its host view is unparented and reparented, which is what every connection switch does. That is why a failed resolution is no longer cached: an uncached failure heals for free on the next switch, a cached one never does.

`serverVersion` left the cache key entirely. Keying on it meant reading it from a SwiftUI body through `DatabaseManager.driver(for:)`, and `PluginDriverAdapter` is not observable, so a version learned after connect reached no body and the profile stayed cached under a nil-version key for the life of the tab. It changes only across a reconnect, which already clears the cache.

## Collateral, found while investigating and shipped here

- **PGlite** was offered SSH, SSL, Cloudflare Tunnel and SOCKS panes, plus `~/.pgpass`, the AWS IAM block and a password field, for an embedded WASM engine on loopback. Its own curated entry declares none of them, and three shipped docs pages say it has none.
- **Redshift's `padb_harvest` and CockroachDB's `system`** listed in the sidebar as ordinary user databases, because `systemDatabaseNames` resolved to PostgreSQL's empty list.
- **The AI schema context listed no columns for any table named with a capital letter.** It wrote `columnsByTable[table.name.lowercased()]` while `AISchemaContext` read `columnsByTable[table.name]`. The two other producers in the repo are each self-consistent; this was the only mismatched pair.

## One thing worth a reviewer's attention

Narrowing `additionalConnectionFields` for a variant would also have narrowed the **secret-redaction and Keychain-deletion lists** that read it. A PGlite connection saved while the form was still wrongly offering PostgreSQL's fields can hold a secret under a field PGlite never declares, so the exact list would have orphaned it in the Keychain and stopped redacting it on export.

`PluginManager.secureConnectionFieldIds(for:)` returns the union of the variant's fields and its serving plugin's. All five deletion and redaction paths use it; rendering a form stays exact, which is the opposite requirement.

Checked separately: this downgrades TLS nowhere. Redshift, CockroachDB and MariaDB keep `supportsSSH` and `supportsSSL` true; ScyllaDB and Turso have no curated entry so they fall back to their primary exactly as before; PGlite is the only type that flips, correctly.

## Caught in self-review

A `code-review` pass over the finished diff found eight issues; seven are fixed here.

The one that mattered most was mine and would have shipped a broken upgrade. `DatabaseDriver.buildAdditionalFields` loads a connection's secure fields from the Keychain by the **rendered** field list. Once a variant resolves its own curated entry, Redshift's list no longer carries the AWS IAM fields, so a Redshift connection saved on a shipped build with `awsAuth` set would keep that flag (it lives in `additionalFields`) while `awsSecretAccessKey` was never loaded: the connect fails, and the AWS section no longer renders, so there is no way to turn it off. It now uses the superset, like the other four paths.

Two more were real fences that did not hold:

- `QueryCompletionProfileRegistry.clear(connectionId:)` removed the generations it had just bumped, so `default: 0` answered 0 again and a resolution still blocked in the metadata lease could commit a profile from the closed session into the emptied cache. The next connection's scope keys are identical, so it would have been served that profile. The generation is now monotonic across teardown, with a test.
- `SchemaProviderRegistry`'s failure path cleared `loadedScopes` unfenced, so a populate that lost the race and then failed could discard the flag for the union `SchemaRefreshService` had just written.

Also fixed: eviction no longer runs while a connection has no browse cursor (the window a reconnect passes through, where the browse provider is protected by neither the exemption nor `liveScopes`), `getOrCreate` no longer evicts the provider it just created, and `verify.sh` now recognises all three spellings xcodebuild uses for a failing case rather than only the Swift Testing one, which had made every XCTest-named quarantine entry read as a new failure.

Reported and not fixed: `SchemaProviderRegistry.populate` coalesces a refresh that arrives mid-fetch into the older in-flight fetch, so a table created during a tab's initial load will not appear in that tab's completions until the next refresh. Completion stays correctly scoped, and the fix needs a re-run mechanism with its own race surface, so it is better as its own change.

## Test plan

- `verify.sh build`: **PASS**.
- `verify.sh test` over 24 suites: **PASS**, 359 cases, 358 passed. The one failure is `SQLCompletionProviderTests/testCommaFromScopesColumnsToAllTables()`, already on line 37 of `.github/macos-test-quarantine.txt`.
- `verify.sh lint` over 14 changed paths: **0 violations**.
- `verify.sh docs`: **PASS**.
- `verify.sh abi`: see below.
- `verify.sh plugins`: could not run here. The pinned `oracle-nio` fork fails to build locally with `unknown attribute 'usableFromInlinenonisolated'` from a `@TaskLocal` macro expansion, in target `OracleNIO`, with no error in any file this branch touches. CI's `AllPlugins` step covers it.

20 new test cases across three suites:

- `PluginManagerVariantAccessorTests` pins the accessors rather than the registry, which is the end that was wrong. It includes a general guard asserting every accessor agrees with `snapshot(for:)` for every known type, so a future accessor written against `pluginTypeId` fails on the variants

author: silkepilon
body: Follow-up to #39, from actually deploying it. **The trap.** klipper's hostPort rule for port 53 has no destination match and is entered from `OUTPUT -m addrtype --dst-type LOCAL`, so every packet a node sends to port 53 of any local address gets DNAT'd into Pi-hole. The Fedora nodes resolved via systemd-resolved's stub at `127.0.0.53` — a local address — so creating the Service deadlocked the deploy: Pi-hole could not be pulled because pulling needed DNS, and DNS now pointed at Pi-hole. ``` Failed to pull image "pihole/pihole:...": lookup registry-1.docker.io: Try again ``` `getent hosts` kept working and hid it — Fedora's nsswitch puts `resolve` before `dns`, and nss-resolve uses D-Bus, never port 53. The Pis were fine: their resolver is the router, a remote address. All seven nodes now use `1.1.1.1`/`9.9.9.9` directly, with the stub listener disabled on Fedora. That is also correct independent of the bug — cluster infrastructure should not resolve through the ad blocker it hosts. Host config, so it is documented rather than managed: `apps/pihole/README.md`. **Also:** `ignoreDifferences` on the root app for `/metadata/finalizers`. Argo CD adds pre-delete finalizers to child Applications whose charts have pre-delete hooks (longhorn), which are never in git, so the root app sat permanently OutOfSync on a field it wrote itself. Pre-existing, unrelated to Pi-hole. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Documents the hostPort 53 DNAT trap that can deadlock DNS during Pi-hole deploy and adds host setup steps to avoid it. Also prevents Argo CD root app drift by ignoring child Application finalizers. - **Bug Fixes** - Root `Application`: ignore `/metadata/finalizers` on `argoproj.io/Application` to avoid permanent OutOfSync from Argo CD’s pre-delete finalizers (e.g., longhorn). - **Migration** - On all nodes, set static DNS to 1.1.1.1 and 9.9.9.9 (don’t use a local stub). - On Fedora nodes, disable the systemd-resolved stub listener and point `/etc/resolv.conf` to the resolved-managed file. - Verify with `getent -s dns hosts registry-1.docker.io`. ## Summary

- require a Qwen3-capable Transformers release for the Fun-ASR-Nano backend
- keep the dependency below Transformers 5 to avoid an untested major-version upgrade

## Root cause

GPT-SoVITS advertises `FunAudioLLM/Fun-ASR-Nano-2512`, whose bundled language model declares `model_type: qwen3`. The current `transformers>=4.43,<=4.50` constraint cannot resolve that architecture, so selecting Fun-ASR-Nano fails with `KeyError: qwen3` before transcription starts. author: bbirkinbine
body:
The incomplete-shard-set advisory **silently did not fire** on `Uniboshi/Kimi-K3-Abliterated-V1`. That repo ships `model-00001-of-000096.safetensors` — six digits in the total, where both conventions cited in `pull_advisory.py`'s provenance header (HF's big-model docs, llama.cpp's `SPLIT_PATH_FORMAT`) pad to five. `_SHARD_RE` required `\d{5}` for both fields, so nothing in that repo parsed as a shard at all.

## Why it matters

That advisory is what stands between a partial pull and an archive that cannot load — the failure this tool exists to prevent. Measured against the live repo, same 9-of-96 selection:

| | advisories |
|---|---|
| `-of-000096` (what the repo ships) | **0** |
| `-of-00096` (documented width), identical shape | 1 |

After this change the real repo reports:

```
sharded weight set 'model-*.safetensors' is incomplete: 87 of 96 shards
excluded — add --include '*model-*.safetensors'
```

Every existing fixture used the documented five-digit width, which is exactly why no test caught it.

## The lazy prefix is load-bearing

Relaxing `\d{5}` to `\d+` alone would have made things worse. With a greedy `.+`, the prefix eats the leading zeros, so `model-00001-of-000096` parses as prefix `model-0000` with index `1` — a distinct single-shard set per file, which reports nothing. `test_a_variable_width_set_groups_under_one_prefix_not_one_per_shard` pins that specifically, and `test_a_digit_bearing_prefix_survives_the_lazy_match` pins that the lazy match does not stop at the first digit run (`layer-01-model-…`).

## Scope

Four regression tests, one regex, one comment block recording the measurement. No behavior change for five-digit repos — the existing shard tests pass untouched, which is the neutrality proof. No docs claim a padding width, so `docs/cli.md` needs no change.

Found while walking a `discover` session for spec 0018 against a real repo. Unrelated to that spec's listing work, so it lands on its own branch.

**Merge order:** this should go in before #31. That PR's shard-set roll-up reuses this regex, and on the old one it would group a six-digit set one-shard-per-line.

author: ioworker0
body:
## Overview

DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 shares a pre-tokenizer regex with the DeepSeek V3, Hunyuan Dense, and JoyAI presets. Without a custom implementation, it falls back to `std::regex`.

Long letter runs can trigger recursive backtracking in libstdc++, accumulating tens of thousands of stack frames and crashing a server thread before inference starts.

This change routes the exact regex through a non-recursive scanner while preserving Unicode property handling and number grouping from earlier passes.

## Additional information

Validation performed:

- Compared short inputs against `std::regex`.
- Verified identical output before and after the change: 8,624 token IDs for a 17,368-byte DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 corpus.
- Verified that 51,294-byte, 51,295-byte, and 128 KiB letter runs complete without crashing.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES — AI usage disclosure: YES — AI was used to help create the initial version of this change. I completed the final implementation and verified the test results.

author: mkrze
body:
## Summary

MiniMax-M3 occasionally drops the leading `<` of a tool-call invoke opening tag,
emitting `]<]minimax[>[invoke name="...">` instead of
`]<]minimax[>[<invoke name="...">`. The HPU MiniMax-M3 tool parser detects invoke
tags via the literal marker `INVOKE_START = NS + "<invoke"`, so a dropped `<`
caused the call to be silently missed — no tool call was produced in the
streaming path, and the entire generation was returned as plain content in the
non-streaming path.

This PR makes invoke detection tolerant of the dropped `<`, mirroring the
parser's existing headless-recovery tolerance for dropped *parameter* opening
tags.

## Changes

- **Parser fix** (`vllm_gaudi/entrypoints/openai/tool_parsers/minimax_m3.py`):
  - Add a variant marker `INVOKE_START_NOLT = NS + "invoke"` and a
    `_find_invoke_open()` helper that returns the earliest of the well-formed or
    dropped-`<` opener along with its length (preferring the well-formed form on
    ties).
  - Use it in the streaming path, and accept either opener in the non-streaming
    `_parse_block` / `_parse_one_invoke`.
  - The fix is **position-preserving** (no text rewriting), so streaming offset
    tracking is unaffected, and it **cannot false-positive** on well-formed text
    (a real invoke always has `<` right after the namespace marker). Scope is
    limited to the opening invoke tag; `INVOKE_END` and other tags are untouched.
- **Tests** (`tests/unit_tests/test_minimax_m3_tool_parser.py`): add regression
  tests for the dropped-`<` case in both the non-streaming and streaming paths.
- **Docs** (`docs/getting_started/validated_models.md`): add MiniMax-M3
  (TP=8, BF16, Gaudi 3) to the validated models list.

## Resumen
- `guardarAsientoFn()` (Contabilidad → Diario, asiento manual) ya no hace `API.post`/`API.patch` directo a `asientos` — pasa a usar dos RPC nuevas: `seguros_registrar_asiento_manual` y `seguros_corregir_asiento_manual` (ya aplicadas a producción, admin-only, org `nexus-pro`, idempotentes).
- Corregir un asiento manual **ya no reescribe el original**: la RPC inserta un asiento de reversa exacta + el asiento ya corregido, dejando el original intacto para siempre (mismo criterio que ya usa la anulación de facturas). Pide un **motivo obligatorio**.
- Un asiento que viene de otro flujo (facturas automáticas `F-NNN`, cobros `AST-COB*`, anulaciones `AST-ANUL-*`, auto-facturación `AUTO-*`) ya no se puede "corregir" desde aquí por accidente — avisa y dirige al flujo correcto de ese módulo.
- Registrar/corregir sigue siendo exclusivo de admin de `nexus-pro` (chequeo doble: dentro de la RPC del lado del servidor, y del lado del cliente solo para feedback inmediato).

## Alcance (Bloque 3A, autorizado por ChatGPT)
NO se tocó: `_genFacturasInterno()`, `anularFactura()`, la política `all_asientos` (sigue `USING(true)`, sin tocar RLS de `asientos` en este bloque), ninguna otra tabla (clientes/facturas/abonos/NCF/recibos/cuentas bancarias).

## Test plan

author: karmabutuzgun
body:
## Major Balance + Mythical Expansion V9

Implements the full large-scale balance, progression, itemization, enemy-build, and Mythical ecosystem update on top of Riftbound's existing production patch stack.

### Special Powers and combat systems
- Speedster Time Portal is a real third-most-recent Ultimate-state rewind using combat snapshots while permanent inventory/rewards stay outside the rewind.
- Pyrokinesis damaging moves use AP scaling; Fireball and Inferno create distinct persistent Burning Ground hazards.
- Light Manipulation receives dynamic 2x normal MP.
- Blood Sorcery applies stackable 2-turn Anti-Heal with capped healing reduction and status presentation.
- Shrine Cleave adapts per target from 10% to 70% Durability negation.
- Cursed Child gains a Partial-Rika damage summon meter; Full Rika is gated behind the meter and copied/stored Stun moves are rejected through metadata rather than a fixed move list.
- Ki Warrior charges Ultimate more easily.
- Anti-Spiral Ultimate uses the centralized Causality classification.
- Bomb Hybrid automatically enters explosive Flight beyond normal movement allowance.
- Devil Trigger Judgement Cut becomes Causality-level only while Devil Trigger is active.
- Base One For All reuses Prime's Might behavior.
- Faux 100% is a user-moving speedblitz that destroys valid route obstacles and damages crossed hostiles rather than spawning a projectile.
- Gravity Crush removes 50% of actual target MP, scales bonus damage from MP really removed, then restores the suppressed movement correctly when the effect ends.

### Progression, Pochita, and OFA
- All For One is Calamity rarity and completely excluded until persistent Floor 50 progression unlocks Calamity.
- Symbol of Fear's Decay evolution path additionally requires a persistent Floor 50 clear as All For One.
- Pochita now presents an intentional Keep Him / Let Him Go decision; rejection is non-punitive and blocks the companion route.
- Pochita contract revival enters Chainsaw Hybrid form immediately.
- Base One For All replaces the existing normal Special Power cleanly.
- One For All Prime can coexist with an original Special Power through a Bonus Action moveset toggle.

### Itemization and enemies
- Enemy item builds remain empty on Floors 1-5, then scale slot count and rarity gradually by floor and boss status.
- AI build scoring uses actual Special Power/stat/build synergy rather than random equipment piles.
- Battle Intel remains responsible for enemy-item visibility while hidden item stats still apply.
- Shop recommendation scoring understands the expanded Mythical synergies instead of blindly preferring rarity.

### True Mythical tier
- Adds 24 new Mythical items on top of existing Sparda for exactly 25 total Mythicals.
- Enforces one Mythical globally through buying, crafting/recipe planning, save normalization, and debug grants.
- Mythical is a first-class item rarity in the production item system.
- Required items are implemented: Air Force Gloves, Zeta Suit, Bandit's Secret, Open Domain, Sukuna's Finger, and Andúril · Flame of the West.
- The remaining catalog covers movement, transformations, summons, domains, copied powers, high-risk resource play, weapon builds, defensive builds, clash builds, cooldown control, regeneration, ranged combat, and other distinct archetypes.
- Every new Mythical has an explicit production-mechanic coverage entry and a dedicated source-shaped portrait selector/profile. Sparda deliberately keeps its approved bespoke V5 portrait.
- Additional build-defining mechanics include Mimic Tear's HP-paid temporary clone, Prison Realm's proximity capture, Millennium Puzzle Intel/Clash recovery, Flying Raijin marks, Sling Ring repositioning, Sandevistan heat/recoil, Iron Halo overload, Arc Reactor high-energy shielding/cooldown flow, Choice Scarf technique streaks, and more.

### UI, history, debug, and hardening
- Adds/updates V9 status UI, battle-history lines, battlefield/minimap VFX, Mythical-slot messaging, open-domain state, Rika progress, Anti-Heal, Cleave adaptation, explosive Flight, and progression messaging.
- Adds production-system debug hooks for Calamity, AFO Floor 50, Symbol gating, Mythical ownership, Rika, Speedster rewind, enemy builds, recommendations, extra Vessel, and Mythical mechanic coverage.
- Preserves permanent item ownership across time rewinds and sanitizes legacy/invalid multi-Mythical save states.

## Validation

Exact PR build at head `2c13bc0` is green:
- production patch-stack build and JS syntax checks
- Bizarre Update runtime
- Build Expansion runtime: 205 items, 67 Legendaries, 213 damaging moves audited
- Itemization Expansion
- Shop + Portrait V2
- Literal Portrait V3
- Premium Portrait V4
- Legendary Portrait V5 + middle-click quick-buy
- Reference Lore V6
- Shop Performance V7
- Major Balance + Mythical V9 verifier: exactly 25 Mythicals, all 24 new Mythicals have production mechanic coverage and dedicated portraits
- Spartan Blood runtime
- LAN Co-op network layer
- built-site artifact upload

A final downloaded artifact was also syntax-checked locally and confirmed to contain the V9 feature marker, combat-audit layer, Calamity progression, Mythical mechanic registry, Mimic Tear, Prison Realm, Gunbai reflection state, dedicated Andúril portrait styling, and preserved Sparda V5 art.

body: ## Summary - add a durable per-recipient notification table and schema - expose the `Storyarn.Notifications` facade for personal delivery, effective project-member fan-out, recent/unread reads, unread count, and read mutations - enforce recipient isolation, current project access, self-notification suppression, and database-backed deduplication - publish lightweight per-user PubSub invalidations only after the source transaction commits ## Why This provides the smallest durable backend required by the in-app notification bell and the first asynchronous and structural notification producers, without introducing preferences, external channels, or a generic activity-log model. ## Validation - `mix test test/storyarn/notifications_test.exs` — 16 tests, 0 failures - `MIX_TEST_PORT=4195 MIX_TEST_PARTITION=1874 mix precommit` — 9,240 tests, 0 failures - independent implementation review — no remaining findings ## Scope The bell UI and producer integrations remain in ENG-88, ENG-89, and ENG-90. Linear: ENG-87 --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a durable notifications model and the `Storyarn.Notifications` API for the in‑app bell. Meets ENG‑87 by supporting per‑recipient delivery, listing, unread counts, and read mutations with access enforcement and deduplication. - Data model: `notifications` table with per‑recipient unique `(recipient_id, dedupe_key)`, feed/unread indexes, cascades (recipient/project) and actor nilify, and checks for actor ≠ recipient, consistent entity identity, project‑scoped entity types requiring a project, valid async statuses, and non‑blank `kind`/`dedupe_key`. - API: `deliver` (personal; optional project with access check; suppresses self‑notifications), `deliver_to_project_members` (fan‑out to direct and workspace‑inherited members, excludes actor, per‑recipient dedupe, validates non‑blank `dedupe_key`), `list_notifications` with `unread_only` and `limit` (default 20, cap 100), `unread_count`, `mark_read`, `mark_all_read`, `subscribe`, and `publish_committed`. PubSub invalidations publish only via `publish_committed/1` after the source transaction commits; suppressed/deduplicated outcomes do not publish. `publish_committed/1`, `mark_read/2`, and `mark_all_read/1` must be called outside DB transactions. - Migration - Run `mix ecto.migrate` to create `notifications`. - Producers must provide a trimmed, non‑blank `dedupe_key` and call `publish_committed/1` only after the surrounding transaction commits. author: tiagoemicheli160512-dotcom
body:
## O que aconteceu

Investigando o relato de que uma "Saída pra Terceiros" registrada no Nova
América (MASSA PASTEL → Estoque São Gonçalo) sumiu depois de aparecer na
tela: confirmei no banco que o registro realmente não existe em
`gn_lojas.all_data.avariasAll` do Nova América, apesar de ter sido
confirmado duas vezes na hora (ver prints).

## Causa raiz

`sbEditVersion` só era incrementado dentro de `sbScheduleSync()` (o
debounce de 1.5s usado no autosave normal). Só que várias ações chamam
`sbPush()` **direto**, sem passar por ali: `addSaidaTerceiro` (Saída pra
Terceiros), `addTransferencia` (Empréstimo entre lojas), `quitarEmprestimo`
e `marcarPagamentoDinheiro`.

Nessas ações, `sbEditVersion` nunca avançava — então `sbTemPendente()`
(que decide se `sbPull()` pode sobrescrever os campos desta loja) ficava
**falso** durante a própria janela do push. Se o poll periódico de
`sbPull()` (a cada 20s) caísse nesse meio-tempo — antes do push confirmar
—, ele reaplicava a versão antiga vinda da nuvem por cima de
`avariasAll`/`transferAll` locais, apagando o registro recém-criado antes
que o push conseguisse gravá-lo de vez (ou, se já tinha gravado,
sobrescrevendo de volta na próxima sincronização com o estado local agora
corrompido).

## Fix

`sbEditVersion++` movido pra dentro do próprio `sbPush()`, então toda
chamada — direta ou via debounce — marca a edição como pendente pelo
tempo todo que o push está em voo. Corrige os quatro fluxos citados de
uma vez, sem precisar mexer em cada um.

## Nota

O registro específico do Nova América (MASSA PASTEL → São Gonçalo) foi
perdido antes desse fix e precisa ser refeito manualmente — não dava pra
reconstruir com segurança via SQL sem risco de bater o estoque errado.

## Test plan

- [ ] Registrar uma Saída pra Terceiros ou Empréstimo e aguardar ~20-30s
      sem sair da tela — conferir que o registro continua lá (e no banco)
- [ ] Conferir que o fluxo normal de autosave (debounce) continua
      funcionando igual

author: znat
body:
## Summary

- Adds `logging.text` (default `true`) and `logging.audio` (default `false`) to `config.yaml`.
- Text logging gates `Log.write`'s file output — `~/Library/Logs/ParrotFlow.log` / `ParrotFlow-Dev.log`. NSLog (the unified system log) is untouched; the setting only controls the file, matching how the task described it.
- Audio logging gates whether a dictation's `.wav` clip survives on disk once nothing needs it any more. Capture still writes the file during recording — transcription reads it from disk — but it is now discarded: right after transcription finishes, immediately when transcription is disabled, and for a clip kept "for diagnosis" when too much audio was lost to a device change. This is a default-off behaviour change: existing users who never set `logging:` will stop accumulating clips.
- `--check-config` reports both settings, next to `feedback`.
- `config.example.yaml` and `docs/configuration.md` are updated to match. `README.md` and `docs/setup.md` are untouched, as requested.

## Decisions on the CLI commands that write to the log

- `--peek` and `--edit-test`/`--span-test` always write to the log regardless of `logging.text`. `--peek`'s own doc comment says the log is its only transport — it's meant to be launched via `open -na ParrotFlowDev --args --peek` to carry the app's Accessibility grant, and LaunchServices throws away that process's stdout. `--edit-test`/`--span-test` are launched the same way for the same reason, and `scripts/check-inplace.sh`/`check-span.sh` read their output back out of the log file (confirmed by grepping those scripts). Both commands now pass `force: true` to `Log.write`.
- Every other CLI command (`--record`, `--transcribe`, `--boost-eval`, `--spot`, etc.) just runs from an ordinary terminal, so its own `print()` output is available regardless of the log setting; their `Log.write` calls are left to respect `logging.text` like the rest of the app.
- Deliberate audio-writing commands (`--record`, `--transcribe <file>`, `--spot`, `--audio-recovery`) are unaffected by `logging.audio` — a person running them is asking for the file, and they manage their own clips directly rather than going through the app's live-dictation cleanup path.

## Test plan

- [x] `swift build` and `swift build -c release` both succeed.
- [x] `scripts/check-audio-recovery.sh` — 11/11 (its scratch config has no `logging:` key, so it now defaults to `audio: false`; verified this doesn't change any of its assertions, since it manages its own clip files directly).
- [x] `scripts/check-default-config.sh` — passes; `logging:` now matches between `Config.defaultYAML` and `config.example.yaml`.
- [x] Verified with a scratch `PARROTFLOW_CONFIG_DIR`: a config with no `logging:` key reports `text=on audio=off`; a config with only `logging: { audio: true }` reports `text=on audio=on` (partial override keeps the other default).
- [x] Ran the rest of the fast `scripts/check-*.sh` suite locally — all green (one `check-replacements.sh` run showed a known-flaky NSSpellChecker timeout, reproduced as green on rerun, and is unrelated to this change).
- [x] `swiftlint lint` — no new violations introduced.

author: agydaslihan
body:
Faz 2C'nin açık kalan tek maddesi. ILERLEME.md'de *"Aslıhan'ın mevcut tablo düzeni bilinince"* diye bekletiliyordu — **beklemeye gerek olmadığı anlaşıldı.** Düzeni sormak yerine düzeni tanıyan bir eşleme yazıldı.

## Akış

`/admin/gözlem-ice-aktar` → **dosya → sütun eşlemesi → önizleme → aktar**

Önizleme atlanabilir bir adım değil: her satırın *ne olarak okunduğu* rakamlarıyla gösteriliyor, sonra yazılıyor.

## Verdiğim kararlar

**Sabit sütun düzeni dayatılmadı.** Başlıklardan tahmin edilir, ekranda düzeltilir. Eşlenemeyen sütun sessizce atılmaz — "bu sütun kullanılmadı" diye bildirilir.

**Hiçbir satır sessizce düzeltilmez ve sessizce atlanmaz.** Her satır üç durumdan birinde: *hazır*, *uyarılı* (aktarılır, işaretlenir), *hatalı* (aktarılmaz, sebebi yazılır). "Anlamadığım satırı atlarım" davranışı, 500 satırlık dosyadan 430 satır aktarıp kimseye söylememektir.

**Ayrıştırıcı elle yazıldı — kütüphane değil.** Çözülmesi gereken sorun genel CSV değil, **Türkçe Excel'in CSV'si:** noktalı virgül ayırıcı, BOM, CRLF, Windows-1254 kodlama, `4.300.000` biçiminde sayı. Hazır kütüphanelerin çoğu virgül varsayar ve noktalı virgüllü dosyayı *tek sütun* okur — hata da vermez. Sessizce yanlış çalışan içe aktarma, hata veren içe aktarmadan çok daha pahalıdır.

**Türkçe sayı ayrıştırma ayrı bir tehlike olarak ele alındı.** `4.300.000` İngilizce ayrıştırıcıda `4,3` olur; bu hata endekse girer ve fark edilmesi aylar sürer. Belirsizlik tamamen yok edilemediği için önizleme **çözümlenmiş sayıyı** gösteriyor — asıl güvence gözle doğrulama.

**Tarih `new Date()` ile ayrıştırılmıyor** (ay/gün sırasını ortam farklı yorumlar; 3 Ağustos ↔ 8 Mart farkı endekste beş aylık kaymadır) ve **UTC öğlen yazılıyor** (gece yarısı, saat dilimi kaymasıyla gözlemi bir önceki aya taşıyabilirdi).

**Güven varsayılanı Düşük** — CSV yolu tipik olarak geriye dönük veri taşır (ENDEKS-VERI-YONETIMI.md §5). Görünür ve değiştirilebilir; gizli kural değil.

## Güvenlik

**İstemcinin çözümlediği veriye güvenilmiyor.** Sunucu CSV metnini + eşlemeyi + ayarları **yeniden çözümler** ve yalnızca kendi ürettiğini yazar. Kullanıcının seçebildiği tek şey hangi satırların dışarıda kalacağı — değerler değil. Aksi hâlde ağ isteğini düzenleyen biri, önizlemede gördüğünden bambaşka rakamları endeksin ham verisine yazdırabilirdi.

**Yazma yolu Local API + `overrideAccess: false`.** Toplu yazma, kancaları atlamak için bahane değil: `beforeChange` m² fiyatını, `ay` alanını ve özeti hesaplıyor ve endeks bunlardan besleniyor.

**Oturum kapısı** görünüm gövdesinde (`if (!req.user) return null`) — bu ekran veri *yazıyor*.

## Test

- **48 birim testi** (26 ayrıştırıcı + 22 eşleme/doğrulama)
- **10 entegrasyon testi**, gerçek veritabanına karşı: kancanın m²/ay hesabı, ayın 1'i saat dilimi sınavı, elenen satır, hatalı satır, mükerrer uyarısı, zorunlu alan eksikse hiçbir şey yazılmaması
- **Duman testi:** gerçek oturum açılıp `/admin/gozlem-ice-aktar` yüklendi, üç adım da basıldı, konsol temiz. Test kullanıcısı silindi.

### Testlerin yakaladığı iki gerçek hata

1. **`"falan filan"` → `portal_ilan`.** Kaynak sezgisi alt dize araması yapıyordu; `"falan filan"` metni `ilan` alt dizesini içerdiği için *tanınmadığı hâlde tanınmış* sayılıyor, uyarı bile üretmiyordu. Kelime sınırı eşleşmesine çevrildi.
2. **Kaynakta U+FFFD karakteri.** Faz E'de yazılan font alt kümesi denetimi, kaynağa doğrudan yazılmış değiştirme karakterini yakaladı.

Kapı: `typecheck` ✅ `lint` ✅ `test` (1044 test) ✅ `build` ✅

## Bilinen sınırlar

- Tek seferde 5.000 satır / 2 MB (3,2 GB RAM koruması). Üstü için dosya bölünür; ekran bunu söylüyor.
- **Toplu geri alma yok.** Yanlış aktarılan kayıtlar Gözlemler koleksiyonundan elle silinir; ekran bunu aktarımdan *önce* uyarıyor. Toplu geri alma için "içe aktarma partisi" kimliği tutmak gerekirdi — veri modelini bu uğurda genişletmek yerine önizlemeye yatırım yapıldı.

author: dan-seo
body:
검증을 두 축으로 자동화한다. 둘 다 **"돌려야 할 때만 돌린다"** 가 설계 기준이다 — Lighthouse는 CI 분이, evals는 API 토큰이 비용이다.

## 1. Lighthouse 회귀 게이트 (main push 전용)

`ci.yml`의 verify 잡 끝에 붙였다. PR CI에는 넣지 않는다 — PR은 그대로 빠르게 두고 회귀는 머지 후에 잡는다. **별도 워크플로로 빼지 않은 이유**: `oncall.yml`이 `workflow_run: [ci]`만 보므로, 여기 있어야 회귀가 사고 대응으로 이어진다.

### 게이트는 러너 속도와 무관한 값에만 건다

main CI 실패는 oncall 헤드리스 에이전트를 깨워 API 토큰을 쓴다. 타이밍 지표에 error를 걸면 회귀가 없는데도 사고 대응이 헛돈다.

| | 항목 |
|---|---|
| **error (게이트)** | script·font·total 전송 바이트, script 요청 수, accessibility·best-practices·seo |
| **warn (리포트만)** | performance 점수, TBT, LCP |

**이 설계는 머지 전에 실제로 검증했다** (`ci` workflow_dispatch, [run 31598974988](https://github.com/Dan-Seo/mdtproject/actions/runs/31598974988)):

| | 로컬 | GitHub 2코어 러너 |
|---|---|---|
| performance | 0.91 | 0.67 / 0.69 / 0.69 |
| TBT | 242 ms | 17,743 / 15,840 / 15,715 ms |
| 바이트 예산·a11y·BP·SEO | 통과 | **error 0건 통과** |

performance를 error로 걸었다면 **회귀가 없는데도 main이 깨지고 oncall이 떴다.** TBT가 65배 벌어지는 건 하드웨어 차이가 아니라 러너에 GPU가 없어 WebGL이 SwiftShader로 돌기 때문이다 — 사용자 체감 지연이 아니므로 절대값으로 읽지 않고 같은 러너 위 상대 회귀로만 쓴다. 두 번째 커밋에서 warn 임계값을 러너 실측 기준으로 다시 잡았다.

예산 숫자는 전부 실측이다(da48de3, lighthouse 12.8.2, preset=desktop). 근거·측정 조건·조이는 규칙은 `lighthouserc.cjs` 주석에 있다.

### 실측이 짚어낸 결함 4건 — 이번 PR에서 고치지 않았다

게이트를 현재 점수(a11y 0.96 / BP 0.96 / SEO 0.90)에 열어둔 이유다. 다음 PR에서 고치고 예산을 조인다 — 그게 루프의 한 바퀴다.

1. `aria-allowed-role` — `<aside role="status">`. aside에 status 롤은 허용되지 않는다 (`AppShell.tsx:93`)
2. `aria-conditional-attr` — `<tr aria-expanded>`. row의 `aria-expanded`는 treegrid 안에서만 유효 (`TakeoffPane.tsx:465`, 내역서 행 15개 전부)
3. `errors-in-console` — `favicon.ico` 404
4. `meta-description` 부재

## 2. evals 자동 실행 (경로 필터)

판정이 의존하는 것은 `CLAUDE.md`(qa 트랙)와 `prompts.ts`(review 트랙)뿐이고, 케이스는 코드 스니펫을 자기 안에 인라인한다. **그래서 배근 코드 PR에서는 한 번도 돌 필요가 없다** — `paths` 필터가 그 사실을 그대로 옮긴 것이다. `CLAUDE.md`만 바뀌면 qa 4케이스로 끝난다.

`EVAL_TRACK`(`all`|`qa`|`review`)을 `run.ts`에 추가했다(TDD). 무결성 검증은 **항상 전체 집합**으로 하고 실행만 좁힌다. 오타난 트랙은 조용히 전부로 되돌리지 않고 실패한다 — 되돌리면 4케이스를 돌린 줄 알고 9케이스를 과금한다.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` 저장소 시크릿이 필요하다. 지금 없으므로 첫 실행은 실패한다.**
> 일부러 스킵 가드를 넣지 않았다 — 조용히 건너뛰게 만들면 eval이 한 번도 안 돌아도 전부 초록으로 보인다.

## 3. CLAUDE.md

하네스 운용 조항 둘. index.json이 `blocked`·`error`인데 프로세스가 살아 있으면 기다리지 말고 끊을 것(1800초 타임아웃까지 버려진다). 스텝 사양의 브라우저 검증은 「브라우저에서 확인」이 아니라 실행 가능한 `npx dev-browser … run` 명령으로 적을 것 — codex는 사람이 아니라서 전자에는 `blocked`로 답한다.

## 검증

lint 0 errors(기존 warning 1) · typecheck · test 582 passed · build · evals 유닛 10 passed · 리눅스 러너에서 Lighthouse error 단언 0건.

author: m-m-n
body:
## 概要

`wide-pair-overwrite-cleanup` のレビュー round1 で deferred になった architecture findings 2 件（`b8a62feaf016ef08` / `931abe859e23fa5d`）に対応する、挙動保存の内部リファクタリング。

## 変更内容

### 相方セル空白化プリミティブの統一（FR1〜FR3）

重複していた 2 実装を、セル変更基盤層に置いた 1 本に統合した。

- `terminal_cells.rs` に `pub(crate) fn blank_wide_pair_half(col, row)` を新設。幅 0/2 と `cell_index` の自己ガードを内側に持つ
- `csi_edit.rs` の `blank_wide_pair_split` を削除し、ICH/DCH の 6 箇所を移行
- `print_handler.rs` の `blank_wide_pair_partner` を削除し、3 箇所を移行

これで print 経路と CSI 編集経路が同一プリミティブを通るようになり、D2 不変条件の修復に SSOT ができた。旧構成では共有ヘルパーが編集オペレーション専用モジュール `csi_edit.rs` に置かれ、そこへ `csi_screen.rs` が依存する逆向きの参照になっていたが、これも解消している。

### 範囲消去の端修復 chokepoint 化（FR4, FR5）

`csi_screen.rs` に `erase_range_with_edge_repair(row, start, end)` を新設し、同一の capture→clear→repair パターンをコピーしていた 5 箇所（ECH / EL 0 / EL 1 / ED 0 / ED 1）を集約した。

全行消去系（`clear_line`、EL 2、ED 2）は従来どおり `clear_line` を直接呼び、相方掃除の挙動を獲得しない。この制約を記したコメントは新関数側へ移設して保持している。

### 性能特性（NFR1）

`old_width != 1` のゲートは `print_handler.rs:149, 225, 452` に温存してあるので、width-1 の ASCII 常道ケースでは呼び出し自体が発生しない。ワークスペース root の `profile.release` が fat LTO のため、プリミティブを別モジュールへ移してもインライン化は失われない。

## 起票時からの前提の変化

タスク起票時は「後続で EL / ED を同じ受け皿に載せられる形にする」という要件だったが、姉妹タスク `el-ed-wide-pair-cleanup` が先にマージされていたため、端修復のコピーは ECH のみでなく 5 箇所に増えていた。そのため本 PR は受け皿を用意するのではなく、既存 5 箇所を実際に移行している。起票時の行番号 `csi_screen.rs:65` も陳腐化していた（現在 `handle_erase_characters` は `:131`）。

## 検証

- `cargo test --manifest-path crates/term_core/Cargo.toml --lib` — 802 passed / 0 failed / 13 ignored。既存テストのアサーションは 1 行も変更していない
- `cargo check --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml` — pass
- `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/term_core/Cargo.toml --check` — 本 PR が触った 4 ファイルは clean。報告される差分は `print_handler/tests.rs` のみで、base commit 時点の内容と完全一致する既存ドリフト（本 PR は同ファイルを変更していない）
- 新プリミティブには属性保持・overflow 削除・自己ガードの直接ユニットテストを追加

## レビュー

5 観点（comprehensive / security / spec / architecture / performance）を Claude で、うち 4 観点を cross-model（codex / vertex-glm-5 / vertex-deepseek-v3.2）でも実行し、critical / high の指摘は 0 件。

medium 1 件は deferred とした。既存の ASCII fast path（`terminal_dispatch.rs`）が新プリミティブを通らないという指摘で、本 PR が作ったギャップではなく、変更対象ファイル外の既存の穴。修正は挙動変更を伴うため別タスクとする。

author: takumi3488
body:
## Overview

`agent-host/src/tools.test.ts` (added in #20) imported `tools.ts`, and through it
`valibot`. The root `bun test` runs `bun test src agent-host/src` from the repo
root, where `agent-host/node_modules` is not installed — so a fresh clone doing
`bun install && bun test` failed with `Cannot find package 'valibot'`. CI installs
agent-host's dependencies in the same job before running the tests, so CI stayed
green and this went unnoticed.

The cost is not just the confusing error: `agent-host/README.md` documents the
`lib/` split as existing precisely so agent-host logic is unit-testable outside
agent-host's own Node-only install/build cycle, and that had quietly stopped
being true.

## Changes

Very little of `tools.ts` actually needed a dependency:

- **`telemetry-client.ts` → `lib/telemetry-client.ts`** (moved unchanged). It had
  **no import statements at all** and already took `fetchImpl: typeof fetch =
  fetch`, so it already satisfied `lib/`'s convention — I/O injected rather than
  performed — and was simply in the wrong directory.
- **`telemetryCallbackConfigFromEnv` → `lib/telemetry-callback-config.ts`.** Nine
  lines of env reading, but it is a security gate: returning `undefined` is what
  stops `tools.ts` registering `query_telemetry` at all, so a deployment with no
  callback token can never hand the model a live telemetry tool. Every other
  security-relevant deterministic decision in this package (`sql-guard`,
  `redaction`, `output-sanitizer`, `tamper-check`) already sits in this tier. The
  `env` argument is now injectable so tests need not mutate global process state.
- **`tools.ts`** keeps only what genuinely needs dependencies: the Valibot schemas
  and the `defineTool` wiring (98 → 73 lines).

## Tests

`tools.test.ts` is deleted; its coverage is preserved, redistributed by what each
assertion actually requires:

| Was testing | Now |
|---|---|
| env gating (none set, each one missing) | `lib/telemetry-callback-config.test.ts`, plus new cases for an *empty-string* var and for the `process.env` default |
| `run()` POSTs with the bearer token | already covered dep-free by `lib/telemetry-client.test.ts` (request body, auth header, non-2xx without leaking the token, malformed JSON) |
| tool construction + description | `scripts/smoke.mjs` |
| input schema accepts/rejects | `scripts/smoke.mjs` |
| output schema accepts the parent's response | `scripts/smoke.mjs` — and this one earns its place there: it is a hand-written mirror of `FollowUpTelemetryQueryResponse` in `src/telemetry/followup.ts`, so it is what catches the two drifting apart |
| `run()` wiring (env gate → callback client) | `scripts/smoke.mjs`, with a stubbed `fetch` asserting the URL and `Authorization` header |

`smoke.mjs` was already importing `createTelemetryTools` and validating schemas
with Valibot under Node, and already runs in CI (`bun run smoke`) — so these
assertions land in an existing home rather than a new one.

**Verified the actual goal**: moved `agent-host/node_modules` out of the way and
ran the root suite — 1001 pass / 0 fail. Restored it and ran the rest: integration
63 pass (testcontainers), `typecheck` / `fmt` / `lint` clean, agent-host `build` +
`smoke` pass.

## Docs

`agent-host/README.md`'s rationale for `lib/` overstated the constraint as
"`@flue/*`-free"; it is actually **dependency-free**, for two independent reasons
(the `node:sqlite` one, and the uninstalled-`node_modules` one). Corrected there,
along with the layout tree, the "Unit tests" section (which claimed `tools.ts` and
`telemetry-client.ts` "run fine under Bun" — the specific claim that was wrong),
and `docs/architecture.md`'s module tree.

No behaviour change.

author: pgh0621
body:
## 🔗 관련 이슈

Closes [#76](https://github.com/FogMap2026/FogApp/issues/76)

## 🎯 왜

[#68](https://github.com/FogMap2026/FogApp/pull/68)로 사진 보관이 Firebase Storage에서 **서버 디스크**로 옮겨지면서, 무제한 업로드의 결과가 달라졌습니다.

| | Firebase Storage | 서버 직접 보관 |
|---|---|---|
| 무제한 업로드의 결과 | Google 요금 증가 | **디스크 고갈 → 서비스 중단** |

`POST /api/visits/photo` 는 반경 검증을 하지 않으므로(그건 `POST /api/visits` 몫), 실제로 그 장소에 가지 않아도 계속 올릴 수 있었습니다.

## ✨ 방어를 세 겹으로 넣었습니다

### 1. 스팟 존재 검증

없는 `spotId` 로도 업로드가 되면 **영원히 인증에 쓰이지 못하는 파일**만 쌓입니다.

컨트롤러가 스토리지를 직접 부르던 것을 `VisitService.uploadPhoto()` 경유로 바꿔 이 규칙을 넣었습니다. 컨트롤러에 리포지토리를 넣지 않고 업무 규칙을 서비스에 두는 편이 기존 구조와 맞습니다.

> 반경 검증은 **여기서 하지 않습니다.** 사진을 찍는 시점과 인증하는 시점이 다를 수 있고, 위치 검증은 `verify()` 몫입니다.

### 2. 스팟당 1장 유지

정복은 `visits (user_id, spot_id)` 유니크로 **1인 1회**라, 한 스팟에 여러 장을 가질 이유가 없습니다. 재업로드 누적과 **고아 파일 상당수를 함께** 막습니다.

**순서가 중요합니다** — 새 파일을 쓴 **뒤에** 이전 파일을 지웁니다.

```java
Files.copy(in, target, REPLACE_EXISTING);
// 반대로 하면 복사가 실패했을 때 기존 사진까지 잃는다.
deleteSiblingsOf(dir, fileName);
```

지우기가 실패해도 업로드는 성공으로 둡니다(다음 업로드가 정리).

### 3. 사용자 총량 상한 (기본 200MB)

**1·2만으로는 부족합니다.** 스팟당 1장이어도 전국 스팟이 수만 개라 한 계정이 수백 GB를 점유할 수 있습니다.

> 같은 스팟에 재업로드하는 경우 **교체될 디렉터리를 사용량에서 뺍니다.** 빼지 않으면 상한 근처에서 **덮어쓰기조차 거부되는** 이상한 상태가 됩니다.

용량 계산이 IO 오류로 실패하면 **0으로 보고 통과**시킵니다. 상한은 방어선이지 필수 경로가 아니라, 계산 실패로 저장 자체가 막히면 안 됩니다.

## 🧪 검증

`VisitPhotoStorageTest` 에 **5건 추가**했습니다.

| 케이스 | 확인 |
|--------|------|
| 같은 스팟 재업로드 | 이전 사진 삭제, 1장만 남음 |
| 다른 스팟 | 지우지 않음 |
| 총량 초과 | 거부 |
| 같은 스팟 덮어쓰기 | 상한 근처에서도 허용 |
| 다른 사용자 사용량 | 내 상한에 미포함 |

> 로컬에 Gradle이 없어 CI(server 잡)로 검증합니다.

## 📋 남은 후속

**완전한 고아 파일 정리**(업로드 후 422·409로 인증 실패한 경우)는 이 PR 범위 밖입니다. 스팟당 1장 유지로 **누적은 막히지만**, 인증에 실패한 1장은 남습니다.

`visits` 테이블과 대조하는 정리 배치가 필요해지면 별도 이슈로 열겠습니다. 현재 규모에서는 이 PR로 충분하다고 봅니다.

## ⚙️ 설정

```yaml
visit:
  max-photo-bytes-per-user: ${VISIT_MAX_PHOTO_BYTES_PER_USER:209715200}   # 200MB
```

5MB 사진 기준 약 40개 스팟입니다. 실사용에서 부족하면 올리면 되지만 **무제한으로 두지는 마세요.**

## ✅ 체크리스트

- [x] 관련 이슈 연결 (Closes #76)
- [x] 실제 값(키·시크릿) 포함 없음
- [ ] CI 통과 확인
- [ ] 리뷰어 승인

author: hf-cygg
body:
## Summary

#38 之后，写事务必须经由 `runInTransaction` 才能享受 SQLite 串行化。但这个约定此前只写在文件头注释里、靠人自觉；真绕过了也要等 CI 跑完 `task8:verify` 的并发用例才会暴露。本次把它提前到静态检查。

新增 `backend/scripts/write-transaction-contract-verify.ts`，用 TypeScript 编译器 API 解析 AST 后遍历，覆盖三类事务入口：

| 入口 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `xxx.transaction` | DataSource / EntityManager |
| `xxx.startTransaction` | QueryRunner |
| `xxx.query('BEGIN' \| 'START TRANSACTION' \| …)` | 直接下发事务控制 SQL |

关键设计不是「认哪些写法」，而是**在哪一层记账**：

- **前两类在成员引用处记账，而非调用处**。只认调用会被一层间接绕过——`const start = qr.startTransaction.bind(qr); await start()` 里，唯一的调用表达式是 `.bind(...)` 和 `start()`，事务方法从未出现在被调用位置。改为引用处记账后，绑定、赋值、作为回调传出去都会在引用点被捕获。
- **第三类求首参的静态可知前缀，而非完整字面量**。事务控制 SQL 必然以关键字开头，而模板字符串的 head 是字面的，`` `BEGIN ${x}` `` 据此即可判定——不需要求出整条 SQL。覆盖常量变量、变量重新赋值、多跳别名、字符串拼接、三元分支、模板 head。判定前会剥掉 SQL 前导注释（数据库会先忽略注释再执行）。
- 成员名解析同时接受点号与字符串下标（`ds.query` 与 `ds['query']` 运行时是同一个 API），且**只有一处判定**，不会出现两支逻辑走偏。

白名单键为「文件 + 所在函数 + 接收者 + 方法名」四元组，并校验每个键命中的调用数量**精确等于**登记值：

- 命中 0 处 → 死条目，代码已删改，留着会误放行同位置的新调用；
- 命中多于登记值 → 同一函数内新增了未登记调用；
- 换个函数写的调用不命中既有豁免。

每条豁免都必须写明原因，让豁免是一次**显式决定**而非一次疏漏。另确认 `runInTransaction` 调用点非零，防止闸门被整体架空后本门禁仍然「通过」。

接入 `verify-db-concurrency` 流水线与 `verify:all` 聚合套件，排在所有运行时验收**之前**——纯静态、秒级、无运行时依赖。

## 门禁到底挡住什么（#35 引入协调器之后）

`transaction-coordinator.ts` 会 patch `dataSource.transaction` / `query` / queryBuilder / 全局 EntityManager，所以直接调用 `AppDataSource.transaction` 在协调器装好后也会被串行化。但仍有三处缺口需要本门禁把守：

1. **`queryRunner.startTransaction()` 完全不在 patch 范围内**——协调器全文 0 次引用 `createQueryRunner`；
2. **`query('BEGIN')` 这类原始事务 SQL 同样不受保护**——`patchDataSourceQuery` 只按单条语句获取租约，`BEGIN` 返回后租约即释放；
3. `runInTransaction` 保证「先装协调器、再开事务」的次序，直接调用不保证。

## 已登记的豁免（5 条）

| 位置 | 原因 |
|---|---|
| `transaction-runner.ts` `runInTransaction` | 闸门自身的实现 |
| `transaction-coordinator.ts` `patchDataSourceTransaction` ×2 | 协调器安装点：先 bind 保留原实现、再覆写 |
| `database-bootstrap.ts` `migrateLegacyFeedbackAttachments` | 启动期一次性迁移，运行在服务接受请求之前 |
| `database-migration.service.ts` `migrateSingleTableByPrimaryKey` | 面向迁移目标库 `targetDataSource`，不走本进程 SQLite 数据源 |
| `seed-database-migration-e2e.ts` `main` | 一次性 CLI 独占进程，需在同一 QueryRunner 上串接 PRAGMA 与批量播种 |

后三条是本 PR 扫描才发现的、此前完全没人注意到的既有直调。

## 门禁有效性验证

新加的门禁如果是哑弹就毫无价值，所以每一类都做了反向验证——注入绕过写法确认拦截，恢复后确认复验通过：

| # | 写法 | 结果 |
|---|---|---|
| A | 链式调用换行 | 拦截 |
| B | `queryRunner.startTransaction()` | 拦截 |
| C | 已豁免文件内、来源不同的调用 | 拦截 |
| D | 已豁免函数内新增第二个调用 | 报出「登记 1 处，实际命中 2 处」 |
| E | `qr.startTransaction.bind(qr)` 绑定后调用 | 拦截 |
| F | 赋值给变量后 `.call` | 拦截 |
| G | `qr['startTransaction']()` | 拦截 |
| H | `query('BEGIN TRANSACTION')` | 拦截 |
| I | `queryRunner.query('BEGIN')` | 拦截 |
| J | 模板字面量 `` `start   transaction` `` | 拦截 |
| K | `const sql = 'BEGIN'` | 拦截 |
| L | 多跳别名 | 拦截 |
| M | `` `BEGIN ${t}` `` | 拦截 |
| N | `'BEGIN' + ' TRANSACTION'` | 拦截 |
| O | 三元分支 | 拦截 |
| Q | `AppDataSource['query']('BEGIN')` | 拦截 |
| R | `'/* maintenance */ BEGIN'` | 拦截 |
| S | `let sql='SELECT 1'; sql='BEGIN'` | 拦截 |
| — | `SELECT 1` / `BEGINNING_OF_TIME` / `` `/* hint */ SELECT * FROM ${t}` `` | **不误报** |

其中 A/B/C/D/E/G/H/I/Q/R/S 来自审查意见，均为审查者复现后提出、本 PR 逐条修复。

## 已知边界（重要）

**不要把本门禁当成完备证明。**

事务控制 SQL 的识别依赖静态求值，唯一判不了的是「整条 SQL 以无法静态解析的值开头」——例如 `` `${verb} TRANSACTION` ``，或 SQL 由函数参数、配置、数据库内容传入。这是静态分析的固有边界，靠继续加规则堵不住。

**真正的收口在运行时**：协调器只要接管 `createQueryRunner` 与跨语句租约，这些绕过写法在运行时就不成立，不需要静态分析去枚举。已记录为 **#41**。本 PR 的定位是「让人不容易走错路」，不是「证明没人能走错路」。

## 为什么不是 ESLint 规则

本仓库没有引入任何 linter（无 `eslint` / `oxlint` / `biome` 配置，`package.json` 里也没有 lint 脚本）。静态契约在这里一贯由 `scripts/` 下的 `*-contract-verify.ts` 承担——`task2-route-permission-contract-verify.ts` 就是同类门禁（路由权限契约 + 显式白名单）。沿用同一范式，可避免为单条规则引入整套工具链及其对存量代码的连带改造。将来仓库真要引入 linter，这条规则再迁过去也不迟。

## Test plan

- [x] `cd backend && npm run write-transaction:contract:verify`
- [x] `cd backend && npm run check`（tsc --noEmit）
- [x] `cd backend && npx tsx scripts/task8-verify.ts`（含并发用例）
- [x] `node scripts/verify-unit-functional-suite.mjs` 全流程（含新增步骤）
- [x] workflow YAML 解析校验，步骤顺序符合预期
- [x] 上表 18 种绕过写法逐条反证拦截，3 种正常 SQL 确认不误报，恢复后复验通过

author: ecfromthedc
body:
## The problem

In a crew pad, every SEAT has a wake source — the keeper (open tasks), the session watchdog (idle-with-pending-work), and @mention delivery. The LEAD seat has none. If the lead's only watcher is keyed on the operator's posts, the crew can finish everything — SHIP verdicts, DONEs, handoffs — and sit waiting while the orchestrator idles. Finished-but-unmerged work is the same defect as stale data with no alarm. This bit the Mon Rovia build today hard enough that the operator had to come wake the orchestrator by hand, and the fix ran as a session-local /tmp script; it belongs in the tooling.

## The fix

`tool/bin/stitchpad-await` — a wake primitive in the house standalone-helper style (like `stitchpad-ping`): blocks until someone ELSE posts on the pad, prints the message, exits 0. Run it as a background job whose EXIT is the wake signal — the pattern for harnesses where task-completion notifications are dependable and long-lived monitors are not. Re-arm after every firing.

- Keys on a **content hash** of the newest matching message header (unique via `#m-id`), so it survives rewrites, trims and `archive`. The README's count-keyed sample poller goes deaf after a shrink (count drops, `-gt` stays false until the pad regrows past its old high-water mark) — the README now says so.
- `--authors 'kimi|deepseek'` filters to named seats; default is everyone except `$STITCHPAD_NAME`.
- No deps beyond grep/awk/shasum; never tails the pad (per `test/pad-io-and-archive.sh`'s rules).

## Tests

`test/orchestrator-await.sh`, 10 assertions in the house harness style: fires-and-prints on a crew post · exits 0 · ignores own posts · `--authors` filtering both ways · **shrink does not fire, next real post does** · byte-identical rewrite does not fire. The suite caught a real bug on its first run (newline-inconsistent hashing between arm and poll → instant false fire), which is why both sides hash through `printf '%s'`.

author: nayeem-ahmad
body:
## The bug

With the channel list working, pushing a post failed on all three channels:

> Buffer request failed: Variable `$input` got invalid value `"now"` at `input.mode`; Value `"now"` does not exist in `"ShareMode"` enum.

Buffer's enum is `addToQueue | shareNext | shareNow | customScheduled`. `BufferPostMode` used `now` and `next` for two of the four, so **"Publish now" and "First slot in the queue" could never have worked** — Buffer rejects the whole mutation at validation. Not a regression: those two modes have been broken since the feature shipped. The other two spell identically and were the only modes ever reaching Buffer.

Enum taken from [Buffer's schema reference](https://developers.buffer.com/reference.html), not guessed. The same page confirms `mode: ShareMode!` and that the non-null `assets` / `tagIds` / `needsApproval` fields carry defaults — consistent with the push reporting `mode` as its only coercion error.

## Why translate instead of renaming `BufferPostMode`

That constant is not just an internal name:

- `BUFFER_POST_MODES` is the DTO's `@IsIn` allow-list → renaming breaks the API contract
- the value is persisted on `socialMediaPostPush.mode` → existing rows keep the old spelling
- the composer's dropdown builds labels from `p.modes[value]` in en/bn/ms → renaming orphans the keys

So a `SHARE_MODE` map translates at the Buffer boundary, keeping Buffer's vocabulary a Buffer detail.

## Verification

- `src/social-media/` — 3/3 suites, 46 tests green
- Both new tests confirmed **red** first (`Expected "shareNow", Received "now"`) — one per differing mode, plus one pinning the two pass-through modes so a later edit can't quietly rewrite them
- Backend typecheck at its known 4-error baseline (pre-existing accounting/billing specs)

**Not verified: no post has actually been published through Buffer yet.** I could not introspect Buffer's live schema with the real token — copying a script into the production container was blocked — so the docs are strong evidence, not proof.

Also closes out the previous PR's open question: the composer now lists all three live channels, which only `listChannels` can populate, confirming `OrganizationId!` was correct.

author: cfarm6
body:
### Ticket
Closes https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-mlir/issues/9210

### Problem description
`ttnn.scatter` into a rank-1 operand with exactly one index compiles and runs but silently drops the write (returns the operand unchanged). Repro: `jnp.zeros(3).at[jnp.array([0])].set(7)` -> `[0, 0, 0]` on device; two or more indices work.

### Root cause
`pre_scatter_transform_tensor` early-returns rank-1 tensors of shape `{1}` (and `{0}`), so a rank-1 index/source stays rank-1 while the input is 4-D-transformed. The scatter kernel derives per-dimension shape varargs from the transformed ranks (`num_runtime_varargs = (input_rank-1) + (index_rank-1)`), so the missing index dims read past the provided varargs; `in_bounds()` then evaluates false and the scatter phase is skipped entirely — the output is just the input copy.

The `{1}` early return was introduced in the scatter cleanup (#25167); dropping it restores the pre-cleanup transform path (index/source get transposed and 4-D-transformed like every other rank). `{0}` (empty) is kept and is also handled by `scatter()` itself before any transform.

### What changed
Removed the `Shape{1}` condition from both `pre_scatter_transform_tensor` overloads.

### Verification
On Blackhole (jax 0.7.1 via pjrt-plugin-tt): `jnp.repeat(arange(256), 256, total_repeat_length=65536)` now returns the correct repeat (was bucket-rotated); `jnp.zeros(3).at[[0]].set(7)` -> `[7, 0, 0]`. The kUPS neighborlist candidate enumeration (which depends on `jnp.repeat`) matches the CPU reference exactly (see cfarm6/tt-matmol#84).

author: kauandinubila
body:
## Contexto

Discussao sobre a UX de categoria no Pomodoro: hoje todo usuario novo comeca com zero categorias e precisa criar uma antes do primeiro pomodoro. "Trabalho" e "Estudo" batem com a propria proposta do Astra (estudos + trabalho), entao viram default sensato — continuam editaveis/apagaveis, e o usuario pode criar outras mais especificas do jeito que ja funciona.

## Como foi feito

Em vez de `UserService` chamar `CategoryService` direto (o que criaria uma dependencia nova `user -> tracking`, fora do grafo hoje documentado como `stats -> {tracking,learning}`, `tracking -> learning`), usei um evento de dominio:

- `shared.event.UserRegisteredEvent(UUID userId)` — novo, no pacote neutro que ambos os modulos ja usam
- `UserService.register()` publica o evento apos salvar o usuario (`ApplicationEventPublisher`)
- `CategoryService.onUserRegistered` escuta com `@TransactionalEventListener` (so dispara depois do commit da transacao de registro — se o registro falhar/dar rollback, as categorias nao sao criadas) e `@Transactional(propagation = REQUIRES_NEW)` (obrigatorio: o listener AFTER_COMMIT roda fora de qualquer transacao ativa, entao precisa abrir a propria)

`user` continua sem importar nada de `tracking` — so publica um evento generico em `shared`, que `tracking.category` escuta. Sem ciclo novo no grafo de modulos.

## Verificacao

- `mvnw verify` completo (Testcontainers) — verde. Pegou um erro real na primeira tentativa (`@TransactionalEventListener` nao aceita `@Transactional` simples sem `REQUIRES_NEW`/`NOT_SUPPORTED`), corrigido antes deste PR
- Testado ao vivo: `curl` registrando usuario novo -> `GET /categories` ja retorna `[{"name":"Trabalho"...}, {"name":"Estudo"...}]`
- Testado no navegador: cadastrei um usuario pela tela de registro, fui direto pra Sessoes -> Pomodoro -> dropdown de categoria ja vem com Trabalho/Estudo, sem nenhum passo manual

Fresh comparison resolves merge base exactly to current #280 and reports this branch ahead 32 / behind 0; this lane's effective child delta remains its seven collaboration/workflow paths. This lane provides collaborative parity for already-verified host diagnostics: host-supplied props, accessible guidance panel and imperative Focus / Apply / Ignore / Dismiss / Explain methods; exact strong-revision verification before local Apply; plain-text replacement through an ordinary collaborative ProseMirror/Yjs transaction; immediate stale-all invalidation for local or remote changes; two-client convergence and collaborative undo/redo; no fabricated remote action events; read-only Apply prevention; stable editor identity/latest callback ownership; race rejection when remote updates arrive during verification or pending Apply digest; awareness privacy; and host ownership of supplied `Y.Doc` lifecycle.

Inkspan performs no semantic inference and calls no LLM/model provider/network reviewer/database/persistence service. Diagnostic identifiers, titles, explanations, replacements, revisions, provenance and authored text are not written into awareness state.

author: carbonitesolutions
body:
My last change set `max_date` on the date field to grey out future dates. That broke the picker outright — clicking Date opened nothing. Two reasons: the datepicker's options object is built once when the control is created, so setting the property afterwards in `onload` never reaches it; and nothing in Frappe or ERPNext sets `max_date` anywhere, so it is an untested hook rather than a supported one.

Reverted. The same guarantee now comes from a plain `date` handler that says so and resets to today, which touches none of the picker's internals. The server-side refusal is unchanged and remains authoritative.

Fuel Used, Fuel Supplied and Fuel Adjustment also had no default on a required date field, so every new form opened blank — Fuel Transfer already defaulted to today. All four now match.

author: totollygeek
body:
## What & why

Identity resolution — which maps a reworded finding back onto the identity the
review state already holds — only ever considered entries the state had
**decided**: dismissed or fixed. A finding that was merely still **open** and
came back reworded was not compared against anything.

That has a worse consequence than a missed optimisation. The reworded finding
keeps its fresh id, so the old id is not reported this round; the progress pass
then sees an open entry that no longer appears and records it as **fixed, no
longer reproduces against the current diff**. The report tells the maintainer a
finding was resolved and, immediately below, lists the very same concern as a new
finding — and the state block now carries two identities for one problem, which
compounds every round after.

The false claim is the damaging half. A maintainer reading "✅ Fixed since first
review" is being told a live issue is gone.

Observed on `master` before the fix, from a real run through the reviewer: the
console printed `fixed: Eval of user input` while reporting the reworded wording
as a live finding, and the posted state held both ids. After the fix the same
inputs yield one entry, still open, with the rewording recorded as its alias.

## The ordering, made explicit

Open entries now take part in the comparison, and the sort is spelled out rather
than left incidental: **fixed, then dismissed, then still-open**. Both halves
matter and are commented in the code:

- Fixed before dismissed keeps the existing precedence — a candidate matching
  both reopens, which reports, rather than inheriting a dismissal, which
  silences.
- Decided entries before open ones stops the newcomers crowding a sticky
  dismissal out of the per-candidate comparison cap.

**The risk this adds, stated plainly:** two genuinely distinct open findings in
one file can now be merged by a wrong "same" verdict. It is bounded by the
existing same-file rule and severity ceiling, and by the refusal to collapse two
findings onto one identity. The failure direction is one merged row rather than a
silenced finding — where the bug being fixed produces a false claim of
resolution, which is worse.

## Testing

A flow test drives the real reviewer with a still-open prior finding and a
reworded re-report, asserting there is no "fixed" line anywhere in the report,
that the state holds exactly one entry, that it is still `open`, that it still
gates, and that the rewording is recorded as an alias so later rounds resolve it
for free.

`deno task ci` is green, run with GITHUB_ACTIONS set so host detection matches
CI.

## Related issues

A regression from the reworded-finding work in #338, found while designing item 2
of the `@zuke/ai` v2.x follow-up plan — inline review threads would have turned
this into a "✅ Fixed" reply posted into a maintainer's live conversation, so it
is fixed first and on its own.

## Checklist

- [x] The PR title is a [Conventional Commit](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`type(scope): summary`).
- [x] `deno task ci` passes locally (lint, fmt, type-check, tests, spell).
- [x] Tests were added or updated; coverage stays at 95%+ (lines and branches).
- [x] Docs updated in the same PR (`README.md`, JSDoc, `docs/`) when behaviour changed.
- [x] Public API changes were regenerated with `./zuke apiDocs` (`llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, package README `## API`).
- [x] No `any`, no `as` casts or `!` non-null assertions in `src/` (narrow with type guards instead).
- [ ] A new package was wired into all seven places (see [AGENTS.md](../blob/master/AGENTS.md#good-open-source-practices-to-follow)), if applicable.
- [x] The code is written using AI assisted coding.

author: rizaleow
body:
Closes every outstanding item from the PR #1 review. Each finding was re-verified by execution before being fixed; a few turned out to need more than the review described.

## Security

- **`Attr::build` emitted attribute names raw.** Values were escaped, names were not. Named args are safe PHP identifiers, but `attrs: [...]` keys are arbitrary — a key holding a quote closed the attribute and opened a new one. Now rejected.
- **CSRF degraded silently.** `Hx::csrfHeaders()` and `Form::csrfField()` caught `\Throwable` and returned empty, rendering a form that looked correct but carried no token, with no signal anywhere. I checked what actually throws: `getHash()` doesn't, and neither path throws in a request or test context — the catches only hid unrelated errors. Removed, so a broken security service fails loudly.

## Silent failures

- **A corrupt or missing `catalog.json` decoded to an empty catalog**, so one root cause produced three contradictory messages (`ui:list` empty, `ui:add` "Unknown component", `ui:add --all` "specify a component"). Now throws, reported as a clean CLI error.
- **A dangling `registryDependencies` entry was skipped**, installing an incomplete component and reporting success.
- **`Resolver::files()` returned `[]` when the package namespace was unresolvable**, so `ui:publish` walked all 50 components, printed nothing, and exited 0. Now throws; entries that legitimately publish nothing (`icon`) say so explicitly.
- Catalog parsing is memoized instead of re-read per lookup, and a `componentsPath` escaping `app/Views` is rejected.

## Correctness

- **`Services::ui($config)` was inert** — `Registry` took a `Ui` config and never read it, so a custom `componentsPath` was ignored and view resolution silently used the global config. Threaded through to `ViewResolver`.
- **`class:` and `className:` assigned rather than appended**, so passing both dropped one; `attrs: ['class' => ...]` was overwritten by the class merge; `data()['attributes']` omitted the class `$attrs` carried.
- **`Tooltip` and `Menu` had no `conflictGroups()`** while always emitting a direction modifier, so `class: 'tooltip-bottom'` could never win — daisyUI resolves by stylesheet order, not class order.
- **Five documented props were dead**: `alert.title`, `modal.closable`, `sheet.size`, `stat.action`, `slider.size`. Implemented rather than withdrawn.
- **The sidebar trigger hardcoded `lg:hidden`** while `breakpoint` was configurable.
- `Button` used `'md'` as its no-size sentinel while every other component uses `''`, so `size: ''` emitted a bare `btn-`.

## Distribution

- **`menu-items` is now publishable.** It had no catalog entry and was hard-referenced by package namespace, so after `ui:add menu` the published view still reached into the package for every item — the user owned the wrapper but not a single item. Moved to the standard view layout, added `ui_menu_items()`, and made `menu`/`dropdown`/`context-menu` depend on it.

## Config and JS

- **`defaultTheme`, `darkTheme`, `buildTool` and the pinned versions were read nowhere** while their docblocks claimed otherwise. The theme toggle now takes its theme names from config, and `ui:init` branches on `buildTool` and reports the pinned versions.
- **`uiCommand` and `uiContextMenu` leaked window listeners.** `Alpine.initTree` runs on every `htmx:afterSwap`, so each swap added a handler bound to an orphaned instance and Cmd+K fired once per stale copy. Both clean up in `destroy()` — the documented `Alpine.data` hook, confirmed against the Alpine docs.
- Dropped the Alpine theme store (no consumers, docblock claimed the toggle used it) and a comment pointing at waves that had already shipped.

## Tests

`assertNotFalse(command('ui:list'))` asserted nothing — CI4's `command()` returns the output buffer and these commands write to STDOUT, so it always returned `''` and the same test passed for a garbage command name. Replaced with exit-code assertions. That immediately exposed a real gap: `ui:add`/`ui:publish`/`ui:init` read flags only via `CLI::getOption()`, so their options did nothing when invoked through `command()`. Fixed both.

New coverage for the previously untested layers: `ui:add`/`ui:publish` actually copying files, dependency pull-in, `-o` overwrite, the published-view override path, `Hx`, and `Label`.

**250 → 266 tests, 2060 assertions, all green. Pint clean.** All five `ui:*` commands smoke-tested against the demo app.

author: lhames
body:
Reimplement EPCGenericJITLinkMemoryManager's reserve/initialize/release calls using rt::Proxy objects rather than direct
ExecutorProcessControl::callSPSWrapperAsync calls, matching EPCGenericMemoryAccess and EPCGenericDylibManager. The manager's behavior is unchanged.

Details:

* SymbolAddrs (five ExecutorAddrs) becomes Bindings: the allocator instance address plus rt::Proxy handles.

* The proxy types and SPS specs are hoisted into shared headers -- RTBridge/GenericMemoryManagerProxies.h and RTBridge/SPS/GenericMemoryManagerProxySpecs.h -- since they now need only Shared/SPS vocabulary. Deinitialize is included in the family for completeness though this manager does not call it.

* Release is a single proxy over ArrayRef<ExecutorAddr>: abandon passes the allocation base directly, deallocate extracts base addresses from its FinalizedAllocs. This retires the SPSSerializationTraits<SPSExecutorAddr, FinalizedAlloc> specialization (previously used only to serialize vector<FinalizedAlloc> in deallocate).

* The spec signatures are declared inline, duplicating the SPSSimpleExecutorMemoryManager* signatures in OrcRTBridge.h; a follow-up will retire those.

author: mohsen1
body:
Fixes #17235: a real wrong-code conformance regression (`verbatimModuleSyntaxNoElisionCJS` lost its `TS1283`), oracle-confirmed by m4's 11:59:59Z comment on the issue.

## Structural rule

When a whole-module `import [type] X = require(module)` is type-only and targeted by `export =` under `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `tsc` picks between `TS1282` ("`X` only refers to a type") and `TS1283` ("`X` resolves to a type-only declaration") based on `X`'s **fully-merged meaning across the alias chain**: `TS1283` when the target genuinely has a value somewhere in that chain, `TS1282` when it never does anywhere. tsz does this through the checker's `check_vms_export_equals` (and its `export default` sibling, `check_verbatim_module_syntax_export_default`'s `TS1284`/`TS1285` pick, which shares the identical defect).

Both sites answered the "does the target have a value" question by looking up a member named after the **local binding** in the target module — correct for a named import (`import type { X } from './mod'`, where `import_name()` legitimately means "look up this name"; it returns `None` there only when the name is un-renamed, falling back to the local name by design), but wrong for `import X = require(module)`: `X` aliases the module's own `export =` target as a single unit, not a member called `X` — no such member exists, so the lookup always missed and every whole-module `import type X = require(...)` collapsed to `TS1282` regardless of whether the target actually carried a value.

## Fix

Owner layer: checker. A shared `type_only_import_alias_target_has_value` helper (`declarations/import/verbatim.rs`) distinguishes the two shapes by the alias's own declaration node kind — `IMPORT_EQUALS_DECLARATION` with a resolved (string-literal) module specifier means a whole-module require, since `import J = SomeNamespace.Member` (the other `import =` form) never sets a module specifier at all. For that shape it consults the existing `is_module_export_equals_type_only` query (already used elsewhere for the same "what does this module's `export =` really mean" question) instead of a member lookup. Both call sites (`check_vms_export_equals` for `TS1282`/`TS1283`, `check_verbatim_module_syntax_export_default` for `TS1284`/`TS1285`) now share this one helper instead of duplicating the (buggy) inline logic.

## Adjacent-case matrix (oracle-verified, pinned `typescript@7.0.2`)

| Case | tsc | tsz before | tsz after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `import type J = require("./c")`, `c`'s `export = I` where `I` is `interface I {} / namespace I { export const x = 1 }` (merged, has value) — the exact #17235 repro | TS1283 | TS1282 (wrong) | TS1283 |
| same, but `c`'s `export = I` where `I` is a pure `interface I { x: number }` (no value anywhere) | TS1282 | TS1282 | TS1282 (unchanged) |
| plain (non-`type`) `import I = require("./c")` to a value-carrying target, `export = I` | silent | silent | silent (unaffected — never enters the `is_type_only` branch) |
| renamed binders (`Gadget`/`Gizmo` instead of `J`/`I`) to a value-carrying target | TS1283 | TS1282 (wrong) | TS1283 |
| named ES import control, `import type { Foo } from './types'; export = Foo;` to a value-carrying class member | TS1283 | TS1283 | TS1283 (unchanged — member-lookup path untouched) |

## Goal
Goal: hold

## Verification
- New test file `verbatim_module_syntax_export_equals_require_ts1282_ts1283_tests.rs`, 5 tests covering the matrix above: 5/5 green.
- Targeted sweep (`verbatim_module_syntax`, `export_equals`, `export_default_alias`, `export_default_type_only`, `ts2303`, `ts2498`): 72/72 green, 0 regressions (includes all pre-existing TS1282/1283/1284/1285/1289/1290/1291/1484/1485 coverage).
- Full `cargo test -p tsz-checker --lib` (~11.2k tests) launched in the background; no failures observed through the bulk of the suite so far. Will post the final count on this PR before landing, or note the documented slow-tail cutoff if it hasn't finished.
- `cargo clippy --release -p tsz-checker --lib -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt -p tsz-checker -- --check`: clean.
- `python3 scripts/arch/arch_guard.py`: clean.
- Manual CLI check with a debug `tsz` build against the exact #17235 repro: emits `d.ts(3,10): error TS1283: An 'export =' declaration must reference a real value when 'verbatimModuleSyntax' is enabled, but 'J' resolves to a type-only declaration.` — byte-identical to the pinned oracle.
- Conformance: not run this session (`TypeScript` submodule not checked out; the reduced oracle-verified repro above is #17235's own minimal reproduction of the `verbatimModuleSyntaxNoElisionCJS` regression, so it is the primary evidence for that row).
