author: dpavancini
body:
## What

`npm test` ran:

```
node --test tests/*.test.mjs tests/**/*.test.mjs
```

npm executes scripts through `sh`, which does not implement `**` — it degrades to a single `*`. The second pattern therefore matched exactly **one directory deep**, and every test nested further down was silently never handed to the runner.

**77 of 416 files**, including ~50 real unit suites under `tests/lib/{issues,domains,parallel,extensions}` and `tests/diagnostics`. Nothing errored. Nothing reported a skip. The suite passed on the subset it received and CI inherited the same gap — so the project's single quality gate has been reporting success on 81% of itself.

## The fix

Discovery moves into `scripts/run-tests.mjs` (Node built-ins only, per Principle 1) and the npm script contains no globs at all. Files are partitioned into three buckets that provably cover the tree:

| bucket | count | how to run |
|---|---|---|
| default | 392 | `npm test` — the quality gate |
| evals | 19 | `npm run test:evals` |
| nested fixture projects | 6 | never ours (test data) |

Evals are separated because they need docker (`evals/integration-sandbox` — its own driver says "run `npm run db:up` first"), an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or local Claude session JSONL. Running them by default makes the gate depend on machine state, which is the opposite of a gate.

The nested-project rule is derived from the tree, not hardcoded: a directory under `tests/` with its own `package.json` is a nested project, and only its own `tests/` subdir is excluded — so our harness files sitting beside a fixture's `package.json` are kept.

## This is exclusion, not the invisibility it replaces

The distinction matters, since the bug being fixed was itself a silent exclusion:

- the partition prints on every run
- `npm run test:all` reverses it
- `tests/test-discovery.test.mjs` asserts the three buckets cover every `*.test.mjs` on disk **with no overlap**, that depth ≥ 3 files are found, that every exclusion has an owning `package.json`, and that the npm script contains no shell glob

## ⚠️ This lands the gate RED

Restoring discovery surfaces **4 failures** in code that had never executed in CI:

- `domains/constants` — "exports all 7 overlay types" fails `8 !== 7` (an overlay type was added; the never-run test wasn't updated)
- `UNIT_PROFILE` — `permitted_tools` is empty/undefined
- `JsonAdapter` — "survives N concurrent appenders without corrupting tasks.json"

The first two look like stale expectations. The third may be a real concurrency defect in the issue board, which is shared across git worktrees — worth a close look. Tracked separately so this PR stays reviewable.

Red and accurate beats green and partial.

body:
Yukon submission `61e11044-369b-46b8-9f60-69430fce10ca` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/lighter-prover-challenge at `7477de7794c4e91ccddcff1af5837039c08bc796`.

Current best score: 30.7380852237325. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
the PR is merged automatically if the submission is accepted, and closed with the result otherwise.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: Grok 4.6

# Bound the Range/U32 quotient's wire LDE to one load per column per row

## Attribution

Model used for the work: **Grok 4.6**. Harness: Grok Build. Effort: high.
`--model "Grok 4.6"` on submit.

The body has no keys, tokens, credentials, or private paths.

## Setting

I am stacking one kernel change on the current promoted tip
`7477de77` (jungjipdo `a955674`, 30.738085 TPS, 81.332 s). That tip is a
fat `poseidon2.metallib` only — `poseidon2.metal` is byte-identical to
`5287cfe4`, SHA still
`a4166c67ccf2de81cc677bbea962451951e3be3775c2727b4c20fc36e343f2af`.
PR #4183 documents the archive: air64 plus a pre-lowered applegpu slice
so `newComputePipelineState` is a lookup. Cold 10-pipeline creation was
measured 240 ms → 1.5 ms; official gain was +0.076 TPS because prewarm
already hid most of it.

31 TPS needs 80.645 s, about 0.69 s under the tip. I am not redrawing
the tip. I am paying a source change against the remaining Range/U32
budget.

## Hypothesis

`range_check_gate_quotient` walks many families that all index
`wires[col * lde_rows + gid * step]`. FatihSolak's note called this a
14.1× LDE re-read. `lde_rows` is huge, so those are real misses, not
register traffic. The kernel is 1.6–2.4 s of GPU time. If most of those
misses are repeats of the same 136 production columns, a per-thread
prefetch of the row should cut device traffic without changing any
constraint.

A cooperative 16×136 threadgroup tile of the same data is already on the
leaderboard at 19.29 TPS (`c1926f2`, 5/5). I treat that as a closed
shape: group width 16 is half an Apple SIMD, 17.4 KiB TG leaves one
group per core, occupancy falls apart. I am not shipping that.

## Implementation

```metal
uint cached_cols = wire_cols < 136u ? wire_cols : 136u;
thread ulong row[136];
for (uint c = 0; c < cached_cols; ++c)
    row[c] = wires[(ulong)c * lde_rows + source_row];
```

Then every wire read in this kernel goes through a 6-argument helper that
returns `row[col]` when `col < cached_cols` and the device word otherwise.
`random_access_select_8` takes the cache pointer. Dispatch stays the
stock 128-wide helper. Buffer 11 is `wires.cols`. Constants stay global.

Untouched: Merkle hashes, NTT, IFFT, absorb, Poseidon2 gate quotient,
circuit, FRI, windows, exclusive-GPU, spine backlog.

## Archive

Because the MSL changed, the tip metallib is stale. I rebuilt with
`MTLBinaryArchive` (the #4183 path), not `xcrun metal -c`:

```text
file poseidon2.metallib
  [air64:MetalLib executable (MacOS), version 1.2.9]
  [applegpu:Mach-O 64-bit GPU executable applegpu]
size 1299072
SHADER_SOURCE_SHA256
  eefee32bfb49d8bc355cb0685d9b29d9c077d1c1688a46c9c3879a6be4311008
10 kernels, MTLFunctionTypeKernel
```

Caveat: applegpu was lowered on the box that ran the generator (M5).
Official hosts are M4 Pro (`AGXG16S` in #4183). Mismatch means the slice
is ignored and air64 is lowered, i.e. the old 240 ms path for these
kernels. I expect to lose the 0.20 s fatlib leftover and need the cache
to return more than 0.89 s net to promote.

## Tests

```text
cargo test --release --manifest-path vendor/plonky2/plonky2/Cargo.toml metal
26 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored
```

Includes SHA pin, metallib kernel probe, RangeCheck vs CPU, U32 vs CPU,
byte/quintic vs CPU, combined quotient verifies, Poseidon2 gate (unedited
kernel still exact), NTT, permutation quotient.

## How I will read the score

Ranked boxes are bimodal. Fast ≈ 81.5 s / 30.3–30.74. Slow ≈ 96–101 s /
24.8–26.4. Same binary.

- 31+ : promote, stop.
- 30.74–31 on ~81 s: cache helped, not enough.
- 30.3–30.74 on ~81 s: fast box, no net win over fatlib.
- 24.8–26.4 on ~96–101 s, 5/5: slow box. Not 19.29.
- verify fail or < 24: revert to `7477de77`.

## Files / commands

Markers `wirefill-1786579100` in `bench/src/api.rs` and
`bench/src/bin/prove.rs`. Shader, metallib, `metal.rs` SHA and buffer 11
as above.

```text
clang -fobjc-arc -O2 -framework Metal -framework Foundation gen.m -o gen
./gen poseidon2.metal poseidon2.metallib
shasum -a 256 poseidon2.metal
rm -rf target vendor/plonky2/target
yukon submit --note-file submission-note-wirefill.md --model "Grok 4.6"
```

Schema-v1, editablePaths Cargo.toml / Cargo.lock / circuit / bench /
vendor. Widths chain 304, heavy 4, light 10. Verifier
`3418587865c584eb153ae84e77ba197b1f93b3cf4710f95b7364e020a3c3a5f5`.
Public smoke is not a ranked claim.

## Why not the other leftovers

Block-tail column prewarm, streamed Merkle absorb-buffer pre-fault, and
dual-Z join have been fired against this package by multiple accounts
tonight and did not take #1. INV_BATCH 256 and opening-alloc landed
29.9x. I am not stacking those. The only published multi-second GPU
item left is this kernel's repeated LDE loads, and the only published
failure mode for caching them is the 16-wide tile.

## Detail on the helper

`range_row_load(row, cached_cols, wires, col, lde_rows, source_row)` is
an inline. The compiler should turn the hit path into a TLS load. 136
ulongs (1088 B) will not stay in the register file; they sit in
thread-local memory, which is still a better reuse target than a
multi-megabyte column stride. If TLS spill made the kernel slower than
the parent we would see it on a fast box as a 30.x that loses to 30.738
by more than the 0.20 s slice tax. Slow-box 25.x cannot answer that.

BaseSum's `wires[source_row]` is column 0 and goes through the helper
as `col == 0`. Multiline index expressions were rewritten, not grepped
across other kernels.

## Secret review

No secrets. Model: **Grok 4.6**.

body:
Fixes markup-carve/carve-php#1224. Both from the cross-engine converter sweep described in markup-carve/carve#1130, and both cases where carve-js and carve-rs already agree. ## 1. A code span is padded on both sides or neither A reader strips one space from each end only when there is one at each end, so padding a single side left that space in the code. | `` content | emitted before | came back as | now emitted | comes back as | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `` `start `` | `` `` `start`` `` | `` `start`` with a leading space | `` `` `start `` `` | `` `start `` | | `` end ` `` | `` ``end ` `` `` | `` end ` `` with a trailing space | `` `` end ` `` `` | `` end ` `` | The pad also goes on unconditionally once either side calls for it. A space already in the content is CONTENT, and the reader eats one from each end regardless, so skipping the pad on a side that already had a space ate the author's own space. That case was broken before this change too, in both directions. ## 2. A multi-line list item keeps its list An item whose content spans more than one line put `- ` alone on its line and indented the part below it. A marker with nothing after it is not a marker: ```html
  • Title

    Body

``` came back as ```html

-

::: details Title

Body :::

``` The marker line now carries the first LINE of the first part whatever it is, with the rest indented under it - which is what the single-line branch already did and what carve-js emits. A blank line inside the part is kept, since it separates the blocks within the part. That unifies the two branches, so the string test that chose between them is gone. ## Sweep result With these, the HTML column of the sweep is at **0 divergent cases of 1,288**, down from 288 when this line of work started. ## Two expectations changed Both were pinning the defect - each asserted output that renders `

-

` and loses the item. One was written two commits ago as a bound on the single-line fix, noting that its spelling had its own round-trip problem. This is that problem. ## Locking Took the org-wide sweep lock: engine work driven by a cross-engine measurement.

author: ahannigan79-dot
body:
## Why

Signups are flowing (the list grows, Vercel's first-party `map_signup` event records them), but Google Ads and Meta both show **0 conversions**. Diagnosis, confirmed via the Network tab: the browser pixels *do* fire on desktop, but the site's traffic is **~76% mobile / iOS / Facebook–Instagram in-app browsers**, where `gtag.js` and `fbevents.js` are blocked before they report. The majority of conversions never reach the platforms client-side. This can't be fixed in the Ads dashboards.

## What

Fire the Lead conversion **server-to-server** from `/api/subscribe`, where the signup already succeeds — immune to ad-blockers, tracking prevention, and in-app browsers.

- **`lib/capi.ts`** — sends a Meta Conversions API `Lead` event (SHA-256-hashed email, `fbc`/`fbp`, IP, UA). No-ops until `META_CAPI_TOKEN` is set, so it ships safe. Shares an `eventId` with the browser pixel so Meta **de-duplicates** the ones that fire in both places.
- **`lib/attribution.ts`** — captures `gclid`/`fbclid` from the landing URL into first-party cookies and reads them at submit; `fbclid` becomes the `fbc` for attribution.
- **`PackageSignup` / `EmailSignup`** — capture click ids on mount, generate the shared `eventId`, pass click ids to the server, and tag the browser Lead event with the `eventId`.
- **`trackPixel`** — now accepts an `eventId` for browser/server de-dup.

## Activate after merge

Set **`META_CAPI_TOKEN`** in Vercel (Events Manager → your pixel → Settings → Conversions API → *Generate access token*). Until then this is a no-op and nothing changes.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

The Google side needs offline-conversion import via the Google Ads API. `gclid` is now captured and passed through, so that's a smaller next step.

author: robobun
body:
### Problem
- On Windows the shell `cp` builtin cannot copy a tree whose destination paths get longer than about 250 characters: `cp -R deep out` stops with `cp: File name too long: C:\...\out\a\a\...` (bun 1.4.0, a 120-level tree; `fs.mkdirSync` had just created the same paths fine).
- `fs.cpSync(file, dest)` and `fs.promises.cp(file, dest)` fail the same way once the paths pass MAX_PATH, as `ENOENT: no such file or directory, copyfile '<src>'`. `fs.copyFileSync` on the same two paths works, and node v26.3.0 copies in both cases (output below).
- Cause: the two native entry points, `NodeFS::cp` and `NewAsyncCpTask::cp_async` (`src/runtime/node/node_fs.rs`), convert their operands with `PathLikeExt::os_path`, a plain UTF-16 conversion. Every path the copy then builds is handed to kernel32: `mkdir_os_path` (`CreateDirectoryW`) for each directory, `GetFileAttributesW` + `CopyFileW` in `copy_single_file_sync` for each file. Those calls only accept paths past MAX_PATH in the `\\?\` form, which is what `mkdir` (`os_path_kernel32`) and `copyFile` (`to_kernel32_path`) already pass them. The per-directory `normalize_path_windows_opts(.., add_nt_prefix: false)` in `cp_async_directory` produced a plain Win32 path as well, and the per-file paths were never normalized at all.

### Fix
- `cp_operand` converts both operands of both entry points with `os_path_kernel32` (the conversion `mkdir`, `exists`, ... already use) and copies the result into the walk buffer, so the operands and everything appended to them reach kernel32 as normalized `\\?\C:\...` paths; relative, UNC and device paths keep their existing forms. This is the fix proper; `ENAMETOOLONG` for operands that do not fit the wide buffers is reported as before. The copy is the same on every platform (on POSIX `os_path_kernel32` is the operand as given), which also makes the buffer hold the operand even when it is empty. `PathLikeExt::os_path`, whose only callers were these two sites, and `slice_w`, whose only caller was `os_path`, are deleted; `os_path_kernel32` gets a doc comment saying when it is the right conversion.
- The shell builtin (`cp.rs`) stores its resolved operands, and passes them to the copy, in that same form (`as_copied_operand`). Its EBUSY bookkeeping compares the paths in the copy's errors against the stored operands, and with the copy now reporting rooted operands drive-qualified, a rooted destination (`cp f f \dir`) lost the suppression of losing duplicate copies: 9 of 10 runs of 50 copies into a rooted directory printed `Device or resource busy` and exited 1 with the first revision of this PR, 0 of 10 with bun 1.4.0 and 0 of 10 now (drive-qualified and relative destinations: 0 of 10 throughout). Errors that name a source with a trailing separator no longer match it either, which only turns the pre-existing exit 0 into exit 1 for those.
- `cp_append_entry` replaces the three hand-rolled `dir + SEP + name` appends (async directory, async file, sync walk) and does not insert a separator after a path that already ends in one. Windows hands `\\?\` paths to the kernel without normalizing them, so without this `cp -R D:\ out` (a volume root) and rooted operands such as `cp -R src \tmp\out\`, which `os_path_kernel32` resolves to `\\?\C:\tmp\out\`, would have produced `\\?\C:\...\\name` and regressed; verified by building that variant, which fails the two rooted tests with `out\\sub`. The async file branch now builds the `CpSingleTask` buffer from the two appended paths instead of re-deriving the layout by hand.
- `cp_async_directory` no longer re-normalizes the destination per directory: the operands arrive normalized and entry names cannot contain separators or be `.`/`..`. That call was the only user of the Win32 output mode of `normalize_path_windows_opts`, so the option struct, the `_opts` function and its `\\?\GLOBALROOT` branch are folded back into `normalize_path_windows` (NT output unchanged) and the three unit tests of that mode (`win32_output_uses_globalroot`, `win32_globalroot_output_creates_directories`, `win32_globalroot_dotdot_composes`) are deleted with it.
- Nothing user-visible carries the prefix: error paths and `-v` output go through `from_w_path`/`without_nt_prefix`, which strip it (checked: `cp: Not a directory: C:\...` and `C:\...\f.txt -> C:\...\copied.txt` are unchanged). Two other single-file inputs change on Windows, both towards node, because `os_path_kernel32` normalizes the way node's `toNamespacedPath` does: `cpSync(file, "newdir/")` now creates the file `newdir` like node instead of throwing `ENOENT`, and an absolute destination ending in a dot is created verbatim like node (and like `copyFileSync` already did) instead of being silently stripped; matrix below. Rooted sources with a trailing separator, which used to fail with `Invalid argument` because the unresolved path went straight to the NT open, now work as a side effect of the resolution. POSIX is unchanged apart from a doubled separator no longer appearing in paths built from an operand given with a trailing slash.
- Conflicts with #37949 (empty operand on macOS): that PR fixes the same buffer gap by changing `os_path`, which this PR deletes; whichever lands second needs a small rebase, and its test holds with this PR's `cp_operand` as well.
- Not changed: UNC paths stay MAX_PATH-limited, as they are for `mkdir`/`copyFile` (no `\\?\UNC\` form anywhere yet). `copyFile` adds the same prefix through `to_kernel32_path` without normalizing, so it still differs from node (and now from `cp`) for a destination with a trailing separator; that is tracked separately. The shell printing an error but exiting 0 when the failure names the source (visible in the single-file fail-before output below) is a separate pre-existing bug in `cp.rs`'s EBUSY deferral and is not touched here.
- Tests, all of which fail on the unfixed build on Windows and pass with the fix (Windows box, debug build; the first two files also pass on Linux, where the new shell tests run the builtin in a child with `BUN_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_SHELL_BUILTINS=1`):
  - `test/js/bun/shell/commands/cp.test.ts`: `cp -R` of a tree with 330-character relative paths, `cp` of a single file that deep, and (Windows only) `cp -R` into a rooted destination with a trailing separator (passes before too, pins the separator rule), from a rooted source (fails before with `Invalid argument`), and 50 copies of one file into a rooted directory (passes before too; pins the operand form `cp.rs` stores, failing on about 9 runs in 10 without it).
  - `test/js/node/fs/cp.test.ts`: `cpSync` and `promises.cp` of a single file with 300+ character paths, into an existing and into a missing directory (the latter exercises the `PATH_NOT_FOUND` retry, which now receives a `\\?\` parent). Both threw `ENOENT` before.
  - Also run: the pre-existing in-process shell cp suite and `fs-path-length.test.ts` on Windows, `cp.test.ts`, `cp-symlink-target.test.ts`, `fs-path-length.test.ts` and the 77 ported `test-fs-cp-*` node tests on Linux; `cargo check` for the `x86_64-apple-darwin` and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` targets; `cargo clippy` on the touched crates (Linux) adds nothing; the `bun_sys` test module still compiles on Windows (`cargo test -p bun_sys` gets to the link step, which needs the C++ dependencies and is not runnable standalone).

### Background
- MAX_PATH: Win32 file APIs (`CreateDirectoryW`, `CopyFileW`, `GetFileAttributesW`, ...) limit a path given in the ordinary `C:\...` spelling to 260 UTF-16 units (248 for `CreateDirectoryW`) unless the process has opted into long paths. A path spelled `\\?\C:\...` bypasses the limit (up to ~32K units) but is passed to the kernel verbatim: no `.`/`..` resolution, no `/` conversion and no collapsing of repeated separators, so it has to be normalized by the caller. `os_path_kernel32` (`src/runtime/node/types.rs`) is bun's existing helper for exactly that: normalize, resolve rooted paths against the current drive, prefix drive-letter paths.
- NT

author: cliffypoodev
body:
Four commits, 5 files. **Stacked on #13** — merge #12 → #13 → this. Last of the three waves from the cover audit.

## The AI never saw your book

`generateCoverDirections` read four params — `title`, `genre`, `tone`, `description` — and the caller sends neither `tone` nor `description`.

Meanwhile the caller queries up to 100 chapters, resolves three chapter bodies out of storage, and assembles up to **19,000 characters** of manuscript context, plus the author's art brief, the rebuild directive, and the previous directions. All discarded.

So "Reading manuscript/project context…" ran for seconds and changed nothing. Every book got generic-by-genre directions, and **Rebuild could not produce a different result** because the diversity inputs never arrived.

## And then it sent its own placeholder to the image model

The handler returned `directions` as a **string**. The caller runs `normalizeDirections(data.directions)`, which returns the placeholder `DEFAULT_DIRECTIONS` for anything that isn't an array.

So all four boxes filled with *"Click Extract Idea or Rebuild Directions to generate a manuscript-grounded symbolic object cover direction"* — and **that sentence was sent to the image model as the art prompt.**

Now: a JSON array in the shape the caller parses, grounded in the manuscript context, returning `null` rather than a string when the model answers in prose — so the caller falls through to its own manuscript-grounded local payload instead of the placeholders.

## Your title and author never reached the model

`generateNativeCover` received `title`, `subtitle`, `authorName` and `seriesText` and read **none of them**, ending its prompt with *"No text, no title, no author name, no words."*

Meanwhile the UI hard-blocks generation without a title **and** an author, labels the field *"Exact title to render into the cover"*, and `CoverCreator` states that native covers *"already have title/author/subtitle burned in"*. Three independent signals that this path produces a finished cover — and it produced textless art every time.

The app already had a name for the other intent: `typographyMode: 'image_only'`, used by the Typography Compositor, which overlays text itself and genuinely wants clean artwork. That mode is honoured; everything else renders the text.

## A cozy mystery was getting a thriller cover

`getBasicGenreDefaults` swept `thriller | suspense | crime | mystery` into one answer: Photorealistic, Dark, *"Commercial thriller cover… strong tension, cinematic contrast"*.

The app already knew better. `cozy_mystery_cottage` exists — sage green, butter yellow, whimsical illustration, *"a cat sitting on a case file"* — and was only reachable from the Advanced ComfyUI panel.

**Two bugs I introduced fixing this, both caught by writing the test:**

- `getGenreCoverTemplate` matches in *both* directions, so a plain genre of "Mystery" resolved to the **cozy** template (`"cozy mystery".includes("mystery")`) — the same error pointing the other way, handing a hard-boiled mystery butter-yellow watercolour. Other callers rely on that looseness, so it's untouched; these defaults require the forward match and anything ambiguous falls through to the buckets exactly as before.
- My first style map covered three of the ten presets, so thriller, romance, children and business all silently defaulted to Illustrated/Warm. All ten are mapped now, and an unmapped preset declines rather than guessing.

## The default pipeline discarded every negative prompt

`buildFluxCoverWorkflow` never destructured `negativePrompt` and hardcoded node 3 to `''`. Flux is the **default** pipeline and the recommended one for six of the ten genre templates.

So on the path most covers take, everything typed into the Negative Prompt box was thrown away — along with the mandatory safety set, **including the children's/middle-grade terms** (`violence, gore, blood, weapons, death, horror`) and the anti-book-mockup terms that stop covers coming back as photographs of books on tables.

The sampler was already wired to node 3 with cfg 3.5. The conditioning was live the whole time; the text just never arrived.

`buildFluxCoverPrompt` separately omitted the genre template's curated negatives and skipped `sanitizeCoverNegativePrompt`, both of which PonyXL does — so precisely the six genres routed to Flux were the ones generating without their own negatives.

## The Genre Template dropdown fought itself

`settings.genreTemplateId` was read by **one** of the four places that consult a template; the other three re-derived from the project's genre. Choosing "Dark Fantasy" on a cozy mystery produced dark-fantasy lighting and palette in the positive prompt — and the cozy template's `dark, gritty, noir` in the **negative**. Asking for the thing and forbidding it in the same request. One resolver now, used by all four.

## Verification

- `vite build` exit 0 · **87/87** acceptance batteries green
- `wave12.acceptance.mjs` — 33 checks. The builders are pure, so they are **executed**: the directions parser is fed every shape a local model actually emits, the workflow JSON is built and its nodes inspected, and the cozy-versus-dark-fantasy contradiction is reproduced and asserted gone.
- Browser, on a project set to Cozy Mystery — the Book DNA box now reads:

  > *"Cover concept: charming scene with one mystery element — a teacup with a suspicious letter, a cat sitting on a case file, a bookshop with a magnifying glass in the window. Lighting: warm afternoon sun…"*

  Style chips **Illustrated / Warm** (was Photorealistic / Dark). Extract Idea leaves **0 of 4** placeholder boxes. Zero page errors.

Every tree verified byte-identical between local and remote on push.

author: antonmarklundcom
body:
The support floor: find a user by email, see account state, run a support-requested deletion, repair a family invite. **Metadata only, never health content.**

### The two contracts other work will build on

**Route guard.** `requireAdmin()` returns the actor or throws `notFound()`. It's called in `app/admin/layout.tsx`, so it covers every current *and future* route in the group by construction — a page that forgets it still can't render, because the layout never resolves. **Every server action re-authorises anyway**: an action is a POST endpoint like any other and does not inherit a layout's guard just because the user arrived from a rendered page.

**Audit write rule.** Every mutating action calls `recordAudit(db, { actorUserId, action, targetUserId?, meta? })` with an action from the pinned `ADMIN_ACTIONS` list. The order in each action is **authorise → validate → act → audit**, and the audit is neither optional nor conditional. `meta` carries context (an invite code, a deletion's per-table row counts) and structurally cannot carry health content, because nothing in the admin code can read any.

### Found and fixed: the 404 was leaking

`title: "Panel"` in the admin layout put **"Panel · Mi Bebé" in the `<title>` of the 404 a stranger receives** — Next resolves a segment's static `metadata` even when the layout below throws `notFound()`. That is exactly the rule §9 exists to enforce, broken by a metadata export rather than by the guard. Removed; the 404 is now visibly identical to any other, asserted in e2e.

Honest limit, recorded in DECISIONS.md: the RSC flight data still references an `app/admin/page-*.js` chunk, as it would for any Next route. Suppressing that needs middleware and is outside A7. The properties that matter — no data, and no different response for "exists but you're forbidden" — hold.

### The metadata-only rule is enforced against the source

A7's "done when" asks for a test that no route returns payload contents. Testing a response body would only cover routes somebody remembered to test. Instead the test strips comments from every file under `app/admin`, `components/admin` and `lib/server/admin.ts` and fails if any contains `payload`, `.note`, `symptoms:`, `noteEncrypted`, `mood` or `decryptNote` — covering every route in the group, **including the ones Phase I hasn't written yet**.

Two guards protect the guard: one asserts the scan actually found files, another that comment-stripping left real code behind. A scan that silently matches nothing passes forever.

Store *names* are deliberately allowed — the panel has to say "Registros de síntomas: 37", and naming the store is how it does that. Naming a field inside one is the line.

### Smaller decisions

- **The database role is the authority**, not the allowlist and not the session. `ADMIN_EMAILS` only *promotes*, at sign-in — that solves the chicken-and-egg problem (nobody can grant the first admin role through an admin-gated panel) without making an env var the live access control. Revoking is a database change effective on the next request; removing an address never silently strips access mid-incident.
- **Search is by exact email.** Substring search over a health app's user table is a browsing tool, and browsing isn't support — all three real tickets start with someone telling you their address.
- **Support deletion reuses A5's `deleteAccountData`**, so there's one answer to "what does deletion remove" and A5's `TABLE_DISPOSITION` coverage test protects this path too. The admin must type the account's email to enable the button.
- **Invite repair extends rather than re-issues** — the code is already in a WhatsApp message the person is looking at.
- `/admin` sits outside the `(app)` group: no AppHeader, no BottomNav. An admin screen wearing the app's navigation invites a founder to think they're seeing what a user sees.

Gates: `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` (251), `npm run build`, `npm run test:e2e` (21) all pass. No migration — `users.role` and `adminAudit` already existed from A1.

author: samiu349
body:
Self-audit finding, with the test written first.

**The gap.** `ngx_http_pgp_throttle_record()` runs from `verify_finalize()`, but the submit handler returns earlier on two paths — an unreadable body, and a body rejected by the clear-sign pre-check. Both tell the client "verification failed", so both are failed logins from the client's point of view, but neither was counted. A client could POST malformed submissions at the login endpoint forever without the adaptive per-IP throttle ever banning it — the cheapest automated failure pattern, and exactly what the throttle is for.

**The fix.** Both paths now go through `verify_finalize(NGX_DECLINED)`: the attempt is recorded, the client gets the same re-rendered challenge as before, and each emits a structured `pgp_auth_event` line (`unreadable_body` / `not_clear_signed`) so denials are visible to a log pipeline too.

**Tests.** The throttle had no test coverage at all. This adds four end-to-end cases, on their own nginx instance because the main suite deliberately fails logins from 127.0.0.1 and would ban itself mid-run:

- below the limit → not banned
- a valid login still succeeds while failures are pending
- a successful login clears the counter
- the configured number of failures → `429`

The last one fails without the fix and passes with it.

`SECURITY.md` now records that every failed submission counts, including pre-verification rejections, so the limit can be sized accordingly.

Suite 51/51 on Trixie; ASan/UBSan clean. No behaviour change for a successful login.

- add strict conformance identifiers, diagnostics, canonical boundaries, fail-closed applicability/assertion/case scaffolds, and valid-first property strategies
- add a provider-neutral private host-preflight binary with bounded process output, immutable tool/engine provenance, cache/export/persistence checks, guaranteed cleanup, and one isolated smoke lifecycle

The new inventory is intentionally still blocking: registering a capability or policy row does not claim that Rust implements it. Exact added, removed, moved, and fingerprint-changed rows are reported before a replacement scope digest can be accepted.

The separately identified infrastructure preflight observed a 32-vCPU, 64-GiB-class Linux/amd64 host with approximately 198 GB free workspace storage. It used the checked private binary and one pinned prebuilt `v1.0.0-beta.9` smoke engine, proved service reachability, then stopped and reaped it. It did not build the exact target, install the Rust SDK, execute a conformance case, or claim a capability.

The retained record contains only canonical redacted observations and is bound to the profile, plan, preflight binary, Docker client/daemon identity, smoke-engine digest, phase timings, and its own recomputed record digest.

author: mreiden
body:
## What

Follow-up to #111, catching the commit that missed its merge window: the coverage-job flake class. All seven Python tools share the same copy-pasted nginx teardown — `terminate() → wait(5) → kill() → wait(5)` — and every reap budget becomes 30 s.

## Why

#111's first CI run failed the coverage job with a `TimeoutExpired` from `tools/test_zstd_long_ldm.py`'s teardown, *after* every assertion in the phase had already passed. A gcov-instrumented nginx flushing `.gcda` profile data at exit on a loaded runner can outlive a 5-second reap — uninterruptible I/O shrugs off even the SIGKILL for a while — so the verdict was decided and the reap alone failed the tool. The identical-tree retry passed, confirming runner noise on an untouched code path: same disease #111 treats (tight infrastructure assumptions failing on the shared runner with the module verdict nowhere in sight), different organ.

Every teardown block sits in `finally` after the success return, so the larger budget costs nothing on healthy runs — a normal exit reaps in well under a second — and only spends time where 5 s used to fail spuriously.

## Verification

`py_compile` across all seven tools; the `test_encoding` harness self-checks; live runs of `test_encoding.py` and `test_zstd_long_ldm.py` (the tool that flaked) against a local ASAN-instrumented build.

### Motivation

- El cálculo de `residualMatching` se reconstruía íntegramente en cada hijo provocando trabajo repetido y consumo excesivo de ramas; la intención es reutilizar trabajo válido del padre mediante un certificado local y reducir la contabilidad pagada.
- El certificado debe ser inmutable/branch-local y permitir detectar qué aristas deben reevaluarse conservadoramente sin cambiar las reglas de validación (`materializeAnchoredOperation` / `canPlaceTask`).
- Mantener invariantes operativas: no alterar presupuesto, ordering, hard constraints ni `canPlaceTask`, y cumplir la contabilidad SPEC-09 (cada unidad de trabajo pagada queda registrada).

### Description

- Introduzco tipos internos `ResidualMatchingEdge`, `ResidualMatchingCertificate` y `ResidualMatchingResult` y modifico `residualMatching` para devolver un `ResidualMatchingResult` que incluye el certificado cuando procede. 
- Implemento derivación padre→hijo que elimina el `main` y la posición consumida, conserva aristas previamente inválidas, invalida conservadoramente aristas afectadas mediante la función pura `residualMatchingOperationsMayInteract`, y sólo reevalúa las aristas marcadas como afectadas usando la misma autoridad (`materializeAnchoredOperation` + deadlines). 
- Mantengo el matching padre cuando sea posible y ejecuto augmenting paths únicamente para los `tasks` unmatched resultantes; adiciono `consumeMatchingBranch` y contabilizo `residualMatchingInvocations`, `residualMatchingFullBuilds`, `residualMatchingIncrementalUpdates`, `residualMatchingEdgeCacheHits`, `residualMatchingEdgeCacheMisses`, `residualMatchingPositionChecks`, `residualMatchingAugmentTraversals`, `residualMatchingBranchesExplored`, `residualMatchingRepairs` y `residualMatchingRepairFailures` en la `evidence` compartida. 
- Añadí la opción de test `residualMatchingMode: "FULL_RECOMPUTE" | "INCREMENTAL"` (solo como oráculo de paridad), y pasé el certificado hijo-local al `search` para aislamiento byte-for-byte de padres/siblings; además se proyectan los nuevos contadores en `ExactItinerantPlanEvidence`. 
- Añadí pruebas focales `engine/planner-next/residualMatchingCertificate.spec.ts` que cubren paridad full-recompute, ausencia de falsas podas, invalidaciones por participant/coach/space/resource/dependency, cache-hits no relacionados, sibling-isolation, determinismo y contabilidad de ledger.

### Testing

- Typecheck y build: `npx tsc --noEmit` y `npm run build` pasaron sin errores y la compilación produjo artefactos.

author: lestherll
body:
Closes [LES-85](https://linear.app/lestherll/issue/LES-85/power-usage-and-energy-cost-dashboard). Completes the chain: #31 made the RAPL series exist, #32 made them durable, this makes them legible.

## Design: two rows, because honest and useful differ here

**Measured** carries only what RAPL actually reports — CPU package power, per-zone breakdown, CPU energy over range.

**Estimated** adds a `baseline_w` variable to approximate whole-system draw, and is where every currency figure lives.

That split is the entire design, not decoration. RAPL sees the CPU package and DRAM only — not the display panel, either disk, fans, chipset, WiFi, or the charger's AC/DC conversion loss. On this Inspiron 5770 that omitted set is *most* of the real draw: **~2.5 W measured against a likely 10–20 W at the wall.** A cost figure taken straight off RAPL would understate the bill several-fold.

So the assumption is an editable variable with a text panel stating it at the top, rather than a constant buried in a query. When a metering plug exists, repoint the Estimated panels at real wall power and delete the variable.

## Variables

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `datasource` | VictoriaMetrics | Prometheus only keeps 15d; cost panels span billing periods |
| `tariff` | `0.26` | £/kWh — a rough UK average, **not** your actual rate |
| `baseline_w` | `10` | Assumed non-CPU draw. The load-bearing assumption |

## Two correctness details, written into panel descriptions

Both are things I got wrong or nearly wrong while investigating, so they are recorded where a future editor will see them rather than in a commit message:

- **`psys` is deliberately excluded.** I initially assumed it was whole-SoC power that includes the package. Measured, it reports ~0.08 W against a ~2.5 W package — non-functional on this chip, as is common on OEM laptops. Including it would look like a whole-system reading and be off by ~30x.
- **`core`/`uncore`/`dram` are labelled "within package"** so nobody sums them into a double-counted total.

## Verification

Every expression run against VictoriaMetrics with variables substituted:

| Panel | Result |
| --- | --- |
| CPU package power | 2.17 W |
| Estimated total power | 12.17 W |
| Estimated cost / month | £2.30 |

The monthly figure checks out by hand: 12.17 W × 730 h × £0.26/kWh = £2.31. Grid programmatically checked for overlaps and gaps (none, rows 0–22 contiguous); JSON parses with unique panel ids; `kubectl kustomize infrastructure/` builds clean.

Not yet rendered in a live Grafana — that needs the merge, since Flux tracks `main`. Queries and layout are verified; visual confirmation is the post-merge step.

## Known limitation, by design

The monthly projection extrapolates average power across the selected range to 730 h, so a short or unrepresentative range gives a misleading number. The panel description says to select at least 24h. This is inherent to projecting from a window, not a bug to fix.

author: airwhale
body:
`NaturalMC` currently collapses two fundamentally different situations into the same `NaN` result:

| situation | current behavior | behavior after this PR |
|---|---|---|
| No reports exist for a treatment arm | `NaN` with the existing missing-arm warning | unchanged |
| Estimator fitting or prediction fails | silently converted to `NaN` | original exception is raised with run context, stopping the run |
| An interrupt occurs | swallowed and converted to `NaN` | propagates normally |

This prevents an estimator failure from masquerading as absent treatment data.

## Changes

- replace the bare exception handler with `except Exception`;
- preserve the original exception type and traceback for fitting and prediction failures;
- attach the estimator type, trial, outcome, data shape, and observed treatments to the exception;
- update the existing one-class IPW test to verify that its real fitting error propagates with outcome context.

Successful estimates and intentional missing-arm `NaN` results are unchanged. The PR does not add estimator-specific prevalidation.

## Validation

- `pytest -q tests/test_natural_mc.py tests/test_estimate_ate.py` (`20 passed`)
- `pytest -q --ignore=tests/sources/reddit` (`144 passed`)
- Ruff lint and formatting checks passed

The complete Windows test run cannot collect the existing Reddit tests because `contextualize.py` imports the Unix-only `resource` module.

Fixes #43

author: soramaru777
body:
## 作業サマリー

ISSUE #41 の修正。`register.ps1` / `unregister.ps1` のレジストリ操作にあった 3 つの不具合を、根本原因である「キーの扱い方」から直す。

### 根本原因

PowerShell のレジストリプロバイダでは、**既存キーへの `New-Item -Force` はキーを削除して再作成する**（サブキーも値も消える）。一方、親が存在しないパスへの `New-Item` は `-Force` が無いと失敗する。この 2 つの性質が同居しているため、`-Force` を素直に付けたコードが既存データを壊していた。

実測（使い捨てキーで確認、実行後に削除済み）:

| 検証 | 結果 |
|---|---|
| 既存キーへ `New-Item -Force` | before: subkeys=1, values=[(default),Extra] → after: **subkeys=0, values=[]** |
| 子キーへ `New-Item -Force` | 親の値は保持される（壊れるのは対象キー自身のみ） |
| 親が無いパスへ `New-Item`（`-Force` 無し） | `ArgumentException` で失敗 |
| `Remove-ItemProperty -Name '(default)'` | `PSArgumentException`、**値は残存** |
| `.NET DeleteValue('', $false)` | 既定値のみ削除、キーは残存。値が無くても例外なし |

### 修正した 3 つの不具合

| # | 不具合 | 原因 | 修正 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `.md` の OpenWithProgIds 登録が残らない | 手順 2 で追加した直後、手順 3 で親の `.md` を `New-Item -Force` していた | 手順 2・3 を 1 つの関数に統合し、この順序自体を消した |
| 2 | 他アプリの `.md` 関連付けを無言で破壊 | 同上。既定値も消えるため「既存値は上書きしない」ガードが常に空振りしていた | 共有キーは作り直さず、値を 1 つずつ操作する |
| 3 | `.md` の既定プログラムを解除できない | `Remove-ItemProperty -Name '(default)'` が例外になるのを握り潰し、成功メッセージだけ無条件表示 | .NET の `RegistryKey.DeleteValue` で削除。メッセージは削除できたときだけ |

### 設計の軸: キーを所有権で 2 分する

| 分類 | 対象 | 扱い |
|---|---|---|
| 共有キー | `.md` / `.markdown` / `OpenWithProgIds` | **作り直さない**。無ければ作るだけ（`Initialize-RegistryKey`）。値は 1 つずつ操作する |
| Hirake 名義のキー | `Hirake.md` / `hirake` | **作り直さない**（インプレース更新）。削除時は `shell\open\command` の実行ファイル名を確認してから |

どちらの分類でも「削除して作り直す」操作は行わない。途中で失敗すると元の設定が失われ、ロールバックできないため。

### 既定値の 3 状態

不具合 3 と往復の不一致の根にあったのが、既定値を 2 値でしか見ていなかったこと。`GetValueNames()` で 3 状態を区別する。

```
状態 A: 値が存在しない   → Hirake を設定する（解除時に削除すれば完全に元へ戻る）
状態 B: 空文字が入っている → 他アプリが明示的に書いた設定として尊重し、上書きしない
状態 C: 非空             → 上書きしない（従来どおり）
```

> 状態 B は現行からの挙動変更です。従来は `[string]::IsNullOrEmpty` で A と B を同一視して上書きしていましたが、解除側は「値を削除する」ことしかできないため、上書きすると B → A に変わって元へ戻せません。空文字は既定プログラムとして機能しないため、実害は「`.md` の既定が Hirake にならない」だけで、`OpenWithProgIds` には登録されるため「プログラムから開く」からは選べます。

### 変更内容

| ファイル | 変更 |
|---|---|
| `scripts/association-lib.ps1`（新規） | 両スクリプトが共用するレジストリ操作と、拡張子単位の登録・解除を集約 |
| `scripts/register.ps1` | 共通化、インプレース更新、所有権の事前確認、失敗時の終了コード |
| `scripts/unregister.ps1` | 共通化、既定値削除の .NET 化、空キーの掃除、条件付きメッセージ、中止パス |
| `tests/test-association-lib.ps1`（新規） | 回帰テスト（Pester 非依存、89 アサーション） |
| `README.md` | 他アプリの関連付けを変更しないこと、解除の契約、所有権判定の限界、失敗時の挙動 |

**拡張子を引数に取る設計にしたのが要点。** `Register-HirakeExtension -Extension '.md'` という形にしたことで、テストから使い捨て拡張子 `.zzmdtest` を渡して**本番と同一の関数**で「他アプリ共存」を検証できる。テスト用の再実装を作らずに済んでいる。

## レビューで検出し、修正した問題

Codex の敵対的レビューを 5 サイクル + 各サイクルでローカルレビュー。**High 12 / Medium 12 / Low 2** を検出。

| 重大度 | 指摘 | 対応 |
|---|---|---|
| High | `Hirake.md` / `hirake` キーを無条件に破壊していた | 作り直しをやめてインプレース更新へ。ユーザーが追加した verb も残る |
| High | 解除時に同名キーを無条件で丸ごと削除していた | `shell\open\command` の実行ファイル名を確認してから削除 |
| High | 部分一致（`*Hirake.exe*`）は迂回可能だった | コマンドラインから先頭の実行ファイル名を切り出して完全一致で比較 |
| High | 引用符の直後に非空白が続くと誤判定（`"…\Hirake.exe".bak`） | 閉じ引用符の直後が末尾か空白でなければ判定不能として扱う |
| High | 所有権の確認が拡張子の処理より後だった | 先に全ターゲットを確認し、1 つでも駄目ならレジストリを変更せず中止 |
| High | `-ExePath` に別名の exe を渡すと登録できるが解除不能になった | 実行ファイル名が `Hirake.exe` でなければレジストリを触らず中止 |
| High | register が同名キーを他アプリから奪い取り得た | register 側も同じ確認を最初に行う |
| High | `OpenWithProgIds` の既存値を無条件に上書きしていた | 既に正しい形なら書き込まない（再実行が完全な no-op に） |
| Medium | 空判定と削除の間の競合 | `Remove-Item -Recurse` をやめ、サブキーがあると失敗する `DeleteSubKey` へ |
| Medium | 失敗しても「完了」と表示して成功終了していた | 失敗件数を数えて警告し、終了コード 1 |
| Medium | 解除の途中失敗後も ProgId を消してダングリング参照を作っていた | 拡張子の解除に失敗したら ProgId とプロトコルの削除を見送る |
| Medium | `shell\open\command` が無いキーの扱いが登録側・解除側で同じだった | `Unknown` 状態を追加。登録側は修復のため許可、解除側は削除せず中止 |
| Medium | ドキュメントが実際の挙動と食い違っていた | 解除の契約、部分適用、空キーの掃除、所有権判定の限界を明記 |
| Low | 実際には上書きしているのに「既に登録されています」と表示 | 書き込んだときだけ「登録しました」と表示 |
| Low | 空キー掃除の競合に対して文書表現が強すぎた | 「通常の逐次実行では変更しません」に緩和し、限界をコメントに明記 |

### 採用しなかった指摘（判断の記録）

- **所有者 GUID マーカーの導入** — HKCU に書ける主体はマーカーも同じように書けるためセキュリティ境界にならず、区別できるのは善意の名前衝突だけになる。その衝突には「別アプリが ProgId `Hirake.md` またはスキーム `hirake` を使う」かつ「実行ファイル名も `Hirake.exe`」という二重の偶然が必要。既存の登録にはマーカーが無いため互換分岐も要る。実行ファイル名の確認を多層防御として残し、**限界を README に明記**する形にした
- **値スナップショットによるロールバック** — 両スクリプトは冪等で再実行すれば回復できる。失敗時に一部の変更が適用済みになり得ることを README とヘッダに明記した
- **`.md` の既定値が元から `Hirake.md` でも解除する** — unregister の目的は Hirake の関連付けを解除することなので、誰が設定したかに関わらず外すのが正しい。契約としてドキュメントに明記した

## 補足事項（残した指摘）

- **#43** — `register.ps1` / `unregister.ps1` の**制御フロー**を通す統合テストが無い（今回のテストは関数単体のため、呼ぶ順序の誤りを検出できない）。最終サイクルで実際にこのクラスの不具合が 1 件見つかったため（`Unknown` の中止判定が拡張子処理より後だった。本 PR で修正済み）、スクリプト本体を注入可能な関数へ切り出す対応を別 ISSUE にした

## 検証

### 単体（`tests/test-association-lib.ps1`、リポジトリに追加）

使い捨てキー `ZZHirakeTest` と使い捨て拡張子 `.zzmdtest` のみを使用（実際の関連付けには未接触、実行後に削除）。**89 アサーション全件成功**。

- レジストリ層のプリミティブ（既存キーを壊さない・中間キー作成・既定値の 3 状態・既定値の削除・空キーの掃除）
- 実行ファイル名の抽出 7 ケース、`NotOwned` 7 ケース、`Owned` 2 ケース、`Unknown`
- 他アプリ共存での往復（既定 ProgId・他アプリの OpenWithProgIds エントリ・`ShellNew` サブキーがすべて保持され、解除後に**実行前と完全一致**）
- 何も無い状態からの往復（キーごと消えて実行前と一致）、空文字の既定値、未登録での解除、引数の書式検証

### 実キーでの往復（成功条件の確認）

`reg export` で退避したうえで実施し、検証後は登録済み状態へ復帰させています。

| 成功条件 | 結果 |
|---|---|
| `.md` と `.markdown` の**両方**の OpenWithProgIds に `Hirake.md` が存在する | ✅（従来は `.md` 側が消えていた） |
| 他アプリの既定 ProgId / OpenWithProgIds エントリが保持される | ✅ |
| register → unregister の往復で各キーが実行前の状態に戻る | ✅ 完全一致 |
| 何も登録されていない状態で unregister しても誤った成功メッセージを出さない | ✅ 「削除しました」0 件 |

その他: 別名 exe を `-ExePath` に渡すとレジストリを触らず終了コード 1、4 ファイルとも PowerShell パーサで構文エラー 0。

## ユーザーが手動でやること

1. `.\tests\test-association-lib.ps1` を実行して全件成功を確認
2. `.\scripts\register.ps1` → `.md` をダブルクリックして Hirake で開くこと、`hirake://open?path=…` のリンクが動くことを確認
3. `.\scripts\unregister.ps1` → 関連付けが外れること、メッセージが実際に削除された項目だけであることを確認
4. もう一度 `.\scripts\unregister.ps1` → 「削除しました」が 1 行も出ないことを確認
5. 使い続ける場合は `.\scripts\register.ps1` で再登録

> 現在このマシンのレジストリは、検証の結果として**登録済み**の状態です。`.md` の OpenWithProgIds が欠けていた不具合 1 の状態も解消されています。

Closes #41

author: atomantic
body:
## Summary

Open PR #136 already covers most of #135 — it rewrote the `--issues` bullet and the `--scan-only` gate in `better.md`, `better-swift.md`, `depfree.md`, `lib/plan-issue-mode.md`, and `lib/review-config-defaults.md`. This is the disjoint remainder: the two places that still describe `--issues` as if it were a run mode, on files #136 does not touch (no overlap, no conflict).

- **`commands/do/simplify.md`** — the pass-through flag list lumped `--issues`/`--issues-label` in with the flags that *stop* the run (`--scan-only`, `--no-merge`), which is precisely the misreading #135 was filed about; the issue's Context section names a `/do:simplify --issues` run as where it surfaced. `--issues` now gets its own bullet stating that it selects where deferred findings are recorded, that the run still remediates / PRs / merges, and that `--scan-only --issues` files **every** surviving finding as the run's entire output.
- **`commands/do/config.md`** — both places describing the saved `issues` default (the prose paragraph and the key reference) now note that issue mode changes only where findings are recorded, never whether the run remediates. This is the config key #135 identifies as load-bearing: someone with `{"defaults": {"issues": true}}` needs to know it does not silently disable fixes.

`review.md` and `rpr.md` are deliberately untouched — both already scope their `--issues` bullet to *deferred* findings, the same reasoning #136 gave for leaving `review.md` alone. The `--triage` alias floated in #135 is also out, matching #136's decision that one discoverable spelling (`--scan-only --issues`) beats two.

`Refs`, not `Closes`, since #136 carries the `Closes #135` trailer and lands the larger half.

## Remaining

Nothing beyond what #136 already ships. Once both merge, #135's acceptance criteria are covered except the optional `--triage` alias, which both PRs explicitly declined.

## Test plan

Docs-only; no executable behaviour changes.

- [x] `npm test` — 187/187 pass

- [x] No file overlap with PR #136 (`better.md`, `better-swift.md`, `depfree.md`, `lib/plan-issue-mode.md`, `lib/review-config-defaults.md`)

author: malk13r
body:
## Summary

- add an optional per-platform `gateway_restart_channel` for gateway startup and shutdown broadcasts
- preserve the existing home-channel fallback and `gateway_restart_notification` suppression flag
- route both native and Relay-fronted lifecycle targets with thread and owner provenance intact
- warn and fall back safely when the hand-authored lifecycle target is malformed

Closes #76780.

## Why

Gateway lifecycle notices currently share the platform home channel with ordinary conversation and scheduled delivery. Operators must either accept restart noise in that channel or disable lifecycle visibility entirely.

This change separates those concerns without changing normal home-channel routing:

```yaml
gateway:
  platforms:
    slack:
      gateway_restart_channel:
        platform: slack
        chat_id: "C0123456789"
        name: system-messages
```

When omitted, behaviour remains unchanged and lifecycle notices use `home_channel`.

Active-session interruption messages deliberately remain in the affected conversation; only platform-level startup/shutdown broadcasts use the lifecycle destination.

## Compatibility and failure behaviour

- no new environment variable
- supports top-level platform blocks, `platforms.*`, and `gateway.platforms.*`
- preserves documented config precedence
- malformed lifecycle channel mappings log a warning and fall back to the home channel without dropping the platform config or preventing gateway startup
- Relay-fronted targets retain `user_id` and `scope_id` provenance

## Verification

- focused canonical suite: **91 passed, 2 skipped**
- full gateway suite: **5,271 passed, 4 failed, 33 skipped**
- the same 4 failures reproduce on pristine `origin/main`:
  - macOS abstract systemd socket test

- `ruff check`: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed
- independent exact-commit review of `0b4b107a7deaef9d49f91eec1d6ae0ed322f967f`: **PASS**, no findings

This uses a structured `HomeChannel` target rather than a bare chat ID, addressing the Relay provenance and malformed-config gaps previously identified on #76787.

author: geoffe-ga
body:
## Summary

- **Closes the disarm.** `check_privacy_compliance` took its ceiling from exactly one source — the medium contract's `default_privacy_tier` — and `_resolve_contract_path` prefers a **vault-deployed** contract at `<vault>/00-Creek-Meta/Skills/mediums/<medium>.MEDIUM.md`. One edited YAML line inside the vault therefore disarmed a HARD privacy leak gate. A new `author.max_reproduced_tier` config key (default `open`) is folded in, and the effective ceiling is now the **more restrictive** of the two, so a contract can only ever *narrow* the gate.
- **Both surfaces, one read.** The fold happens inside `check_privacy_compliance`, using the `vault` argument it already receives. No signature changes anywhere — `ReflectionNode.review`, the `Reflector` protocol, `Conductor`, `build_default_conductor`, `run_author`, `creek/cli.py` and `creek_mcp/tools/author.py` are all untouched — so the `creek author` CLI and the MCP `creek.author` verb reach the same read by construction, not by two pieces of plumbing that can drift apart.
- **The finding now names the effective ceiling and who set it**, so an operator knows which file to edit: `Cited fragment 'frag-int' is 'intimate' (above the effective 'open' ceiling, set by author.max_reproduced_tier) yet its protected text appears in the draft.`

### The issue understated this in two ways (both reproduced by execution, both now covered)

1. **It can be a total no-op, not a partial one.** The body says "Only `unclassified` (the fail-closed rank 3) would still be caught." That holds only for `default_privacy_tier: intimate`. A one-word edit to `default_privacy_tier: unclassified` — a valid tier `MediumContract` accepts from frontmatter, rank 3 — makes `rank > ceiling` false for **every** tier, including the UNCLASSIFIED rank the body says survives. Measured at `55e0611`, fragment tier x contract ceiling -> findings:

   | frag \ ceiling | open | personal | intimate | unclassified |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | personal     | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
   | intimate     | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
   | unclassified | 1 | 1 | 1 | **0** |
   | unvouched    | 1 | 1 | 1 | **0** |

   Post-fix at default config, every row above `open` reads `1 1 1 1`.

2. **Both surfaces leaked.** Measured on a vault with the deployed `research` contract tampered to `intimate`: `creek author` went from `exit 1` / withheld to `exit 0` with the intimate sentence on stdout; `author_tool(..., privacy_tier_ceiling=ALL)` went from `status: refused` to `status: ok` with the protected sentence in the serialized envelope. #1353's refusal and #1310's CLI withholding were both bypassed by the same YAML line. Both are now asserted independently, on their own surfaces.

## What this does NOT do — please read before approving

- **It creates no trust boundary.** `creek_config.yaml` lives at `<vault>/00-Creek-Meta/creek_config.yaml` — **inside the vault**, editable by exactly the same actor who can edit the medium contract. This makes widening deliberate, single-sourced and self-evidently security-relevant. It does not make it impossible. The docs say this in those words; nothing in this PR claims otherwise.
- **It is worse in one respect, knowingly.** `creek skills sync`'s drift guard covers `00-Creek-Meta/Skills/` only, so moving the widening lever into `creek_config.yaml` takes it **out of the drift-detection surface entirely**. And `creek skills sync` is not a mitigation for this issue at all: since #1306 / PR #1396 it *refuses* on medium drift and **leaves** a tampered `default_privacy_tier` in place indefinitely (measured at HEAD).
- **`MediumContract.default_privacy_tier` becomes inert at default config.** `open` is rank 0 — already the strictest ceiling — and all six shipped templates declare it. So with `max_reproduced_tier: open` and a `min` fold, the contract narrows nothing on any shipped medium. That is a deliberate, documented outcome, not a field left dead by accident: raise the key to `intimate` and a contract declaring `personal` gates at `personal`, pinned by `test_a_stricter_contract_still_governs_when_the_config_is_raised`.
- **The escape hatch is the config key and only the config key.** A medium that may legitimately reproduce above-`open` text is reachable by an operator editing `creek_config.yaml`, never by a skill file that deploys by default.

## Decisions and departures from the issue text

- **Key name is `author.max_reproduced_tier`, not `privacy_tier_floor`.** "floor: open" reads backwards — `open` is the *least private* tier and the *strictest* ceiling. `max_reproduced_tier: open` says what the value means, and it keeps the **reproduction** axis visibly distinct from the **admission** axis already owned by `--include-tier` and the MCP `privacy_tier_ceiling`.
- **One acceptance criterion is factually wrong and was satisfied in spirit, not to the letter.** The AC asking for `tests/test_vault_structure.py` to be updated misreads that file: it contains **zero** `creek_config` references, and its `default_privacy_tier:` at line 320 belongs to `test_other_authors_manifest_template_shape`, asserting on the `11-Other-Authors/_author.md` manifest — that is `AuthorProfile`, a *different model with a same-named field*. The AC's intent (prove `creek init` seeds the key) is served by `tests/test_config.py::TestAuthorMaxReproducedTier::test_generate_default_config_seeds_the_key`. That file was deliberately not edited to make a checkbox true.
- **`creek/config.py` cannot import `creek.models` at module level, at any position.** Proven by executing the edit: `config -> models ->` the bottom-of-file `# noqa: E402` import at `creek/models.py:1153` `-> creek.classify.weighted -> ... -> creek/generate/ai_style/model.py:20 -> from creek.config import AIStyleCategory`, which lands in a partially-initialised `creek.config`. (`import creek.cli` happens to survive because it imports other modules first; `import creek.config` on its own does not.) A `TYPE_CHECKING` import does not help either — the file has no `from __future__ import annotations`, and a Pydantic field's *default value* needs a real object at class-creation time. Hence `PrivacyTierName = Literal["open","personal","intimate","unclassified"]` plus a **function-local** import in the `mode="before"` validator. The mirror is pinned equal to the enum by `test_the_literal_mirrors_every_privacy_tier`, so a fifth tier added to `PrivacyTier` fails a test rather than silently rejecting an operator's value.
- **A typo'd config key fails closed.** `AuthorConfig` inherits pydantic's `extra="ignore"`, so `author.max_reproduce_tier: intimate` is dropped and the field keeps its `open` default — the strictest ceiling. Verified: the ignored-key path cannot widen the gate.

## Filed separately, deliberately not folded in

- #1464 (P2) — `assert_contract_conformant` has no production caller, so `_preflight_medium_contract`'s docstring overstates what actually validates.
- #1465 (P1) — `run_author` reads a bare `AuthorConfig()` (`conductor.py:514`), so the MCP verb ignores the vault's `author.max_author_rounds`. This design deliberately loads no `CreekConfig` in `run_author`, so it stays open on its own terms.

## Test plan

Everything below was run by me in the worktree, not reported by a subagent.

- **Gate 1 RED, proved:** 55 new/affected cases failed at `55e0611` for the right reason — `assert [] == [('privacy_compliance', 'HIGH')]`, not an ImportError. The headline RED is `tests/test_reflection.py::test_a_contract_alone_cannot_widen_the_privacy_gate`.
- **`./scripts/check-all.sh` -> exit 0.** 12/12 checks. Aggregate coverage 94.65%, per-file gate green on every touched file. Ruff re-verified with `--no-cache` (lint and format): clean. `check_privacy_compliance` complexity **improved** from B(6) to A(5) — extracting the fold removed a branch. Per the operator's standing instruction for this worktree, `pre-commit run --all-files` was **not** run; `./scripts/check-all.sh` (which pre-commit's hooks mirror) is the ga

author: seanmck
body:
Report the timezone rule in `doctor`

Two environments running this code can disagree about what "11:45 local" means, and
nothing will notice. The timetable is stored as local clock times and converted to
UTC instants, so a stale tz database shifts every sailing window by an hour without
raising anything.

That is not hypothetical here. The production container is on BC's permanent-DST
rule -- one transition in 2026, none in 2027, settling at UTC-07:00 labelled MST --
while this laptop still expects clocks to change twice a year. They agree about today
and disagree about every date after 2026-11-01. Neither is detectably wrong from the
inside; they are just different, and nothing in the app compares them.

So `doctor` now prints a fingerprint:

  info  timezone America/Vancouver: now UTC-07:00 (PDT), next change 2026-11-01,
        in 12 months UTC-07:00 (PDT)

Informational, not pass/fail. A tz database cannot be shown wrong by the code
running on top of it; it can only be shown different from somewhere else, and a
line that can be eyeballed across two machines is the cheapest way to see that.

Tests use synthetic zones rather than real ones. Asserting that America/Vancouver
changes on a particular date would pass or fail depending on which tz database the
machine ships -- pinning a test to the exact problem being diagnosed.

Nothing renders a timezone abbreviation to users, so the MST label never surfaces.
Pinning tzdata as a dependency would not help either: zoneinfo prefers the system
database over the pip package, so the real fix is the container base image and the
developer's own machine. This just makes the mismatch visible.

author: m1zuke
body:
## What

The dashboard capture carries the slotted inner ways in `passiveSlots`. The gear
import now reads them and writes the four mind-method slots, alongside the gear
it already imported.

## The id table

`src/data/innerWays/passiveIds.ts` maps a dashboard passive id to an inner-way
id, typed against `InnerWayId` so a typo is a build error rather than a silently
unmapped row:

```ts
export const PASSIVE_ID_TO_INNER_WAY: Readonly<Record<string, InnerWayId>> = {
  "81": "moraleChant",
  "151": "wolfchasersArt",
  "153": "insightfulStrike",
  "154": "swordHorizon",
}
```

## Rules it holds to

- **Tier** — kept as reported when the inner way's ladder models it, otherwise
  narrowed to the highest modelled tier at or below it, never rounded up into a
  stronger build. Flagged as assumed in the preview when it moved.
- **Slot 0 stays the class's own inner way** (`syncClassPermanent`'s lock): it
  takes the capture's entry for that inner way when there is one and keeps the
  current slot otherwise.
- **An inner way the active class cannot slot is refused**, the same way an
  affix choice illegal for a slot is.
- **Nothing resolving writes nothing** — an import against ids the table does
  not carry leaves the slots the user set by hand alone.
- **A stale bookmarklet says so.** A capture that lists `passiveSlots` under
  `unrecognizedPayloadKeys` was made by a bookmarklet too old to carry it, and
  the dialog asks for a re-drag instead of silently importing no inner ways.

## UI

The inner ways sit at the top of the preview as a four-column card grid,
mirroring the graduation dialog's summary cards (#44) — tier as the label, name
as the value, with the reason underneath for anything left out:

```
TIER 6              TIER 5              TIER 4              NO TIER
Sword Horizon       Wolfchaser's Art    #3019999            #3011007
                                        no mapping yet…     no mapping yet…
```

Those style rules are local for now; #44 extracts the shared gear-preview
stylesheet they belong in, so they fold in once it merges.

## Payload shape

The passive-slot entry shape is not yet confirmed against a live account, so the
reader accepts a bare id, an `[id, tier]` tuple and a record (`id`/`passiveId`/
`no` + `tier`/`level`/`lv`/…), drops empty slots, and keeps every entry verbatim
in `raw` — which the diagnostics dump, so the true shape can be pinned down and
the speculative branches dropped.

## Migration

**No migration needed**: `MindMethodSlot` and `Inputs.mindMethods` are unchanged
in shape and content — the import writes the same
`{ id, name, stacks: "tier N" }` the Mind Methods panel does, so no saved
profile can be stale or illegal under this change.

## Verification

`tsc -b`, eslint, prettier, `vite build` and the full suite pass — 107 files /
1092 tests, 24 of them new in `tests/ui/gearImportInnerWays.test.ts`.

author: klasolsson81
body:
**This unblocks every open PR in the repo, including #1330 and #1331.** It is not related to their scope — it was found while shepherding them to green.

## What broke

`GHSA-q939-rpr3-3284` was published **2026-08-12 15:19 UTC** — HIGH, *ScpClient recursive download allows arbitrary file write via server-controlled SCP filenames*. It covers `SSH.NET <= 2025.1.0`, which `Testcontainers 4.13.0` declares as its floor in **every** TFM group of its nuspec (measured).

`NuGetAudit` raises `NU1903`, `TreatWarningsAsErrors` turns it into an error, and `dotnet restore Jobbliggaren.sln` then fails on the three Testcontainers-using test projects. That takes `backend` and `coverage` down, and with them the `ci` aggregate, on every open PR; `audit (observe-only)` fails with them on some (measured FAILURE on #1331).

Measured on #1330, whose diff touches no project file at all:

```
tests/Jobbliggaren.QA.Corpus/…csproj : error NU1903: Warning As Error: Package 'SSH.NET'
2025.1.0 has a known high severity vulnerability, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q939-rpr3-3284
```

`backend (.NET 10)` → step **Restore**; same in `coverage` and `audit`; `ci` → *Verify all jobs passed*.

## The fix

Pinned to **2026.0.0**, the first patched version, using the transitive-CVE-pin pattern `Directory.Packages.props` already carries four times (OpenTelemetry ×2, Scriban.Signed, Microsoft.OpenApi). We do not reference SSH.NET directly and never call `ScpClient`; the pin takes effect only through `CentralPackageTransitivePinningEnabled`.

**This is a repair, not a suppression.** Nothing added to `NoWarn`, nothing to an ignore list, `--audit-level` untouched — so the `security-auditor` trigger for the suppression surface (ADR 0065 Amendment 2026-07-28 Beslut 4) does not arise. Flagging it explicitly because that trigger is easy to reach by accident on a change that looks like this one.

There is no Testcontainers bump to take instead: 4.13.0 is the latest. 2026.0.0 sits above the declared floor → upward unification, no NU1605 downgrade, and it ships a `net10.0` group.

## Verified locally

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `dotnet restore Jobbliggaren.sln` | clean, no NU1903 (12 `Restored` lines; up-to-date projects are not logged, so this is not a project count) |
| `project.assets.json` resolved version | `SSH.NET/2026.0.0`; `grep -c "SSH.NET/2025.1.0"` → **0** |
| `dotnet build Jobbliggaren.sln -warnaserror` | **0 warnings, 0 errors** |
| Advisory metadata | `gh api advisories/GHSA-q939-rpr3-3284` → vulnerable `<= 2025.1.0`, first patched `2026.0.0`, published 2026-08-12 |

## Agent reports

**`code-reviewer` — ✓ Approved, 0 Blocker / 0 Major, 1 Minor.** It re-measured all ten factual claims in the comment against the sources and the repo — every one held, including that all five TFM groups in the Testcontainers nuspec declare the vulnerable floor, that `grep -rn "Renci|ScpClient|SshClient|SftpClient" src tests perf` returns **0 hits**, and that 4.13.0 is the newest Testcontainers with no prerelease after it. It also verified the graph where it resolves rather than where it is declared: `SSH.NET/2026.0.0` in the three consuming projects, zero occurrences of `2025.1.0` repo-wide. And it confirmed the suites actually ran — `backend` and `coverage` both report `total: 22673`, `failed: 0`, which is the real risk in a pin of this shape: forcing SSH.NET up under Testcontainers could have broken the runtime binding, and did not.

It confirmed the repair-vs-suppression judgement independently: the repo has exactly two suppression surfaces (`tests/Directory.Build.props:10` `CA1707`, and `web/…/package.json:68` `ignoreGhsas`) and **this diff touches neither**. `security-auditor` is therefore not triggered for this PR. §12's "non-BUILD.md libraries" does not fire either: measured 3-of-4 precedent that a transitive CVE pin is not a library add and needs no BUILD.md §3.1 row.

author: rishabh7g
body:
## The bug

`CopyButton` wrote to the clipboard with no `.catch`:

```ts
void navigator.clipboard.writeText(code).then(() => { … });
```

A refused write therefore rejected unhandled — the only console output the entire live QA pass produced:

```
pageerror: Failed to execute 'writeText' on 'Clipboard': Write permission denied.
```

and the button stayed on `COPY`, so nothing told the learner the code was not copied. The `if (!navigator.clipboard) return` branch was the same silence for a browser that does not expose the API at all.

## The fix

The write goes through one small function that cannot reject:

```ts
export async function copyStatusOf(
  code: string,
  clipboard: Pick<Clipboard, 'writeText'> | undefined = globalThis.navigator?.clipboard,
): Promise<CopyStatus>
```

A rejected promise, a **synchronous** throw and a missing clipboard API all resolve to `'failed'` — one outcome the UI can show. On failure:

- the button reads **`COPY FAILED`**;
- a note under the block says what to do instead — *This browser blocked the clipboard. Select the code and copy it by hand — or type it out, which is what these examples are for anyway.*

Both share the existing 1.5 s timer, so the button always returns to offering the copy. The note is a `role="status"` live region, matching the transient-state pattern of the Settings notice (#15-era) and the stalled-progress screen (#35). No new dependency.

The happy path is unchanged: `COPIED` for ~1.5 s, code written verbatim.

## Changed

- `src/ModuleView.tsx` — `copyStatusOf` / `copyLabelOf` exported; `CopyButton` holds a 3-state status instead of a boolean; `aria-label` follows the status so the failure is not hidden behind a static name.
- `src/module.css` — `.mod-copy--failed` (slightly narrower type so the longer label still clears the code block's reserved 96px right gutter — no overlap on mobile) and `.mod-copy-note`.
- `src/ModuleView.test.tsx` — 3 new cases.
- `docs/ENGINEERING.md` §7 — the copy button's failure contract.

## Tests

`npx vitest run src/ModuleView.test.tsx` — 12 cases. Red before (`copyStatusOf` / `copyLabelOf` did not exist; the old handler had no failure path at all), green after:

- **a refused write never rejects** — rejected promise, synchronous throw and `undefined` clipboard all resolve to `'failed'`
- **granted write** — resolves to `'copied'` and `writeText` received the example's code verbatim
- **labels** — `idle → COPY`, `copied → COPIED`, `failed → COPY FAILED`

Scoped run also over `src/ExerciseView.test.tsx` and `src/App.test.tsx` (34 passing). CI gates locally: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint:content`, `npm run build` all pass.

**Honest limit on live verification:** the repo's headless probe cannot revoke `clipboard-write` on an already-launched context, so the refused-permission path is verified by unit test and by reading the code, not by a live click. What the live run does confirm is that the Module screen still renders, the buttons still read `COPY`, and the page is console-clean.

Closes #44
