author: turlang
hughgrigg
body: A post can point at the part of its snippet the image is about. This is the last of the ideas that came out of looking at how other snippet tools are used: theirs is a rectangle you drag onto a canvas with a mouse, and this is the frontmatter equivalent. ```yaml meta_img_props: template: code language: javascript mark: "'QUERY'" code: | fetch('/search', { method: 'QUERY' }) ``` A string is text, boxed where it first appears. An object names the place instead, for when the same text appears twice or the thing worth marking is a whole line: ```yaml mark: - text: "'QUERY'" - line: 5 # a band across the line - { line: 2, column: 11, length: 7 } - { text: JSON, color: "#facc15" } ``` ## Decisions worth knowing **Text is the form to reach for and coordinates are the escape hatch.** Frontmatter is hand-written, and naming the text survives an edit above the line it sits on, which a line number does not. Coordinates are there because the same text can appear twice, and because a whole line has no text to name. **Marks are located in the snippet as drawn**, after fitting and clipping, rather than in what the post wrote. A mark on a line the fitting dropped has nowhere to go, and finding it in the original snippet would only mean drawing a box where that line used to be. That is why a mark that cannot be placed goes to `onWarning`: an image cannot show that it is missing one, so nothing else would ever say the post asked for it. **A bare line is a band, columns are a box.** Filled against stroked, which is the difference between highlighting something and pointing at it. Both are drawn under the code, so a band sits behind the glyphs rather than washing over them. **There is no `code.markColor`.** `Required` needs a concrete default and the palette is not available where those are declared, so the colour is `colors.brandWarm`, with a per-mark `color` for anything else. That is the same tie to the palette the terminal prompt has, and it is worth knowing before adding any colour to `config.code`. ## Verification `pnpm check` passes, with seven tests covering both forms, the list, the per-mark colour, and each of the three ways a mark can fail to be placed. A scratch site was built through the CLI: the mark rendered, the second run skipped, changing the mark re-rendered, and a mark naming text that is not there warned with the post's path in front of it.

author: robertinoc
body:
Closes both export items from the backlog. They're the same problem seen from two sides, so they're one change.

## The problem

A playlist imported from local audio files only ever knew a **filename** — or a folder-relative path at best. The browser never exposes the absolute one. So `toTraktor` has to synthesise a placeholder volume (`VOLUME="EnergyCurve"`), and Traktor opens the playlist with **every entry greyed out as missing**.

Nothing warned about this. And a warning after the click is worthless: the file is already in the downloads folder.

## What changed

**M3U8 is now the default for file-sourced playlists** (was CSV). It's the one format that can still resolve those paths — saved next to the music, it references it relatively. So for these playlists the default isn't a memory of how the playlist arrived, it's advice about what works, and the badge reads **"recommended"** instead of "default".

**The menu explains it before you choose.** A caution block above the DJ-software group, in the user's terms rather than ours:

> ⚠️ **Rekordbox and Traktor won't find these tracks**
> This playlist came from files on your computer, so we only know their names — not where they live. Those two formats will open with every track missing. Use M3U8 and save it in the same folder as your music.

**The affected rows are marked** with an amber triangle and a dimmed label. They stay selectable on purpose — someone may only want the metadata — they just can't read as an equal choice next to the one that works.

## Note on the implementation

`nativeExportWillMissTracks(importSource, format)` is a named predicate rather than an inline `importSource === "files" && …`, so the rule lives in one place next to the explanation of *why*, and is covered by tests. Including the case that matters for not over-warning: a Rekordbox or Traktor **import** is unaffected, because those carry real absolute locations.

## One thing I got wrong first

The first pass put the whole explanation in a per-row badge ("TRACKS WILL BE MISSING"). Rendered, it wrapped every label onto two or three lines and looked broken. The block above already carries the explanation, so the row only needs to mark which formats are hit — the long text became the hover/aria label and the menu got wider. Verified in a browser afterwards: all six rows single-line at 36px, marker on exactly Rekordbox and Traktor.

## Verification

`npm test` → **422 passing**, 3 new cases in `tests/export.test.ts` · `tsc --noEmit` clean · `lint` clean · rendered and measured in a browser with a file-sourced playlist.

EN + ES copy both added.

author: chemaclass
body:
## 🤔 Background

Related #1059 · fifth of the [#1062](https://github.com/TypedDevs/bashunit/issues/1062) order

`report_lcov` walked every line of every tracked file in Bash, calling the classifier per line — the exact shape `perf-fork-budget.md` records as losing to a single awk fork.

## 💡 Changes

- The rules now exist twice **on purpose**: `is_executable_line` stays the reference, `rules_awk.sh` holds the same rules as awk source for whole-file scans. The DA/LF/LH block is one awk pass that also applies the #722 continuation propagation.

  | input | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | 40 files × 752 lines | 8520 ms | **6632 ms** |
  | 40 files × 156 lines | 2108 ms | **1803 ms** |

- Byte-identical LCOV against main for `src/util`, `src/assert`, `src/coverage`, `src/runner`, on both engines, same `LF` under BusyBox awk.
- `classifier_differential_test.sh` compares the two implementations line by line over **all 460** `git ls-files '*.sh'`, and passes under BusyBox awk (verified in Alpine).

Two things worth reviewing closely, both caught here rather than in CI:
- The **mutation test** now removes one rule and leaves a valid program. The first version redefined the whole function, which awk rejects — so it was passing on an awk *error*, not on a disagreement.
- The two-file awk guard is `FILENAME`, not `FNR == NR`: with no recorded hits the first file is empty, and `FNR == NR` then swallows source line 1.

author: antomicblitz
body:
## Summary

Closes #189.

Slice 12 (PR #186) carried four engine-neutral MDSpec fields on the spec but explicitly deferred them on the OpenMMConfig / runner side: `equilibration_ps`, `pme`, `minimization_max_iterations`, `constraints`. The runner hardcoded values that happened to match the canonical ACTIVIN_E_PRODUCTION_PROFILE (100/100/200 ps, PME=True, 50k-iter cap, HBonds), so the deferral was silent.

This PR wires them end-to-end.

## What's in the change

### `OpenMMConfig` (4 new fields)
- `equilibration_ps: tuple[float, float, float]` — 3-stage NVT / NPT-restrained / NPT-free durations
- `pme: bool` — nonbonded method selector
- `minimization_max_iterations: int` — steepest-descent cap
- `constraints: str` — bond constraint algorithm (`None` / `HBonds` / `AllBonds` / `HAngles`)

Defaults match the runner's legacy hardcodes (100/100/200 ps, PME=True, 1k-iter cap, HBonds) so callers that don't go through `MDSpec` / `from_md_spec` keep working unchanged.

### `OpenMMConfig.from_md_spec` projects all 4
`spec.equilibration` (a tuple of stage dicts in the canonical wire format) is reduced to the 3-tuple via a private `_extract_equilibration_ps` helper that **raises** if the spec carries a non-3-stage equilibration. The runner is hardcoded to 3 stages; a future profile change requires runner updates.

### `OpenMMRunner._run_equilibration` reads from config
- Stage 1 / 2 durations come from `config.equilibration_ps[0]` / `[1]`.
- Stage 3 splits `equilibration_ps[2]` into ramp (5 k-values × 20 ps each = 100 ps) + unrestrained remainder; logs a warning if the configured `npt_free` is shorter than the ramp.
- `simulation.minimizeEnergy(maxIterations=...)` reads `config.minimization_max_iterations`.

### `system_builder._create_system` reads from config
- `nonbondedMethod` = `app.PME` if `config.pme` else `app.Cutoff`
- `constraints` mapped via `getattr(app, config.constraints)`; raises `ValueError` on unknown

### Wire-format round-trip
`OpenMMConfig.to_dict` includes the 4 fields under the `simulation` block; `from_json` parses them back. Legacy `system_config.json` files written before this PR default to the legacy values.

## Test coverage

8 new tests in `TestDeferredFieldsProjected` (alongside the existing 18 in `test_openmm_config_md_spec.py`):

| Test | What it pins |
|---|---|
| `test_equilibration_ps_extracted_from_spec` | Happy path: spec → OpenMMConfig 3-tuple |
| `test_equilibration_ps_default_matches_canonical_profile` | ACTIVIN_E_PROFILE reproduces 100/100/200 |
| `test_equilibration_ps_with_wrong_stage_count_raises` | 4-stage guard at projection boundary |
| `test_total_equil_steps_uses_spec_durations` | `__post_init__` derives step count from spec |
| `test_pme_propagates` | `pme=False` round-trips |
| `test_minimization_max_iterations_propagates` | 20,000 round-trips |
| `test_constraints_propagates` | `"AllBonds"` round-trips |
| `test_to_dict_includes_deferred_fields` | JSON wire round-trip via `simulation` block |

Plus the existing `test_from_md_spec_matches_manual_construction` equivalence test now includes the 4 new fields so a future drift between `from_md_spec` and the legacy `__init__` path is caught.

## Validation

`make validate` green: ruff check, ruff format, pyright strict (0 errors), 441 tests passing (was 433; +8 new), bandit clean on touched files (the pre-existing `utils.py` findings are not from this change), pre-commit (gitleaks + semgrep) clean, pre-push (trufflehog + detect-secrets + make validate) clean.

author: stoltembergg-png
juargo
body:
## Chain position

`📍` **PR 1 of 2** (feature-branch-chain) — targets the **tracker branch** `feat/us-040-editar-perfil` (draft, no-merge), not `main`.

```
main
 └─ feat/us-040-editar-perfil (tracker, draft, no-merge)
     └─ 📍 PR #1 (this PR) — identity read + nombre/email write
         └─ PR #2 (next) — password change + session revocation
```

Part of #274.

## What this PR does

Adds `PATCH /api/perfil` — the caller updates their own `nombre` and/or `email`, with the encrypted-column + blind-index invariant kept intact by construction — plus `nombre` on `GET /api/auth/me` (AUTH-09 delta). Password change and session revocation are PR #2.

This is the **first application-layer writer** of `User.email`/`emailBlindIndex` (ADR-013). Until now the only writers were `prisma/seed.ts` and `prisma/backfill-email-blind-index.ts`, both one-off scripts that open-code the pair — one of them caused a real production lockout on 2026-08-02. The design's job was to give that derivation **one structural home** whose shape makes a half-write unrepresentable:

- `IUserCredentialRepository.actualizarPerfil` takes the `Email` **value object**, never a raw string — a body string cannot reach the write path, it does not type-check.
- `PrismaUserCredentialRepository`'s private `camposEmail(email)` returns `{}` or the **full pair**, derived from the same `email.valor` in one literal, in one `prisma.user.update()`.
- A P2002 collision inspects the error and maps ONLY the `emailBlindIndex` constraint to a typed rejection — everything else (`googleSub`, unrecognized) rethrows fail-closed.
- Current password is required for any email change (`buscarCredencialPorId` + `IPasswordHasher`); wrong password, missing password, and email-already-taken all collapse into the same generic `403 PERFIL_RECHAZADO` (anti-enumeration).
- Demo sessions are rejected `403 DEMO_SOLO_LECTURA` before any repository call.

## Real bug found and fixed on the way

`design.md`'s P2002 disambiguation assumed `error.meta.target` (Prisma's documented shape). Verified against the **real driver adapter this repo actually uses** (`@prisma/adapter-pg`, Prisma 7, via `createPrismaClient`) against the real local Postgres: `meta.target` is **never populated** with driver adapters. The genuine collision info lives under `meta.driverAdapterError.cause.constraint.fields` / `.originalMessage`. A P2002 handler written only against the documented shape silently rethrows every real collision as a `500`, defeating the anti-enumeration collapse (PERF040-04) — caught by `test/perfil-crud.int-spec.ts` against the real DB, not by a mocked-Prisma unit test. Fixed by widening the check to recognize both shapes; unrecognized shapes still rethrow (fail-closed intact). Pinned with 2 new unit tests using the exact verified real shape.

## Deviation from design

`design.md` §7 lists `test/auth-login.e2e-spec.ts` as a regression check that "stays green, unmodified." `GET /api/auth/me`'s response body legitimately grows the required `nombre` field (AUTH-09 delta) — an exact `toEqual()` assertion cannot stay literally unmodified against an additive contract change. Applied the minimal 2-line fix (added `nombre` to the two assertions), its own commit (`Phase 7.5`), separate from the binding e2e. No other behavior in that file changed.

## The binding e2e

`test/perfil-email-change.e2e-spec.ts` is the change's headline test and the regression test for the 2026-08-02 incident: login with the OLD email succeeds → `PATCH /api/perfil` with a new email (mixed case + surrounding spaces, pinning normalization) → login with the NEW email succeeds → login with the OLD email fails `401` → the DB row is independently re-derived (fresh `crypto`/`blindIndex` instances, not the container's) and confirmed to match as a pair. If only one test survives review, it is this one.

## Review budget

`size:exception` — confirmed by the maintainer. `47 files changed, +4301/-37` including the SDD planning artifacts (`openspec/changes/us-040-editar-perfil/`, not previously committed to any branch); excluding those, the code diff is `42 files changed, +2328/-37`. Well over the 400-line budget, consistent with `tasks.md`'s forecast (`Chained PRs recommended: Yes`) — the bulk is test churn (unit + 3 new/extended integration/e2e specs), the safest lines in this diff and the ones the change's headline risk depends on.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm api test` — 212 files / 1686 tests green
- [x] `pnpm api exec tsc --noEmit` — 0 errors
- [x] `ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_DB=1 pnpm api test:integration` — 23 files / 120 tests green
- [x] `ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_DB=1 pnpm api test:e2e` — 11 files / 52 tests green
- [x] `pnpm api openapi:check` — green
- [x] `pnpm --filter @moneydiary/api-client typecheck` — green
- [x] `pnpm web test` — 61 files / 560 tests green, **zero edits under `apps/web/**`/`apps/mobile/**`**
- [x] `prisma/schema.prisma` + `prisma/migrations/**` — untouched (verified via diff, no migration needed per design §3.6)

## Out of scope (PR #2)

`Password` VO, `CambiarPasswordUseCase`, `PATCH /api/perfil/password`, session revocation (`revocarOtrasPorUserId`), `tokenHash` surfacing through `ValidarSesionResult`/`req.sessionTokenHash`.
